While believers direct their efforts toward upholding divine truth and justice, non-believers serve false ideologies and corrupt systems. The verse reassures believers that despite Satan's schemes appearing formidable, they are ultimately fragile and defeatable when confronted with divine truth and sincere faith.
orig: الذين آمنوا يقاتلون في سبيل الله والذين كفروا يقاتلون في سبيل الطاغوت فقاتلوا أولياء الشيطان إن كيد الشيطان كان ضعيفا

translation: Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and pay zakat"? But when fighting was ordained for them, behold, a group of them feared people as they fear Allah or with even greater fear. They said, "Our Lord, why have You ordained fighting for us? If only You had delayed it for us for a short time!" Say, "The enjoyment of this world is brief, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged even by as much as a thread of a date stone."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the human tendency to waver in commitment when faced with difficult tests of faith. While some people may appear devout in times of ease, performing prayers and giving charity, their true level of faith becomes apparent when faced with more challenging commands like fighting for a righteous cause. The verse criticizes those whose fear of worldly consequences exceeds their fear of Allah, highlighting how attachment to worldly life can compromise one's spiritual integrity. It reminds believers that this world's pleasures are temporary and that true reward lies in maintaining steadfast faith despite difficulties.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين قيل لهم كفوا أيديكم وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة فلما كتب عليهم القتال إذا فريق منهم يخشون الناس كخشية الله أو أشد خشية وقالوا ربنا لم كتبت علينا القتال لولا أخرتنا إلى أجل قريب قل متاع الدنيا قليل والآخرة خير لمن اتقى ولا تظلمون فتيلا

translation: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in lofty towers. And if good comes to them, they say, "This is from Allah"; but if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you." Say, "All is from Allah." So what is [wrong] with those people that they can hardly understand any statement?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal and inevitable nature of mortality, challenging the human tendency to attribute positive outcomes to divine will while blaming negative experiences on others, particularly the Prophet. It critiques the selective reasoning that fails to recognize Allah's ultimate sovereignty over all events, both favorable and unfavorable, reflecting a deeper spiritual immaturity in understanding divine decree.
orig: أينما تكونوا يدرككم الموت ولو كنتم في بروج مشيدة وإن تصبهم حسنة يقولوا هذه من عند الله وإن تصبهم سيئة يقولوا هذه من عندك قل كل من عند الله فمال هؤلاء القوم لا يكادون يفقهون حديثا

translation: Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself. And We have sent you as a Messenger to mankind, and Allah is sufficient as a Witness.
interpretation: This verse establishes a profound understanding of accountability and divine providence, teaching that while all good originates from Allah's grace and mercy, our misfortunes and hardships often stem from our own choices and actions. It reminds us that humans have free will and must take responsibility for their negative actions rather than attributing them to divine decree. The verse's placement alongside the mention of Prophet Muhammad's messengership suggests that this principle is a fundamental aspect of Islamic theology that he was meant to convey to humanity.
orig: ما أصابك من حسنة فمن الله وما أصابك من سيئة فمن نفسك وأرسلناك للناس رسولا وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah; but those who turn away - We have not sent you over them as a guardian
interpretation: This verse establishes the inseparable connection between obedience to Allah and obedience to Prophet Muhammad, indicating that the Prophet's teachings and commands are divinely inspired and not from his personal desires. It also highlights the Prophet's limited role as a messenger rather than an enforcer, emphasizing that guidance is offered but not compelled, respecting human free will in matters of faith.
orig: من يطع الرسول فقد أطاع الله ومن تولى فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا

translation: They say, "We are obedient," but when they leave your presence, a group of them spend the night plotting something different from what you say. Allah records what they plot at night. So turn away from them and put your trust in Allah. And sufficient is Allah as a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse exposes the nature of hypocrisy and duplicity, where people present a false facade of obedience while harboring different intentions in their hearts. It teaches us that true faith isn't about superficial compliance but genuine submission. The mention of Allah recording their plots reminds us that nothing escapes divine knowledge, while the command to turn away and trust in Allah suggests that the best response to such betrayal is to rise above it and place our reliance entirely on divine protection rather than becoming consumed by others' deception.
orig: ويقولون طاعة فإذا برزوا من عندك بيت طائفة منهم غير الذي تقول والله يكتب ما يبيتون فأعرض عنهم وتوكل على الله وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: Do they not ponder upon the Qur'an? Had it been from anyone other than Allah, they would have found much contradiction in it.
interpretation: This verse presents a profound challenge to skeptics by highlighting the Qur'an's divine origin through its internal consistency. It suggests that human works, being products of limited and changing understanding, naturally contain contradictions and inconsistencies over time. The absence of such contradictions in the Qur'an, despite its length and complexity, serves as evidence of its divine authorship, as only an all-knowing, unchanging divine source could produce a text that maintains perfect coherence across all its teachings, laws, stories, and principles.
orig: أفلا يتدبرون القرآن ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

translation: When there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it. But if they had referred it back to the Messenger or to those of authority among them, then the ones who can draw correct conclusions from it would have known about it. And if not for Allah's favor upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse teaches us about the importance of proper information handling and chain of command in sensitive matters. It criticizes those who hastily spread news about security matters without verification, which can cause unnecessary panic or harm. The proper approach is to refer such matters to those in authority who have the wisdom and capability to analyze and handle the information appropriately. This principle is particularly relevant in modern times with the spread of unverified news and rumors through social media, reminding us that responsible information sharing is an Islamic obligation.
orig: وإذا جاءهم أمر من الأمن أو الخوف أذاعوا به ولو ردوه إلى الرسول وإلى أولي الأمر منهم لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم ولولا فضل الله عليكم ورحمته لاتبعتم الشيطان إلا قليلا

translation: So fight in the cause of Allah; you are not held responsible except for yourself. And encourage the believers; perhaps Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve. And Allah is greater in might and stronger in punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility in striving for divine truth, highlighting that each individual is ultimately accountable only for their own actions. It suggests that while we can inspire and motivate others to join in righteous causes, we cannot force their participation. The divine promise that Allah's power supersedes all opposition serves as reassurance that truth and justice will ultimately prevail, even against seemingly insurmountable odds.
orig: فقاتل في سبيل الله لا تكلف إلا نفسك وحرض المؤمنين عسى الله أن يكف بأس الذين كفروا والله أشد بأسا وأشد تنكيلا

translation: Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share in its reward, and whoever intercedes for an evil cause will have a share in its burden. And Allah is ever, over all things, a Keeper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of moral responsibility and accountability in advocating for others. When someone uses their influence or position to help facilitate something beneficial, they earn spiritual rewards for their role in that good deed. Conversely, if someone facilitates or enables harmful actions, they bear partial responsibility for those negative consequences. This teaching encourages believers to be mindful of their role in supporting or opposing various causes, as they will be held accountable for the ripple effects of their advocacy.
orig: من يشفع شفاعة حسنة يكن له نصيب منها ومن يشفع شفاعة سيئة يكن له كفل منها وكان الله على كل شيء مقيتا

translation: When you are greeted with a greeting, respond with a better greeting or return it. Indeed, Allah takes account of all things.
interpretation: This verse teaches the importance of reciprocating kindness and maintaining positive social interactions. It suggests that Muslims should strive to exceed others' good gestures, fostering a society built on mutual respect and increasing goodwill. The mention of Allah's accounting reminds us that even these seemingly small social courtesies are significant in His sight and will be counted among our deeds.
orig: وإذا حييتم بتحية فحيوا بأحسن منها أو ردوها إن الله كان على كل شيء حسيبا

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. He will surely assemble you for [account on] the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute authority over the final judgment, asserting that His promise of resurrection and accountability is an irrefutable truth that stems from His unique position as the source of ultimate truth. The rhetorical question at the end serves to reinforce that divine promises are more reliable than any human assurance, establishing the foundation for belief in the Day of Judgment.
orig: الله لا إله إلا هو ليجمعنكم إلى يوم القيامة لا ريب فيه ومن أصدق من الله حديثا

translation: Why are you divided into two groups concerning the hypocrites, when Allah has cast them back [to disbelief] for what they have earned? Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has left astray? Whoever Allah leaves astray - never will you find for him a way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in dealing with those who choose hypocrisy. It warns believers against attempting to rationalize or defend hypocritical behavior, as Allah's judgment on such individuals is based on their own conscious choices. The verse emphasizes that true guidance is ultimately in Allah's hands, and when someone persistently chooses deception and disbelief, their spiritual blindness becomes a divine decree that cannot be reversed by human intervention.
orig: فما لكم في المنافقين فئتين والله أركسهم بما كسبوا أتريدون أن تهدوا من أضل الله ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be alike. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate for the cause of Allah. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them and take not from among them any ally or helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological warfare and social pressure that early Muslims faced from those who rejected faith, showing how disbelievers often seek to draw others into their disbelief to validate their own choices. It warns against forming alliances with those who actively work against the faith while providing a path to reconciliation through sincere acceptance of faith ("until they emigrate"). The stern warning about dealing with those who "turn away" specifically referred to those who were actively fighting against the Muslim community in the historical context of warfare, not a general command for all times.
orig: ودوا لو تكفرون كما كفروا فتكونون سواء فلا تتخذوا منهم أولياء حتى يهاجروا في سبيل الله فإن تولوا فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث وجدتموهم ولا تتخذوا منهم وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: Except those who join a group between whom and you there is a treaty, or those who come to you with hearts restraining them from fighting you or fighting their own people. If Allah had willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. So if they withdraw and do not fight you and offer you peace, then Allah has not made for you a cause against them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Islamic principle of respecting treaties and showing mercy to those who choose peace. It teaches Muslims to exercise restraint and not to fight against those who either have peace treaties with them or those who clearly show no intention of hostility. The verse highlights Allah's preference for peace over conflict when the opposing party demonstrates peaceful intentions, establishing an important foundation for diplomatic relations and conflict resolution in Islamic law.
orig: إلا الذين يصلون إلى قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق أو جاءوكم حصرت صدورهم أن يقاتلوكم أو يقاتلوا قومهم ولو شاء الله لسلطهم عليكم فلقاتلوكم فإن اعتزلوكم فلم يقاتلوكم وألقوا إليكم السلم فما جعل الله لكم عليهم سبيلا

translation: You will find others who wish to obtain security from you and obtain security from their people. Every time they are returned to [the influence of] temptation, they fall back into it. So if they do not withdraw from you or offer you peace or restrain their hands, then seize them and kill them wherever you overtake them. And those - We have made for you against them a clear authorization.
interpretation: This verse addresses the complex nature of dealing with hypocrites who attempt to maintain allegiances with both the Muslim community and their own hostile tribes. It reveals Allah's guidance on handling those who demonstrate duplicitous behavior, showing that while Islam encourages peace and reconciliation, it also recognizes the necessity of taking firm action against those who consistently prove treacherous and pose a threat to the community's security.
orig: ستجدون آخرين يريدون أن يأمنوكم ويأمنوا قومهم كل ما ردوا إلى الفتنة أركسوا فيها فإن لم يعتزلوكم ويلقوا إليكم السلم ويكفوا أيديهم فخذوهم واقتلوهم حيث ثقفتموهم وأولئكم جعلنا لكم عليهم سلطانا مبينا

translation: Never should a believer kill a believer unless by mistake. And whoever kills a believer by mistake must free a believing slave and pay blood-money to the victim's family unless they forgo it. If the victim was a believer from a people hostile to you, then only a believing slave must be freed. If the victim was from a people with whom you have a treaty, then blood-money must be paid to the family and a believing slave freed. Those who are unable must fast two consecutive months—as a means of repentance to Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the sanctity of human life in Islamic law and outlines the specific legal consequences for accidental killing. It demonstrates Islam's emphasis on justice balanced with mercy, as it provides both punishment and pathways for atonement. The requirement of freeing a slave shows Islam's inclination toward emancipation, while the blood money system ensures financial support for the victim's family. The alternative of fasting for those who cannot afford these penalties indicates Islamic law's consideration of different economic circumstances, making justice accessible to all social classes.
orig: وما كان لمؤمن أن يقتل مؤمنا إلا خطأ ومن قتل مؤمنا خطأ فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة ودية مسلمة إلى أهله إلا أن يصدقوا فإن كان من قوم عدو لكم وهو مؤمن فتحرير رقبة مؤمنة وإن كان من قوم بينكم وبينهم ميثاق فدية مسلمة إلى أهله وتحرير رقبة مؤمنة فمن لم يجد فصيام شهرين متتابعين توبة من الله وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, their reward will be Hell, where they will remain forever. Allah's wrath has fallen upon them, He has cursed them, and He has prepared for them a tremendous punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of human life in Islam, particularly that of a believer. The severity of the punishment mentioned reflects how the intentional taking of an innocent life represents a complete rejection of divine moral order and human brotherhood. The eternal nature of the punishment indicates that murder not only violates human rights but also represents a fundamental breach of trust with the Creator, as it involves destroying what Allah has made sacred.
orig: ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها وغضب الله عليه ولعنه وأعد له عذابا عظيما

translation: O you who believe! When you go forth in the cause of Allah, investigate carefully, and do not say to one who greets you with peace, "You are not a believer," seeking the perishable goods of worldly life. There are much greater riches with Allah. You yourselves were like this before, then Allah conferred His favor upon you; therefore investigate carefully. Indeed, Allah is well aware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of exercising careful judgment and avoiding hasty conclusions about others' faith. It warns against dismissing someone's profession of faith merely for worldly gain, reminding believers that they too were once in a similar position before embracing Islam. The divine instruction to "investigate carefully" establishes a fundamental principle in Islamic jurisprudence that requires thorough verification before making judgments about others' faith or character.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ضربتم في سبيل الله فتبينوا ولا تقولوا لمن ألقى إليكم السلام لست مؤمنا تبتغون عرض الحياة الدنيا فعند الله مغانم كثيرة كذلك كنتم من قبل فمن الله عليكم فتبينوا إن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: Not equal are those believers who sit (at home) - except those who are disabled - and those who strive in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit by a degree. And to all, Allah has promised good, but Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit with a great reward.
interpretation: This verse establishes a divine hierarchy of spiritual merit, emphasizing that active sacrifice and struggle for faith carries greater spiritual weight than passive belief. It acknowledges that while all believers are promised good, those who actively invest their resources and risk their lives for their beliefs demonstrate a superior level of commitment. However, the verse carefully includes an exemption for those with disabilities, showing divine recognition of human limitations and circumstances beyond one's control.
orig: لا يستوي القاعدون من المؤمنين غير أولي الضرر والمجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم فضل الله المجاهدين بأموالهم وأنفسهم على القاعدين درجة وكلا وعد الله الحسنى وفضل الله المجاهدين على القاعدين أجرا عظيما

translation: Degrees [of high position] from Him and forgiveness and mercy. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine system of spiritual elevation, where He not only forgives sins but also raises the status of those who strive in His path. The mention of degrees (darajat) suggests that spiritual growth isn't binary but rather a continuous journey of ascending levels, with each level bringing the believer closer to divine mercy and forgiveness.
orig: درجات منه ومغفرة ورحمة وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: Indeed, those whom the angels take [in death] while wronging themselves - [the angels] will say, 'In what [condition] were you?' They will say, 'We were oppressed in the land.' [The angels] will say, 'Was not Allah's earth spacious [enough] for you to emigrate therein?' For those, their refuge is Hell - and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse addresses those who remain in a state of oppression or persecution when they have the ability to migrate to safer places where they can practice their faith freely. It criticizes those who make excuses for staying in situations where they compromise their religious principles, when Allah has provided vast alternatives on Earth. The angels' questioning highlights personal responsibility in seeking better circumstances for one's spiritual well-being, rather than passively accepting oppressive conditions that lead to religious compromise.
orig: إن الذين توفاهم الملائكة ظالمي أنفسهم قالوا فيم كنتم قالوا كنا مستضعفين في الأرض قالوا ألم تكن أرض الله واسعة فتهاجروا فيها فأولئك مأواهم جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Except for the oppressed among men, women and children who cannot devise a plan nor are they directed to a way
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and compassion towards those who are genuinely powerless and vulnerable in society. It acknowledges that there are people who face legitimate barriers to practicing their faith or migrating from oppression due to their weakness, lack of resources, or inability to find means of escape. These individuals are exempt from blame for their situation, as Allah recognizes their genuine constraints and limitations.
orig: إلا المستضعفين من الرجال والنساء والولدان لا يستطيعون حيلة ولا يهتدون سبيلا

translation: For those, Allah may pardon them, and Allah is Ever-Pardoning, Most Forgiving
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's boundless mercy and forgiveness, suggesting that even when people fall into error or face difficult circumstances beyond their control, there remains hope for divine pardon. The use of "may" (عسى) indicates an optimistic expectation of forgiveness, while emphasizing that Allah's pardoning nature is an eternal attribute of His character.
orig: فأولئك عسى الله أن يعفو عنهم وكان الله عفوا غفورا

translation: And whoever emigrates for the cause of Allah will find on earth many locations and abundance. And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger and then death overtakes him - his reward has already become incumbent upon Allah. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual and material rewards of making sacrifices for one's faith. It suggests that when someone leaves their comfort zone and familiar surroundings for the sake of their religious convictions, Allah promises both physical provisions and spiritual openings. The divine guarantee of reward, even if one dies during such migration, indicates that the intention behind the action is more valuable than its completion, highlighting Allah's recognition of the heart's sincere commitment over the final outcome.
orig: ومن يهاجر في سبيل الله يجد في الأرض مراغما كثيرا وسعة ومن يخرج من بيته مهاجرا إلى الله ورسوله ثم يدركه الموت فقد وقع أجره على الله وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may disrupt you. Indeed, the disbelievers are ever to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and consideration for the practical needs of believers, acknowledging that during times of travel or danger, flexibility in religious obligations is permissible. It demonstrates that Islam is a religion of ease rather than hardship, adapting to circumstances while maintaining the essence of worship. The mention of fear from disbelievers also indicates that Muslims should remain vigilant and practical in their approach to worship when facing potential threats.
orig: وإذا ضربتم في الأرض فليس عليكم جناح أن تقصروا من الصلاة إن خفتم أن يفتنكم الذين كفروا إن الكافرين كانوا لكم عدوا مبينا

translation: When you are with them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you, taking their weapons. After they prostrate, let them be behind you, and let another group that has not prayed come forward to pray with you, taking their precautions and weapons. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and belongings so they could attack you in a single assault. But there is no blame upon you, if you are troubled by rain or are ill, for putting down your weapons, but take your precautions. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the remarkable balance in Islam between spiritual duties and practical security measures. It shows that even in times of danger and warfare, the obligation of prayer is not suspended, but rather modified to ensure both spiritual fulfillment and physical safety. The instruction to pray in groups while maintaining armed vigilance reflects the pragmatic nature of Islamic teachings, acknowledging that faith must be protected through both spiritual and physical means. The verse also reveals the constant threat believers faced from their enemies, who would exploit any moment of vulnerability, teaching Muslims to remain vigilant while never compromising their religious duties.
orig: وإذا كنت فيهم فأقمت لهم الصلاة فلتقم طائفة منهم معك وليأخذوا أسلحتهم فإذا سجدوا فليكونوا من ورائكم ولتأت طائفة أخرى لم يصلوا فليصلوا معك وليأخذوا حذرهم وأسلحتهم ود الذين كفروا لو تغفلون عن أسلحتكم وأمتعتكم فيميلون عليكم ميلة واحدة ولا جناح عليكم إن كان بكم أذى من مطر أو كنتم مرضى أن تضعوا أسلحتكم وخذوا حذركم إن الله أعد للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, or [lying] on your sides. But when you become secure, re-establish [regular] prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuous nature of spiritual consciousness, teaching that our connection with God shouldn't be limited to formal prayer times. Even in times of fear or unusual circumstances, we must maintain our remembrance of Allah in whatever position we find ourselves. The verse suggests that spiritual mindfulness should permeate all our physical states and daily activities, while also highlighting that formal prayers should be properly established once safety is restored, indicating a balance between flexibility in extraordinary circumstances and maintaining religious discipline in normal conditions.
orig: فإذا قضيتم الصلاة فاذكروا الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبكم فإذا اطمأننتم فأقيموا الصلاة إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا

translation: And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you are suffering, then surely they are also suffering as you suffer, but you hope from Allah what they do not hope, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse provides spiritual motivation during times of hardship, emphasizing that while both believers and non-believers experience similar worldly difficulties, the believer's position is superior because they possess hope in Allah's rewards and divine assistance. This hope, coupled with faith, should serve as a source of strength and perseverance that distinguishes believers from others, enabling them to endure challenges with greater resilience and purpose.
orig: ولا تهنوا في ابتغاء القوم إن تكونوا تألمون فإنهم يألمون كما تألمون وترجون من الله ما لا يرجون وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book with the truth so that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the deceitful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine purpose behind the revelation of the Qur'an, highlighting that leadership and judgment must be based on divine guidance rather than personal inclination. It serves as a reminder that those in positions of authority have a sacred responsibility to deliver justice according to God's teachings, while warning against defending those who engage in dishonesty or betrayal, even if they appear to be allies or friends.
orig: إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق لتحكم بين الناس بما أراك الله ولا تكن للخائنين خصيما

translation: And seek forgiveness from Allah, indeed Allah is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perpetual opportunity for spiritual renewal through seeking Allah's forgiveness. The use of "kana" (was/is) with Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy suggests these are intrinsic, timeless qualities of the Divine. The command to seek forgiveness, coupled with the affirmation of Allah's forgiving nature, indicates that no sin is too great to be forgiven when one turns to Allah with sincere repentance.
orig: واستغفر الله إن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves. Indeed, Allah does not like those who are deceitful and sinful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of moral integrity and warns against defending those who knowingly engage in dishonest behavior. The deeper message is that supporting or justifying wrongdoing makes one complicit in the sin, and Allah's disapproval extends not only to the wrongdoers but also to those who advocate for them. The verse teaches that we should stand for truth and justice rather than becoming advocates for those who betray trust and moral principles.
orig: ولا تجادل عن الذين يختانون أنفسهم إن الله لا يحب من كان خوانا أثيما

translation: They seek to hide from people, but they cannot hide from Allah - for He is with them when they plot by night with words He does not approve. And Allah ever encompasses what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of hypocrisy and deceptive behavior, emphasizing that while people may successfully conceal their misdeeds from other humans, they can never escape Allah's awareness. The specific mention of nighttime plotting suggests that darkness and secrecy don't provide any cover from divine knowledge, serving as a powerful reminder that Allah's presence and knowledge are absolute and inescapable, regardless of how well-concealed one's actions might be from other people.
orig: يستخفون من الناس ولا يستخفون من الله وهو معهم إذ يبيتون ما لا يرضى من القول وكان الله بما يعملون محيطا

translation: Here you are, those who argued for them in this worldly life - but who will argue with Allah for them on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning about the futility of defending wrongdoers in this world, as such defense will be meaningless on the Day of Judgment. It highlights that those who advocate for unjust causes or defend wrongdoers in this life will find themselves powerless before Allah's judgment, where no advocate or guardian can help against divine justice.
orig: ها أنتم هؤلاء جادلتم عنهم في الحياة الدنيا فمن يجادل الله عنهم يوم القيامة أم من يكون عليهم وكيلا

translation: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks Allah's forgiveness, he will find Allah Most Forgiving, Most Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite capacity for forgiveness and highlights the transformative power of sincere repentance. It suggests that no sin is too great to be forgiven when one genuinely turns back to Allah with remorse. The verse also implies that humans are prone to mistakes and self-harm through their actions, but the door to divine mercy remains perpetually open, encouraging believers to maintain hope and never despair of Allah's forgiveness regardless of their past actions.
orig: ومن يعمل سوءا أو يظلم نفسه ثم يستغفر الله يجد الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And whoever commits a sin only earns it against themselves. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability in Islam, highlighting that the consequences of our misdeeds ultimately affect our own spiritual well-being. When someone commits a sin, they aren't harming Allah or diminishing His authority; rather, they're damaging their own soul and standing before their Creator. The mention of Allah being All-Knowing and All-Wise indicates that no sin goes unnoticed, and His judgment is based on perfect wisdom and complete knowledge of our intentions and circumstances.
orig: ومن يكسب إثما فإنما يكسبه على نفسه وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: And whoever commits a mistake or sin and then blames it on an innocent person, has taken upon himself a slander and a clear sin
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe moral and spiritual consequences of false accusation, highlighting how attempting to escape responsibility for one's actions by blaming innocent people compounds the original sin with an even greater transgression. It warns against the human tendency to deflect blame and underscores the importance of personal accountability in Islamic ethics.
orig: ومن يكسب خطيئة أو إثما ثم يرم به بريئا فقد احتمل بهتانا وإثما مبينا

translation: And if it were not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have determined to mislead you. But they do not mislead except themselves, and they will not harm you at all. And Allah has revealed to you the Book and wisdom and has taught you that which you did not know. And ever great is the favor of Allah upon you.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine protection granted to Prophet Muhammad against those who sought to deceive him, emphasizing that Allah's guidance and wisdom serve as a shield against malicious attempts at deception. It demonstrates how spiritual enlightenment and divine knowledge act as safeguards against misguidance, suggesting that when one is connected to divine wisdom, attempts by others to mislead become ineffective.
orig: ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته لهمت طائفة منهم أن يضلوك وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم وما يضرونك من شيء وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما

translation: There is no good in most of their private conversations except those who enjoin charity, kindness, or reconciliation between people. And whoever does this seeking Allah's pleasure, We will give them a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that idle talk and secret conversations often lead to negativity and harm, but conversations become valuable when they focus on three specific purposes: encouraging charitable acts, promoting goodness, or mediating conflicts. The divine wisdom here teaches that our private discussions should be purposeful and directed toward improving society rather than engaging in gossip or harmful speech. When these positive actions are done with sincere intention for Allah's pleasure, they elevate from mere social acts to worship deserving magnificent spiritual rewards.
orig: لا خير في كثير من نجواهم إلا من أمر بصدقة أو معروف أو إصلاح بين الناس ومن يفعل ذلك ابتغاء مرضات الله فسوف نؤتيه أجرا عظيما

translation: And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken and drive him to Hell, and evil it is as a destination
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of deliberately rejecting divine guidance after having clear knowledge of it. It suggests that conscious deviation from the Prophet's teachings and the collective path of the faithful community isn't merely an individual choice but a grave spiritual transgression. The mention of "the way of the believers" indicates that there's wisdom in following the consensus of the believing community, as it serves as a safeguard against individual misguidance.
orig: ومن يشاقق الرسول من بعد ما تبين له الهدى ويتبع غير سبيل المؤمنين نوله ما تولى ونصله جهنم وساءت مصيرا

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of shirk (polytheism) in Islamic theology, indicating that it represents the ultimate boundary in divine forgiveness. While Allah's mercy is vast enough to potentially forgive all other sins through His will, the conscious decision to associate partners with Him places one outside the realm of divine pardon unless there is sincere repentance before death. This underscores the fundamental importance of monotheism in the Islamic faith and serves as a warning about the severe consequences of compromising this core belief.
orig: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء ومن يشرك بالله فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: They call upon instead of Him none but females [deities], and they call upon none but a rebellious Satan
interpretation: This verse exposes the irony and futility of idolatry by highlighting how pagans often worship feminine deities, which they themselves would consider inferior in their patriarchal society, while unknowingly serving Satan who leads them astray from true monotheism. The feminine deities were seen as intercessors, but in reality, they were merely names without power, and their worship was ultimately a form of Satan's deception.
orig: إن يدعون من دونه إلا إناثا وإن يدعون إلا شيطانا مريدا

translation: Allah cursed him, and he [Satan] said, "I will surely take from among Your servants a specific portion"
interpretation: This verse reveals Satan's arrogant defiance and his strategic approach to misleading humanity. By declaring he will take a "specific portion," Satan indicates his methodical and calculated plan to target human souls, suggesting that spiritual warfare isn't random but rather a systematic campaign against human faith. The use of "specific portion" also implies Satan's acknowledgment of his limitations, as he can't mislead all of God's servants, particularly those who maintain strong faith.
orig: لعنه الله وقال لأتخذن من عبادك نصيبا مفروضا

translation: And I will surely mislead them, and I will arouse in them desires, and I will command them so they will slit the ears of cattle, and I will command them so they will change the creation of Allah. And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly sustained a clear loss.
interpretation: This verse reveals Satan's strategic methods of corrupting humanity through a progression of spiritual and physical alterations. By promising false desires and encouraging the modification of God's natural creation, Satan leads people away from their innate spiritual nature (fitrah). The reference to slitting cattle's ears symbolizes how Satan normalizes the distortion of God's creation, leading to broader acts of changing what Allah has created - whether physically or spiritually. This serves as a warning that following Satan's path inevitably leads to disconnection from one's true nature and divine purpose.
orig: ولأضلنهم ولأمنينهم ولآمرنهم فليبتكن آذان الأنعام ولآمرنهم فليغيرن خلق الله ومن يتخذ الشيطان وليا من دون الله فقد خسر خسرانا مبينا

translation: Satan makes them promises and creates false hopes for them—but Satan's promises are nothing but delusion
interpretation: The verse reveals the deceptive nature of Satan's influence on human beings, showing how he operates by exploiting our desires through empty promises and false hopes. These promises are ultimately hollow and lead to disappointment, serving as a warning that any path or promise that leads away from divine guidance is essentially an illusion designed to mislead.
orig: يعدهم ويمنيهم وما يعدهم الشيطان إلا غرورا

translation: Their refuge is Hell, and they will find no escape from it
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute finality and inescapability of divine justice for those who persistently reject truth and righteousness. The use of the word "refuge" (ma'wa) ironically suggests that what they seek as shelter becomes their prison, highlighting how their choices lead to an inevitable consequence from which there is no diplomatic immunity, no technological solution, no wealth, or power that can provide an alternative path.
orig: أولئك مأواهم جهنم ولا يجدون عنها محيصا

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. [It is] the promise of Allah, [which is] truth, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of divine justice and reward, highlighting that true success isn't measured by worldly achievements but by faith manifested through good actions. The imagery of flowing rivers represents continuous renewal and sustenance, suggesting that the rewards of paradise are ever-fresh and perpetual. The rhetorical question at the end serves to reinforce absolute trust in Allah's promises, challenging humans to recognize that divine assurance surpasses all human guarantees.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات سندخلهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا وعد الله حقا ومن أصدق من الله قيلا

translation: It is not by your wishes, nor by the wishes of the People of the Book: whoever does evil will be requited for it, and will not find any protector or helper besides Allah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal principle of accountability and divine justice, reminding both Muslims and People of the Book that mere wishful thinking or claims of religious superiority don't guarantee salvation. What truly matters is one's actions and deeds, as everyone will face the consequences of their misdeeds without any intermediary's intervention to shield them from Allah's judgment.
orig: ليس بأمانيكم ولا أماني أهل الكتاب من يعمل سوءا يجز به ولا يجد له من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged [even as much as] the speck on a date seed
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute justice and the universal nature of divine reward, transcending gender distinctions. It establishes that spiritual elevation and rewards are attainable by all believers based solely on their faith and good actions, not their gender or social status. The mention of "naqira" (the tiny speck on a date seed) illustrates that Allah's justice is so precise that not even the smallest amount of good deeds will go unrewarded.
orig: ومن يعمل من الصالحات من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة ولا يظلمون نقيرا

translation: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Abraham as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the essence of true religious devotion, highlighting that the highest form of faith combines three essential elements: complete submission to Allah's will, actively doing good deeds, and following the pure monotheistic path of Prophet Abraham. The mention of Abraham as Allah's intimate friend (Khalil) underscores the special relationship that develops between the Divine and those who sincerely follow this path, suggesting that such spiritual closeness is attainable through genuine devotion and righteous conduct.
orig: ومن أحسن دينا ممن أسلم وجهه لله وهو محسن واتبع ملة إبراهيم حنيفا واتخذ الله إبراهيم خليلا

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever, of all things, encompassing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and complete knowledge, illustrating that His dominion extends beyond physical ownership to include total awareness and control of every particle, thought, and occurrence in existence. The term "muhit" (encompassing) suggests that nothing can escape Allah's knowledge or power, much like how an ocean encompasses everything within it, indicating His complete mastery over all dimensions of reality.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله بكل شيء محيطا

translation: They ask you concerning women. Say: Allah instructs you about them and about what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphaned women to whom you do not give what is ordained for them, and whom you desire to marry, and concerning the oppressed children, and that you should deal with orphans in justice. And whatever good you do, Allah is ever Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse addresses the deep concern for social justice in Islamic society, particularly regarding vulnerable groups. It emphasizes the moral responsibility of guardians to protect the rights of orphaned women, ensuring they receive their due inheritance and are not exploited through marriage for their wealth. The mention of "oppressed children" alongside this instruction suggests a broader divine mandate to protect all vulnerable members of society, establishing a comprehensive ethical framework for social welfare and justice.
orig: ويستفتونك في النساء قل الله يفتيكم فيهن وما يتلى عليكم في الكتاب في يتامى النساء اللاتي لا تؤتونهن ما كتب لهن وترغبون أن تنكحوهن والمستضعفين من الولدان وأن تقوموا لليتامى بالقسط وما تفعلوا من خير فإن الله كان به عليما

translation: And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion, there is no sin upon them if they make terms of settlement between them - and settlement is best. And present in [human] souls is stinginess. But if you do good and fear Allah - then indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse addresses the delicate balance in marital relationships, emphasizing that when difficulties arise, particularly in cases where a wife senses emotional distance or neglect from her husband, Islam encourages constructive dialogue and compromise rather than immediate separation. The mention of "stinginess in souls" acknowledges the human tendency to be self-centered and unwilling to sacrifice personal desires, suggesting that successful conflict resolution requires both parties to overcome their natural inclination toward selfishness. The verse promotes the idea that maintaining family unity through mutual understanding and concessions is preferable to dissolution, while also reminding couples that their efforts toward reconciliation are noticed and valued by Allah.
orig: وإن امرأة خافت من بعلها نشوزا أو إعراضا فلا جناح عليهما أن يصلحا بينهما صلحا والصلح خير وأحضرت الأنفس الشح وإن تحسنوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive. So do not incline completely [toward one] and leave another hanging. And if you amend and fear Allah, then indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful
interpretation: This verse acknowledges the natural human limitation in maintaining perfect emotional equality between multiple wives, while simultaneously establishing a moral imperative to strive for fairness. It warns against showing such extreme preference to one wife that another is left in a suspended state, neither properly married nor divorced. The divine recognition of human imperfection, coupled with the encouragement to maintain justice and God-consciousness, reflects Islam's practical approach to managing complex human relationships.
orig: ولن تستطيعوا أن تعدلوا بين النساء ولو حرصتم فلا تميلوا كل الميل فتذروها كالمعلقة وإن تصلحوا وتتقوا فإن الله كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance. And Allah is ever Encompassing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse conveys Allah's reassurance about divorce, teaching that one should not remain in an unhealthy marriage out of fear of financial hardship. It emphasizes that Allah's provision is not limited to marital relationships, and He has the power to provide sustenance and contentment to both parties independently through His infinite resources and wisdom.
orig: وإن يتفرقا يغن الله كلا من سعته وكان الله واسعا حكيما

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And We have instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and yourselves to fear Allah. But if you disbelieve - then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's universal sovereignty and highlights the continuity of divine guidance across different religious traditions. It suggests that the fundamental message of God-consciousness (taqwa) has been consistent throughout all divine revelations, creating a spiritual lineage between previous scripture-bearing communities and Muslims. The repetition of Allah's ownership over everything serves as both a comfort to believers and a reminder that human disbelief doesn't diminish Allah's power or majesty, as He is self-sufficient and independent of His creation.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ولقد وصينا الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم وإياكم أن اتقوا الله وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكان الله غنيا حميدا

translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and complete ownership over all creation, both visible and invisible. It reassures believers that since Allah owns and controls everything, we can place our complete trust in Him to manage our affairs, solve our problems, and fulfill our needs. The phrase "sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs" particularly indicates that we need not seek other sources of help or protection, as Allah's care and management is complete and perfect.
orig: ولله ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring forth others, and Allah is ever Capable of doing that
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over creation, reminding humans of their replaceable nature. It serves as both a warning against arrogance and a demonstration that no individual or group is indispensable in Allah's grand scheme. Just as civilizations have risen and fallen throughout history, Allah has the power to replace any people with others who might be more faithful and obedient to His commands.
orig: إن يشأ يذهبكم أيها الناس ويأت بآخرين وكان الله على ذلك قديرا

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world - then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty over both worldly and eternal rewards, reminding believers that focusing solely on worldly gains is short-sighted when Allah has authority over all forms of success. It encourages Muslims to broaden their aspirations beyond temporary worldly benefits and consider the eternal rewards, as Allah's power encompasses both realms and He is fully aware of people's intentions and desires.
orig: من كان يريد ثواب الدنيا فعند الله ثواب الدنيا والآخرة وكان الله سميعا بصيرا

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So follow not personal inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Aware
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme importance of justice in Islamic ethics, elevating it above personal interests, family ties, and socioeconomic status. It teaches that true faith requires the courage to stand for truth and justice even when it conflicts with our own interests or those of our loved ones. The mention of rich and poor indicates that justice must be blind to social status, while the warning about following personal inclination acknowledges human tendency to be biased. The verse concludes with a powerful reminder of divine accountability, suggesting that every act of justice or injustice is recorded and will be accounted for.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين بالقسط شهداء لله ولو على أنفسكم أو الوالدين والأقربين إن يكن غنيا أو فقيرا فالله أولى بهما فلا تتبعوا الهوى أن تعدلوا وإن تلووا أو تعرضوا فإن الله كان بما تعملون خبيرا

translation: O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book that He sent down upon His Messenger and the Scripture which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive nature of Islamic faith, indicating that true belief requires accepting all aspects of divine revelation throughout history. It suggests that faith isn't a one-time declaration but a continuous commitment to deepen one's conviction in all pillars of faith. The verse implies that rejecting any single element of faith is equivalent to rejecting the whole system, as these elements are interconnected and inseparable in God's divine plan.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا آمنوا بالله ورسوله والكتاب الذي نزل على رسوله والكتاب الذي أنزل من قبل ومن يكفر بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر فقد ضل ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Those who believe, then disbelieve, then believe, then disbelieve, then increase in disbelief - Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe spiritual consequences of repeatedly wavering between faith and disbelief, suggesting that persistent indecision and returning to disbelief after accepting faith indicates a deeper rejection of truth. Such behavior reflects a fundamental lack of sincerity and commitment, making one's heart increasingly resistant to divine guidance and forgiveness.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم آمنوا ثم كفروا ثم ازدادوا كفرا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم سبيلا

translation: Give tidings to the hypocrites that they will have a painful punishment
interpretation: The divine sarcasm in using "give tidings" - typically reserved for good news - to announce punishment highlights the severity of Allah's displeasure with hypocrisy, suggesting that duplicity in faith is among the gravest spiritual transgressions that warrant severe consequences in the afterlife
orig: بشر المنافقين بأن لهم عذابا أليما

translation: Those who take disbelievers as allies instead of believers - do they seek honor with them? For indeed, honor belongs to Allah entirely.
interpretation: This verse warns against seeking validation and protection from those who oppose faith while abandoning fellow believers. It addresses a deeper psychological tendency where some might gravitate toward powerful but unbelieving forces hoping to gain status or security. The verse reminds us that true honor and dignity come exclusively from alignment with divine principles, not from worldly alliances. It suggests that seeking honor from those who reject faith is ultimately futile since Allah is the sole source of genuine respect and dignity.
orig: الذين يتخذون الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أيبتغون عندهم العزة فإن العزة لله جميعا

translation: And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being denied and ridiculed, do not sit with them until they engage in another conversation. Indeed, you would then be like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and disbelievers in Hell all together.
interpretation: This verse establishes a crucial principle of maintaining one's spiritual integrity by actively disassociating from environments where religious mockery occurs. It suggests that passive presence during acts of disrespect towards divine teachings makes one complicit in the transgression, highlighting how our choice of company and social environments directly impacts our spiritual state. The verse's conclusion serves as a powerful reminder that those who participate in or silently condone such mockery align themselves with disbelievers, facing similar consequences in the afterlife.
orig: وقد نزل عليكم في الكتاب أن إذا سمعتم آيات الله يكفر بها ويستهزأ بها فلا تقعدوا معهم حتى يخوضوا في حديث غيره إنكم إذا مثلهم إن الله جامع المنافقين والكافرين في جهنم جميعا

translation: Those who wait and watch you; if there is a victory for you from Allah, they say, "Were we not with you?" But if the disbelievers have success, they say, "Did we not help you prevail and protect you from the believers?" Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers.
interpretation: This verse exposes the duplicitous nature of hypocrites who strategically align themselves based on perceived advantages. They exhibit opportunistic behavior, claiming allegiance to believers when Muslims are victorious, yet revealing their true loyalties when disbelievers gain the upper hand. The verse reassures believers that despite such manipulative tactics, Allah's final judgment will prevail, and He has decreed that true believers will ultimately not be dominated by those who reject faith.
orig: الذين يتربصون بكم فإن كان لكم فتح من الله قالوا ألم نكن معكم وإن كان للكافرين نصيب قالوا ألم نستحوذ عليكم ونمنعكم من المؤمنين فالله يحكم بينكم يوم القيامة ولن يجعل الله للكافرين على المؤمنين سبيلا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little
interpretation: This verse reveals the psychological state of hypocrites who attempt to maintain a false appearance of faith while harboring disbelief. Their attempt to "deceive Allah" demonstrates their fundamental misunderstanding of divine omniscience, as one cannot deceive the All-Knowing. Their lazy approach to prayer and performative worship exposes their lack of sincerity, as true faith manifests in enthusiastic devotion rather than mechanical motions done for public approval.
orig: إن المنافقين يخادعون الله وهو خادعهم وإذا قاموا إلى الصلاة قاموا كسالى يراءون الناس ولا يذكرون الله إلا قليلا

translation: Wavering between them, [belonging] neither to these [believers] nor to those [disbelievers]. And whoever Allah sends astray - never will you find for him a way.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the precarious spiritual state of hypocrites who lack genuine conviction, perpetually oscillating between faith and disbelief. Their indecisiveness stems from their attempt to maintain favor with both believers and non-believers, ultimately leading to a state of spiritual limbo that reflects their lack of authentic commitment to truth. Their condition serves as a warning about the consequences of inauthentic faith and the importance of making a clear, committed choice in matters of belief.
orig: مذبذبين بين ذلك لا إلى هؤلاء ولا إلى هؤلاء ومن يضلل الله فلن تجد له سبيلا

translation: O you who believe! Do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to provide Allah with clear evidence against yourselves?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining loyalty within the believing community, warning against forming close alliances with those who actively oppose Islamic faith and values. The reference to "clear evidence" suggests that choosing disbelievers as allies over believers could be seen as a form of betrayal to one's faith, potentially indicating a weakness in one's commitment to Allah. The verse highlights the spiritual and social boundaries that should be maintained while still allowing for normal, respectful interactions with non-believers in daily life.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الكافرين أولياء من دون المؤمنين أتريدون أن تجعلوا لله عليكم سلطانا مبينا

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire - and never will you find for them a helper
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of hypocrisy in faith, suggesting that those who maintain a false outward appearance of belief while harboring disbelief internally face the worst possible spiritual fate. Their position at the lowest level of Hell indicates that religious hypocrisy is considered even more dangerous than outright disbelief, as it undermines the community's trust and corrupts faith from within.
orig: إن المنافقين في الدرك الأسفل من النار ولن تجد لهم نصيرا

translation: Except for those who repent, correct themselves, hold fast to Allah, and are sincere in their religion for Allah - those will be with the believers. And Allah is going to give the believers a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite mercy and the transformative power of sincere repentance. It teaches that no matter how far one has strayed, the path to redemption remains open through four essential steps: genuine repentance, active self-correction, steadfast attachment to Allah, and purification of one's faith from all forms of insincerity. When these conditions are met, the past becomes irrelevant, and the repentant person is fully integrated into the community of believers, deserving of the same divine rewards.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا وأصلحوا واعتصموا بالله وأخلصوا دينهم لله فأولئك مع المؤمنين وسوف يؤت الله المؤمنين أجرا عظيما

translation: Why would Allah punish you if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is ever Appreciative, All-Knowing
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and lack of desire to inflict punishment, highlighting that His purpose isn't to torment humanity but rather to guide them. It suggests that genuine gratitude and faith serve as spiritual protection from divine punishment, as Allah recognizes and appreciates these qualities in His servants. The mention of Allah being "appreciative" indicates that He multiplies and rewards even the smallest acts of faith and gratitude, while His attribute of being "All-Knowing" assures us that He perfectly understands the true state of our hearts and the sincerity of our beliefs.
orig: ما يفعل الله بعذابكم إن شكرتم وآمنتم وكان الله شاكرا عليما

translation: Allah does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. And Allah is ever Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining dignity and restraint in speech, highlighting that speaking ill of others publicly is generally disapproved by Allah. However, an exception is made for those who have been genuinely wronged, allowing them to speak up about their oppression to seek justice. This exception demonstrates Allah's recognition of the need for victims to voice their grievances while maintaining the general principle of avoiding harmful speech.
orig: لا يحب الله الجهر بالسوء من القول إلا من ظلم وكان الله سميعا عليما

translation: Whether you disclose a good deed or conceal it or pardon an evil, Allah is Ever-Pardoning, Most Capable
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's attribute of forgiveness while encouraging believers to embody this divine quality. It suggests that whether we choose to do good openly or privately, and whether we forgive others' misdeeds, what matters most is cultivating a forgiving heart. The verse implies that since Allah, with all His power, is so forgiving of human shortcomings, we too should strive to be forgiving toward others despite our relative weakness.
orig: إن تبدوا خيرا أو تخفوه أو تعفوا عن سوء فإن الله كان عفوا قديرا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to discriminate between Allah and His messengers and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and wish to adopt a way in between
interpretation: This verse highlights the inconsistency and illogical nature of partial faith. Those who attempt to selectively believe in certain aspects of divine guidance while rejecting others are essentially trying to create their own customized version of faith, which undermines the fundamental principle that divine guidance is an interconnected whole. It's like trying to accept a sender while rejecting their authorized messenger, which is inherently contradictory.
orig: إن الذين يكفرون بالله ورسله ويريدون أن يفرقوا بين الله ورسله ويقولون نؤمن ببعض ونكفر ببعض ويريدون أن يتخذوا بين ذلك سبيلا

translation: Those are truly the disbelievers, and We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine justice that awaits those who consciously reject truth after it has been made clear to them. The use of "humiliating" punishment specifically indicates that since their rejection of faith stemmed from arrogance and pride, their punishment will particularly target these aspects of their character, bringing them low from their perceived position of superiority.
orig: أولئك هم الكافرون حقا وأعتدنا للكافرين عذابا مهينا

translation: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not discriminate between any of them - those He will grant them their rewards. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of accepting all of Allah's prophets equally, without elevating some while rejecting others. It teaches that authentic faith requires believing in the complete chain of divine guidance, from Adam to Muhammad. The promise of reward highlights that spiritual success comes from embracing the unity and continuity of divine revelation rather than fragmenting one's faith through selective belief.
orig: والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله ولم يفرقوا بين أحد منهم أولئك سوف يؤتيهم أجورهم وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven. Indeed, they asked Moses for even more than that, saying, "Show us Allah directly," and they were struck by a thunderbolt for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf for worship after clear signs had come to them, but We pardoned them for that and gave Moses clear authority.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the pattern of unreasonable demands and skepticism that prophets face from their people. The comparison between the demands made to Prophet Muhammad and those made to Moses demonstrates how some people persist in seeking extraordinary proofs beyond what's necessary for faith. The mention of God's forgiveness despite such serious transgressions shows His mercy, while also warning against making excessive demands of religious leaders rather than accepting the signs and evidence already provided.
orig: يسألك أهل الكتاب أن تنزل عليهم كتابا من السماء فقد سألوا موسى أكبر من ذلك فقالوا أرنا الله جهرة فأخذتهم الصاعقة بظلمهم ثم اتخذوا العجل من بعد ما جاءتهم البينات فعفونا عن ذلك وآتينا موسى سلطانا مبينا

translation: And We raised above them the Mount by their covenant, and We said to them, "Enter the gate prostrating," and We said to them, "Do not transgress on the Sabbath," and We took from them a solemn covenant
interpretation: This verse illustrates how divine guidance often comes with both physical manifestations and moral obligations. The raising of Mount Tur served as a dramatic reminder of Allah's power and authority, while the commands about proper entry and Sabbath observance represented the essential elements of humility and discipline in worship. The "solemn covenant" suggests that spiritual commitments require serious dedication and have profound consequences when broken.
orig: ورفعنا فوقهم الطور بميثاقهم وقلنا لهم ادخلوا الباب سجدا وقلنا لهم لا تعدوا في السبت وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا

translation: So for their breaking of the covenant and their disbelief in the signs of Allah and their killing of the prophets without right and their saying, "Our hearts are wrapped." Rather, Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief, so they believe not, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the spiritual consequence of persistent disobedience and rejection of divine guidance. When people repeatedly violate their moral commitments and deny truth, their hearts gradually become hardened, not by divine injustice, but as a natural result of their own choices. Like a muscle that atrophies from disuse, the spiritual faculty becomes increasingly unable to recognize and accept truth when it's continuously rejected.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم وكفرهم بآيات الله وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق وقولهم قلوبنا غلف بل طبع الله عليها بكفرهم فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا

translation: And for their disbelief and their speaking against Mary a great slander
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of false accusations, particularly those made against the virtuous. The slander against Mary's chastity by some of the Jews was considered especially egregious because it targeted not only her honor but also attempted to discredit a miraculous divine sign. It teaches us about the gravity of defamation in God's eyes, especially when directed at the righteous and pure.
orig: وبكفرهم وقولهم على مريم بهتانا عظيما

translation: And their saying, "Indeed, we killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the messenger of Allah." And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but it appeared so to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him, for certain.
interpretation: This verse challenges the historical narrative of Jesus's crucifixion, suggesting that divine intervention created an illusion that protected Jesus from actual death. It points to the limitations of human perception and knowledge, highlighting how even those who claimed to have witnessed or participated in the event were deceived by appearances. The verse criticizes those who make definitive claims about Jesus's death, indicating that they base their beliefs on conjecture rather than certain knowledge.
orig: وقولهم إنا قتلنا المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وما قتلوه وما صلبوه ولكن شبه لهم وإن الذين اختلفوا فيه لفي شك منه ما لهم به من علم إلا اتباع الظن وما قتلوه يقينا

translation: Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms Allah's supreme power and wisdom in elevating Prophet Jesus (Isa) to the heavens, protecting him from his enemies who sought to harm him. It demonstrates that divine intervention supersedes human schemes, and that Allah's plans are executed with absolute authority and perfect wisdom.
orig: بل رفعه الله إليه وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: And there is none from the People of the Book but will believe in him before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them
interpretation: This verse speaks to the ultimate recognition of Jesus's true nature and message by all People of the Book (Jews and Christians). It suggests that before a person's death, they will come to acknowledge the truth about Jesus as described in Islamic teachings - that he was a prophet of God but not divine. This moment of clarity comes when it's too late to change one's worldly actions, highlighting the importance of accepting truth while one still has the opportunity to live by it.
orig: وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته ويوم القيامة يكون عليهم شهيدا

translation: So for the wrongdoing of those who were Jewish, We prohibited them from good things which had been lawful to them, and for their averting many people from the way of Allah
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine justice and consequence, showing how the collective actions of some among the Jewish people led to specific restrictions being placed upon them. Their transgressions, particularly their persistent disobedience and their active efforts to prevent others from following Allah's path, resulted in the withdrawal of certain privileges they once enjoyed. This serves as a universal lesson about how spiritual and moral corruption can lead to the loss of divine favors and blessings.
orig: فبظلم من الذين هادوا حرمنا عليهم طيبات أحلت لهم وبصدهم عن سبيل الله كثيرا

translation: And [for] their taking of usury while they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming of the people's wealth unjustly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights how the practice of usury represents a severe moral transgression, as it exploits people's financial vulnerabilities and creates socioeconomic inequality. The divine condemnation of usury, despite clear prohibitions, reflects how economic exploitation through interest-based transactions disrupts the ethical fabric of society and perpetuates cycles of poverty and dependence. The mention of "consuming wealth unjustly" alongside usury suggests that any financial gain obtained through deceptive or exploitative means is viewed as a serious violation of divine law and human dignity.
orig: وأخذهم الربا وقد نهوا عنه وأكلهم أموال الناس بالباطل وأعتدنا للكافرين منهم عذابا أليما

translation: But those firm in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and the establishers of prayer and the givers of zakah and the believers in Allah and the Last Day - those We will give a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between true scholars and believers who possess deep understanding versus those who merely follow without comprehension. It suggests that genuine knowledge leads to recognition of divine truth across different revelations, while emphasizing that authentic faith combines intellectual conviction with practical religious observance. The promise of great reward indicates that integrating knowledge, belief, and religious practice represents the highest form of spiritual achievement.
orig: لكن الراسخون في العلم منهم والمؤمنون يؤمنون بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك والمقيمين الصلاة والمؤتون الزكاة والمؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أولئك سنؤتيهم أجرا عظيما

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you [O Muhammad] as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and We gave David the Psalms
interpretation: This verse establishes the continuity and unity of divine revelation throughout human history, emphasizing that Muhammad's message is part of the same chain of prophetic guidance that includes all major prophets. It demonstrates that Islam doesn't claim to be a new religion but rather a continuation and completion of God's message to humanity, validating the authenticity of previous prophets while positioning Muhammad within this sacred lineage.
orig: إنا أوحينا إليك كما أوحينا إلى نوح والنبيين من بعده وأوحينا إلى إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق ويعقوب والأسباط وعيسى وأيوب ويونس وهارون وسليمان وآتينا داوود زبورا

translation: And We have already told you the stories of some messengers before, and of some messengers We have not told you. And Allah spoke to Moses directly.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's selective revelation of prophetic narratives, indicating that divine wisdom determines which stories are shared and which remain untold. The specific mention of Moses' direct communication with Allah emphasizes his unique status among prophets, known as "Kalimullah" (the one who spoke directly with Allah), demonstrating that Allah's methods of communication with His messengers varied according to His divine wisdom.
orig: ورسلا قد قصصناهم عليك من قبل ورسلا لم نقصصهم عليك وكلم الله موسى تكليما

translation: Messengers as bearers of good news and warners, so that humanity would have no argument against Allah after the messengers. And Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's perfect justice and mercy in that He never holds people accountable without first providing them clear guidance through His messengers. By sending prophets who both gave glad tidings and warnings, Allah removed any possible excuse people might have on the Day of Judgment, claiming they were unaware of divine truth. This demonstrates Allah's wisdom in establishing clear proof against those who reject faith, while simultaneously showing His mercy in giving everyone a fair chance at guidance.
orig: رسلا مبشرين ومنذرين لئلا يكون للناس على الله حجة بعد الرسل وكان الله عزيزا حكيما

translation: But Allah bears witness to that which He has revealed to you. He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness [as well]. And sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes divine authentication of revelation, asserting that the truth of the message doesn't depend on human acceptance but carries the highest form of validation through Allah's own testimony. The mention of His knowledge suggests that the revelation is perfectly aligned with divine wisdom and purpose, while the angels' witness adds another layer of celestial confirmation, establishing an unbreakable chain of authenticity for the divine message.
orig: لكن الله يشهد بما أنزل إليك أنزله بعلمه والملائكة يشهدون وكفى بالله شهيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah have certainly gone far astray
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of rejection of faith - not only do these individuals reject truth themselves, but they actively work to prevent others from finding guidance. Their straying is described as "far" because they compound their own misguidance by becoming obstacles in others' spiritual journeys, making their deviation particularly severe in Allah's sight.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وصدوا عن سبيل الله قد ضلوا ضلالا بعيدا

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged - Allah would not forgive them, nor would He guide them to a path
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine principle of accountability and personal responsibility. It suggests that persistent rejection of truth and deliberate wrongdoing, when maintained until death without repentance, places one beyond the reach of divine forgiveness and guidance. The verse isn't about Allah's inability to forgive, but rather about how one's own choices can create a spiritual barrier that prevents them from receiving Allah's mercy and direction.
orig: إن الذين كفروا وظلموا لم يكن الله ليغفر لهم ولا ليهديهم طريقا

translation: Except the path of Hell, wherein they shall abide forever, and that is ever easy for Allah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permanence of divine justice, indicating that those who persistently reject guidance will find themselves on an unchangeable course. The phrase "easy for Allah" suggests that implementing eternal consequences requires no effort from the Divine, highlighting Allah's absolute power and the natural flow of cause and effect in spiritual matters.
orig: إلا طريق جهنم خالدين فيها أبدا وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا

translation: O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you. But if you disbelieve - then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy in sending divine guidance through the Prophet Muhammad, while also highlighting human free will and responsibility. It suggests that belief benefits humans themselves, not Allah, as He remains completely self-sufficient. The mention of Allah's ownership over everything in existence serves as a reminder that human rejection doesn't diminish His authority or power. The verse concludes by affirming Allah's complete knowledge and wisdom in offering this guidance, indicating that His invitation to faith is based on His perfect understanding of what's best for humanity.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم الرسول بالحق من ربكم فآمنوا خيرا لكم وإن تكفروا فإن لله ما في السماوات والأرض وكان الله عليما حكيما

translation: O People of the Book! Do not go to extremes in your religion, and do not say about Allah except the truth.
