The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger of Allah and His Word which He conveyed to Mary, and a spirit from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And do not say "Trinity." Stop! It is better for you. Indeed, Allah is only one God. Glory be to Him! He is far above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse addresses a fundamental theological correction to Christian beliefs, particularly warning against the deification of Jesus and the concept of Trinity. It establishes the Islamic view of Jesus's nature as being purely human while acknowledging his miraculous birth and special status as a messenger. The verse emphasizes absolute monotheism (tawhid) and rejects the notion of God having offspring, presenting this as incompatible with divine perfection. The phrase "do not go to extremes" suggests that elevating religious figures beyond their proper status leads to theological error.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم ولا تقولوا على الله إلا الحق إنما المسيح عيسى ابن مريم رسول الله وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم وروح منه فآمنوا بالله ورسله ولا تقولوا ثلاثة انتهوا خيرا لكم إنما الله إله واحد سبحانه أن يكون له ولد له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وكفى بالله وكيلا

translation: Never would the Messiah disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor would the angels near [to Him]. And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant - He will gather them to Himself all together.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound concept of universal servitude to Allah, highlighting that even exalted beings like Jesus (the Messiah) and the angels embrace their role as servants of God. It challenges the notion of Jesus's divinity by showing that he himself accepts and honors his position as Allah's servant. The verse also warns against spiritual arrogance, suggesting that true greatness lies in humble submission to God, not in refusing to acknowledge one's created nature.
orig: لن يستنكف المسيح أن يكون عبدا لله ولا الملائكة المقربون ومن يستنكف عن عبادته ويستكبر فسيحشرهم إليه جميعا

translation: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and grant them extra from His bounty. But as for those who disdained and were arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine principle of ultimate justice and reciprocity, emphasizing that Allah's response to human actions goes beyond mere equivalence. For the faithful who combine belief with good actions, Allah promises not just fair compensation but additional rewards, demonstrating His boundless generosity. Conversely, those who reject faith through arrogance face isolation and vulnerability, as their self-imposed separation from divine guidance leaves them without any genuine source of protection or assistance.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات فيوفيهم أجورهم ويزيدهم من فضله وأما الذين استنكفوا واستكبروا فيعذبهم عذابا أليما ولا يجدون لهم من دون الله وليا ولا نصيرا

translation: O mankind! There has come to you a convincing proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy in providing humanity with undeniable evidence of His existence and truth through the Qur'an and Prophet Muhammad. The "clear light" metaphorically represents divine guidance that illuminates the path of truth, dispelling spiritual darkness and confusion from people's hearts and minds.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءكم برهان من ربكم وأنزلنا إليكم نورا مبينا

translation: As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him, He will admit them into His mercy and grace, and guide them to Himself on a straight path
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound relationship between sincere faith and divine guidance. When believers demonstrate their trust in Allah through unwavering faith and actively seek His protection, Allah responds with a transformative spiritual embrace. The "straight path" mentioned represents not just moral guidance, but a direct spiritual connection to Allah, suggesting that authentic faith leads to an intimate understanding of divine truth and purpose in life.
orig: فأما الذين آمنوا بالله واعتصموا به فسيدخلهم في رحمة منه وفضل ويهديهم إليه صراطا مستقيما

translation: They seek your ruling. Say, "Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalālah [those who die leaving neither descendants nor ascendants as heirs]. If a man dies, leaving no child but [only] a sister, she will have half of what he left. And he inherits from her if she [dies and] has no child. But if there are two sisters, they shall have two-thirds of what he left. If there are both brothers and sisters, the male will have the share of two females. Allah makes clear to you [His law], lest you go astray. And Allah is Knowing of all things."
interpretation: This verse reflects Allah's divine wisdom in establishing a comprehensive inheritance system that maintains family bonds and ensures economic justice. The specific focus on kalālah cases demonstrates Islam's attention to detail in protecting the rights of extended family members when direct heirs are absent. By allocating specific shares and establishing the 2:1 ratio between males and females, the verse establishes a balanced economic system that considers the broader financial responsibilities placed on men in Islamic society.
orig: يستفتونك قل الله يفتيكم في الكلالة إن امرؤ هلك ليس له ولد وله أخت فلها نصف ما ترك وهو يرثها إن لم يكن لها ولد فإن كانتا اثنتين فلهما الثلثان مما ترك وإن كانوا إخوة رجالا ونساء فللذكر مثل حظ الأنثيين يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: O you who believe! Fulfill your contracts. Lawful to you are grazing livestock, except for what is recited to you, hunting not being permitted while you are in the state of ihram. Indeed, Allah ordains what He wills.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of trustworthiness and reliability in all contractual obligations, whether they be with Allah or fellow humans. The divine command to honor agreements reflects how maintaining one's word is integral to the believer's character and essential for establishing a just society built on mutual trust and respect.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أوفوا بالعقود أحلت لكم بهيمة الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم غير محلي الصيد وأنتم حرم إن الله يحكم ما يريد

translation: O you who believe! Do not violate the rites of Allah, nor the sacred month, nor the sacrificial animals, nor the garlanded ones, nor those heading to the Sacred House seeking bounty and pleasure from their Lord. When you have completed your pilgrimage rites, you may hunt. And do not let the hatred of people who once barred you from the Sacred Mosque lead you to transgress. Help one another in righteousness and piety, and do not help one another in sin and transgression. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes fundamental principles of ethical conduct and social justice in Islam, emphasizing that personal grievances or historical conflicts should never justify transgression or violation of moral boundaries. It teaches that even when faced with those who have wronged us, Muslims must maintain their moral integrity and not let emotions override their commitment to justice and ethical behavior. The command to cooperate in righteousness while avoiding cooperation in wrongdoing creates a framework for positive social interaction and collective moral responsibility.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحلوا شعائر الله ولا الشهر الحرام ولا الهدي ولا القلائد ولا آمين البيت الحرام يبتغون فضلا من ربهم ورضوانا وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم أن صدوكم عن المسجد الحرام أن تعتدوا وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان واتقوا الله إن الله شديد العقاب

translation: Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and the strangled animals, and those beaten to death, and those killed by falling, and those killed by goring, and those eaten by wild animals - except what you slaughter - and that which is sacrificed on stone altars, and that you seek division by divining arrows. That is grave disobedience. This day those who disbelieve have despaired of your religion, so fear them not, but fear Me. This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have chosen for you Islam as religion. But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes a comprehensive ethical framework for dietary laws while simultaneously marking a pivotal moment in Islamic history. The detailed prohibitions of specific foods and practices reflect Allah's concern for both physical and spiritual purity, protecting believers from harmful substances and pagan rituals. The latter part of the verse carries profound historical significance, declaring the completion of religious legislation and the establishment of Islam as a complete way of life. This declaration was revealed during the Prophet's final pilgrimage, signifying that the fundamental principles of faith had been fully communicated. The allowance for necessity in cases of extreme hunger demonstrates Islam's practicality and Allah's mercy, showing that preservation of life takes precedence over dietary restrictions when survival is at stake.
orig: حرمت عليكم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير وما أهل لغير الله به والمنخنقة والموقوذة والمتردية والنطيحة وما أكل السبع إلا ما ذكيتم وما ذبح على النصب وأن تستقسموا بالأزلام ذلكم فسق اليوم يئس الذين كفروا من دينكم فلا تخشوهم واخشون اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم وأتممت عليكم نعمتي ورضيت لكم الإسلام دينا فمن اضطر في مخمصة غير متجانف لإثم فإن الله غفور رحيم

translation: They ask you what is lawful for them. Say: "Lawful for you are all good things, and [the prey] that you have trained of hunting animals which you train as Allah has taught you. So eat of what they catch for you and mention Allah's name upon it, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning."
interpretation: This verse establishes a divine framework for ethical hunting and consumption, emphasizing the importance of proper training and respect for God's creation. It suggests that humans have been given the responsibility to train hunting animals according to divine guidance, indicating a balanced relationship between human needs and animal welfare. The requirement to mention Allah's name reinforces the sacred nature of taking life for sustenance and serves as a reminder that all provisions ultimately come from God.
orig: يسألونك ماذا أحل لهم قل أحل لكم الطيبات وما علمتم من الجوارح مكلبين تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم واذكروا اسم الله عليه واتقوا الله إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: This day [all] good foods have been made lawful, and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them. And [lawful in marriage are] chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their due compensation, desiring chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse or taking [secret] lovers. And whoever denies the faith - his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse establishes important social and dietary principles that facilitate positive interfaith relations, particularly with People of the Book (Jews and Christians). It demonstrates Islam's openness to social interaction by permitting Muslims to share meals with People of the Book and marry their chaste women, provided proper marriage conditions are met. This ruling helped create bridges between communities while maintaining moral standards and religious identity. The verse's conclusion warns that rejecting faith nullifies good deeds, emphasizing that these social freedoms must be exercised within the framework of maintaining one's religious commitment.
orig: اليوم أحل لكم الطيبات وطعام الذين أوتوا الكتاب حل لكم وطعامكم حل لهم والمحصنات من المؤمنات والمحصنات من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم إذا آتيتموهن أجورهن محصنين غير مسافحين ولا متخذي أخدان ومن يكفر بالإيمان فقد حبط عمله وهو في الآخرة من الخاسرين

translation: O you who believe! When you rise to pray, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles. And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, then purify yourselves. But if you are ill or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself, or you have been in contact with women, and you find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual significance of physical purification, teaching us that external cleanliness is intrinsically linked to internal purity. Allah's prescription of ablution (wudu) and dry ablution (tayammum) demonstrates His mercy by providing alternatives when water is unavailable, showing that Islam is a religion of ease, not hardship. The detailed instructions for purification serve as a regular reminder of our covenant with Allah and help prepare our hearts and minds for prayer, while the mention of gratitude suggests that these rituals are actually blessings rather than burdens.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا قمتم إلى الصلاة فاغسلوا وجوهكم وأيديكم إلى المرافق وامسحوا برءوسكم وأرجلكم إلى الكعبين وإن كنتم جنبا فاطهروا وإن كنتم مرضى أو على سفر أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط أو لامستم النساء فلم تجدوا ماء فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم منه ما يريد الله ليجعل عليكم من حرج ولكن يريد ليطهركم وليتم نعمته عليكم لعلكم تشكرون

translation: And remember Allah's favor upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey." And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound spiritual contract between believers and Allah, reminding them that their verbal commitment to obedience carries deep responsibility. The mention of Allah knowing "what is within the breasts" suggests that mere verbal declarations aren't sufficient; true faith and obedience must be rooted in sincere inner conviction and genuine intention.
orig: واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم وميثاقه الذي واثقكم به إذ قلتم سمعنا وأطعنا واتقوا الله إن الله عليم بذات الصدور

translation: O you who believe! Stand firmly for Allah as witnesses to fair dealing, and let not the hatred of others make you swerve to wrong and depart from justice. Be just: that is closer to piety; and fear Allah, for Allah is well-acquainted with all that you do.
interpretation: This verse establishes a fundamental principle of Islamic ethics that justice must be maintained even in the face of personal animosity. It teaches that a believer's commitment to justice should transcend their emotional biases and personal feelings. Even when dealing with enemies or those we dislike, Muslims are commanded to maintain objectivity and fairness in their judgments and dealings. The verse connects justice with piety (taqwa), suggesting that being just is not merely a social obligation but a spiritual duty that brings one closer to divine consciousness.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا كونوا قوامين لله شهداء بالقسط ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم على ألا تعدلوا اعدلوا هو أقرب للتقوى واتقوا الله إن الله خبير بما تعملون

translation: Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have forgiveness and a great reward
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine contract between Allah and the faithful, highlighting that true faith must be accompanied by positive actions. The promise of both forgiveness and reward suggests that even devoted believers will have shortcomings needing forgiveness, but their sincere efforts in faith and good deeds will ultimately lead to an extraordinary reward that transcends worldly comprehension.
orig: وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم مغفرة وأجر عظيم

translation: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability and the consequences of conscious rejection of divine guidance. It specifically addresses those who not only disbelieve but actively deny the truth after it has been made clear to them. The use of "companions" (أصحاب) rather than just "dwellers" suggests a deep, lasting association with their fate, indicating that this outcome is a result of their deliberate choices and persistent denial.
orig: والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب الجحيم

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend their hands [in aggression] against you, but He withheld their hands from you. And fear Allah, and upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine protection Allah provides to the faithful, reminding believers of a specific instance when they were saved from physical harm or aggression. It teaches that while human beings may plot and plan against the believers, Allah's protection supersedes all threats when we maintain our trust in Him. The verse serves as a powerful reminder that true security comes not from worldly defenses but from divine protection, encouraging believers to cultivate both God-consciousness (taqwa) and reliance on Allah (tawakkul) as their primary means of safety.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا نعمت الله عليكم إذ هم قوم أن يبسطوا إليكم أيديهم فكف أيديهم عنكم واتقوا الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And Allah had already taken a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We appointed from among them twelve leaders. And Allah said, "I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and loan Allah a goodly loan, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever of you disbelieves after that has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine contract between Allah and the Children of Israel, emphasizing that spiritual leadership and divine guidance come with reciprocal obligations. The appointment of twelve leaders symbolizes organized spiritual governance, while the conditions set forth - prayer, charity, belief in messengers, and supporting the cause of faith - represent the essential elements of maintaining a relationship with the Divine. The metaphor of lending Allah a "goodly loan" suggests that any sacrifice made for faith will be repaid abundantly, highlighting that sincere religious commitment leads to both spiritual purification and ultimate reward.
orig: ولقد أخذ الله ميثاق بني إسرائيل وبعثنا منهم اثني عشر نقيبا وقال الله إني معكم لئن أقمتم الصلاة وآتيتم الزكاة وآمنتم برسلي وعزرتموهم وأقرضتم الله قرضا حسنا لأكفرن عنكم سيئاتكم ولأدخلنكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار فمن كفر بعد ذلك منكم فقد ضل سواء السبيل

translation: So for their breaking of the covenant We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their places and have forgotten a portion of that of which they were reminded. And you will still observe deceit among them, except a few of them. But pardon them and overlook [their misdeeds]. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the spiritual and moral consequences of breaking divine covenants, showing how persistent disobedience leads to a gradual hardening of the heart and spiritual blindness. When people repeatedly violate their commitments to God, it creates a spiritual callousness that makes them more prone to distorting religious truths and forgetting their moral obligations. However, the verse's conclusion with a call for pardoning demonstrates that divine mercy and forgiveness remain available even after serious transgressions, emphasizing that the path to righteousness remains open through compassion and good conduct.
orig: فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم لعناهم وجعلنا قلوبهم قاسية يحرفون الكلم عن مواضعه ونسوا حظا مما ذكروا به ولا تزال تطلع على خائنة منهم إلا قليلا منهم فاعف عنهم واصفح إن الله يحب المحسنين

translation: And from those who say "We are Christians," We took their covenant, but they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. So We caused among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah will inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine consequence of breaking sacred covenants, specifically referring to how certain Christian communities deviated from their original teachings and abandoned their spiritual obligations. The resulting disunity and sectarian conflicts among Christian denominations are presented as a divine punishment for this deviation, serving as a warning about the serious implications of neglecting divine guidance and breaking spiritual commitments.
orig: ومن الذين قالوا إنا نصارى أخذنا ميثاقهم فنسوا حظا مما ذكروا به فأغرينا بينهم العداوة والبغضاء إلى يوم القيامة وسوف ينبئهم الله بما كانوا يصنعون

translation: O People of the Book! Our Messenger has come to you, revealing much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture and overlooking much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy in sending Prophet Muhammad to correct the distortions and manipulations that had been introduced into previous divine scriptures. The "overlooking much" suggests Allah's compassion in not exposing all alterations, focusing instead on essential corrections needed for humanity's guidance. The "light" refers to Prophet Muhammad's guidance which illuminates the path to truth, while the "clear Book" (Qur'an) serves as an uncorrupted, transparent source of divine law.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم كثيرا مما كنتم تخفون من الكتاب ويعفو عن كثير قد جاءكم من الله نور وكتاب مبين

translation: Through it Allah guides those who pursue His pleasure to the ways of peace and brings them out from darkness into light by His permission and guides them to a straight path
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine guidance system, where those who actively seek His pleasure are rewarded with inner peace and clarity. The metaphorical transition from darkness to light represents the journey from ignorance and confusion to spiritual enlightenment and understanding. The "straight path" signifies the clear moral and spiritual direction that leads to eternal success, emphasizing that true guidance comes only through divine permission and sincere intention.
orig: يهدي به الله من اتبع رضوانه سبل السلام ويخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور بإذنه ويهديهم إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary." Say, "Then who could prevent Allah at all if He had intended to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, or his mother or everyone on the earth?" And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse refutes the concept of Jesus's divinity by presenting a logical argument: if Jesus were truly God, he would have possessed absolute power and control. However, his existence, like his mother's and all creation's, was dependent on Allah's will. This demonstrates that Jesus was a created being, subject to Allah's authority, not divine himself. The verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and creative power over all existence.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم قل فمن يملك من الله شيئا إن أراد أن يهلك المسيح ابن مريم وأمه ومن في الأرض جميعا ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما يخلق ما يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And the Jews and Christians say, "We are the children of Allah and His beloved." Say, "Then why does He punish you for your sins?" Rather, you are human beings from among those He has created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the final destination.
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of spiritual superiority and divine favoritism claimed by certain religious groups. It emphasizes that true divine favor isn't based on hereditary or tribal affiliations, but on one's actions and God's mercy. The verse establishes the universal principle that all humans stand equal before God, and no community has an exclusive claim to divine love or salvation.
orig: وقالت اليهود والنصارى نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه قل فلم يعذبكم بذنوبكم بل أنتم بشر ممن خلق يغفر لمن يشاء ويعذب من يشاء ولله ملك السماوات والأرض وما بينهما وإليه المصير

translation: O People of the Book! Our Messenger has come to you, making things clear to you after a period without messengers, lest you say, "There has not come to us any bearer of good news or a warner." But now there has come to you a bearer of good news and a warner. And Allah has power over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy in sending Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to humanity after a long gap in divine guidance. It specifically addresses the Jews and Christians, reminding them that they can no longer claim ignorance or absence of divine guidance as an excuse. The verse suggests that Allah's wisdom in sending messengers at specific intervals serves to maintain the connection between divine guidance and human civilization, ensuring that humanity always has access to spiritual and moral direction.
orig: يا أهل الكتاب قد جاءكم رسولنا يبين لكم على فترة من الرسل أن تقولوا ما جاءنا من بشير ولا نذير فقد جاءكم بشير ونذير والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: And [recall] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you when He appointed among you prophets and made you possessors and gave you that which He had not given anyone among the worlds."
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's special favor upon the Children of Israel, emphasizing their unique position in history as a community blessed with continuous prophetic guidance. The mention of making them "possessors" or "kings" suggests that they were given both spiritual and worldly authority, a combination of blessings that set them apart from other nations of their time. This divine favor came with great responsibility, and Moses's reminder serves as both an encouragement and a subtle warning about the accountability that accompanies such privileges.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه يا قوم اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ جعل فيكم أنبياء وجعلكم ملوكا وآتاكم ما لم يؤت أحدا من العالمين

translation: O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has destined for you, and do not turn back, for then you will become losers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine promise and responsibility given to the Children of Israel. The "Holy Land" represents not just a physical territory, but a spiritual mandate and test of faith. The warning against turning back symbolizes how retreating from divinely ordained missions and responsibilities leads to both spiritual and worldly loss. It teaches that when Allah designates a path or purpose for believers, moving forward with faith and conviction is essential for success.
orig: يا قوم ادخلوا الأرض المقدسة التي كتب الله لكم ولا ترتدوا على أدباركم فتنقلبوا خاسرين

translation: They said: "O Moses, indeed there are tyrannical people in it, and we will never enter it until they leave from it. And if they leave from it, then we will enter."
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep-rooted fear and lack of faith among the Children of Israel. Despite having witnessed Allah's miracles through Moses, they allowed their fear of powerful enemies to override their trust in divine support. Their conditional statement reveals a mindset seeking the easy path rather than showing willingness to strive in Allah's cause, demonstrating how human weakness can manifest as rationalization for disobedience.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إن فيها قوما جبارين وإنا لن ندخلها حتى يخرجوا منها فإن يخرجوا منها فإنا داخلون

translation: Two men among those who feared Allah and on whom Allah had bestowed His grace said: "Enter upon them through the gate, for when you enter it, you will be victorious. And put your trust in Allah if you are believers."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power of unwavering faith and trust in Allah's divine plan. The two righteous men's advice emphasizes that victory comes not through numerical strength or material resources, but through complete reliance (tawakkul) on Allah. Their statement reflects the Islamic principle that when believers take the initiative while maintaining absolute trust in Allah, they position themselves for success. The mention of entering through the gate symbolizes taking decisive action rather than remaining paralyzed by fear, showing that faith must be paired with practical steps.
orig: قال رجلان من الذين يخافون أنعم الله عليهما ادخلوا عليهم الباب فإذا دخلتموه فإنكم غالبون وعلى الله فتوكلوا إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: They said: "O Moses, we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we will remain here sitting"
interpretation: This verse reveals the deep-rooted cowardice and spiritual deficiency among the Children of Israel. Their response to Moses demonstrates not only their unwillingness to struggle in God's cause but also a profound disrespect towards both divine authority and prophetic leadership. By telling Moses to go fight with "your Lord," they display a detachment from their own relationship with God, suggesting they viewed Him as Moses' deity rather than their own, indicating their weak faith and lack of true belief in divine providence.
orig: قالوا يا موسى إنا لن ندخلها أبدا ما داموا فيها فاذهب أنت وربك فقاتلا إنا هاهنا قاعدون

translation: He said: "My Lord! I have power only over myself and my brother, so separate us from the rebellious people."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound sense of helplessness and isolation that righteous leaders may feel when confronting widespread corruption. Moses' plea reflects the reality that true believers sometimes must distance themselves from those who persistently reject divine guidance, acknowledging that they can only be responsible for their own actions and those who stand with them in faith.
orig: قال رب إني لا أملك إلا نفسي وأخي فافرق بيننا وبين القوم الفاسقين

translation: He (Allah) said: "Then indeed, it (the Holy Land) will be forbidden to them for forty years, they will wander throughout the land, so do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people"
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine punishment through deprivation, where Allah's response to the Israelites' disobedience was to deny them entry into the Promised Land. The forty-year wandering period served as both a punishment and a purification process, allowing the rise of a new generation untainted by the slave mentality and cowardice of their forefathers. The instruction not to grieve over the disobedient shows that those who deliberately reject divine guidance deserve their fate.
orig: قال فإنها محرمة عليهم أربعين سنة يتيهون في الأرض فلا تأس على القوم الفاسقين

translation: And recite to them the story of Adam's two sons in truth, when they offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not from the other. He said, "I will surely kill you." He replied, "Allah only accepts from the righteous."
interpretation: This verse illustrates that the true measure of any deed lies not in its outward form but in the sincerity and God-consciousness (taqwa) behind it. Even identical actions can have vastly different spiritual values depending on the state of the doer's heart and their genuine devotion to Allah. The rejection of one brother's sacrifice and his subsequent violent reaction also demonstrates how spiritual failure can lead to moral degradation when one responds to divine judgment with pride and envy rather than self-reflection and improvement.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ ابني آدم بالحق إذ قربا قربانا فتقبل من أحدهما ولم يتقبل من الآخر قال لأقتلنك قال إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين

translation: If you stretch out your hand against me to kill me, I shall not stretch out my hand against you to kill you; for I fear Allah, the Lord of the Worlds
interpretation: This verse illustrates the noble principle of non-violent resistance and moral superiority in the face of aggression. The speaker's refusal to reciprocate violence, rooted in their fear and reverence for Allah, demonstrates that true strength lies not in revenge or retaliation, but in maintaining ethical conduct even when confronted with hostility. It suggests that accountability to God should override our basic instincts for self-defense through violence.
orig: لئن بسطت إلي يدك لتقتلني ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك لأقتلك إني أخاف الله رب العالمين

translation: Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin so you will be among the companions of the Fire, and that is the recompense of wrongdoers
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound spiritual consequence of harboring ill intentions towards others, as the speaker wishes their victim to bear both their sins, reflecting how negative actions can lead to a cycle of spiritual destruction where both the aggressor and victim may be condemned if they succumb to hatred and vengeance
orig: إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك فتكون من أصحاب النار وذلك جزاء الظالمين

translation: Then his soul prompted him to kill his brother, so he killed him and became among the losers
interpretation: This verse illustrates how unchecked jealousy and negative emotions can corrupt one's inner self (nafs) to the point where it makes evil actions appear acceptable. When we allow our base desires to overcome our moral judgment, we ultimately harm ourselves more than others, leading to a profound spiritual and moral loss that extends beyond the immediate consequences of our actions.
orig: فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه فقتله فأصبح من الخاسرين

translation: Then Allah sent a crow searching in the ground to show him how to hide the disgrace of his brother. He said, "O woe to me! Have I failed to be like this crow and hide the disgrace of my brother?" And he became of the regretful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how divine guidance can come through natural phenomena, as demonstrated in the story of Cain and Abel. When Cain killed Abel, he didn't know what to do with the body until Allah sent a crow to teach him through example. The verse reveals humanity's capacity to learn from nature and Allah's signs, while also highlighting the profound weight of remorse that follows wrongdoing. It shows that even basic knowledge like burial may not be innate to humans, and we must remain humble and open to learning from all of Allah's creation.
orig: فبعث الله غرابا يبحث في الأرض ليريه كيف يواري سوءة أخيه قال يا ويلتا أعجزت أن أكون مثل هذا الغراب فأواري سوءة أخي فأصبح من النادمين

translation: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves one - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And Our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, after that, throughout the land, were transgressors.
interpretation: This verse establishes the paramount sanctity of human life in Islamic ethics, equating the murder of one innocent person with the murder of all humanity, and conversely, the saving of one life with saving all of humanity. The principle transcends religious and ethnic boundaries, demonstrating that the value of human life is universal and absolute. It also shows how a single moral action can have far-reaching spiritual implications that affect the entire human community.
orig: من أجل ذلك كتبنا على بني إسرائيل أنه من قتل نفسا بغير نفس أو فساد في الأرض فكأنما قتل الناس جميعا ومن أحياها فكأنما أحيا الناس جميعا ولقد جاءتهم رسلنا بالبينات ثم إن كثيرا منهم بعد ذلك في الأرض لمسرفون

translation: Indeed, the penalty for those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth [to cause] corruption is none but that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment
interpretation: This verse establishes the Islamic legal framework for dealing with those who actively engage in terrorism, banditry, or severe criminal activities that threaten societal peace and security. The severity of punishments reflects the gravity of crimes that destabilize community safety and public order. The mention of multiple punishment options suggests that the penalty should be proportional to the severity of the crime, allowing judicial discretion based on circumstances. The verse emphasizes that such actions are not just worldly crimes but violations against divine order, hence carrying both worldly and spiritual consequences.
orig: إنما جزاء الذين يحاربون الله ورسوله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا أن يقتلوا أو يصلبوا أو تقطع أيديهم وأرجلهم من خلاف أو ينفوا من الأرض ذلك لهم خزي في الدنيا ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: Except for those who repent before you overpower them. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's boundless mercy by offering a path to redemption for those who sincerely repent before being caught or apprehended for their wrongdoings. It teaches that genuine repentance, when done voluntarily before facing consequences, demonstrates true remorse and earns divine forgiveness. The mention of Allah's attributes as Forgiving and Merciful reinforces that His desire to pardon supersedes His desire to punish.
orig: إلا الذين تابوا من قبل أن تقدروا عليهم فاعلموا أن الله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who believe! Fear Allah and seek the means to approach Him and strive in His cause, so that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the three essential components of spiritual elevation: maintaining consciousness of Allah through piety, actively seeking ways to become closer to Him through good deeds and worship, and dedicating oneself to the struggle for His cause. The combination of these elements creates a comprehensive path to achieving true success in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وابتغوا إليه الوسيلة وجاهدوا في سبيله لعلكم تفلحون

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve - if they possessed all that is in the earth and the like of it with it to ransom themselves from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: The verse illustrates the absolute worthlessness of material wealth in the face of divine judgment. No matter how vast one's worldly possessions might be, they cannot serve as a substitute for true faith and righteous deeds. This emphasizes that salvation and success in the afterlife cannot be bought or negotiated, but must be earned through sincere belief and good actions during one's lifetime.
orig: إن الذين كفروا لو أن لهم ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه ليفتدوا به من عذاب يوم القيامة ما تقبل منهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: They will wish to get out of the Fire, but they will not get out of it. And for them will be a permanent punishment.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the eternal nature of divine justice in the afterlife, emphasizing that once judgment is passed, there's no possibility of escape or redemption. Those who have earned their place in the Fire through their deeds and choices in worldly life will face the permanence of their situation, highlighting the gravity and finality of our earthly decisions and their consequences.
orig: يريدون أن يخرجوا من النار وما هم بخارجين منها ولهم عذاب مقيم

translation: As for the thief, both male and female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they have earned, a punishment from Allah. And Allah is All-Mighty, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes a strong deterrent against theft in society, emphasizing that the protection of property rights is fundamental to social stability. The severity of the punishment reflects the seriousness with which Islam views violations of people's property, while also serving as a powerful preventive measure. However, historical implementation shows this punishment was applied with strict conditions and numerous prerequisites, including proof that the theft wasn't motivated by poverty or necessity.
orig: والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما جزاء بما كسبا نكالا من الله والله عزيز حكيم

translation: But whoever repents after their wrongdoing and reforms, then Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite mercy and the transformative power of sincere repentance. It teaches that no matter how grave one's sins may be, the door to divine forgiveness remains open through genuine remorse and behavioral reformation. The phrase "and reforms" is particularly significant as it indicates that true repentance isn't merely verbal but must be accompanied by concrete changes in one's actions and character.
orig: فمن تاب من بعد ظلمه وأصلح فإن الله يتوب عليه إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and Allah has power over all things
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah, highlighting that His authority transcends both physical and spiritual realms. It underscores the divine balance between justice and mercy, where Allah's decisions to punish or forgive are based on His perfect wisdom and knowledge. The mention of His power over all things reminds us that human beings, despite their perceived autonomy, are ultimately subject to divine authority and judgment.
orig: ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض يعذب من يشاء ويغفر لمن يشاء والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: O Messenger! Let not those grieve you who hasten to disbelief among those who say, "We believe" with their mouths, but their hearts believe not, and among the Jews. They are listeners of falsehood and listeners for other people who have not come to you. They distort words beyond their contexts and say, "If you are given this, take it; but if you are not given it, then beware." And whoever Allah wants to put in trial - never will you have from Allah any power to help him. Those are the ones for whom Allah does not intend to purify their hearts. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse reveals the psychological warfare and deception faced by the early Muslim community, particularly addressing the Prophet's emotional response to hypocrites and opponents. It highlights how some people's declarations of faith were merely superficial, while their hearts harbored disbelief. The verse particularly warns against those who would manipulate religious teachings for their own ends, distorting words and creating selective interpretations to suit their purposes. It emphasizes that true guidance and purification of hearts come only from Allah, and those who persist in such deception are destined for both worldly shame and divine punishment.
orig: يا أيها الرسول لا يحزنك الذين يسارعون في الكفر من الذين قالوا آمنا بأفواههم ولم تؤمن قلوبهم ومن الذين هادوا سماعون للكذب سماعون لقوم آخرين لم يأتوك يحرفون الكلم من بعد مواضعه يقولون إن أوتيتم هذا فخذوه وإن لم تؤتوه فاحذروا ومن يرد الله فتنته فلن تملك له من الله شيئا أولئك الذين لم يرد الله أن يطهر قلوبهم لهم في الدنيا خزي ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم

translation: They are eager listeners to falsehood, devourers of forbidden things. So if they come to you, either judge between them or turn away from them. If you turn away from them, they cannot harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ethical responsibility of those in positions of authority when dealing with people of questionable character. It teaches that even when faced with those who readily accept lies and engage in corruption, a leader must maintain moral integrity. The option to either engage or disengage is given, but if one chooses to engage, absolute fairness is mandatory. The verse reassures that choosing not to engage with such people carries no negative consequences, while emphasizing that justice must be the foundation of any judgment, regardless of the character of those being judged.
orig: سماعون للكذب أكالون للسحت فإن جاءوك فاحكم بينهم أو أعرض عنهم وإن تعرض عنهم فلن يضروك شيئا وإن حكمت فاحكم بينهم بالقسط إن الله يحب المقسطين

translation: But how do they come to you for judgment while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah? Then they turn away after that, and they are not believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who seek judgment from sources other than what they already possess in divine scripture. It specifically criticizes certain Jewish groups who, despite having Allah's laws clearly stated in their own scripture (Torah), would seek alternative judgments that might better suit their desires. This action demonstrates a lack of true faith, as genuine believers would adhere to divine law rather than shopping around for more convenient rulings.
orig: وكيف يحكمونك وعندهم التوراة فيها حكم الله ثم يتولون من بعد ذلك وما أولئك بالمؤمنين

translation: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to Allah] judged by it for the Jews, as did the rabbis and scholars by that with which they were entrusted of Allah's Scripture and of which they were witnesses. So do not fear the people but fear Me, and do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine continuity in religious guidance, showing how Allah's message has been consistent throughout different prophetic traditions. It particularly highlights the responsibility of religious leaders to maintain the integrity of divine law without compromising it for worldly gains or social pressure. The mention of "small price" suggests that spiritual and moral principles should never be sacrificed for material benefits, while the command to fear Allah rather than people points to the importance of moral courage in upholding divine truth.
orig: إنا أنزلنا التوراة فيها هدى ونور يحكم بها النبيون الذين أسلموا للذين هادوا والربانيون والأحبار بما استحفظوا من كتاب الله وكانوا عليه شهداء فلا تخشوا الناس واخشون ولا تشتروا بآياتي ثمنا قليلا ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الكافرون

translation: And We prescribed for them therein: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds is legal retribution. But whoever gives up his right as charity, it is an expiation for him. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of proportional justice in Islamic law, emphasizing that the punishment should match the crime. However, it also introduces a higher moral principle by encouraging forgiveness and mercy, suggesting that when someone forgives rather than seeking retribution, this act of mercy serves as a spiritual purification for the forgiver. This dual approach balances justice with compassion, allowing for both legal rights and moral elevation.
orig: وكتبنا عليهم فيها أن النفس بالنفس والعين بالعين والأنف بالأنف والأذن بالأذن والسن بالسن والجروح قصاص فمن تصدق به فهو كفارة له ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: And We sent, following in their footsteps, Jesus son of Mary, confirming the Torah that came before him. And We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light, confirming the Torah that came before it and as guidance and admonition for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine revelation and the interconnectedness of God's messages, showing that Islam recognizes Jesus as a legitimate messenger who was sent to build upon, not replace, previous divine teachings. The mention of the Gospel containing "light and guidance" suggests that each divine scripture serves both to illuminate spiritual truths and provide practical guidance, while being tailored to its specific time and audience.
orig: وقفينا على آثارهم بعيسى ابن مريم مصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وآتيناه الإنجيل فيه هدى ونور ومصدقا لما بين يديه من التوراة وهدى وموعظة للمتقين

translation: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine mandate that followers of previous scriptures must adhere to the laws and guidance revealed within their own books during their time. It suggests that religious authority must be based on divine revelation rather than human preferences or innovations, and those who knowingly deviate from God's revealed laws are considered transgressors against divine order.
orig: وليحكم أهل الإنجيل بما أنزل الله فيه ومن لم يحكم بما أنزل الله فأولئك هم الفاسقون

translation: And We have revealed to you the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations away from what has come to you of the truth. To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. Had Allah willed, He would have made you one community, but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you; so race to [all that is] good. To Allah is your return all together, and He will [then] inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom in allowing religious diversity while maintaining the unity of core spiritual truth. It suggests that while different communities have been given different laws and methods of worship, this variation is intentional and serves as a test from Allah. Rather than focusing on differences, people should channel their energies into competing in good deeds and righteous actions. The ultimate resolution of theological and legal differences will come from Allah himself, highlighting the importance of maintaining mutual respect and focusing on virtue rather than arguing about differences in religious practices.
orig: وأنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه من الكتاب ومهيمنا عليه فاحكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم عما جاءك من الحق لكل جعلنا منكم شرعة ومنهاجا ولو شاء الله لجعلكم أمة واحدة ولكن ليبلوكم في ما آتاكم فاستبقوا الخيرات إلى الله مرجعكم جميعا فينبئكم بما كنتم فيه تختلفون

translation: And judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their desires, and beware that they do not tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. And if they turn away, then know that Allah only intends to afflict them with some of their sins. And indeed, many among the people are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the critical importance of maintaining judicial integrity and religious authenticity in the face of social pressure. It warns religious and judicial authorities about the constant challenge of being swayed by popular opinion or powerful interests rather than adhering to divine principles. The verse suggests that when people reject divine guidance, their rejection itself becomes a form of self-inflicted punishment, as they deprive themselves of the protection and wisdom inherent in divine law.
orig: وأن احكم بينهم بما أنزل الله ولا تتبع أهواءهم واحذرهم أن يفتنوك عن بعض ما أنزل الله إليك فإن تولوا فاعلم أنما يريد الله أن يصيبهم ببعض ذنوبهم وإن كثيرا من الناس لفاسقون

translation: Do they then seek the judgment of (the days of) ignorance? And who is better in judgment than Allah for a people who have firm faith?
interpretation: This verse critiques those who prefer human-made laws and customs over divine guidance, suggesting that seeking alternatives to Allah's perfect system of justice reflects a regression to pre-Islamic ignorance. It emphasizes that divine law, being rooted in perfect wisdom and knowledge, is inherently superior to any human-devised system for those who truly understand and believe.
orig: أفحكم الجاهلية يبغون ومن أحسن من الله حكما لقوم يوقنون

translation: O you who believe! Do not take the Jews and Christians as allies - they are allies only to one another. And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed, he is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes maintaining the distinct identity of the Muslim community while establishing clear boundaries in political and strategic alliances. It doesn't prohibit normal social interactions or kindness to non-Muslims, but rather warns against compromising Islamic principles and interests through alliances that might undermine the Muslim community's autonomy and religious integrity. The context relates to a specific historical period when some hypocrites were secretly aligning with opponents of the emerging Muslim state for personal gain.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا اليهود والنصارى أولياء بعضهم أولياء بعض ومن يتولهم منكم فإنه منهم إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: So you see those in whose hearts is disease hastening to them, saying, "We fear that a misfortune may strike us." But perhaps Allah will bring victory or a decision from Him, and they will become regretful over what they had concealed within themselves.
interpretation: This verse exposes the behavior of hypocrites who maintain secret alliances with enemies of the faith out of fear and self-preservation, rather than trusting in Allah's promise of victory. Their actions stem from spiritual weakness and lack of true faith, as they prioritize worldly security over divine protection. The verse suggests that their calculated hedging will ultimately lead to regret when Allah's victory manifests, revealing the futility of their duplicitous strategy.
orig: فترى الذين في قلوبهم مرض يسارعون فيهم يقولون نخشى أن تصيبنا دائرة فعسى الله أن يأتي بالفتح أو أمر من عنده فيصبحوا على ما أسروا في أنفسهم نادمين

translation: And those who believe will say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah their strongest oaths that they were with you?" Their deeds have become worthless, and they have become losers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stark contrast between outward declarations and inner reality, highlighting how hypocrites who made emphatic oaths of loyalty to the believers will ultimately be exposed. Their false pretenses and deceptive behavior lead to the nullification of their deeds, teaching us that sincerity and truthfulness are essential components of faith, while mere verbal assertions without genuine commitment result in spiritual bankruptcy.
orig: ويقول الذين آمنوا أهؤلاء الذين أقسموا بالله جهد أيمانهم إنهم لمعكم حبطت أعمالهم فأصبحوا خاسرين

translation: O you who believe! Whoever among you turns back from his religion, Allah will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble towards the believers, stern towards the disbelievers, striving in the way of Allah, and not fearing the blame of any blamer. That is the favor of Allah; He bestows it upon whom He wills. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse conveys a powerful message about divine succession and unwavering faith. It indicates that Allah's truth will always prevail, even if some people abandon their faith, as He will raise others who embody the perfect balance of spiritual love and practical strength. These special people possess unique qualities: they combine humility towards fellow believers with firmness against opposition, demonstrate courage in defending truth, and remain steadfast in their principles regardless of criticism. Their love for Allah transcends worldly concerns, showing that true faith manifests in both emotional devotion and practical action.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا من يرتد منكم عن دينه فسوف يأتي الله بقوم يحبهم ويحبونه أذلة على المؤمنين أعزة على الكافرين يجاهدون في سبيل الله ولا يخافون لومة لائم ذلك فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء والله واسع عليم

translation: Your ally is none but Allah and His Messenger and those who believe - those who establish prayer and give zakah while they bow [in worship]
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the true nature of spiritual and social leadership in Islam, highlighting that genuine authority and guidance come from three interconnected sources: Allah's divine sovereignty, the Prophet's exemplary leadership, and the sincere believers who maintain their religious duties even in their most humble states. The mention of giving charity while in prayer suggests that true believers maintain their consciousness of social responsibility even in their most intimate moments of worship.
orig: إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة وهم راكعون

translation: And whoever takes Allah and His Messenger and those who believe as allies - then indeed, the party of Allah will be the predominant
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true success and victory ultimately belong to those who align themselves sincerely with divine guidance and the community of believers. The concept of "hizb Allah" (party of Allah) represents a spiritual and ideological alliance rather than mere political affiliation, suggesting that those who maintain loyalty to divine principles and authentic faith will prevail over opposing forces, whether in this life or the hereafter.
orig: ومن يتول الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون

translation: O you who believe! Do not take as allies those who make a mockery and fun of your religion from among those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers. And fear Allah if you are truly believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining strong religious boundaries and protecting one's faith from those who might undermine it through ridicule. It warns believers against forming close alliances with people who mock Islamic beliefs, as such relationships could weaken one's faith and compromise religious integrity. The verse suggests that true faith requires discernment in choosing one's close associates, particularly when others show disrespect towards sacred beliefs.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا الذين اتخذوا دينكم هزوا ولعبا من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم والكفار أولياء واتقوا الله إن كنتم مؤمنين

translation: And when you call to prayer, they take it in mockery and amusement; that is because they are a people who do not understand
interpretation: This verse illustrates how spiritual blindness leads to arrogance and disrespect of sacred matters. Those who mock prayer fail to grasp its profound significance because their hearts are closed to spiritual understanding, not because the truth isn't evident. Their mockery is a reflection of their intellectual and spiritual immaturity rather than any fault in the prayer itself.
orig: وإذا ناديتم إلى الصلاة اتخذوها هزوا ولعبا ذلك بأنهم قوم لا يعقلون

translation: Say, "O People of the Book! Do you resent us only because we believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and because most of you are defiantly disobedient?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the irrationality of religious prejudice, pointing out that the only "crime" of the Muslims in the eyes of some People of the Book was their acceptance of divine truth and adherence to God's message. It suggests that their resentment stems not from any legitimate grievance but from their own deviation from righteous behavior and their unwillingness to accept that truth can exist beyond their immediate circle.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب هل تنقمون منا إلا أن آمنا بالله وما أنزل إلينا وما أنزل من قبل وأن أكثركم فاسقون

translation: Say, "Shall I inform you of those who will have a worse reward from Allah? Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry, and He made some of them into apes and pigs, and those who worshipped false deities. These are worse in position and further astray from the right path."
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine justice and the severe consequences of persistent disobedience and rejection of truth. It specifically references historical incidents where some communities were transformed as punishment for their defiance, serving as a powerful warning about the gravity of opposing divine guidance and choosing to worship false deities. The transformation mentioned isn't merely physical but represents a degradation of human dignity and spiritual status, highlighting how deviation from divine guidance can reduce humans to a bestial state of existence.
orig: قل هل أنبئكم بشر من ذلك مثوبة عند الله من لعنه الله وغضب عليه وجعل منهم القردة والخنازير وعبد الطاغوت أولئك شر مكانا وأضل عن سواء السبيل

translation: And when they come to you, they say, "We believe," but they have entered with disbelief, and they have certainly left with it. And Allah is most knowing of what they conceal.
interpretation: This verse exposes the nature of hypocrites who present a false facade of faith while harboring disbelief in their hearts. It highlights how their outward declarations of belief are meaningless since they enter and leave the presence of believers with their inner rejection of faith intact. The verse emphasizes Allah's complete knowledge of their hidden intentions, suggesting that no amount of deception can hide one's true beliefs from divine awareness.
orig: وإذا جاءوكم قالوا آمنا وقد دخلوا بالكفر وهم قد خرجوا به والله أعلم بما كانوا يكتمون

translation: And you see many of them hastening into sin and aggression and consuming what is unlawful. How wretched is what they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral corruption that can spread within communities when people abandon their principles. The emphasis on "hastening" suggests an eagerness to engage in wrongdoing, rather than merely falling into it through weakness. The consumption of unlawful gains ("suht") specifically points to the way moral corruption often manifests through economic exploitation and illegal financial practices, indicating how ethical and economic misconduct are deeply interconnected.
orig: وترى كثيرا منهم يسارعون في الإثم والعدوان وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Why do not the rabbis and religious scholars forbid them from saying what is sinful and devouring what is unlawful? How wretched is what they have been practicing.
interpretation: The verse critiques religious leadership's failure to fulfill their moral duty as guardians of faith and ethics. When religious authorities remain silent in the face of wrongdoing, they become complicit in society's moral decay. True religious leadership requires active opposition to sinful speech and unlawful gains, not passive acceptance of community wrongdoing.
orig: لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار عن قولهم الإثم وأكلهم السحت لبئس ما كانوا يصنعون

translation: And the Jews say, "Allah's hand is chained." Chained are their hands, and cursed are they for what they say. Rather, both His hands are extended; He spends however He wills. And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. And We have cast among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. Every time they kindled the fire of war, Allah extinguished it. And they strive throughout the land [causing] corruption, and Allah does not like corrupters.
interpretation: This verse reveals the deep spiritual arrogance of those who attempt to limit God's power and generosity. By claiming God's hand is "chained," they essentially accuse Him of being miserly or powerless. The divine response demonstrates that God's generosity is unlimited, flowing continuously through His creation. The consequence of such blasphemy is a self-fulfilling curse - their own spiritual limitations become their chains, and their communities become fractured by internal conflicts. The metaphor of extinguishing the fire of war shows God's ultimate control over human schemes, while highlighting how those who reject divine guidance often become agents of corruption despite their own plans.
orig: وقالت اليهود يد الله مغلولة غلت أيديهم ولعنوا بما قالوا بل يداه مبسوطتان ينفق كيف يشاء وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا وألقينا بينهم العداوة والبغضاء إلى يوم القيامة كلما أوقدوا نارا للحرب أطفأها الله ويسعون في الأرض فسادا والله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: And if only the People of the Book had believed and feared Allah, We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Pleasure
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's boundless mercy and highlights that divine guidance isn't exclusive to one group. It suggests that spiritual elevation and salvation are attainable through sincere faith and God-consciousness, regardless of one's previous religious background. The verse implies that the path to redemption remains open for the People of the Book (Jews and Christians), demonstrating that Allah's forgiveness and rewards are accessible to all who choose to embrace true faith and live righteously.
orig: ولو أن أهل الكتاب آمنوا واتقوا لكفرنا عنهم سيئاتهم ولأدخلناهم جنات النعيم

translation: And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have consumed [provision] from above them and from beneath their feet. Among them is a moderate community, but many of them - evil is what they do
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the direct relationship between spiritual righteousness and material prosperity. It suggests that if the People of the Book had truly followed their scriptures faithfully, including both the original Torah and Gospel, they would have experienced abundance in their sustenance from all directions. The "eating from above and below" metaphorically represents complete provision and prosperity. The verse acknowledges that while some maintain a balanced and moderate approach to faith, many have deviated from the true teachings, resulting in their own spiritual and material deprivation.
orig: ولو أنهم أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليهم من ربهم لأكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم منهم أمة مقتصدة وكثير منهم ساء ما يعملون

translation: O Messenger! Convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord. If you do not, then you have not delivered His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the critical responsibility of Prophet Muhammad to deliver Allah's message without fear or hesitation. The divine assurance of protection reflects Allah's commitment to safeguarding His messenger during the mission of spreading Islam, suggesting that the success of the message is divinely guaranteed despite opposition. It demonstrates that conveying truth requires courage, and those entrusted with divine guidance must fulfill their duty regardless of potential consequences.
orig: يا أيها الرسول بلغ ما أنزل إليك من ربك وإن لم تفعل فما بلغت رسالته والله يعصمك من الناس إن الله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: Say, "O People of the Book! You have no ground to stand upon unless you uphold the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to you from your Lord." And what has been revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve for the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of authentic religious practice, pointing out that merely claiming adherence to a faith tradition is insufficient. True religious legitimacy comes from faithfully implementing divine guidance in its entirety, not selectively following parts while ignoring others. The verse also acknowledges that increased revelation can paradoxically harden the hearts of those who are predisposed to reject truth, serving as a reminder that a prophet's duty is only to convey the message, not to ensure its acceptance.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لستم على شيء حتى تقيموا التوراة والإنجيل وما أنزل إليكم من ربكم وليزيدن كثيرا منهم ما أنزل إليك من ربك طغيانا وكفرا فلا تأس على القوم الكافرين

translation: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabeans and the Christians - whoever believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteousness - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes God's universal mercy and justice, indicating that salvation is not exclusive to any one religious group but is based on three fundamental criteria: sincere faith in God, belief in accountability in the afterlife, and performing good deeds. The verse suggests that what matters most is not the religious label one carries, but rather the authenticity of one's faith and the righteousness of one's actions.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئون والنصارى من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وعمل صالحا فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: We took the covenant of the Children of Israel and sent them messengers. Whenever there came to them a messenger with what their souls did not desire, some they denied and some they killed.
interpretation: This verse reveals a pattern of spiritual resistance among the Children of Israel, highlighting how human beings often reject divine guidance when it challenges their established beliefs or desires. The repeated rejection and violence against messengers demonstrates how deeply entrenched personal interests and ego can become barriers to accepting truth, even when it comes from divine sources. It serves as a warning about the dangers of allowing personal desires to override divine guidance.
orig: لقد أخذنا ميثاق بني إسرائيل وأرسلنا إليهم رسلا كلما جاءهم رسول بما لا تهوى أنفسهم فريقا كذبوا وفريقا يقتلون

translation: And they thought there would be no trial, so they became blind and deaf. Then Allah turned to them in forgiveness, but many of them became blind and deaf again. And Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the cyclical nature of human spiritual weakness and divine mercy. When people become complacent in their faith, they lose their spiritual perception - becoming metaphorically blind and deaf to divine guidance. Even after Allah's mercy grants them awareness, many return to their state of spiritual blindness, highlighting humanity's tendency to take divine blessings for granted and revert to heedlessness despite experiencing Allah's forgiveness.
orig: وحسبوا ألا تكون فتنة فعموا وصموا ثم تاب الله عليهم ثم عموا وصموا كثير منهم والله بصير بما يعملون

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary" while the Messiah has said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." Indeed, he who associates others with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of pure monotheism by addressing a critical theological misconception. It explains that equating Jesus with God contradicts Jesus's own teachings, as he himself called people to worship the one true God. The verse illustrates that Jesus was a messenger who acknowledged his servitude to Allah, not a divine being. It also warns about the severe consequences of associating partners with God (shirk), highlighting that such beliefs can lead to eternal separation from divine mercy.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم وقال المسيح يا بني إسرائيل اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم إنه من يشرك بالله فقد حرم الله عليه الجنة ومأواه النار وما للظالمين من أنصار

translation: They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Allah is the third of three," while there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they are saying, there will surely afflict the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse directly addresses the Christian doctrine of the Trinity, emphasizing that any concept of God that divides His nature into parts or suggests multiple divine beings is fundamentally incompatible with pure monotheism. The warning at the end suggests that holding onto such beliefs despite clear evidence of God's unity represents a conscious rejection of truth rather than mere ignorance.
orig: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله ثالث ثلاثة وما من إله إلا إله واحد وإن لم ينتهوا عما يقولون ليمسن الذين كفروا منهم عذاب أليم

translation: Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's perpetual readiness to forgive, suggesting that despite one's sins or mistakes, the door to divine mercy remains open. The questioning format implies gentle admonishment, indicating that refusing to seek forgiveness is illogical when dealing with such a merciful Creator. It's a reminder that pride or stubbornness shouldn't prevent one from turning back to Allah, as His attributes of forgiveness and mercy are constant and unlimited.
orig: أفلا يتوبون إلى الله ويستغفرونه والله غفور رحيم

translation: The Messiah, son of Mary, was not but a messenger; [other] messengers have passed on before him. And his mother was a supporter of truth. They both used to eat food. Look how We make clear to them the signs; then look how they are deluded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the human nature of Jesus and Mary, countering claims of their divinity. By mentioning their need for food, it highlights their mortal essence, as divine beings wouldn't require sustenance. The verse positions Jesus as one in a line of messengers, neither the first nor unique in his role, while acknowledging Mary's truthfulness and devotion. It serves as a rational argument against deification, inviting people to reflect on how they've strayed from this clear truth.
orig: ما المسيح ابن مريم إلا رسول قد خلت من قبله الرسل وأمه صديقة كانا يأكلان الطعام انظر كيف نبين لهم الآيات ثم انظر أنى يؤفكون

translation: Say, "Do you worship besides Allah that which holds no [power of] harm or benefit for you, while it is Allah who is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the futility of polytheism by highlighting the logical inconsistency of worshipping entities that possess no divine power. It emphasizes that true divinity must include the ability to affect one's existence, either positively or negatively. The mention of Allah's attributes as All-Hearing and All-Knowing creates a stark contrast between the powerless idols and the omnipotent, aware Creator, suggesting that rational worship should be directed only to the One who possesses actual power and knowledge.
orig: قل أتعبدون من دون الله ما لا يملك لكم ضرا ولا نفعا والله هو السميع العليم

translation: Say, "O People of the Book! Do not go to extremes in your religion beyond the truth, and do not follow the desires of people who went astray before and led many astray, and strayed from the right way."
interpretation: This verse warns against religious extremism and blind following of misguided predecessors. It emphasizes that truth in religion lies in moderation and balance, not in excessive practices or beliefs. The mention of "people who went astray before" likely refers to those who distorted their scriptures and religious teachings to suit their desires, suggesting that authentic faith requires adherence to divine guidance rather than human innovations or extremist interpretations.
orig: قل يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم غير الحق ولا تتبعوا أهواء قوم قد ضلوا من قبل وأضلوا كثيرا وضلوا عن سواء السبيل

translation: Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and of Jesus, the son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and [habitually] transgressed.
interpretation: This verse highlights a profound spiritual consequence of persistent wrongdoing, showing how divine condemnation came through respected prophets when people consistently chose to reject truth and transgress boundaries. The mention of both David and Jesus demonstrates how this condemnation spans different eras, suggesting that persistent rejection of divine guidance leads to spiritual degradation regardless of the time period.
orig: لعن الذين كفروا من بني إسرائيل على لسان داوود وعيسى ابن مريم ذلك بما عصوا وكانوا يعتدون

translation: They did not forbid one another from the wrongdoing they committed. Evil indeed was what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral decay of a society where people become complacent about sin and wrongdoing, failing to fulfill their collective responsibility to promote good and prevent evil. When members of a community stop advising each other against wrongful actions, they become complicit in the spread of corruption, leading to the deterioration of social and moral values. The verse serves as a warning that silence in the face of evil is itself a form of participation in that evil.
orig: كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون

translation: You see many of them taking the disbelievers as allies. Evil indeed is what their souls have put forth for them - that Allah became angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dangerous consequences of Muslims forming alliances with those who actively oppose Islamic faith. It suggests that choosing worldly relationships or interests over religious principles leads to spiritual corruption and divine displeasure. The emphasis on "what their souls have put forth" indicates that such choices stem from inner moral failings rather than external pressures, making the individual fully accountable for their decision to align with forces that work against their faith.
orig: ترى كثيرا منهم يتولون الذين كفروا لبئس ما قدمت لهم أنفسهم أن سخط الله عليهم وفي العذاب هم خالدون

translation: And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies. But many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the incompatibility between true faith and forming alliances with those who oppose divine guidance. It suggests that genuine belief in Allah and His messenger naturally leads believers to maintain spiritual and social boundaries with those who actively resist divine truth. The verse implies that choosing inappropriate alliances often indicates a weakness or deficiency in one's faith.
orig: ولو كانوا يؤمنون بالله والنبي وما أنزل إليه ما اتخذوهم أولياء ولكن كثيرا منهم فاسقون

translation: You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers [to be] the Jews and those who associate others with Allah; and you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant.
