interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's boundless generosity, showing how He not only forgives His devoted servants but celebrates their devotion by promising them three ascending levels of reward: His mercy which protects them from hardship, His acceptance which validates their efforts, and eternal gardens that represent the ultimate form of bliss where joy never diminishes or ends
orig: يبشرهم ربهم برحمة منه ورضوان وجنات لهم فيها نعيم مقيم

translation: They will abide therein forever. Indeed, with Allah is a great reward
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of divine reward, suggesting that righteous deeds are not compensated with temporary benefits but rather with everlasting bliss. The phrase "great reward" indicates that human beings cannot fully comprehend the magnitude of Allah's rewards, as they transcend worldly measures of value and satisfaction.
orig: خالدين فيها أبدا إن الله عنده أجر عظيم

translation: O you who believe! Take not your fathers and your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief to faith. And whoever among you takes them as allies - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that loyalty to faith supersedes even the strongest family bonds. It teaches that spiritual truth and religious commitment should take precedence over familial relationships when there is a clear conflict between the two. The believer must maintain their religious integrity even if it means creating distance from family members who actively oppose or reject faith, highlighting the paramount importance of one's relationship with Allah over worldly connections.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا آباءكم وإخوانكم أولياء إن استحبوا الكفر على الإيمان ومن يتولهم منكم فأولئك هم الظالمون

translation: Say, "If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, your relatives, wealth you have acquired, commerce you fear may decline, and dwellings you love are more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until Allah brings about His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people."
interpretation: This verse addresses a fundamental test of faith, warning against allowing worldly attachments and material concerns to supersede one's devotion to Allah. It highlights how natural human bonds and material comforts can become spiritual obstacles when they take precedence over religious obligations. The divine warning at the end suggests that choosing worldly priorities over spiritual duties leads to spiritual deprivation and loss of divine guidance.
orig: قل إن كان آباؤكم وأبناؤكم وإخوانكم وأزواجكم وعشيرتكم وأموال اقترفتموها وتجارة تخشون كسادها ومساكن ترضونها أحب إليكم من الله ورسوله وجهاد في سبيله فتربصوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: Allah has already given you victory in many regions and [even] on the day of Hunayn, when your great numbers pleased you, but they did not avail you at all, and the earth was confining for you with its vastness; then you turned back, retreating.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder about the dangers of overconfidence and self-reliance instead of depending on Allah. At the Battle of Hunayn, Muslims initially felt assured by their large numbers, but this pride led to their near defeat. The lesson emphasizes that victory comes only through Allah's help, not through material advantages or numerical superiority, teaching believers to maintain humility and complete trust in Allah rather than worldly strengths.
orig: لقد نصركم الله في مواطن كثيرة ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم فلم تغن عنكم شيئا وضاقت عليكم الأرض بما رحبت ثم وليتم مدبرين

translation: Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down soldiers [angels] whom you did not see and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine intervention in times of crisis, showing that victory comes not just through physical means but through spiritual and unseen support. The mention of "sakinah" (tranquility) suggests that true strength lies in maintaining inner peace and trust in Allah's help, while the reference to unseen soldiers reminds us that Allah's power extends beyond what's visible to human eyes.
orig: ثم أنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين وأنزل جنودا لم تروها وعذب الذين كفروا وذلك جزاء الكافرين

translation: Then Allah accepts repentance after that for whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's supreme authority in accepting repentance while highlighting the delicate balance between divine justice and mercy. It suggests that genuine repentance isn't automatically guaranteed acceptance, but rather lies within Allah's discretion, reminding believers that they should maintain both hope in Allah's mercy and a healthy fear of His judgment. The mention of Allah's attributes as "Forgiving and Merciful" indicates that His inclination is toward forgiveness when sincere repentance is offered.
orig: ثم يتوب الله من بعد ذلك على من يشاء والله غفور رحيم

translation: O you who believe! Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not come near the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs. And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes a spiritual boundary that emphasizes the sanctity of sacred spaces in Islam. The reference to polytheists as "unclean" is not about physical impurity but rather speaks to the spiritual contamination of associating partners with Allah. The prohibition from approaching the Sacred Mosque reflects the importance of preserving the pure monotheistic worship at Islam's holiest site. The verse also addresses the economic concerns that might have arisen from this restriction, as many polytheists were traders who brought business to Mecca, by reassuring believers that Allah's provision comes through His wisdom and is not dependent on compromising religious principles.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إنما المشركون نجس فلا يقربوا المسجد الحرام بعد عامهم هذا وإن خفتم عيلة فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله إن شاء إن الله عليم حكيم

translation: Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture - until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.
interpretation: This verse outlines the historical context of relations between the early Muslim state and non-Muslim communities, particularly the People of the Book. It establishes a framework for coexistence where non-Muslims could live under Muslim protection by paying a tax (jizyah) while maintaining their faith. The verse's mention of "fighting" was specific to those who were actively hostile to the Muslim community, not a general command against all non-believers. The payment of jizyah essentially represented a social contract that guaranteed religious minorities their rights and protection while contributing to the state's expenses.
orig: قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر ولا يحرمون ما حرم الله ورسوله ولا يدينون دين الحق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم صاغرون

translation: And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah", and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their statement from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental Islamic principle of pure monotheism by addressing historical claims of divine sonship. It suggests that attributing a son to Allah represents a form of spiritual confusion that stems from imitating earlier pagan beliefs rather than from divine truth. The verse indicates that such claims are merely verbal assertions without divine foundation, demonstrating how religious beliefs can be influenced by cultural and historical precedents rather than authentic divine revelation.
orig: وقالت اليهود عزير ابن الله وقالت النصارى المسيح ابن الله ذلك قولهم بأفواههم يضاهئون قول الذين كفروا من قبل قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

translation: They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the practice of blindly following religious authorities to the point of treating them as divine figures. It highlights how some people elevate their religious leaders to a status reserved for God alone, following their rulings even when they contradict divine law. The mention of Jesus emphasizes that even great prophets should not be worshipped, as ultimate authority belongs to God alone. It's a powerful statement against religious hierarchy that usurps divine authority and a reminder that true monotheism requires direct submission to God without intermediaries.
orig: اتخذوا أحبارهم ورهبانهم أربابا من دون الله والمسيح ابن مريم وما أمروا إلا ليعبدوا إلها واحدا لا إله إلا هو سبحانه عما يشركون

translation: They want to extinguish Allah's light with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futile attempts of those who oppose divine truth, comparing their efforts to someone trying to blow out the sun's light with their breath. Just as it's impossible to extinguish sunlight by blowing at it, no human effort can suppress or eliminate Allah's guidance and truth. The verse reassures believers that despite opposition and resistance from non-believers, Allah's message will inevitably prevail and spread throughout the world, as this is His divine will.
orig: يريدون أن يطفئوا نور الله بأفواههم ويأبى الله إلا أن يتم نوره ولو كره الكافرون

translation: It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, even if the polytheists detest it
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's divine plan for Islam's ultimate triumph over all other belief systems and ideologies. The "manifestation" refers not necessarily to forced conversion, but to the clear demonstration of Islam's truth and superiority through its principles, values, and logical foundations. The mention of polytheists' resentment indicates that truth often faces opposition, but divine will prevails regardless of human resistance.
orig: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون

translation: O you who believe! Indeed, many of the rabbis and monks devour people's wealth unjustly and prevent [people] from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against religious leaders who exploit their positions for material gain and emphasizes that true faith requires responsible stewardship of wealth. It criticizes both corrupt religious authority and excessive materialism, suggesting that spiritual leadership should be focused on guiding people to truth rather than accumulating wealth, while wealth itself should be circulated for societal benefit rather than hoarded. The divine warning indicates that using religious authority for personal enrichment and failing to use wealth for charitable purposes are serious spiritual transgressions.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن كثيرا من الأحبار والرهبان ليأكلون أموال الناس بالباطل ويصدون عن سبيل الله والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله فبشرهم بعذاب أليم

translation: The Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell and their foreheads, their flanks, and their backs will be branded therewith [and it will be said], "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the severe consequences of hoarding wealth without fulfilling its charitable obligations. The physical punishment described, where the hoarded wealth becomes an instrument of torment, serves as a powerful metaphor for how our worldly attachments and greed can become sources of our ultimate suffering. It emphasizes that wealth is a trust from Allah that should be used for the benefit of society rather than accumulated selfishly.
orig: يوم يحمى عليها في نار جهنم فتكوى بها جباههم وجنوبهم وظهورهم هذا ما كنزتم لأنفسكم فذوقوا ما كنتم تكنزون

translation: Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve [lunar] months in the register of Allah [from] the day He created the heavens and the earth; of these, four are sacred. That is the correct religion, so do not wrong yourselves during them. And fight against the disbelievers collectively as they fight against you collectively. And know that Allah is with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine organization of time based on a twelve-month lunar calendar, emphasizing Allah's cosmic authority by connecting it to the very creation of the universe. The designation of four sacred months reflects Allah's establishment of special periods for spiritual reflection and peace, warning against transgression during these times. The verse also illustrates the balance between peaceful observance and necessary self-defense, indicating that while peace is preferred, Muslims are permitted to defend themselves against collective aggression, with the assurance of divine support for those who maintain righteousness.
orig: إن عدة الشهور عند الله اثنا عشر شهرا في كتاب الله يوم خلق السماوات والأرض منها أربعة حرم ذلك الدين القيم فلا تظلموا فيهن أنفسكم وقاتلوا المشركين كافة كما يقاتلونكم كافة واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: Indeed, the postponement [of sacred months] is an increase in disbelief by which those who disbelieve are led astray. They make it lawful one year and unlawful another year to correspond to the number made unlawful by Allah and [thus] make lawful what Allah has made unlawful. Made pleasing to them is the evil of their deeds, and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the pre-Islamic Arab practice of manipulating the sacred months for political and economic advantage. The deeper spiritual message warns against the human tendency to alter divine laws for convenience or worldly benefit. When people start adjusting religious principles to suit their desires rather than conforming to God's established order, it represents a form of spiritual corruption that leads to further deviation from divine guidance.
orig: إنما النسيء زيادة في الكفر يضل به الذين كفروا يحلونه عاما ويحرمونه عاما ليواطئوا عدة ما حرم الله فيحلوا ما حرم الله زين لهم سوء أعمالهم والله لا يهدي القوم الكافرين

translation: O you who believe! What is the matter with you that when you are asked to march forth in the cause of Allah, you cling heavily to the earth? Are you content with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? But little is the enjoyment of the life of this world compared to the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse addresses a deep spiritual ailment: the attachment to worldly comforts that prevents believers from making sacrifices for their faith. It highlights how humans often become so engrossed in their immediate material existence that they forget their ultimate purpose. The metaphor of "clinging heavily to the earth" powerfully illustrates how worldly attachments can weigh down our spiritual aspirations, making us hesitant to answer the call of faith when it requires personal sacrifice. The verse serves as a wake-up call to reassess our priorities and remember that all worldly pleasures are temporary and insignificant compared to the eternal rewards of the hereafter.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا ما لكم إذا قيل لكم انفروا في سبيل الله اثاقلتم إلى الأرض أرضيتم بالحياة الدنيا من الآخرة فما متاع الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا قليل

translation: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine principle of replaceability and human accountability. It suggests that Allah's plan will proceed regardless of individual participation, highlighting that no one is indispensable in His grand scheme. Those who refuse to fulfill their duties and responsibilities in supporting truth and justice will face consequences, while Allah can easily raise others who are more dedicated and sincere to carry out His mission.
orig: إلا تنفروا يعذبكم عذابا أليما ويستبدل قوما غيركم ولا تضروه شيئا والله على كل شيء قدير

translation: If you do not aid him [Prophet Muhammad] - Allah has already aided him when those who disbelieved had driven him out [of Makkah] as one of two, when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." And Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with soldiers you did not see and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah - that is the highest. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound concept of divine protection and trust in Allah's plan, specifically through the historical event of the Prophet's migration (Hijra). It demonstrates that even in moments of extreme vulnerability, when one appears to have no worldly support, Allah's help is sufficient. The cave incident with Abu Bakr shows that true strength lies not in numbers or material resources, but in divine accompaniment. The "unseen soldiers" mentioned symbolize that Allah's support manifests in ways beyond human perception, and ultimate victory belongs to truth over falsehood, regardless of apparent circumstances.
orig: إلا تنصروه فقد نصره الله إذ أخرجه الذين كفروا ثاني اثنين إذ هما في الغار إذ يقول لصاحبه لا تحزن إن الله معنا فأنزل الله سكينته عليه وأيده بجنود لم تروها وجعل كلمة الذين كفروا السفلى وكلمة الله هي العليا والله عزيز حكيم

translation: Go forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of Allah. That is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the call to defend faith and community transcends personal comfort or circumstances. Whether one finds it easy or difficult, is young or old, rich or poor, healthy or sick, the obligation to contribute to the greater good remains. It teaches that true commitment requires sacrificing both material resources and personal effort, suggesting that authentic faith manifests in tangible actions rather than mere verbal declarations.
orig: انفروا خفافا وثقالا وجاهدوا بأموالكم وأنفسكم في سبيل الله ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: Had it been a near gain and a short journey, they would have followed you, but the distance seemed too far for them. They will swear by Allah, "If we had been able, we would have gone out with you." They destroy themselves, and Allah knows that they are liars.
interpretation: This verse reveals the psychology of hypocrisy and false excuses, showing how people who lack true faith will readily find reasons to avoid difficult obligations. The mention of "near gain" suggests that such individuals are motivated primarily by immediate worldly benefits rather than spiritual rewards. Their willingness to take false oaths demonstrates how moral corruption leads to increasingly serious spiritual transgressions, as they compound their initial reluctance with dishonesty before Allah.
orig: لو كان عرضا قريبا وسفرا قاصدا لاتبعوك ولكن بعدت عليهم الشقة وسيحلفون بالله لو استطعنا لخرجنا معكم يهلكون أنفسهم والله يعلم إنهم لكاذبون

translation: May Allah pardon you. Why did you grant them permission [to remain behind] until it was evident to you who were truthful and until you knew who were the liars?
interpretation: This verse reflects Allah's gentle reproach to Prophet Muhammad, highlighting the divine wisdom in testing believers' sincerity. It suggests that sometimes immediate acceptance of excuses, though stemming from mercy, may prevent us from discerning truth from falsehood. The lesson is that leadership requires careful discernment and that premature leniency might interfere with the natural process of revealing people's true characters.
orig: عفا الله عنك لم أذنت لهم حتى يتبين لك الذين صدقوا وتعلم الكاذبين

translation: Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission to strive with their wealth and their lives. And Allah is Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: True believers demonstrate their sincerity through their eagerness to participate in righteous causes without hesitation or seeking excuses. Their immediate readiness to sacrifice both their wealth and lives reflects their deep conviction and unwavering faith, as they understand that their ultimate accountability is to Allah. This verse highlights how genuine faith manifests in proactive commitment rather than reluctance or the need for persuasion.
orig: لا يستأذنك الذين يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر أن يجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم والله عليم بالمتقين

translation: Only those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day and whose hearts are in doubt ask your permission. So in their doubt they waver.
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound psychological insight into the nature of hesitation and uncertainty in matters of faith. Those who seek constant permission or exemptions from religious duties often do so because of their underlying lack of conviction. Their wavering isn't merely about specific actions but reflects a deeper spiritual uncertainty. True believers, by contrast, typically show more decisiveness in their commitment because their hearts are firm in faith.
orig: إنما يستأذنك الذين لا يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر وارتابت قلوبهم فهم في ريبهم يترددون

translation: And if they had intended to go forth, they would have prepared for it preparations. But Allah disliked their being sent, so He kept them back, and it was said, "Remain with those who remain."
interpretation: This verse reveals a divine psychological insight: true intentions manifest in concrete actions. When someone genuinely wants to accomplish something, they make tangible preparations. The absence of preparation often indicates a lack of sincere intention, which Allah already knows. Sometimes, divine wisdom prevents people from participating in certain endeavors because their presence would be detrimental to the collective good, even if they don't realize it themselves.
orig: ولو أرادوا الخروج لأعدوا له عدة ولكن كره الله انبعاثهم فثبطهم وقيل اقعدوا مع القاعدين

translation: Had they gone forth with you, they would have added to you nothing except confusion, and they would have been active among you, seeking to cause you dissension. And among you are those who would listen to them. And Allah knows well the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse reveals the divine wisdom in preventing hypocrites from joining the believers in battle, as their presence would have been detrimental to the Muslim community's unity and strength. Their participation would have caused internal discord through spreading rumors, doubts, and false information. The mention of "listeners among you" points to the vulnerability of some believers who might be influenced by hypocrites' propaganda, highlighting the importance of maintaining spiritual vigilance against internal threats to faith and community cohesion.
orig: لو خرجوا فيكم ما زادوكم إلا خبالا ولأوضعوا خلالكم يبغونكم الفتنة وفيكم سماعون لهم والله عليم بالظالمين

translation: They had already sought to spread corruption before and had turned matters against you until the truth came and Allah's command prevailed, even though they were averse.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how those who oppose the truth persistently work to undermine righteous causes through deception and manipulation. However, their schemes ultimately fail when Allah's divine plan manifests itself, demonstrating that no amount of human plotting can overcome Allah's will, even if the opponents despise this outcome. It serves as a reminder that truth and justice will eventually triumph over falsehood and corruption.
orig: لقد ابتغوا الفتنة من قبل وقلبوا لك الأمور حتى جاء الحق وظهر أمر الله وهم كارهون

translation: And among them is he who says, "Grant me permission and do not put me in trial." Surely, into trial they have already fallen. And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of those who seek excuses to avoid participating in righteous causes, claiming they want to avoid temptation or hardship. The irony is that by making such excuses and avoiding their duties, they've already succumbed to the greatest trial - that of failing to stand up for truth and justice. Their attempt to escape difficulty actually reveals their lack of true faith, which ultimately leads to their spiritual downfall.
orig: ومنهم من يقول ائذن لي ولا تفتني ألا في الفتنة سقطوا وإن جهنم لمحيطة بالكافرين

translation: If good befalls you, it grieves them; but if a misfortune befalls you, they say, "We took our precautions beforehand," and they turn away rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse reveals the psychology of hypocrites and enemies of faith, who harbor deep-seated resentment towards believers. Their reaction to others' fortunes exposes their true character - they feel pain at others' joy and secretly celebrate others' misfortunes, while claiming foresight to mask their malicious satisfaction. This behavior pattern indicates a spiritual disease where one's happiness is derived from others' suffering rather than from genuine achievement or goodwill.
orig: إن تصبك حسنة تسؤهم وإن تصبك مصيبة يقولوا قد أخذنا أمرنا من قبل ويتولوا وهم فرحون

translation: Say: "Nothing will happen to us except what Allah has decreed for us: He is our Protector, and on Allah let the believers put their trust."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Islamic concept of divine decree (qadar) and teaches believers to find peace in knowing that all events are within Allah's knowledge and control. It encourages a mindset of resilience and trust, reminding Muslims that while they should take necessary actions, ultimate outcomes are in Allah's hands. The reference to Allah as "mawlana" (protector) reinforces the nurturing relationship between the Divine and His servants, suggesting that whatever Allah has decreed is ultimately for their benefit, even if not immediately apparent.
orig: قل لن يصيبنا إلا ما كتب الله لنا هو مولانا وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: Say, "Do you await for us except one of the two best things [martyrdom or victory] while we await for you that Allah will afflict you with punishment from Himself or at our hands? So wait; indeed, we, along with you, are waiting."
interpretation: This verse reveals the spiritual fortitude of believers in the face of opposition, highlighting that their outlook is positive regardless of the outcome. They see both victory and martyrdom as favorable outcomes, demonstrating their deep faith and commitment. The verse also serves as a warning to adversaries, showing that while they plot against believers, they themselves are vulnerable to divine retribution or defeat at the hands of the faithful. It reflects the Islamic principle that true success isn't necessarily in worldly victory, but in remaining steadfast to one's faith regardless of consequences.
orig: قل هل تربصون بنا إلا إحدى الحسنيين ونحن نتربص بكم أن يصيبكم الله بعذاب من عنده أو بأيدينا فتربصوا إنا معكم متربصون

translation: Say, "Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will never be accepted from you. You have certainly been a defiantly disobedient people"
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of hypocritical charity, emphasizing that the mere act of giving without sincere faith and righteous conduct is meaningless in Allah's sight. It specifically addresses those who outwardly perform good deeds while harboring disbelief or disobedience, teaching us that Allah looks at the intention and spiritual state of the giver rather than the quantity or form of the contribution.
orig: قل أنفقوا طوعا أو كرها لن يتقبل منكم إنكم كنتم قوما فاسقين

translation: And what prevents their spending from being accepted from them is only that they have disbelieved in Allah and in His Messenger and that they come not to prayer except while they are lazy, and that they do not spend except unwillingly.
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound spiritual truth: that the acceptance of good deeds depends on the sincerity and faith behind them, not merely their outward performance. The hypocrites' charitable acts are rejected not due to the acts themselves, but because they lack genuine faith and perform these duties with reluctance and insincerity. True worship and charity must spring from authentic belief and willing devotion.
orig: وما منعهم أن تقبل منهم نفقاتهم إلا أنهم كفروا بالله وبرسوله ولا يأتون الصلاة إلا وهم كسالى ولا ينفقون إلا وهم كارهون

translation: So let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in worldly life and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: The verse reveals that material wealth and offspring, rather than being signs of divine favor, can actually serve as instruments of divine punishment. When people become excessively attached to worldly possessions and children, these blessings can become a source of constant anxiety, distraction from spiritual matters, and ultimately lead to their spiritual downfall. The punishment comes through their own attachment and preoccupation with these worldly matters, causing them to neglect their relationship with Allah and die in a state of disbelief.
orig: فلا تعجبك أموالهم ولا أولادهم إنما يريد الله ليعذبهم بها في الحياة الدنيا وتزهق أنفسهم وهم كافرون

translation: And they swear by Allah that they are from among you, but they are not from you; rather, they are a people who are afraid
interpretation: This verse exposes the nature of hypocrites who falsely claim allegiance to the Muslim community. Their oaths are merely a defensive mechanism stemming from fear and self-preservation, not from genuine faith. By emphasizing their desperate attempts to belong through false oaths, the verse highlights how fear can drive people to deceive others and themselves, while actually standing apart from the authentic believers in their hearts.
orig: ويحلفون بالله إنهم لمنكم وما هم منكم ولكنهم قوم يفرقون

translation: If they could find a refuge, or caves, or a place to enter, they would turn to it, running wild
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deep-seated aversion and fear that hypocrites have towards facing the truth and their responsibilities. Like frightened animals seeking escape, they would desperately search for any hiding place - physical or metaphorical - to avoid confronting their obligations to faith and community. Their behavior is not rational or measured, but rather like that of uncontrolled beasts ("running wild"), showing how fear and insincerity can reduce humans to an animalistic state of panic.
orig: لو يجدون ملجأ أو مغارات أو مدخلا لولوا إليه وهم يجمحون

translation: And among them are some who criticize you concerning the charities. If they are given from them, they are pleased; but if they are not given from them, at once they become angry
interpretation: This verse reveals a deep psychological insight into human nature, specifically addressing those who approach charity and wealth distribution with self-interest rather than genuine concern for justice or community welfare. It points to the hypocrisy of individuals who support charitable systems only when they personally benefit, showing how material interests can corrupt one's moral judgment and religious sincerity.
orig: ومنهم من يلمزك في الصدقات فإن أعطوا منها رضوا وإن لم يعطوا منها إذا هم يسخطون

translation: If only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them and said, "Sufficient for us is Allah; Allah will give us of His bounty, and [so will] His Messenger; indeed, we are desirous toward Allah."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual virtue of contentment and trust in divine providence. It suggests that true satisfaction comes not from constantly seeking more material gains, but from having faith that Allah's provisions are sufficient and optimal for each individual. The verse critiques those who are discontent with their portion and implies that the proper attitude of a believer should be one of grateful acceptance combined with hopeful optimism in Allah's continued generosity.
orig: ولو أنهم رضوا ما آتاهم الله ورسوله وقالوا حسبنا الله سيؤتينا الله من فضله ورسوله إنا إلى الله راغبون

translation: Zakat is only for the poor and the needy and those employed to collect it and those whose hearts are to be reconciled and for freeing slaves and for those in debt and for the cause of Allah and for the wayfarer - an obligation from Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes a comprehensive social welfare system in Islam by identifying eight specific categories of recipients for charitable giving (zakat). It demonstrates Allah's concern for social justice and economic equality, ensuring that wealth circulates throughout society rather than remaining concentrated among the wealthy. The inclusion of categories like reconciling hearts and freeing slaves shows how charity serves both material and spiritual purposes in building a harmonious community. The verse's conclusion emphasizing Allah's knowledge and wisdom suggests that this distribution system is perfectly designed to address both individual and societal needs.
orig: إنما الصدقات للفقراء والمساكين والعاملين عليها والمؤلفة قلوبهم وفي الرقاب والغارمين وفي سبيل الله وابن السبيل فريضة من الله والله عليم حكيم

translation: And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say, "He is all ears." Say, "[Being] all ears is better for you; he believes in Allah and believes the believers and [is] a mercy to those who believe among you." And those who harm the Messenger of Allah - for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound ethical dimension of leadership and communication in Islam, where the Prophet's attentive listening to all people, rather than being a weakness as his critics claimed, is actually a manifestation of divine wisdom and mercy. It demonstrates that being receptive and accessible to people's concerns is a virtue in leadership, not a flaw, while also establishing a clear moral boundary against those who would abuse such openness with harmful intentions.
orig: ومنهم الذين يؤذون النبي ويقولون هو أذن قل أذن خير لكم يؤمن بالله ويؤمن للمؤمنين ورحمة للذين آمنوا منكم والذين يؤذون رسول الله لهم عذاب أليم

translation: They swear by Allah to you to please you, but Allah and His Messenger are more worthy of being pleased by them, if they are believers
interpretation: This verse highlights the misplaced priorities of hypocrites who are more concerned with gaining people's approval than Allah's pleasure. It emphasizes that true faith requires prioritizing Allah's and His Messenger's satisfaction over seeking validation from others.
orig: يحلفون بالله لكم ليرضوكم والله ورسوله أحق أن يرضوه إن كانوا مؤمنين

translation: Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger will have the Fire of Hell, wherein they will abide forever? That is the great disgrace.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe spiritual consequences of actively opposing divine guidance, suggesting that conscious resistance to truth isn't merely a worldly matter but carries eternal implications. The permanence of the punishment indicates that deliberate opposition to divine authority represents a fundamental breach in one's relationship with the Creator, rather than a minor transgression.
orig: ألم يعلموا أنه من يحادد الله ورسوله فأن له نار جهنم خالدا فيها ذلك الخزي العظيم

translation: The hypocrites fear that a surah will be revealed about them, informing them of what is in their hearts. Say, "Mock on! Indeed, Allah will expose that which you fear."
interpretation: The verse reveals the deep psychological state of hypocrisy, where those who harbor ill intentions live in constant fear of being exposed. Their anxiety about divine revelation uncovering their true nature demonstrates that they are fully aware of their own deception, yet choose to persist in it. Allah's challenge to them to continue mocking shows that divine truth will ultimately prevail over human attempts at deception.
orig: يحذر المنافقون أن تنزل عليهم سورة تنبئهم بما في قلوبهم قل استهزئوا إن الله مخرج ما تحذرون

translation: And if you ask them, they will surely say, "We were only conversing and playing." Say, "Is it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?"
interpretation: This verse reveals the serious nature of making light of religious matters, highlighting how some people try to dismiss their disrespectful behavior towards sacred things by claiming it was mere jest. The divine response shows that attempting to trivialize mockery of Allah, His revelations, or His Messenger is itself a grave offense, as matters of faith should be treated with utmost reverence and sincerity.
orig: ولئن سألتهم ليقولن إنما كنا نخوض ونلعب قل أبالله وآياته ورسوله كنتم تستهزئون

translation: Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon one faction of you, We will punish another faction because they were criminals
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of apostasy and highlights that once true faith has been established, attempting to justify its abandonment is futile. It suggests that accountability for betraying one's faith is inevitable, though divine mercy may spare some based on their specific circumstances while others face consequences for their deliberate transgression.
orig: لا تعتذروا قد كفرتم بعد إيمانكم إن نعف عن طائفة منكم نعذب طائفة بأنهم كانوا مجرمين

translation: The hypocrite men and hypocrite women are of one another. They enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right and close their hands. They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them. Indeed, the hypocrites - they are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse reveals the symbiotic relationship between hypocrites, regardless of gender, showing how they form a unified front in opposing righteousness. Their actions reflect a complete inversion of the believer's duty - instead of promoting good and preventing evil, they do the opposite. Their "closed hands" symbolizes their extreme stinginess and unwillingness to contribute to good causes. The phrase "forgotten Allah" suggests their deliberate choice to ignore divine guidance, resulting in Allah withdrawing His mercy from them, which serves as a warning about the severe consequences of persistent hypocrisy.
orig: المنافقون والمنافقات بعضهم من بعض يأمرون بالمنكر وينهون عن المعروف ويقبضون أيديهم نسوا الله فنسيهم إن المنافقين هم الفاسقون

translation: Allah has promised the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally. It is sufficient for them. And Allah has cursed them, and for them is an enduring punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine justice system where those who maintain a facade of faith while harboring disbelief face severe consequences. The mention that Hell is "sufficient" for them suggests that their punishment perfectly matches their crime of deceiving others and rejecting truth while pretending to accept it. The eternal nature of the punishment reflects the gravity of hypocrisy in faith, which is considered even more dangerous than outright disbelief because it undermines the community from within.
orig: وعد الله المنافقين والمنافقات والكفار نار جهنم خالدين فيها هي حسبهم ولعنهم الله ولهم عذاب مقيم

translation: Like those before you who were mightier than you in power, and more abundant in wealth and children. They enjoyed their portion, and you have enjoyed your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion, and you have engaged in idle talk as they engaged in idle talk. Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and they are the losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a cautionary lesson about the cyclical nature of human complacency and downfall. It warns against following the path of previous civilizations who, despite their superior strength and resources, were ultimately ruined because they became consumed by worldly pleasures and idle diversions rather than focusing on spiritual growth and meaningful actions. The verse emphasizes that temporary material success can lead to moral decay and spiritual bankruptcy, resulting in ultimate loss both in this life and the hereafter.
orig: كالذين من قبلكم كانوا أشد منكم قوة وأكثر أموالا وأولادا فاستمتعوا بخلاقهم فاستمتعتم بخلاقكم كما استمتع الذين من قبلكم بخلاقهم وخضتم كالذي خاضوا أولئك حبطت أعمالهم في الدنيا والآخرة وأولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Has there not reached them the news of those before them - the people of Noah and [the tribes of] 'Aad and Thamud and the people of Abraham and the companions of Madyan and the towns overturned? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. And Allah would never have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse serves as a powerful reminder of divine justice and personal accountability, highlighting how historical precedent demonstrates that civilizations' downfall comes not from divine injustice but from their own choices. The mention of multiple destroyed nations emphasizes that divine patterns of justice are consistent throughout history, and people's suffering is invariably the result of their own rejection of truth and guidance rather than any divine oppression.
orig: ألم يأتهم نبأ الذين من قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود وقوم إبراهيم وأصحاب مدين والمؤتفكات أتتهم رسلهم بالبينات فما كان الله ليظلمهم ولكن كانوا أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: The believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those - Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the fundamental concept of spiritual and social solidarity within the Muslim community, emphasizing that faith transcends gender barriers. It illustrates how a healthy society functions through mutual support and collective responsibility, where believers actively participate in maintaining moral standards. The mention of specific duties - commanding good, preventing evil, prayer, and charity - suggests that true faith must manifest in both personal worship and social activism. The promise of Allah's mercy at the end indicates that this cooperative model of community building is divinely ordained and rewarded.
orig: والمؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أولياء بعض يأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر ويقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة ويطيعون الله ورسوله أولئك سيرحمهم الله إن الله عزيز حكيم

translation: Allah has promised to the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence; but approval from Allah is greater. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that while the physical pleasures of Paradise are magnificent, the greatest reward is Allah's pleasure with His servants. The mention of "pleasant dwellings" suggests that Paradise provides a sense of permanent home and belonging, contrasting with the temporary nature of earthly dwellings. The verse also notably addresses both men and women equally, indicating that spiritual rewards are not gender-specific but based on faith and righteousness.
orig: وعد الله المؤمنين والمؤمنات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ومساكن طيبة في جنات عدن ورضوان من الله أكبر ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: O Prophet! Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them. Hell will be their home, and evil is the destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of the Prophet's struggle: an external one against open disbelievers who actively oppose the truth, and an internal one against those who pretend to be believers while harboring disbelief. The command to be stern reflects the necessity of maintaining strong boundaries and principles when dealing with those who threaten the moral and spiritual fabric of society, whether through outright rejection or through deception and undermining from within.
orig: يا أيها النبي جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المصير

translation: They swear by Allah that they did not say [anything against the Prophet], while they had certainly said the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their [pretense of] Islam and planned that which they were not to attain. And they were not resentful except [for the fact] that Allah and His Messenger had enriched them of His bounty. So if they repent, it will be better for them; but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And there will not be for them on earth any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse reveals the psychological complexity of hypocrites who outwardly profess faith while harboring inner disbelief. It demonstrates how wealth and prosperity, rather than inspiring gratitude, can sometimes lead to arrogance and rebellion against divine guidance. The verse also illustrates Allah's justice system, offering a path to redemption through repentance while warning of severe consequences for persistent defiance, emphasizing that no earthly power can protect those who choose to oppose divine truth.
orig: يحلفون بالله ما قالوا ولقد قالوا كلمة الكفر وكفروا بعد إسلامهم وهموا بما لم ينالوا وما نقموا إلا أن أغناهم الله ورسوله من فضله فإن يتوبوا يك خيرا لهم وإن يتولوا يعذبهم الله عذابا أليما في الدنيا والآخرة وما لهم في الأرض من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah, [saying], "If He should give us from His bounty, we will surely spend in charity and we will surely be among the righteous"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the dangerous nature of making empty promises to Allah, particularly when one is in a state of need. It warns about those who make grand declarations of future righteousness while seeking divine favor, but often fail to fulfill these promises once their wishes are granted. The verse serves as a reminder that sincerity in promises to Allah must be matched with actual follow-through, as empty pledges can lead to spiritual hypocrisy.
orig: ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله لنصدقن ولنكونن من الصالحين

translation: But when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it and turned away in aversion
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ingratitude and moral weakness inherent in human nature, where people who eagerly seek God's blessings often become miserly and ungrateful once they receive them. It's a critique of those who forget their dependence on divine providence once they achieve prosperity, showing how wealth can corrupt the heart and lead to spiritual disconnection
orig: فلما آتاهم من فضله بخلوا به وتولوا وهم معرضون

translation: So He made hypocrisy follow as a consequence in their hearts until the Day they will meet Him because they failed Allah in what they promised Him and because they used to lie
interpretation: The spiritual consequence of breaking promises to Allah and engaging in dishonesty is that hypocrisy becomes deeply rooted in one's heart, creating a permanent spiritual affliction that persists until one faces Allah on the Day of Judgment. This verse illustrates how moral corruption is not just an external action but transforms one's inner spiritual state
orig: فأعقبهم نفاقا في قلوبهم إلى يوم يلقونه بما أخلفوا الله ما وعدوه وبما كانوا يكذبون

translation: Do they not know that Allah knows their secrets and their private conversations and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?
interpretation: This verse serves as a powerful reminder of divine omniscience, warning those who engage in secret plots or private conspiracies that nothing escapes Allah's knowledge. It challenges those who think they can hide their true intentions or secret plans, emphasizing that every whispered word and concealed thought is fully known to Allah. This awareness should inspire believers to maintain sincerity and transparency in all their affairs, knowing that pretense is futile before the All-Knowing.
orig: ألم يعلموا أن الله يعلم سرهم ونجواهم وأن الله علام الغيوب

translation: Those who criticize the contributors among the believers concerning [their] charities and [criticize] the ones who find nothing [to spend] except their effort, so they ridicule them - Allah will ridicule them, and they will have a painful punishment
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice against those who mock sincere believers, particularly addressing the hypocrites who ridiculed both wealthy and poor Muslims during the time of charity collection. The wealthy were mocked for showing off, while the poor were derided for their modest contributions. Allah's promise to "ridicule them" demonstrates that mocking sincere charitable acts, regardless of their size, invites divine retribution, teaching us that sincerity in giving is more valuable than the quantity given.
orig: الذين يلمزون المطوعين من المؤمنين في الصدقات والذين لا يجدون إلا جهدهم فيسخرون منهم سخر الله منهم ولهم عذاب أليم

translation: Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them - even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times - Allah will never forgive them. That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the finality of Allah's judgment against those who have fundamentally rejected faith, particularly the hypocrites in Medina. The number "seventy" here symbolizes infinity, indicating that no amount of intercession can help those who have consciously chosen to reject faith and persist in their disobedience. It demonstrates that while Allah's mercy is vast, it is contingent upon one's sincere acceptance of faith and willingness to follow divine guidance.
orig: استغفر لهم أو لا تستغفر لهم إن تستغفر لهم سبعين مرة فلن يغفر الله لهم ذلك بأنهم كفروا بالله ورسوله والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين

translation: Those who remained behind rejoiced in their staying [at home] after [the departure of] the Messenger of Allah and disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah and said, 'Do not go forth in the heat.' Say, 'The fire of Hell is more intense in heat' - if they would but understand.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stark contrast between sincere faith and hypocrisy, showing how those who make excuses to avoid religious duties ultimately harm themselves. By choosing temporary comfort over spiritual obligation, they ironically subject themselves to a far greater discomfort in the afterlife, demonstrating how shortsighted reasoning can lead to eternal consequences.
orig: فرح المخلفون بمقعدهم خلاف رسول الله وكرهوا أن يجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله وقالوا لا تنفروا في الحر قل نار جهنم أشد حرا لو كانوا يفقهون

translation: Let them laugh a little and weep much as a recompense for what they used to earn
interpretation: This verse conveys a divine warning about the temporary nature of worldly pleasures and the serious consequences of heedless behavior. Those who laugh carelessly in this world while disregarding their spiritual obligations will face prolonged sorrow in the hereafter as a natural outcome of their choices and actions. The contrast between "little" laughter and "much" weeping emphasizes the disproportion between fleeting worldly enjoyments and their lasting consequences.
orig: فليضحكوا قليلا وليبكوا كثيرا جزاء بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: If Allah returns you to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out, say: "You will never go out with me, nor will you ever fight an enemy with me. You were pleased to sit back the first time, so sit back with those who stay behind."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom in dealing with those who show hesitation and insincerity in their commitment to faith and community. It teaches that those who demonstrate reluctance and choose comfort over duty in critical moments forfeit their right to future participation. Their initial choice to stay behind reveals their true character, and allowing them to rejoin later would risk compromising the integrity and strength of the believing community.
orig: فإن رجعك الله إلى طائفة منهم فاستأذنوك للخروج فقل لن تخرجوا معي أبدا ولن تقاتلوا معي عدوا إنكم رضيتم بالقعود أول مرة فاقعدوا مع الخالفين

translation: And never pray [the funeral prayer] over any of them who has died or stand at his grave. Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died while they were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete spiritual separation between true believers and those who persistently reject faith until death. By prohibiting the Prophet from performing funeral prayers for hypocrites, it establishes that religious rituals and honors should align with one's genuine faith and actions in life, not merely social customs or familial ties. The directive serves as a powerful reminder that ultimate spiritual consequences stem from conscious choices made during one's lifetime.
orig: ولا تصل على أحد منهم مات أبدا ولا تقم على قبره إنهم كفروا بالله ورسوله وماتوا وهم فاسقون

translation: And let not their wealth and their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in this world and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound spiritual truth that material abundance can be a form of divine trial rather than a blessing. What appears as prosperity could actually be a subtle form of punishment, as attachment to wealth and children can lead to spiritual heedlessness and distract from the path of righteousness. The verse warns against envying the apparent success of disbelievers, as their worldly possessions may become sources of anxiety, fear, and suffering, ultimately leading to their spiritual demise.
orig: ولا تعجبك أموالهم وأولادهم إنما يريد الله أن يعذبهم بها في الدنيا وتزهق أنفسهم وهم كافرون

translation: And when a surah is revealed [enjoining them] to believe in Allah and to strive with His Messenger, those of wealth among them ask your permission [to stay back] and say, 'Leave us to be with those who sit [at home].'
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrisy of wealthy individuals who seek excuses to avoid religious obligations, particularly jihad. Despite having the means and ability to support the cause, they prefer comfort over commitment, revealing how material prosperity can sometimes weaken spiritual resolve and lead to moral cowardice.
orig: وإذا أنزلت سورة أن آمنوا بالله وجاهدوا مع رسوله استأذنك أولو الطول منهم وقالوا ذرنا نكن مع القاعدين

translation: They were content to be with those who stayed behind, and their hearts were sealed, so they do not understand
interpretation: This verse illustrates the spiritual consequence of choosing comfort over duty, highlighting how repeated choices to avoid responsibility can lead to a gradual hardening of the heart, ultimately resulting in a diminished capacity to comprehend spiritual and moral truths. The divine "sealing" of hearts represents the natural outcome of consistently choosing the path of least resistance, where one's ability to recognize and respond to higher truths becomes progressively impaired through their own choices.
orig: رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف وطبع على قلوبهم فهم لا يفقهون

translation: But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their lives, and those will have [all that is] good, and it is those who are the successful
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound commitment and sacrifices made by true believers, emphasizing that genuine faith requires active dedication of both material resources and personal effort. The promise of success and goodness for such individuals suggests that real prosperity isn't measured by worldly standards but by one's willingness to devote everything in service of their beliefs.
orig: لكن الرسول والذين آمنوا معه جاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم وأولئك لهم الخيرات وأولئك هم المفلحون

translation: Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. That is the great triumph.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's ultimate reward for the righteous, highlighting the eternal nature of Paradise as the supreme achievement. The flowing rivers symbolize perpetual abundance and vitality, while eternal residence represents complete fulfillment and the end of all earthly struggles. The description of it as "great triumph" suggests that all worldly successes pale in comparison to this divine reward.
orig: أعد الله لهم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And those with excuses among the Bedouins came seeking permission, while those who lied to Allah and His Messenger remained behind. A painful punishment will strike those who disbelieved among them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between sincere believers and hypocrites during times of hardship. While some Bedouins had genuine reasons for seeking exemption from joining military campaigns, others simply made false excuses out of cowardice or lack of faith. The divine wisdom here teaches that Allah knows the true intentions in people's hearts, and those who deliberately deceive with false pretenses will face consequences for their dishonesty and lack of commitment to the faith.
orig: وجاء المعذرون من الأعراب ليؤذن لهم وقعد الذين كذبوا الله ورسوله سيصيب الذين كفروا منهم عذاب أليم

translation: There is no blame upon the weak or upon the ill or upon those who do not find anything to spend when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger. There is not upon the doers of good any cause [for blame]. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and understanding of human limitations, teaching that those who are genuinely unable to participate in religious duties or charitable giving due to physical weakness, illness, or poverty are not held accountable as long as their hearts remain sincere in their faith. It highlights that true righteousness lies in one's intention and sincerity rather than in material contributions or physical abilities. The mention of Allah being "Forgiving and Merciful" reinforces that He understands human constraints and judges based on what is within one's capacity.
orig: ليس على الضعفاء ولا على المرضى ولا على الذين لا يجدون ما ينفقون حرج إذا نصحوا لله ورسوله ما على المحسنين من سبيل والله غفور رحيم

translation: Nor (is there blame) on those who came to you to be provided with mounts, when you said: "I can find no mounts for you," they turned back, with their eyes overflowing with tears of grief that they could not find anything to spend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sincerity of believers who were so eager to participate in the cause of Allah that their inability to contribute due to poverty brought them to tears. Their emotional response demonstrates that true faith isn't measured by material contributions but by the sincerity of one's heart and willingness to serve. It also teaches us that genuine excuses due to lack of means are acceptable to Allah, and that emotional investment in good causes is as valuable as material investment.
orig: ولا على الذين إذا ما أتوك لتحملهم قلت لا أجد ما أحملكم عليه تولوا وأعينهم تفيض من الدمع حزنا ألا يجدوا ما ينفقون

translation: The way (of blame) is only against those who ask permission of you while they are rich. They are satisfied to be with those who stay behind, and Allah has sealed over their hearts, so they do not know.
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound spiritual truth about the connection between material comfort and spiritual complacency. Those who have the means to support the cause of truth but choose to make excuses are suffering from a deeper spiritual ailment. Their preference for comfort over commitment has led to a gradual hardening of their hearts, making them blind to higher truths and spiritual obligations. The divine "sealing" of hearts isn't an arbitrary punishment but rather the natural consequence of repeatedly choosing worldly ease over moral responsibility.
orig: إنما السبيل على الذين يستأذنونك وهم أغنياء رضوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالف وطبع الله على قلوبهم فهم لا يعلمون

translation: They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say, "Make no excuses; we will not believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news. And Allah will observe your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger; then you will be taken back to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of false excuses and the ultimate accountability everyone faces. The hypocrites' attempts to justify their actions are rendered meaningless because Allah has already exposed their true nature. It emphasizes that no deception can succeed against divine knowledge, and every action will eventually be judged by the One who knows both the visible and invisible aspects of all matters.
orig: يعتذرون إليكم إذا رجعتم إليهم قل لا تعتذروا لن نؤمن لكم قد نبأنا الله من أخباركم وسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله ثم تردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them so that you may turn away from them. So turn away from them; indeed, they are filth, and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse reveals the divine wisdom in dealing with hypocrites who attempt to deceive believers through false oaths. It teaches that sometimes disengagement is the best response to those who persistently lie and deceive, as their internal corruption makes them unworthy of attention or reconciliation. Their ultimate destination of Hell reflects the serious nature of using sacred oaths for deception.
orig: سيحلفون بالله لكم إذا انقلبتم إليهم لتعرضوا عنهم فأعرضوا عنهم إنهم رجس ومأواهم جهنم جزاء بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: They swear to you so that you may be pleased with them. But even if you are pleased with them, Allah is not pleased with the people who are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse reveals the nature of hypocrites who use false oaths and external displays of piety to gain acceptance from believers. It warns that seeking human approval at the expense of divine truth is futile, as Allah's judgment is based on genuine faith and conduct, not superficial gestures or social acceptance. The emphasis on Allah's displeasure with "fasiqin" (defiantly disobedient) indicates that true success lies in earning divine pleasure rather than worldly validation.
orig: يحلفون لكم لترضوا عنهم فإن ترضوا عنهم فإن الله لا يرضى عن القوم الفاسقين

translation: The Bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy and more likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and religious disconnect that existed among the nomadic Bedouin tribes, suggesting that their lifestyle and isolation from centers of religious learning made them more susceptible to religious ignorance and insincerity. Their physical distance from the Prophet's teachings often resulted in a superficial understanding of faith, leading to greater tendencies toward disbelief and hypocrisy. The verse serves as a reminder that genuine faith requires proper knowledge and understanding of divine guidance.
orig: الأعراب أشد كفرا ونفاقا وأجدر ألا يعلموا حدود ما أنزل الله على رسوله والله عليم حكيم

translation: And among the Bedouins are some who consider what they spend as a loss and await misfortunes for you. Upon them will be the misfortune of evil, and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse reveals the hypocritical nature of certain desert Arabs who viewed their religious obligations, particularly charitable giving, as a burdensome loss rather than an act of worship. Their reluctance to spend in Allah's cause stemmed from their weak faith, and they secretly hoped for the downfall of the Muslim community. The divine response shows that their ill intentions would ultimately backfire on themselves, as Allah is fully aware of their inner thoughts and malicious wishes.
orig: ومن الأعراب من يتخذ ما ينفق مغرما ويتربص بكم الدوائر عليهم دائرة السوء والله سميع عليم

translation: And among the bedouins are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and consider what they spend as means of nearness to Allah and of [obtaining] invocations of the Messenger. Unquestionably, it is a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them to His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual authenticity that exists even among seemingly simple desert dwellers, showing that sincere faith transcends social status or sophistication. It teaches that what matters is not one's cultural background or social standing, but rather the purity of intention and genuine desire to draw closer to Allah through charitable giving. The mention of the Prophet's prayers for such people suggests that spiritual elevation comes through both direct devotion to Allah and the blessings of following His Messenger's guidance.
orig: ومن الأعراب من يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر ويتخذ ما ينفق قربات عند الله وصلوات الرسول ألا إنها قربة لهم سيدخلهم الله في رحمته إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: And the first forerunners [in the faith] among the Muhajireen and the Ansar and those who followed them with good conduct - Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great triumph.
interpretation: This verse establishes a spiritual hierarchy in early Islam, highlighting the special status of those who embraced Islam first and supported the Prophet's mission. It particularly emphasizes that sincere faith and righteous actions, not merely chronological precedence, are what earn divine pleasure. The mutual satisfaction between Allah and these believers ("Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him") suggests that true faith culminates in a profound spiritual relationship where the believer finds complete contentment in Allah's decrees while striving to earn His pleasure.
orig: والسابقون الأولون من المهاجرين والأنصار والذين اتبعوهم بإحسان رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه وأعد لهم جنات تجري تحتها الأنهار خالدين فيها أبدا ذلك الفوز العظيم

translation: And among the bedouins around you are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah [there are some who] are obstinate in hypocrisy. You do not know them, [but] We know them. We will punish them twice; then they will be returned to a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound spiritual truth about the complex nature of faith and deception within communities. It points to the existence of deeply rooted hypocrisy that can become so sophisticated that even the most discerning believers cannot detect it. Only Allah possesses the complete knowledge of what lies in people's hearts, highlighting the limitations of human judgment and the futility of attempting to definitively categorize people's faith. The mention of double punishment suggests that hypocrites suffer both in this world through their internal spiritual turmoil and social exposure, and in the afterlife through divine judgment.
orig: وممن حولكم من الأعراب منافقون ومن أهل المدينة مردوا على النفاق لا تعلمهم نحن نعلمهم سنعذبهم مرتين ثم يردون إلى عذاب عظيم

translation: And [there are] others who have acknowledged their sins. They had mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad. Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's infinite mercy by showing that sincere repentance can outweigh past mistakes. It suggests that even those who have committed sins while also doing good deeds still have hope for divine forgiveness, emphasizing that Allah's mercy extends to those who honestly acknowledge their shortcomings and show genuine remorse. The use of "perhaps" (عسى) in this context actually indicates certainty of Allah's forgiveness for the truly repentant, following Arabic linguistic tradition.
orig: وآخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم خلطوا عملا صالحا وآخر سيئا عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and pray for them. Indeed, your prayers are a source of comfort for them. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse establishes the profound spiritual and social impact of charitable giving in Islam. The act of giving purifies not just the wealth but the human soul from greed and attachment to material possessions. The mention of the Prophet's prayers for the givers suggests that spiritual growth requires both material sacrifice and divine blessing, creating a beautiful cycle of purification where financial giving is complemented by spiritual support.
orig: خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها وصل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم والله سميع عليم

translation: Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities, and that it is Allah who is the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite mercy and the direct, personal relationship He maintains with His creation. It suggests that there is no need for intermediaries between humans and God, as He directly accepts both our spiritual rectification (repentance) and our material acts of worship (charity). The questioning format implies gentle admonishment to those who might doubt Allah's direct involvement in accepting and acknowledging human acts of devotion.
orig: ألم يعلموا أن الله هو يقبل التوبة عن عباده ويأخذ الصدقات وأن الله هو التواب الرحيم

translation: And say, "Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger and the believers. And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound concept of accountability and divine awareness in Islam. It suggests that every action we perform is witnessed not just by Allah, but also by His Messenger and the believing community, creating a multi-layered system of moral responsibility. The verse serves as both a warning and a motivation, reminding believers that their deeds have eternal consequences and will ultimately be judged by the One who knows both the visible and invisible aspects of reality.
orig: وقل اعملوا فسيرى الله عملكم ورسوله والمؤمنون وستردون إلى عالم الغيب والشهادة فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And others are deferred for the command of Allah - whether He will punish them or whether He will forgive them. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute authority over judgment and redemption. It suggests that some individuals' fates remain in a state of suspense, teaching us that divine justice operates on a timeline that may not align with human expectations. The verse emphasizes that while some people's spiritual status may be uncertain, Allah's decisions are always based on perfect knowledge and wisdom, not arbitrary choice.
orig: وآخرون مرجون لأمر الله إما يعذبهم وإما يتوب عليهم والله عليم حكيم

translation: And those who took a mosque for causing harm and disbelief and division among the believers and as a station for whoever had warred against Allah and His Messenger before. And they will surely swear, "We intended only the best." And Allah testifies that indeed they are liars.
interpretation: This verse warns against the exploitation of religious institutions for malicious purposes, highlighting how hypocrites can disguise harmful intentions behind a facade of piety. It demonstrates that building places of worship with the intent to divide communities, spread disbelief, or support those who oppose divine guidance is a serious transgression. The verse also reveals the duplicitous nature of those who attempt to justify their harmful actions with false oaths, emphasizing that Allah knows their true intentions despite their outward claims of good will.
orig: والذين اتخذوا مسجدا ضرارا وكفرا وتفريقا بين المؤمنين وإرصادا لمن حارب الله ورسوله من قبل وليحلفن إن أردنا إلا الحسنى والله يشهد إنهم لكاذبون

translation: Never stand [for prayer] there. A mosque founded on righteousness from the first day is more worthy for you to stand in. Within it are men who love to purify themselves; and Allah loves those who purify themselves.
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that true worship and spiritual gatherings should be centered in places established with genuine piety and pure intentions, rather than in spaces built to cause harm or division. It suggests that the company we keep in worship matters, as those who strive for spiritual and physical cleanliness attract divine love. The mention of men who love purification indicates that sincere devotion manifests in both internal and external cleanliness.
orig: لا تقم فيه أبدا لمسجد أسس على التقوى من أول يوم أحق أن تقوم فيه فيه رجال يحبون أن يتطهروا والله يحب المطهرين

translation: Is he who founded his building upon fear of Allah and [His] good pleasure better or he who founded his building on the edge of a cliff about to collapse, so it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse presents a metaphor contrasting two approaches to life and faith. Those who build their lives on a foundation of genuine piety and seeking Allah's pleasure have established themselves on firm, unshakeable ground. In contrast, those who build their lives on weak principles, hypocrisy, or false beliefs are like those who have built on the edge of a crumbling cliff - their foundation is unstable and will ultimately lead to their downfall. The metaphor emphasizes the critical importance of establishing one's life choices and religious practices on sincere, righteous principles rather than superficial or insincere motivations.
orig: أفمن أسس بنيانه على تقوى من الله ورضوان خير أم من أسس بنيانه على شفا جرف هار فانهار به في نار جهنم والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: The building which they built will never cease to be a cause of hypocrisy and doubt in their hearts, unless their hearts are cut to pieces. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse reveals how insincere actions and false pretenses create lasting spiritual damage, embedding doubt and internal conflict within one's heart. Only a profound, transformative event that metaphorically "cuts" or breaks the heart - such as genuine repentance or a life-altering realization - can free someone from the consequences of their hypocritical deeds. The verse emphasizes that artificial or superficial religiosity breeds continuous internal turmoil.
orig: لا يزال بنيانهم الذي بنوا ريبة في قلوبهم إلا أن تقطع قلوبهم والله عليم حكيم

translation: Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties [in exchange] for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed. [It is] a true promise [binding] upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than Allah? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And it is that which is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse establishes a profound spiritual contract between Allah and the believers, depicting faith as a divine transaction where believers "sell" their earthly existence to Allah in exchange for eternal paradise. It's a metaphor for complete devotion and surrender to Allah's will, suggesting that true faith requires believers to prioritize spiritual values over worldly possessions and even life itself. The reference to multiple sacred texts emphasizes the universality and timelessness of this spiritual commitment, while also validating the continuity of divine revelation across different prophetic traditions.
orig: إن الله اشترى من المؤمنين أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة يقاتلون في سبيل الله فيقتلون ويقتلون وعدا عليه حقا في التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن ومن أوفى بعهده من الله فاستبشروا ببيعكم الذي بايعتم به وذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: Those who repent, who worship, who praise, who fast, who bow down, who prostrate themselves, who enjoin good and forbid evil, and who observe the limits of Allah - and give good tidings to the believers
interpretation: This verse outlines the exemplary qualities of true believers, emphasizing that authentic faith manifests through a comprehensive lifestyle of devotion and moral conduct. It suggests that genuine spirituality isn't just about ritual worship but requires active engagement in social reform, self-discipline, and maintaining ethical boundaries while encouraging others toward righteousness. The promise of good news at the verse's end indicates that those who embody these qualities will receive divine favor and success.
orig: التائبون العابدون الحامدون السائحون الراكعون الساجدون الآمرون بالمعروف والناهون عن المنكر والحافظون لحدود الله وبشر المؤمنين

translation: It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire
interpretation: This verse establishes a fundamental principle about the limits of spiritual solidarity, teaching that the bonds of faith supersede even the closest family ties. While Muslims are encouraged to show kindness and maintain good relations with non-Muslim relatives, there are boundaries to religious obligations. The verse suggests that once a person has consciously rejected faith and died in a state of disbelief, prayers for their forgiveness become futile, as divine justice has already determined their fate.
orig: ما كان للنبي والذين آمنوا أن يستغفروا للمشركين ولو كانوا أولي قربى من بعد ما تبين لهم أنهم أصحاب الجحيم

translation: And Abraham's prayer for his father's forgiveness was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Abraham was compassionate and forbearing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the importance of prioritizing faith and divine truth over family bonds when they conflict. Even Abraham, known for his compassion and patience, had to sever ties with his father when it became evident that his father's rejection of monotheism was firm and unchangeable. It teaches that while we should honor our family relationships, our primary loyalty must be to divine truth, and we shouldn't compromise our religious principles even for our closest relatives.
orig: وما كان استغفار إبراهيم لأبيه إلا عن موعدة وعدها إياه فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه إن إبراهيم لأواه حليم
