translation: And Allah would not let a people stray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should fear. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's perfect justice and mercy in dealing with His creation. It indicates that divine guidance, once granted, is not withdrawn arbitrarily. Rather, Allah continues to support those who have been guided unless they themselves choose to deviate by ignoring clear warnings and signs. This highlights personal accountability in maintaining one's spiritual path and Allah's fairness in providing complete clarity before holding people accountable for their choices.
orig: وما كان الله ليضل قوما بعد إذ هداهم حتى يبين لهم ما يتقون إن الله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Indeed, to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He gives life and causes death. And you have not besides Allah any protector or any helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah, highlighting that true authority and control over all existence belongs exclusively to Him. By mentioning His power over life and death, it reminds humans of their complete dependence on Allah and their inherent vulnerability. The absence of any other protector or helper underscores the futility of seeking ultimate refuge or assistance from any source other than Allah, establishing the foundation of pure monotheism in both belief and practice.
orig: إن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض يحيي ويميت وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Allah has turned in mercy to the Prophet and to the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of difficulty after the hearts of a group of them had almost deviated, then He turned to them in mercy. Indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's infinite mercy and forgiveness during a critical moment in Islamic history, specifically the Tabuk expedition. It demonstrates how even the most devoted followers can experience moments of doubt or hesitation when faced with extreme hardship, yet Allah's compassion prevails. The "hour of difficulty" refers to a time of severe heat, scarcity, and hardship, teaching us that divine support comes precisely when human endurance is tested to its limits. This verse also shows that having momentary doubts doesn't negate one's faith, as long as one returns to the right path.
orig: لقد تاب الله على النبي والمهاجرين والأنصار الذين اتبعوه في ساعة العسرة من بعد ما كاد يزيغ قلوب فريق منهم ثم تاب عليهم إنه بهم رءوف رحيم

translation: And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind [and regretted their error] to the point that the earth, despite its vastness, closed in upon them, and their souls confined them, and they were certain that there was no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them so they could repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound psychological and spiritual journey of true repentance, showing how genuine remorse often requires reaching a point of complete desperation where one realizes that only Allah can provide solace. The three companions' experience teaches us that divine mercy becomes most apparent when we've exhausted all other options and fully acknowledge our complete dependence on Allah's forgiveness.
orig: وعلى الثلاثة الذين خلفوا حتى إذا ضاقت عليهم الأرض بما رحبت وضاقت عليهم أنفسهم وظنوا أن لا ملجأ من الله إلا إليه ثم تاب عليهم ليتوبوا إن الله هو التواب الرحيم

translation: O you who believe! Fear Allah and be with those who are truthful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vital connection between God-consciousness (taqwa) and authentic companionship. By instructing believers to associate with truthful people, it suggests that spiritual growth and moral development are deeply influenced by the company we keep. The directive implies that truthfulness isn't merely about honest speech, but encompasses sincerity in faith, actions, and character. Being "with" the truthful suggests more than physical proximity - it calls for emulating their qualities, learning from their example, and becoming part of a community that upholds truth as a core value.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله وكونوا مع الصادقين

translation: It was not for the people of Medina and the Bedouins around them to remain behind the Messenger of Allah or to prefer their own lives to his life. That is because they are not afflicted by thirst or fatigue or hunger in the cause of Allah, nor do they take any step that angers the disbelievers, nor do they inflict upon an enemy any infliction but that it is registered for them as a righteous deed. Indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound spiritual principle of sacrifice and solidarity in the Islamic community, particularly highlighting how every hardship endured in the path of Allah has spiritual significance. It teaches that true faith requires putting collective religious duties above personal comfort, and that even seemingly small actions or difficulties faced while serving Islam's cause are divinely recorded and rewarded. The verse establishes that spiritual growth and divine reward come not just from major acts of worship, but from every instance of discomfort, challenge, or effort that advances the cause of faith and righteousness.
orig: ما كان لأهل المدينة ومن حولهم من الأعراب أن يتخلفوا عن رسول الله ولا يرغبوا بأنفسهم عن نفسه ذلك بأنهم لا يصيبهم ظمأ ولا نصب ولا مخمصة في سبيل الله ولا يطئون موطئا يغيظ الكفار ولا ينالون من عدو نيلا إلا كتب لهم به عمل صالح إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: Nor do they spend any amount, small or large, or cross any valley, except that it is recorded for them, so that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's comprehensive system of divine recordkeeping and reward, illustrating that no act of sacrifice or struggle in His cause goes unnoticed. The mention of "crossing valleys" symbolizes both physical and metaphorical journeys undertaken in the pursuit of righteous causes, while the reference to spending encompasses all forms of material sacrifice. The verse reassures believers that their efforts, regardless of scale, are meticulously documented and will be rewarded with divine generosity that exceeds their actual deeds.
orig: ولا ينفقون نفقة صغيرة ولا كبيرة ولا يقطعون واديا إلا كتب لهم ليجزيهم الله أحسن ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And it is not for the believers to go forth [to battle] all at once. For there should separate from every division of them a group [remaining] to obtain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them that they might be cautious.
interpretation: This verse establishes the importance of balancing military duties with religious education in the Muslim community. It suggests that while some members engage in defensive warfare, others should dedicate themselves to studying and teaching Islamic principles, creating a sustainable system of religious knowledge transmission. This division of responsibilities ensures the community's spiritual and physical protection while maintaining continuous religious education and guidance.
orig: وما كان المؤمنون لينفروا كافة فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في الدين ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون

translation: O you who believe! Fight those of the disbelievers who are close to you, and let them find harshness in you, and know that Allah is with those who are pious
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the strategic importance of addressing immediate threats first, similar to how one would deal with closest problems before distant ones. The command for "harshness" refers to showing strength and firmness in defending one's principles and community, not cruelty. The mention of Allah being with the pious reminds believers that military engagement should be conducted with ethical restraint and righteousness, not with unbridled aggression.
orig: يا أيها الذين آمنوا قاتلوا الذين يلونكم من الكفار وليجدوا فيكم غلظة واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين

translation: And whenever a surah is revealed, there are among them those who say, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?" As for those who have believed, it increases them in faith, and they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stark contrast between the attitudes of believers and hypocrites towards divine revelation. While hypocrites approach new revelations with skepticism and mockery, true believers find their faith strengthened and deepened with each new verse, demonstrating that faith is dynamic and can grow stronger through continuous engagement with divine guidance. The believers' joy upon receiving revelation indicates that spiritual growth is a source of happiness and fulfillment for the faithful.
orig: وإذا ما أنزلت سورة فمنهم من يقول أيكم زادته هذه إيمانا فأما الذين آمنوا فزادتهم إيمانا وهم يستبشرون

translation: But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it increased them in evil [in addition] to their evil. And they died while they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the spiritual principle that divine guidance affects people differently based on their inner disposition. Those who harbor spiritual diseases like doubt, hypocrisy, or malice in their hearts will find that exposure to truth only deepens their resistance and aversion to it, much like how sunlight that nourishes healthy plants can cause diseased ones to wither further.
orig: وأما الذين في قلوبهم مرض فزادتهم رجسا إلى رجسهم وماتوا وهم كافرون

translation: Do they not see that they are tried every year once or twice, yet they do not repent nor do they remember?
interpretation: This verse highlights the cyclical nature of life's trials and human forgetfulness. Allah points out how people face various tests and difficulties repeatedly, yet they fail to recognize these as divine reminders. Instead of using these challenges as opportunities for spiritual growth and returning to Allah in repentance, they remain heedless and continue in their ways, not learning from their experiences or taking heed of these recurring wake-up calls.
orig: أولا يرون أنهم يفتنون في كل عام مرة أو مرتين ثم لا يتوبون ولا هم يذكرون

translation: And when a surah is revealed, they look at each other [saying], "Does anyone see you?" Then they dismiss themselves. Allah has dismissed their hearts because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrites' behavior during the revelation of Qur'anic verses, showing how they would seek to escape from hearing divine guidance. Their furtive glances and attempts to slip away unnoticed reveal their deep-seated aversion to truth and spiritual growth. Allah's statement about turning their hearts away is a divine consequence of their own choices - their persistent rejection of understanding led to a spiritual blindness, illustrating how continuous resistance to divine guidance eventually results in the heart's inability to recognize or accept truth.
orig: وإذا ما أنزلت سورة نظر بعضهم إلى بعض هل يراكم من أحد ثم انصرفوا صرف الله قلوبهم بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون

translation: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer; [he is] concerned over you and to the believers is kind and merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep emotional bond between Prophet Muhammad and his followers, emphasizing his compassionate nature. His suffering at the sight of his followers' hardships demonstrates the ideal leadership model in Islam - one that genuinely cares for their community's wellbeing. The use of "from among yourselves" establishes relatability and trust, showing that divine guidance comes through someone who understands human experiences and challenges.
orig: لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه ما عنتم حريص عليكم بالمؤمنين رءوف رحيم

translation: But if they turn away, say, "Sufficient for me is Allah; there is no deity except Him. On Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes complete trust and reliance on Allah in the face of rejection or opposition. When one faces adversity or abandonment from others, the believer should find solace in knowing that Allah's support alone is sufficient. The mention of the "Great Throne" reinforces Allah's supreme authority and control over all matters, suggesting that seeking help from any other source is ultimately futile.
orig: فإن تولوا فقل حسبي الله لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وهو رب العرش العظيم

translation: Alif Lam Ra. These are the verses of the wise Book
interpretation: The divine nature of the Qur'an is emphasized through the mystical letters "Alif Lam Ra," which point to the miraculous composition of the Qur'an using ordinary letters to create extraordinary meaning. The description of the Book as "wise" indicates that its teachings contain perfect wisdom and guidance that transcends human intellectual capacity.
orig: الر تلك آيات الكتاب الحكيم

translation: Is it a wonder to mankind that We revealed to a man from among them, saying: "Warn mankind and give glad tidings to those who believe that they shall have a true rank of honor with their Lord"? The disbelievers say: "Indeed this is a clear magician."
interpretation: This verse addresses the universal human tendency to resist divine guidance when it comes through one of their own. The skepticism shown towards Prophet Muhammad reflects how people often struggle to accept that God would choose an ordinary person as His messenger. The promise of "true rank" (qadam sidq) symbolizes the eternal spiritual elevation awaiting those who overcome this skepticism and embrace faith, while the accusation of sorcery represents how truth is often dismissed as manipulation by those who refuse to believe.
orig: أكان للناس عجبا أن أوحينا إلى رجل منهم أن أنذر الناس وبشر الذين آمنوا أن لهم قدم صدق عند ربهم قال الكافرون إن هذا لساحر مبين

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne, arranging [all] matter. There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Then will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and control over creation, highlighting that even His authority over time itself is demonstrated through the deliberate, measured creation process. The mention of the Throne and Allah's establishment above it symbolizes His supreme authority and governance over all affairs. The reference to intercession serves as a reminder that all power and authority ultimately rest with Allah, and no one can intervene without His explicit permission, reinforcing the direct relationship between the Creator and His creation.
orig: إن ربكم الله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش يدبر الأمر ما من شفيع إلا من بعد إذنه ذلكم الله ربكم فاعبدوه أفلا تذكرون

translation: To Him is your return all together - [it is] the promise of Allah [which is] truth. Indeed, He begins the creation and then repeats it that He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds, in justice. But those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to deny.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of ultimate accountability and divine justice, highlighting that our temporary existence in this world is not the end but rather a prelude to an eternal reality. Just as Allah demonstrated His power by creating us initially, He will resurrect us for judgment, establishing a perfect system of justice where faith and good deeds will be recognized and rewarded, while rejection of truth carries severe consequences.
orig: إليه مرجعكم جميعا وعد الله حقا إنه يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده ليجزي الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات بالقسط والذين كفروا لهم شراب من حميم وعذاب أليم بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a derived light and determined for it phases - that you may know the number of years and account [of time]. Allah has not created this except in truth. He details the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse reveals Allah's divine precision in cosmic engineering, demonstrating how He designed celestial bodies not just for light but as sophisticated tools for humanity's temporal organization. By distinguishing between the sun's self-generated light (ضياء) and the moon's reflected light (نورا), and establishing the moon's predictable phases, Allah provided humanity with a natural calendar system, highlighting how scientific phenomena serve both practical and spiritual purposes in Islam's worldview.
orig: هو الذي جعل الشمس ضياء والقمر نورا وقدره منازل لتعلموا عدد السنين والحساب ما خلق الله ذلك إلا بالحق يفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون

translation: Indeed, in the alternation of night and day and in what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth are signs for people who fear Allah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes how the natural cycles and phenomena serve as profound evidence of Allah's existence and power for those who maintain consciousness of Him. The specific mention of those "who fear Allah" suggests that true understanding of these signs requires a heart that is already spiritually attuned through God-consciousness, indicating that scientific observation alone, without spiritual awareness, may not lead to complete understanding of divine truth
orig: إن في اختلاف الليل والنهار وما خلق الله في السماوات والأرض لآيات لقوم يتقون

translation: Indeed, those who do not expect the meeting with Us and are satisfied with the life of this world and feel secure therein, and those who are heedless of Our signs
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual blindness of those who have become completely engrossed in worldly pursuits, having lost sight of their ultimate purpose and accountability. Their contentment with temporary pleasures and material security has made them forget their spiritual essence and divine destiny, reflecting a state of profound spiritual negligence and disconnection from higher truths.
orig: إن الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ورضوا بالحياة الدنيا واطمأنوا بها والذين هم عن آياتنا غافلون

translation: Their refuge will be the Fire because of what they used to earn
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine principle of accountability, indicating that those who persistently choose evil and reject truth will face the natural consequences of their actions. The use of the word "earn" (يكسبون) suggests that hellfire isn't an arbitrary punishment, but rather the accumulated result of one's conscious choices and deeds, much like how wages are earned through deliberate work.
orig: أولئك مأواهم النار بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - their Lord will guide them because of their faith. Beneath them rivers will flow in the Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine principle of reciprocal relationship between faith and guidance, suggesting that sincere belief coupled with good actions creates a self-reinforcing cycle where Allah increases a person's guidance in proportion to their demonstrated faith. The imagery of flowing rivers beneath them symbolizes that true guidance leads to perpetual spiritual nourishment and refreshment in the afterlife.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات يهديهم ربهم بإيمانهم تجري من تحتهم الأنهار في جنات النعيم

translation: Their prayer therein will be "Glory be to You, O Allah," and their greeting therein will be "Peace," and the last of their prayer will be "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the eternal state of contentment and spiritual fulfillment in Paradise, where the inhabitants are in such a state of divine connection that their natural inclination is to continuously praise and glorify Allah. Their communication with each other reflects perfect peace and tranquility, devoid of worldly negativity or idle talk. The culmination of their worship with "Alhamdulillah" signifies their perpetual gratitude and recognition that all blessings, including their salvation, come from Allah's mercy and grace.
orig: دعواهم فيها سبحانك اللهم وتحيتهم فيها سلام وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: And if Allah was to hasten evil for people as He hastens good for them, their term would have been fulfilled. So We leave those who do not expect to meet Us wandering blindly in their transgression.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's infinite mercy and wisdom in His response to human invocations. While humans often make impulsive prayers in moments of anger or frustration, wishing harm upon themselves or others, Allah in His wisdom does not respond to these negative supplications as swiftly as He does to prayers for good. If He were to fulfill harmful prayers as quickly as beneficial ones, humanity would face swift destruction due to their own hasty and emotional reactions. This delay in responding to prayers for harm is a manifestation of divine mercy, giving people time to reconsider and repent.
orig: ولو يعجل الله للناس الشر استعجالهم بالخير لقضي إليهم أجلهم فنذر الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا في طغيانهم يعمهون

translation: And when adversity touches man, he calls upon Us, whether lying on his side or sitting or standing; but when We remove from him his adversity, he continues [in disobedience] as if he had never called upon Us to [remove] adversity that touched him.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the fickle nature of human faith and behavior, highlighting how people often turn to God only in times of hardship but quickly forget their devotion once comfort is restored. It reveals a profound psychological truth about human tendency to be sincere in worship during difficulties but ungrateful and dismissive of God's help once the crisis passes. This pattern of behavior is particularly characteristic of those who lack genuine faith and demonstrates the importance of maintaining consistent devotion to God in both ease and hardship.
orig: وإذا مس الإنسان الضر دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما فلما كشفنا عنه ضره مر كأن لم يدعنا إلى ضر مسه كذلك زين للمسرفين ما كانوا يعملون

translation: And We had already destroyed generations before you when they wronged, and their messengers had come to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe. Thus do We recompense the criminal people
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's consistent divine law in dealing with nations that persist in wrongdoing and rejection of truth. It emphasizes that divine punishment isn't arbitrary but follows a pattern where people are first given clear guidance through messengers. When they deliberately choose to reject this guidance despite clear evidence, they face consequences. The verse serves as both a warning and a reminder that divine justice operates on established principles that apply equally to all societies across time.
orig: ولقد أهلكنا القرون من قبلكم لما ظلموا وجاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات وما كانوا ليؤمنوا كذلك نجزي القوم المجرمين

translation: Then We made you successors in the land after them to see how you would act
interpretation: This verse emphasizes humanity's role as God's vicegerents on Earth, carrying a profound responsibility to demonstrate moral conduct and ethical behavior. It suggests that our actions are continuously being observed and evaluated by Allah, implying that our stewardship of Earth and treatment of its resources and inhabitants serve as a test of our worthiness for this divine trust.
orig: ثم جعلناكم خلائف في الأرض من بعدهم لننظر كيف تعملون

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring a Qur'an other than this or change it." Say, "It is not for me to change it of my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."
interpretation: This verse reveals the arrogance of disbelievers who, instead of accepting divine guidance, demand alterations to suit their desires. It emphasizes the Prophet's role as a faithful messenger who cannot modify God's word, highlighting the serious responsibility of conveying divine revelation exactly as received. The verse also underscores that divine scripture isn't subject to human preferences or modifications, and warns of severe consequences for attempting to alter God's words.
orig: وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات قال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ائت بقرآن غير هذا أو بدله قل ما يكون لي أن أبدله من تلقاء نفسي إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Say, "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. I had remained among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then understand?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine authenticity of the Prophet Muhammad's message by highlighting that his sudden transformation from an unlettered man to one reciting profound revelations wasn't of his own accord. The fact that he lived among his people for forty years without showing any signs of such knowledge serves as proof that the Qur'an is divine revelation rather than human invention. It challenges skeptics to reflect on how someone who was known for his truthfulness and who had never shown such literary or philosophical capabilities could suddenly produce such profound teachings unless they were truly from Allah.
orig: قل لو شاء الله ما تلوته عليكم ولا أدراكم به فقد لبثت فيكم عمرا من قبله أفلا تعقلون

translation: So who is more unjust than one who fabricates lies about Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe spiritual consequences of two major transgressions: attributing false things to Allah and rejecting divine truth when it comes. Those who commit these acts are placing themselves in a position of extreme spiritual peril, as they are actively working against the fundamental relationship between Creator and creation. The use of the rhetorical question suggests that these are among the worst forms of wrongdoing possible, as they strike at the heart of faith and truth itself.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بآياته إنه لا يفلح المجرمون

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them, and they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah." Say, "Do you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?" Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse exposes the logical fallacy in idol worship and the concept of intermediaries between humans and God. It points out that humans cannot appoint intercessors for themselves with Allah, as this implies they know something Allah doesn't know. The rhetorical question emphasizes that Allah, being the All-Knowing Creator of everything in heaven and earth, cannot be informed of anything He doesn't already know, making the concept of chosen intercessors inherently flawed.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا يضرهم ولا ينفعهم ويقولون هؤلاء شفعاؤنا عند الله قل أتنبئون الله بما لا يعلم في السماوات ولا في الأرض سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And mankind was not but one community, then they differed. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them concerning that over which they differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent unity of human origin and the divine wisdom in allowing differences to exist. It suggests that diversity and disagreement among humans is not the natural state but rather a development that occurred after their original unified condition. The "word" from Allah that preceded refers to His decree to delay judgment until an appointed time, showing His mercy in giving people the chance to resolve their differences and find their way to truth through free will rather than immediate divine intervention.
orig: وما كان الناس إلا أمة واحدة فاختلفوا ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم فيما فيه يختلفون

translation: And they say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "The unseen is only for Allah [to administer], so wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in Allah's sole authority over supernatural signs and miracles. It teaches patience and trust in Allah's timing, reminding us that demanding immediate proofs shows a lack of understanding of divine wisdom. The Prophet's response demonstrates the proper attitude of submission to Allah's will and acceptance that He alone determines when and how to manifest His signs.
orig: ويقولون لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه فقل إنما الغيب لله فانتظروا إني معكم من المنتظرين

translation: And when We give people a taste of mercy after hardship has touched them, they immediately begin to plot against Our signs. Say, "Allah is swifter in plotting." Indeed, Our messengers record what you plot.
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound insight into human psychology and ingratitude. When people face difficulties and God relieves them with His mercy, instead of showing gratitude, they often return to their rebellious ways and try to undermine divine truth. This pattern demonstrates humanity's tendency to forget divine favors during times of ease and comfort. The divine response shows that God's power supersedes any human schemes, and nothing escapes His knowledge as every plot is meticulously recorded.
orig: وإذا أذقنا الناس رحمة من بعد ضراء مستهم إذا لهم مكر في آياتنا قل الله أسرع مكرا إن رسلنا يكتبون ما تمكرون

translation: He is the One Who enables you to travel through land and sea. When you are in ships, sailing with a favorable wind, and rejoicing therein, there comes a stormy wind and the waves come to them from everywhere and they think that they are surrounded, they invoke Allah, making their faith pure for Him alone, saying, "If You save us from this, we will surely be among the grateful."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inherent nature of human beings to turn to Allah in times of severe distress, showing how adversity strips away all pretense and reveals our true dependence on our Creator. When faced with death or disaster, even those who normally neglect their faith instinctively turn to Allah with sincere devotion. However, this also points to human inconsistency - we make earnest promises in times of hardship but often forget them once we're safe, highlighting our need to maintain constant consciousness of Allah, not just during crises.
orig: هو الذي يسيركم في البر والبحر حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك وجرين بهم بريح طيبة وفرحوا بها جاءتها ريح عاصف وجاءهم الموج من كل مكان وظنوا أنهم أحيط بهم دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين لئن أنجيتنا من هذه لنكونن من الشاكرين

translation: But when He saves them, behold! They rebel in the earth wrongfully. O mankind! Your rebellion is only against yourselves - a brief enjoyment of worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We shall inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the cyclical nature of human ingratitude and moral weakness, where people, once delivered from hardship, often return to transgression and corruption. It emphasizes that such rebellious behavior ultimately harms the perpetrators themselves, not God, as it stems from a short-sighted attachment to temporary worldly pleasures. The verse serves as a powerful reminder that all actions will face accountability in the eternal life, where the true consequences of our choices will be revealed.
orig: فلما أنجاهم إذا هم يبغون في الأرض بغير الحق يا أيها الناس إنما بغيكم على أنفسكم متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعكم فننبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: The example of worldly life is like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, from which people and livestock eat. Until, when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified and its people think that they have capability over it, there comes to it Our command by night or by day, and We make it as a harvest, as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus do We explain the signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse presents a profound metaphor about the temporary nature of worldly life and human pride. Just as rain causes plants to grow abundantly, leading people to believe they have control over their prosperity, Allah reminds us that all worldly success and beauty can be stripped away in an instant, whether by day or night. The sudden destruction of the flourishing vegetation symbolizes how quickly fortune can change, serving as a warning against becoming too attached to worldly possessions or becoming arrogant in times of prosperity. It's a powerful reminder that true security lies only with Allah, not in temporal achievements or wealth.
orig: إنما مثل الحياة الدنيا كماء أنزلناه من السماء فاختلط به نبات الأرض مما يأكل الناس والأنعام حتى إذا أخذت الأرض زخرفها وازينت وظن أهلها أنهم قادرون عليها أتاها أمرنا ليلا أو نهارا فجعلناها حصيدا كأن لم تغن بالأمس كذلك نفصل الآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And Allah invites to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's benevolent nature in calling humanity to Paradise, which is characterized by eternal peace and tranquility. The term "dar as-salam" (Home of Peace) represents not just a physical destination but a state of complete spiritual fulfillment where all forms of distress, fear, and anxiety are absent. The verse also highlights divine discretion in guidance, suggesting that while the invitation is universal, the path becomes clear to those who sincerely seek it and align their will with divine wisdom.
orig: والله يدعو إلى دار السلام ويهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: For those who have done good is the best [reward] and extra, and no darkness will cover their faces, nor humiliation. Those are companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's boundless generosity, showing that He not only rewards good deeds with their equivalent but gives additional rewards beyond what was earned. The absence of darkness and humiliation on their faces suggests that the righteous will maintain their dignity and honor in the afterlife, reflecting their inner spiritual purity. This state of eternal contentment in Paradise represents the ultimate success of those who lived their lives in accordance with divine guidance.
orig: للذين أحسنوا الحسنى وزيادة ولا يرهق وجوههم قتر ولا ذلة أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون

translation: And those who have earned evil deeds, the recompense of an evil deed is the like thereof, and humiliation will cover them. They will have no protector from Allah. [It will be] as if their faces are covered with pieces of the dark night. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine principle of perfect justice, where the punishment precisely matches the transgression. The imagery of faces covered with darkness symbolizes the spiritual blindness that led to their misdeeds, now manifesting as actual darkness in their punishment. The humiliation they experience reflects how their sins stripped them of their dignity, and their eternal stay in the Fire represents the permanent nature of their choice to reject divine guidance.
orig: والذين كسبوا السيئات جزاء سيئة بمثلها وترهقهم ذلة ما لهم من الله من عاصم كأنما أغشيت وجوههم قطعا من الليل مظلما أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: And [mention] the Day when We will gather them all together, then We will say to those who associated [others with Allah], '[Remain in] your place, you and your 'partners.' Then We will separate them, and their partners will say, 'It was not us that you used to worship.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate futility and deception of polytheism, showing how on the Day of Judgment, the false deities and objects of worship will disown their worshippers, revealing the profound loneliness and betrayal that awaits those who placed their faith in anything other than Allah. The "separation" mentioned symbolizes the breaking of all perceived bonds between the worshippers and their false objects of worship, exposing the meaningless nature of these worldly attachments.
orig: ويوم نحشرهم جميعا ثم نقول للذين أشركوا مكانكم أنتم وشركاؤكم فزيلنا بينهم وقال شركاؤهم ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون

translation: So Allah is sufficient as a witness between us and you that we were unaware of your worship
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine accountability and truth verification. It suggests that Allah's witnessing is the ultimate testimony, superior to any human claims or counterclaims. The statement reflects a situation where one party distances itself from the false worship of others, affirming that Allah's knowledge of the truth is sufficient to settle any dispute about religious authenticity and sincerity.
orig: فكفى بالله شهيدا بيننا وبينكم إن كنا عن عبادتكم لغافلين

translation: There, every soul will experience [the consequences of] what it has done in the past, and they will be returned to Allah, their true Lord, and all their fabrications will be lost from them
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate accountability that awaits in the afterlife, where each individual's deeds and choices will manifest in their full reality. The use of "there" points to a specific moment of reckoning where all artificial constructs, false beliefs, and worldly pretenses fall away, leaving only the pure truth of one's relationship with the Divine. The mention of Allah as "their true Lord" suggests that all other authorities or powers people might have relied upon will prove meaningless in that moment of truth.
orig: هنالك تبلو كل نفس ما أسلفت وردوا إلى الله مولاهم الحق وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Say, "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight? And who brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living? And who arranges [every] matter?" They will say, "Allah." So say, "Then will you not fear Him?"
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the logical approach to establishing Allah's divinity by pointing to observable phenomena that humans cannot explain or control. It challenges people to reflect on fundamental aspects of existence - sustenance, sensory abilities, the cycle of life and death, and the universe's organization - to recognize that these all point to a supreme power. The fact that even skeptics acknowledge Allah's role in these matters shows that deep down, humans innately recognize divine authority, making their refusal to live righteously a conscious choice rather than genuine disbelief.
orig: قل من يرزقكم من السماء والأرض أمن يملك السمع والأبصار ومن يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ومن يدبر الأمر فسيقولون الله فقل أفلا تتقون

translation: Such is Allah, your true Lord. So what is beyond truth except error? How then are you turned away?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute nature of divine truth, suggesting that any deviation from Allah's guidance represents a form of misguidance. The rhetorical question "how are you turned away" points to the illogical nature of choosing alternative paths when the truth has been clearly established, much like someone deliberately choosing darkness after experiencing light.
orig: فذلكم الله ربكم الحق فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال فأنى تصرفون

translation: Thus the word of your Lord has proven true against those who defiantly disobeyed that they will not believe
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound spiritual law: persistent defiance and disobedience to divine guidance can lead to a hardening of the heart, making it increasingly difficult for a person to accept faith. When someone repeatedly chooses to transgress against divine laws, they may reach a point where their ability to recognize and embrace truth becomes severely impaired, fulfilling Allah's decree about their state of disbelief.
orig: كذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين فسقوا أنهم لا يؤمنون

translation: Say, "Are there any of your partners who originate creation and then repeat it?" Say, "Allah originates creation and then repeats it. So how are you deluded?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the concept of polytheism by highlighting the unique power of Allah in creation. It emphasizes that only Allah possesses the ability to both initiate creation and resurrect it, which none of the false deities can do. The rhetorical question serves to make people reflect on their misguided beliefs, as they worship entities that can't even perform the most fundamental divine act of creation and resurrection.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده قل الله يبدأ الخلق ثم يعيده فأنى تؤفكون

translation: Say, "Are there any of your partners who guides to the truth?" Say, "Allah guides to the truth." So is He who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed or he who guides not unless he is guided? Then what is wrong with you? How do you judge?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the logic of polytheism by highlighting the fundamental difference between Allah and false deities. It points out that only Allah has the inherent power to guide, while the false gods themselves need guidance. This creates a powerful rational argument against idol worship, as it questions how someone could logically follow or worship entities that lack the ability to provide guidance and themselves need to be guided.
orig: قل هل من شركائكم من يهدي إلى الحق قل الله يهدي للحق أفمن يهدي إلى الحق أحق أن يتبع أمن لا يهدي إلا أن يهدى فما لكم كيف تحكمون

translation: And most of them follow nothing but conjecture. Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking certainty and truth rather than relying on assumptions and unverified beliefs. It critiques those who base their beliefs and decisions on mere speculation or cultural inheritance without solid evidence. The divine reminder that Allah knows their actions suggests accountability for choosing to follow conjecture over verified truth, encouraging believers to seek knowledge based on clear evidence rather than unfounded assumptions.
orig: وما يتبع أكثرهم إلا ظنا إن الظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا إن الله عليم بما يفعلون

translation: This Qur'an could not have been produced by anyone other than Allah. However, it confirms what came before it and explains the Scripture in detail - there is no doubt about it - from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine authenticity of the Qur'an by highlighting that its profound wisdom, consistency, and detailed explanations could only come from a divine source. The verse dismisses any notion of human authorship by pointing to how perfectly it aligns with previous divine revelations while providing comprehensive guidance. The fact that it builds upon and confirms earlier scriptures while offering detailed clarifications demonstrates its role as the final, authoritative divine message to humanity.
orig: وما كان هذا القرآن أن يفترى من دون الله ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين

translation: Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"? Say, "Then bring a chapter like it and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful."
interpretation: This verse presents a powerful challenge to those who doubted the divine origin of the Qur'an, highlighting that its literary and spiritual excellence is beyond human capability. The fact that this challenge remains unmet to this day serves as evidence of the Qur'an's divine authorship, as even the most eloquent Arabic poets and writers of the time, despite their mastery of language, could not produce anything comparable to even a single chapter of the Qur'an.
orig: أم يقولون افتراه قل فأتوا بسورة مثله وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Rather, they have denied that which they encompass not in knowledge and that which has not yet come to them its interpretation. Thus did those before them deny. Then observe how was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to reject truths that lie beyond their immediate comprehension or experience. It suggests that skepticism and denial often stem not from rational evaluation, but from an unwillingness to acknowledge matters that exceed one's current understanding. The verse draws a parallel between contemporary deniers and those of the past, implying that hasty rejection of divine messages without proper consideration leads to adverse consequences.
orig: بل كذبوا بما لم يحيطوا بعلمه ولما يأتهم تأويله كذلك كذب الذين من قبلهم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord knows best the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the eternal truth about human nature's diversity in faith and belief. It suggests that despite being presented with the same divine message, people's responses will inherently differ based on their inner disposition and spiritual readiness. The mention of Allah's complete knowledge of the "corrupters" implies that those who reject faith often do so not from genuine doubt, but from an internal corruption that Allah is fully aware of.
orig: ومنهم من يؤمن به ومنهم من لا يؤمن به وربك أعلم بالمفسدين

translation: And if they deny you, say: "For me are my deeds, and for you are your deeds. You are disassociated from what I do, and I am disassociated from what you do."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of individual responsibility and accountability in faith and actions. It teaches that each person's choices and deeds belong to them alone, and no one bears the burden of another's decisions. The verse provides guidance on how to respond to rejection with dignity and composure, avoiding unnecessary conflict while maintaining firm boundaries between truth and falsehood.
orig: وإن كذبوك فقل لي عملي ولكم عملكم أنتم بريئون مما أعمل وأنا بريء مما تعملون

translation: And among them are those who listen to you. But can you make the deaf hear, even though they will not understand?
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of trying to guide those who have willfully closed their hearts to the truth. Just as it's impossible to make a physically deaf person hear, it's equally impossible to make someone understand who has chosen spiritual deafness. The verse suggests that true guidance requires not just physical hearing but an open heart and willingness to comprehend and accept the truth.
orig: ومنهم من يستمعون إليك أفأنت تسمع الصم ولو كانوا لا يعقلون

translation: And among them are those who look at you. But can you guide the blind although they will not see?
interpretation: This verse illustrates the spiritual blindness that affects some people's hearts, not physical blindness. Even when truth and guidance are presented clearly before them, they cannot perceive it because they've chosen to close their hearts to divine guidance. Just as a blind person cannot see despite the presence of light, these individuals cannot receive guidance despite the Prophet's presence and teachings, highlighting that ultimate guidance comes from Allah, and even the Prophet cannot force understanding upon those who willfully reject it.
orig: ومنهم من ينظر إليك أفأنت تهدي العمي ولو كانوا لا يبصرون

translation: Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all, but it is people who wrong themselves
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability and divine justice, highlighting that human suffering and injustice are not caused by Allah but rather stem from humanity's own choices and actions. When people face hardships or negative consequences, they should look inward rather than attribute their misfortunes to divine injustice. Allah has established a perfect system of natural and moral laws, and it is our violation of these laws that leads to our own detriment.
orig: إن الله لا يظلم الناس شيئا ولكن الناس أنفسهم يظلمون

translation: And on the Day when He will gather them, [it will be] as if they had not remained [in the world] except for an hour of the day, [and] they will recognize each other. Those who denied the meeting with Allah will have lost, and they were not guided.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound disorientation and altered perception of time that humans will experience on the Day of Judgment, where their worldly life will seem incredibly brief, like merely an hour. The mutual recognition among people suggests a moment of clarity where they fully comprehend their situation and past relationships, making their previous denial of this reality even more regrettable. The ultimate loss belongs to those who rejected faith, as they squandered their opportunity for guidance by denying their inevitable return to Allah.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم كأن لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من النهار يتعارفون بينهم قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله وما كانوا مهتدين

translation: Whether We show you some of what We have promised them, or We cause you to die - to Us is their return; then Allah is Witness over what they do
interpretation: This verse conveys Allah's absolute control over outcomes and ultimate justice. It reassures the Prophet Muhammad that whether he witnesses the consequences of his opponents' actions in his lifetime or not, divine justice is inevitable. The mention of Allah as witness emphasizes that no action goes unrecorded or unaccounted for, providing a powerful reminder that temporal escape from consequences doesn't equal ultimate escape from divine judgment
orig: وإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإلينا مرجعهم ثم الله شهيد على ما يفعلون

translation: And for every nation is a messenger. So when their messenger comes, it will be judged between them in justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's universal justice and fairness in dealing with all peoples throughout history. Each community has been sent divine guidance through a messenger appropriate to their time and circumstances, demonstrating that no one is left without guidance. When judgment comes, it will be based on how people responded to the message they received, ensuring complete fairness as each nation will be judged according to their own circumstances and the specific message they were given.
orig: ولكل أمة رسول فإذا جاء رسولهم قضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And they say, "When is this promise [to be fulfilled], if you are truthful?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and impatience of disbelievers who mock the warnings of divine judgment and accountability. Their questioning isn't born from genuine curiosity but from disbelief, challenging the authenticity of divine promises with sarcasm. Their demand for immediate fulfillment shows their misunderstanding of divine timing and wisdom, as Allah's promises operate on His schedule, not human expectations.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: Say, "I possess no power to benefit or harm myself except as Allah wills. For every nation there is an appointed time. When their time arrives, they cannot delay it by a single hour, nor can they advance it."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete dependence of all creation, including prophets, on Allah's will. It dismantles human illusions of self-sufficiency and control over destiny, while establishing that divine timing is precise and immutable. The mention of nations' appointed terms suggests that societies, like individuals, have predetermined lifespans that operate according to Allah's wisdom, highlighting the futility of attempting to alter what Allah has decreed.
orig: قل لا أملك لنفسي ضرا ولا نفعا إلا ما شاء الله لكل أمة أجل إذا جاء أجلهم فلا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون

translation: Say, "Have you considered - if His punishment should come to you by night or by day - what [part] of it would the criminals wish to hasten?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility and irrationality of those who mock or challenge divine punishment. It points out that when punishment actually arrives, whether during sleep or wakefulness, these same people who were hastening it will find nothing in it worth rushing towards. The verse serves as a warning about the foolishness of arrogantly demanding divine retribution, as when it comes, there will be no escape regardless of the time of its arrival.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن أتاكم عذابه بياتا أو نهارا ماذا يستعجل منه المجرمون

translation: Is it only then, when it befalls you, that you will believe in it? Now? While you used to seek to hasten it?
interpretation: This verse critiques the human tendency to dismiss divine warnings until disaster strikes, highlighting how people often mock or challenge God's messages, demanding immediate proof, but then scramble to believe only when faced with the consequences they were warned about. It's a commentary on the futility of deferred faith and the importance of heeding warnings before it's too late.
orig: أثم إذا ما وقع آمنتم به آلآن وقد كنتم به تستعجلون

translation: Then it will be said to those who wronged, "Taste the punishment of eternity! Are you being recompensed except for what you used to earn?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine principle of absolute justice, highlighting that eternal punishment is not arbitrary but a direct consequence of one's deliberate actions. The rhetorical question at the end serves to make wrongdoers acknowledge that they are merely facing the natural outcomes of their choices, eliminating any possibility of claiming injustice in their judgment.
orig: ثم قيل للذين ظلموا ذوقوا عذاب الخلد هل تجزون إلا بما كنتم تكسبون

translation: And they ask you, "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord, indeed it is true; and you cannot escape it."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute certainty of divine truth and accountability. When people question or doubt the reality of divine judgment or resurrection, Allah instructs the Prophet to respond with the strongest possible affirmation, swearing by God's own existence. The mention that none can escape or frustrate this reality serves as both a warning to disbelievers and reassurance to believers, highlighting that divine justice is inevitable and inescapable regardless of one's acceptance or denial of it.
orig: ويستنبئونك أحق هو قل إي وربي إنه لحق وما أنتم بمعجزين

translation: And if every soul that did wrong had all that is on the earth, it would seek to ransom itself with it. And they will confide their regret when they see the punishment. And it will be judged between them in justice, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound depth of regret and desperation that wrongdoers will experience on the Day of Judgment. The imagery of offering everything on earth as ransom emphasizes that no material possession or worldly wealth can compensate for spiritual transgressions once the final moment of accountability arrives. The concealment of regret suggests a deep, internal anguish that comes from the realization that the time for repentance has passed. Allah's justice will be absolute and complete, with no soul bearing more than its due burden.
orig: ولو أن لكل نفس ظلمت ما في الأرض لافتدت به وأسروا الندامة لما رأوا العذاب وقضي بينهم بالقسط وهم لا يظلمون

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth. Unquestionably, the promise of Allah is truth, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete and absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, highlighting that His dominion extends beyond our earthly realm into the cosmic expanse. The repetition of "unquestionably" serves to remove any doubt about these fundamental truths. When coupled with the assertion that Allah's promise is truth, it provides reassurance to believers while serving as a gentle rebuke to those who doubt, suggesting that their skepticism stems from a lack of true knowledge rather than from rational grounds.
orig: ألا إن لله ما في السماوات والأرض ألا إن وعد الله حق ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: It is He who gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power over existence itself, highlighting that He alone controls the fundamental cycle of life and death. The mention of return to Him implies accountability and reinforces that our temporary worldly existence serves as a journey back to our Creator, who will judge our deeds and choices.
orig: هو يحيي ويميت وإليه ترجعون

translation: O mankind! There has come to you a guidance from your Lord and a healing for what is in the breasts and guidance and mercy for the believers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's universal compassion by offering spiritual medicine to humanity. The "healing for what is in the breasts" suggests that divine guidance serves as a remedy for spiritual ailments like doubt, anxiety, and moral confusion. Just as physical medicine cures the body, divine revelation treats the soul's afflictions and restores spiritual well-being.
orig: يا أيها الناس قد جاءتكم موعظة من ربكم وشفاء لما في الصدور وهدى ورحمة للمؤمنين

translation: Say, "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy - in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true happiness and fulfillment come from recognizing and appreciating Allah's spiritual gifts rather than material possessions. It suggests that divine guidance and mercy are more valuable than any worldly wealth or achievements that people might amass throughout their lives. The verse serves as a reminder to shift one's perspective from material success to spiritual abundance.
orig: قل بفضل الله وبرحمته فبذلك فليفرحوا هو خير مما يجمعون

translation: Say, "Have you seen what Allah has sent down to you of provision of which you have made [some] lawful and [some] unlawful?" Say, "Has Allah permitted you [to do so], or do you invent [something] about Allah?"
interpretation: This verse challenges those who arbitrarily declare things permissible or forbidden without divine authority. It criticizes the practice of making self-imposed religious restrictions that Allah never mandated, highlighting that only Allah has the authority to determine what is halal (permissible) and haram (forbidden). The verse suggests that inventing religious rules without divine sanction is equivalent to falsely attributing lies to Allah.
orig: قل أرأيتم ما أنزل الله لكم من رزق فجعلتم منه حراما وحلالا قل آلله أذن لكم أم على الله تفترون

translation: And what do those who invent lies against Allah think of the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of them are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine warning against fabricating falsehoods about Allah, suggesting that those who engage in such behavior are failing to recognize the serious consequences they will face on Judgment Day. Despite their ingratitude and false attributions, Allah's mercy continues to encompass humanity, demonstrating His boundless compassion even towards those who transgress against Him.
orig: وما ظن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب يوم القيامة إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثرهم لا يشكرون

translation: Whatever matter you [O Muhammad] may be in, and whatever portion you may recite from the Qur'an, and whatever deed you [O mankind] may do, We are witness over you when you are engaged therein. And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or [anything] smaller than that or greater but that it is in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete and comprehensive knowledge of all things, highlighting the concept of divine omniscience. It serves as both a comfort and a warning - a comfort to the believers that Allah witnesses their good deeds and struggles, and a warning to the wrongdoers that nothing escapes Allah's knowledge. The mention of "atom's weight" and things even smaller demonstrates that Allah's knowledge encompasses even the most minute details of existence, whether physical or metaphysical, past, present, or future.
orig: وما تكون في شأن وما تتلو منه من قرآن ولا تعملون من عمل إلا كنا عليكم شهودا إذ تفيضون فيه وما يعزب عن ربك من مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء ولا أصغر من ذلك ولا أكبر إلا في كتاب مبين

translation: Unquestionably, [for] the allies of Allah there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve
interpretation: This verse speaks to the profound spiritual state achieved by those who have attained true closeness to Allah. These special servants, through their complete trust and devotion, reach a level where worldly fears and anxieties no longer affect them. Their deep connection with the Divine provides them with an inner peace that transcends temporal concerns, as they understand that everything occurs by Allah's will and wisdom.
orig: ألا إن أولياء الله لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Those who believed and used to fear Allah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of true faith - belief must be accompanied by action. It's not enough to merely claim belief; true believers demonstrate their faith through God-consciousness (taqwa) in their daily lives, actively avoiding what displeases Allah and striving to fulfill their religious obligations.
orig: الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: For them are glad tidings in the worldly life and in the Hereafter. No change can there be in the Words of Allah. That is the supreme triumph.
interpretation: This verse conveys Allah's eternal promise of hope and reassurance to the believers, indicating that those who maintain their faith will receive continuous good news and blessings both in this life through peace of mind and divine guidance, and in the afterlife through Paradise. The immutability of Allah's words emphasizes the certainty and reliability of these divine promises, highlighting that true success lies in earning these divine assurances rather than worldly achievements.
orig: لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة لا تبديل لكلمات الله ذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: Let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, all honor belongs to Allah. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing
interpretation: This verse provides divine consolation to believers, particularly leaders and advocates of truth, reminding them that they shouldn't be distressed by the arrogant claims or hostile words of opponents. True power and dignity lie exclusively with Allah, and He is fully aware of every word spoken against His faithful servants. This knowledge should bring peace to the believer's heart, knowing that Allah's recognition is what truly matters, not the opinions or statements of critics.
orig: ولا يحزنك قولهم إن العزة لله جميعا هو السميع العليم

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth. And those who invoke other than Allah do not [actually] follow [His] "partners." They follow not except assumption, and they are only falsifying.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of polytheistic beliefs by highlighting that those who worship false deities are merely following baseless conjectures rather than divine truth. Their claimed "partners" with Allah have no real existence or authority, as everything in creation ultimately belongs to and is subject to Allah's sovereignty. The polytheists are essentially engaging in self-deception, constructing their beliefs on unfounded assumptions rather than certain knowledge.
orig: ألا إن لله من في السماوات ومن في الأرض وما يتبع الذين يدعون من دون الله شركاء إن يتبعون إلا الظن وإن هم إلا يخرصون

translation: It is He who made for you the night to rest therein and the day bright (giving sight). Indeed, in that are signs for a people who listen
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy in establishing the natural cycle of day and night as a manifestation of His divine wisdom. The darkness of night serves as a period of physical and mental restoration, allowing humans to disconnect from their daily struggles and find peace. The brightness of day, in contrast, enables productivity and the pursuit of livelihood. This alternation represents a deeper spiritual truth about the balance between action and reflection, work and rest, highlighting how every aspect of creation serves humanity's wellbeing.
orig: هو الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يسمعون

translation: They say, "Allah has taken a son" - Exalted is He! He is the Self-Sufficient; to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. You have no authority for this claim. Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?
interpretation: This verse addresses the fundamental theological error of attributing offspring to God by emphasizing God's complete self-sufficiency and independence from any need for progeny. It challenges those who make such claims without any evidence, highlighting how this misconception stems from applying human characteristics to the Divine, which fails to recognize God's unique and transcendent nature as the absolute owner and sustainer of all creation.
orig: قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا سبحانه هو الغني له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض إن عندكم من سلطان بهذا أتقولون على الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: Say, "Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning about the severe consequences of attributing false things to Allah's religion or claiming to speak on His behalf without authority. It emphasizes that any attempt to manipulate divine truth for worldly gains or personal agenda will ultimately lead to failure, both in this life and the hereafter. The use of "will not succeed" indicates a definitive and absolute outcome, showing that false religious claims are a path to spiritual and moral bankruptcy.
orig: قل إن الذين يفترون على الله الكذب لا يفلحون

translation: Enjoyment in this worldly life - then to Us is their return, then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the temporary nature of worldly pleasures and warns that those who choose disbelief over faith are trading brief earthly gratification for eternal consequences. The use of "taste" (نذيقهم) suggests that the punishment will be as tangible and real as the worldly pleasures they once enjoyed, highlighting divine justice's inevitability and the serious ramifications of rejecting faith.
orig: متاع في الدنيا ثم إلينا مرجعهم ثم نذيقهم العذاب الشديد بما كانوا يكفرون

translation: And recite to them the story of Noah when he said to his people: "O my people, if my presence and my reminding of the signs of Allah has become burdensome upon you, then I have relied upon Allah. So resolve upon your plan and [call upon] your associates. Then let not your plan be obscure to you. Then carry it out against me and do not give me respite."
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the unwavering faith and courage of Prophet Noah in the face of opposition. By challenging his opponents to do their worst while maintaining complete trust in Allah, he exemplifies the ideal stance of a believer who refuses to compromise their principles despite facing hostility. His bold declaration serves as a powerful reminder that when one truly relies on Allah, they need not fear any worldly opposition or threats, no matter how formidable they may appear.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ نوح إذ قال لقومه يا قوم إن كان كبر عليكم مقامي وتذكيري بآيات الله فعلى الله توكلت فأجمعوا أمركم وشركاءكم ثم لا يكن أمركم عليكم غمة ثم اقضوا إلي ولا تنظرون

translation: But if you turn away, I have not asked you for any reward. My reward is only from Allah, and I have been commanded to be among the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sincere and selfless nature of prophetic mission, highlighting that true guidance and religious leadership should be motivated by divine calling rather than material gain or personal benefit. The prophet's dedication to his mission is purely for Allah's sake, demonstrating that spiritual leadership should be free from financial exploitation or personal advantage.
orig: فإن توليتم فما سألتكم من أجر إن أجري إلا على الله وأمرت أن أكون من المسلمين

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the ship and made them successors and drowned those who denied Our signs. Then see how was the end of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's consistent pattern of divine justice, where those who persist in rejecting truth despite clear warnings face consequences, while those who maintain faith through adversity are elevated to positions of leadership and influence. The drowning of the disbelievers and salvation of the believers in Noah's ark serves as a powerful reminder that divine support ultimately favors those who remain steadfast in their faith, even when they represent a minority.
orig: فكذبوه فنجيناه ومن معه في الفلك وجعلناهم خلائف وأغرقنا الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فانظر كيف كان عاقبة المنذرين

translation: Then We sent after him messengers to their people, and they brought them clear proofs. But they were not to believe in that which they had denied before. Thus do We seal over the hearts of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a profound spiritual principle: when people repeatedly and willfully reject truth despite clear evidence, their hearts become hardened to the point where they lose the capacity to recognize and accept truth. Like a seal that makes an impression permanent, persistent denial of divine guidance creates a spiritual barrier that prevents further enlightenment, highlighting the serious consequences of obstinate rejection of faith.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعده رسلا إلى قومهم فجاءوهم بالبينات فما كانوا ليؤمنوا بما كذبوا به من قبل كذلك نطبع على قلوب المعتدين

translation: Then after them We sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs, but they behaved arrogantly and were a criminal people
interpretation: This verse illustrates a recurring pattern in human history where those in positions of power often reject divine guidance due to their arrogance. Despite being presented with clear signs and evidence through Moses and Aaron, Pharaoh and his officials chose to maintain their oppressive status quo rather than accept the truth. Their criminality wasn't just in their rejection of the message, but in their conscious choice to persist in wrongdoing despite knowing better, highlighting how pride and power can corrupt human nature and lead to spiritual blindness.
orig: ثم بعثنا من بعدهم موسى وهارون إلى فرعون وملئه بآياتنا فاستكبروا وكانوا قوما مجرمين

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Indeed, this is clear sorcery"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the common pattern of denial among those who reject divine guidance, where even when presented with clear evidence and truth, they dismiss it as magic or trickery. It reflects how people often resort to dismissive labels when confronted with truths that challenge their established beliefs or threaten their positions of power.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا إن هذا لسحر مبين

translation: Moses said: "Do you say [thus] about the truth when it has come to you? Is this sorcery? But sorcerers will not succeed."
interpretation: Moses is highlighting the irony and stubbornness of those who reject divine truth by labeling it as mere sorcery. His rhetorical question serves to expose their illogical stance, as they're attempting to discredit a genuine miracle by equating it with magic, even though they know that sorcery is ultimately powerless against divine truth. This verse emphasizes the futility of opposing authentic divine messages with false accusations.
orig: قال موسى أتقولون للحق لما جاءكم أسحر هذا ولا يفلح الساحرون

translation: They said: "Have you come to turn us away from what we found our forefathers following, and so that you two may have greatness in the land? We are not believers in you."
interpretation: This verse reveals the deep-rooted challenge faced by those who bring religious reform: the psychological barrier of traditional practices. The disbelievers' response shows how people often resist change not based on the merit of the message, but due to their emotional attachment to inherited customs. Their accusation about seeking 'greatness' also demonstrates how those opposed to reform often attribute ulterior motives to reformers, using this as a defense mechanism to avoid confronting the actual message.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا لتلفتنا عما وجدنا عليه آباءنا وتكون لكما الكبرياء في الأرض وما نحن لكما بمؤمنين

translation: And Pharaoh said: "Bring to me every learned sorcerer"
interpretation: This verse reveals Pharaoh's arrogance and his reliance on worldly power rather than divine truth. By summoning sorcerers to counter Moses's miracles, he demonstrates how those in positions of authority often attempt to maintain their control through deception and manipulation rather than accepting clear signs of truth. His response also shows how tyrannical systems typically respond to challenges to their authority by trying to match divine signs with human trickery.
orig: وقال فرعون ائتوني بكل ساحر عليم

translation: So when the sorcerers came, Moses said to them: "Cast whatever you are going to cast."
interpretation: This verse illustrates a pivotal moment of psychological warfare where Moses, confident in Allah's support, challenges the sorcerers to demonstrate their skills first. His strategy shows that true divine power doesn't fear human deception, and by letting them go first, Moses is setting the stage to expose the difference between genuine miracles and mere illusion.
orig: فلما جاء السحرة قال لهم موسى ألقوا ما أنتم ملقون

translation: When they had cast down, Moses said: "What you have brought is sorcery. Allah will surely make it void. Indeed, Allah does not support the work of the corrupters."
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the power of unwavering faith in the face of intimidation. When Moses confronts the sorcerers, he doesn't show fear but rather absolute certainty in Allah's power to overcome falsehood. His response teaches us that no matter how impressive or overwhelming evil may appear, divine truth will always prevail over human deception and corruption.
orig: فلما ألقوا قال موسى ما جئتم به السحر إن الله سيبطله إن الله لا يصلح عمل المفسدين

translation: And Allah establishes the truth by His words, even if the criminals dislike it
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's supreme authority in manifesting truth and justice in the universe. Despite the resistance, schemes, or displeasure of those who commit evil, Allah's divine plan and truth will inevitably prevail. The criminals mentioned here represent those who oppose divine guidance and justice, but their opposition is ultimately futile against Allah's will and wisdom.
orig: ويحق الله الحق بكلماته ولو كره المجرمون

translation: But none believed in Moses except some children of his people, [and they believed] while in fear of Pharaoh and their leaders, that they would persecute them. And indeed, Pharaoh was haughty within the land, and indeed, he was of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights how fear can suppress faith and truth, as even when presented with clear signs, most people were too afraid of worldly consequences to follow their convictions. It demonstrates how tyrannical power structures can prevent people from embracing truth and justice, with only the young and vulnerable sometimes having the courage to stand up for what's right despite the risks.
orig: فما آمن لموسى إلا ذرية من قومه على خوف من فرعون وملئهم أن يفتنهم وإن فرعون لعال في الأرض وإنه لمن المسرفين

translation: And Moses said: "O my people! If you have believed in Allah, then put your trust in Him if you are Muslims."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the essential connection between true faith and complete reliance on Allah. Moses is teaching that genuine belief must be accompanied by practical trust in divine providence. It's not enough to merely claim faith; believers must demonstrate their submission by relinquishing control to Allah and trusting in His wisdom and plan. This represents the practical manifestation of the testimony of faith.
orig: وقال موسى يا قوم إن كنتم آمنتم بالله فعليه توكلوا إن كنتم مسلمين

translation: They said: "In Allah we put our trust. Our Lord! Make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people"
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep spiritual maturity of believers who, while facing persecution or challenges, demonstrate complete reliance on Allah while simultaneously recognizing the potential broader implications of their situation. Their prayer shows awareness that if they were to be defeated or overcome by oppressors, it might embolden wrongdoers and cause them to become more tyrannical, or make others doubt the truth of their faith. It's a profound recognition that one's personal trials can have wider consequences for the cause of truth and justice.
orig: فقالوا على الله توكلنا ربنا لا تجعلنا فتنة للقوم الظالمين

translation: And deliver us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound human need for divine protection and salvation in the face of adversity, particularly from those who actively oppose faith and truth. It emphasizes that deliverance comes not through our own strength or merit, but through Allah's mercy, highlighting our complete dependence on divine compassion for safety and success.
orig: ونجنا برحمتك من القوم الكافرين

translation: And We inspired to Moses and his brother, "Settle your people in Egypt in houses and make your houses facing [prayer] and establish prayer and give good tidings to the believers."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine protection and guidance during times of persecution. By instructing Moses and Aaron to establish proper dwellings and places of worship in Egypt, Allah was helping the Israelites maintain their religious identity and community cohesion while living under oppressive rule. The command to make their houses places of prayer suggests the importance of creating sacred spaces even in hostile environments, teaching us that worship and faith can be maintained under any circumstances.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى وأخيه أن تبوآ لقومكما بمصر بيوتا واجعلوا بيوتكم قبلة وأقيموا الصلاة وبشر المؤمنين

translation: And Moses said, "Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his establishment splendor and wealth in the worldly life, our Lord, that they may lead [people] astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse reveals the profound spiritual insight that material wealth and power can become tools of corruption and spiritual blindness. Moses's prayer demonstrates that sometimes divine punishment comes in the form of allowing people to become more entrenched in their wrongdoing, as excessive wealth and power can make people arrogant and resistant to truth.
