He could not have taken his brother within the king's law unless Allah had willed. We raise in degrees whom We will, and over every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine providence and how Allah's wisdom operates beyond human comprehension. While Joseph implemented a clever plan that appeared to be his own strategy, it was actually Allah's design working through him. The verse teaches us that true knowledge and power belong to Allah alone, and even when we think we are executing our own plans, we are actually functioning within His greater scheme. It also emphasizes the concept of hierarchical knowledge, reminding us to remain humble as there is always someone more knowledgeable above us, with Allah being the ultimate source of all knowledge.
orig: فبدأ بأوعيتهم قبل وعاء أخيه ثم استخرجها من وعاء أخيه كذلك كدنا ليوسف ما كان ليأخذ أخاه في دين الملك إلا أن يشاء الله نرفع درجات من نشاء وفوق كل ذي علم عليم

translation: They said, "If he steals - a brother of his has stolen before." But Joseph kept it within himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, "You are in a worse position, and Allah knows best the truth of what you describe."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the importance of emotional restraint and dignified response in the face of false accusations. When Joseph's brothers made an indirect attack on his character by referencing a supposed past theft by his brother, he chose to suppress his hurt and anger rather than retaliate immediately. His response teaches us that sometimes silence and internal processing of emotions is more powerful than immediate defensive reactions, while trusting that Allah knows the full truth of matters.
orig: قالوا إن يسرق فقد سرق أخ له من قبل فأسرها يوسف في نفسه ولم يبدها لهم قال أنتم شر مكانا والله أعلم بما تصفون

translation: They said, "O 'Aziz! He has a very old father, so take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you as one of the righteous."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound depth of familial bonds and sacrifice in Islamic teachings. The brothers' willingness to substitute themselves for Benjamin shows that despite their past mistakes, they had developed genuine compassion and responsibility. It demonstrates how true repentance and moral growth can transform people from being selfish to selfless, willing to sacrifice their own freedom to protect both their younger brother and their elderly father from further pain.
orig: قالوا يا أيها العزيز إن له أبا شيخا كبيرا فخذ أحدنا مكانه إنا نراك من المحسنين

translation: He said, "God forbid that we should take anyone except the one with whom we found our property. Indeed, we would then be wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the principle of justice and accountability in Islam, highlighting that punishing an innocent person for another's crime is a form of oppression that goes against divine principles. It emphasizes the importance of targeting the actual perpetrator rather than an arbitrary substitute, demonstrating that justice must be precise and directed at those who are truly responsible for wrongdoing.
orig: قال معاذ الله أن نأخذ إلا من وجدنا متاعنا عنده إنا إذا لظالمون

translation: So when they had despaired of him, they secluded themselves in private consultation. The eldest of them said, "Do you not know that your father has taken from you an oath by Allah and [that] before you failed in [your duty to] Joseph? So I will never leave [this] land until my father permits me or Allah decides for me, and He is the best of judges."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power of conscience and moral responsibility. The eldest brother's stance represents a transformative moment where past guilt leads to moral redemption. His refusal to return without resolution shows how past mistakes can become catalysts for ethical growth, while acknowledging divine authority as the ultimate arbiter of human affairs.
orig: فلما استيأسوا منه خلصوا نجيا قال كبيرهم ألم تعلموا أن أباكم قد أخذ عليكم موثقا من الله ومن قبل ما فرطتم في يوسف فلن أبرح الأرض حتى يأذن لي أبي أو يحكم الله لي وهو خير الحاكمين

translation: Return to your father and say, 'O our father! Your son has stolen. We testify only to what we know, and we could not be guardians of the unseen.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the complex moral dilemma faced by Joseph's brothers, who must deliver difficult news to their elderly father. Their statement reflects a careful attempt to distance themselves from full responsibility while acknowledging their limited perspective, showing how humans often try to soften the impact of painful truths by qualifying their role in events.
orig: ارجعوا إلى أبيكم فقولوا يا أبانا إن ابنك سرق وما شهدنا إلا بما علمنا وما كنا للغيب حافظين

translation: And ask the city in which we were and the caravan in which we came, and indeed, we are truthful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking verification and evidence to support claims. It demonstrates that even when one is telling the truth, it's perfectly acceptable and sometimes necessary to provide proof or witnesses to establish credibility. The reference to asking both the city and the caravan suggests that multiple sources of verification can be consulted to establish truth.
orig: واسأل القرية التي كنا فيها والعير التي أقبلنا فيها وإنا لصادقون

translation: He said: "Nay, your souls have made up a tale. So patience is most fitting. May Allah bring them all to me. Indeed, He is the All-Knowing, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound trust in divine providence during times of personal crisis. When Jacob responds to his sons' claim about Joseph's fate, his response reflects not just fatherly wisdom but spiritual maturity. Rather than succumbing to despair, he chooses beautiful patience (sabr jameel), demonstrating that true faith means maintaining hope and composure even when circumstances appear hopeless. His statement shows that he suspects deception but chooses to defer judgment to Allah, trusting in His wisdom to eventually reveal the truth and reunite his family.
orig: قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا فصبر جميل عسى الله أن يأتيني بهم جميعا إنه هو العليم الحكيم

translation: And he turned away from them and said, "O my sorrow over Joseph," and his eyes became white with grief, for he was [of that] a suppressor
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound depth of paternal love and the physical manifestation of emotional pain. Prophet Jacob's grief over losing his son Joseph was so intense that it affected his eyesight, yet he maintained dignified restraint, choosing to suppress his anguish rather than complain to others. This teaches us that even the prophets experienced human emotions, and that while feeling deep sorrow is natural, maintaining composure and directing complaints only to Allah is a sign of true faith.
orig: وتولى عنهم وقال يا أسفى على يوسف وابيضت عيناه من الحزن فهو كظيم

translation: They said: "By Allah, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become fatally ill or become among those who perish."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound depth of paternal love and grief, showing how emotional pain can be misunderstood by others. Prophet Jacob's children saw his constant remembrance of Joseph as harmful obsession, but it actually reflected his unwavering faith in Allah's promise and his deep spiritual connection that allowed him to sense Joseph was still alive. It teaches us that what others may view as excessive attachment might actually be a manifestation of deep faith and spiritual insight.
orig: قالوا تالله تفتأ تذكر يوسف حتى تكون حرضا أو تكون من الهالكين

translation: He said, "I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah, and I know from Allah that which you do not know."
interpretation: This verse reveals the essence of true reliance on Allah during hardship. Prophet Ya'qub's statement teaches us that while experiencing intense emotional pain, the most therapeutic and beneficial approach is to direct our complaints exclusively to Allah rather than spreading our grievances to others. His words also indicate a deep spiritual wisdom and connection with Allah that enables him to maintain hope and faith despite his apparent loss, knowing through divine insight that there is a greater plan at work that others cannot perceive.
orig: قال إنما أشكو بثي وحزني إلى الله وأعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: O my sons, go and seek news of Joseph and his brother and do not despair of Allah's mercy. Indeed, no one despairs of Allah's mercy except the disbelieving people
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining hope and optimism in the face of adversity. Ya'qub's statement to his sons teaches us that persistence and continuous effort, coupled with unwavering faith in Allah's mercy, are essential characteristics of a believer. The connection between despair and disbelief suggests that maintaining hope is not just an emotional state but a fundamental aspect of faith, as true believers understand that Allah's power and mercy are limitless.
orig: يا بني اذهبوا فتحسسوا من يوسف وأخيه ولا تيأسوا من روح الله إنه لا ييأس من روح الله إلا القوم الكافرون

translation: When they entered upon him, they said, "O Exalted one, adversity has touched us and our family, and we have come with meager merchandise. So give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the transformative power of hardship in breaking down pride and social barriers. Joseph's brothers, who once acted with arrogance, now approach him with humility and desperation, demonstrating how circumstances can change human behavior and bring about spiritual growth. Their plea for charity, despite their previous wrongdoing, shows that Allah creates situations that lead people to recognize their dependence on divine mercy and human compassion.
orig: فلما دخلوا عليه قالوا يا أيها العزيز مسنا وأهلنا الضر وجئنا ببضاعة مزجاة فأوف لنا الكيل وتصدق علينا إن الله يجزي المتصدقين

translation: He said: "Do you know what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of confrontation where Joseph reveals his identity to his brothers, reminding them of their past misdeeds. The question is rhetorical, aimed at evoking reflection and remorse in the brothers' hearts, while also emphasizing how ignorance and emotional immaturity can lead people to commit grave injustices against their own family members.
orig: قال هل علمتم ما فعلتم بيوسف وأخيه إذ أنتم جاهلون

translation: They said, "Are you really Joseph?" He said, "I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has surely been gracious to us. Indeed, he who fears Allah and is patient - Allah never wastes the reward of the doers of good."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound spiritual principle that hardship and separation can ultimately lead to divine rewards when faced with patience and God-consciousness. Joseph's revelation of his identity after years of separation from his brothers demonstrates that maintaining moral integrity and trust in Allah's plan, despite severe trials, will eventually lead to triumph and reconciliation. The verse emphasizes that righteous conduct and perseverance through adversity are never overlooked by Allah.
orig: قالوا أإنك لأنت يوسف قال أنا يوسف وهذا أخي قد من الله علينا إنه من يتق ويصبر فإن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

translation: They said, "By Allah, certainly Allah has preferred you over us, and we have been sinful."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound moment of recognition and repentance when Joseph's brothers finally acknowledge their past wrongdoing. Their admission reflects a deep transformation from jealousy to humility, showing how divine justice ultimately leads to truth and reconciliation, even among those who once harbored intense resentment.
orig: قالوا تالله لقد آثرك الله علينا وإن كنا لخاطئين

translation: He said: "No reproach on you this day. May Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy."
interpretation: This verse exemplifies the pinnacle of forgiveness and magnanimity in human relations, as demonstrated by Prophet Yusuf towards his brothers. Despite their past betrayal, his response teaches us that true strength lies in pardoning others when we have power over them, and that letting go of past grievances opens the door to divine mercy and healing of relationships.
orig: قال لا تثريب عليكم اليوم يغفر الله لكم وهو أرحم الراحمين

translation: Take this shirt of mine and cast it over my father's face, he will recover his sight. And bring me all your family.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound spiritual connection between Prophet Yusuf and his father Ya'qub, showing how divine healing can work through physical objects that carry spiritual significance. The shirt, bearing Yusuf's scent and essence, serves as a medium of miraculous healing, demonstrating that Allah's power to heal can manifest through seemingly ordinary items when they're connected to pure faith and divine purpose.
orig: اذهبوا بقميصي هذا فألقوه على وجه أبي يأت بصيرا وأتوني بأهلكم أجمعين

translation: And when the caravan departed, their father said, "Indeed, I find the scent of Joseph, if you did not think me weakened in mind."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound spiritual and emotional connection between Prophet Jacob and his son Joseph, demonstrating how true love and faith can transcend physical limitations. Jacob's ability to sense his son's presence from afar reflects both his prophetic intuition and the depth of paternal love, even when others doubted his perception. It teaches us that spiritual truths and emotional bonds can sometimes be felt beyond rational explanation.
orig: ولما فصلت العير قال أبوهم إني لأجد ريح يوسف لولا أن تفندون

translation: They said, "By Allah, you are certainly in your old error."
interpretation: This verse reflects how people often resist change and cling to their preconceptions, even when confronted with truth. The use of "old error" suggests that familiar patterns of thinking, no matter how incorrect, can become deeply ingrained and difficult to abandon. It's a powerful commentary on human nature's tendency to remain comfortable with established beliefs rather than embrace new truths.
orig: قالوا تالله إنك لفي ضلالك القديم

translation: Then, when the bearer of good news arrived, he cast it over his face, and he regained his sight. He said, 'Did I not tell you that I know from Allah what you do not know?'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound faith of Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob) and demonstrates that unwavering trust in Allah's plan will ultimately lead to relief. Despite years of blindness and separation from his son Yusuf (Joseph), Ya'qub's spiritual insight and conviction never wavered. The moment symbolizes how emotional healing and physical restoration can occur simultaneously through divine intervention, validating the spiritual wisdom of those who maintain hope in Allah's mercy even during prolonged hardship.
orig: فلما أن جاء البشير ألقاه على وجهه فارتد بصيرا قال ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون

translation: They said: "O our father! Ask forgiveness for our sins, indeed we have been sinners."
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound human capacity for recognizing one's mistakes and seeking redemption through both divine and familial channels. The children's request for their father's intercession suggests that spiritual healing often involves reconciliation within family relationships, and acknowledges the special position parents hold as intermediaries in seeking divine forgiveness.
orig: قالوا يا أبانا استغفر لنا ذنوبنا إنا كنا خاطئين

translation: He said, "I shall ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful."
interpretation: This verse demonstrates Prophet Ya'qub's deep compassion and spiritual maturity in dealing with his sons' wrongdoing. Despite their grave sin against their brother Yusuf, he doesn't immediately condemn them but instead promises to seek divine forgiveness on their behalf, showing that true parental love includes guiding children back to the path of righteousness through mercy rather than punishment.
orig: قال سوف أستغفر لكم ربي إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to himself and said, "Enter Egypt, Allah willing, safe [and secure]."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound emotional and spiritual significance of family reunification and divine timing. Joseph's act of embracing his parents represents not just physical shelter but spiritual and emotional refuge after years of separation. His invitation to enter Egypt with safety reflects how positions of power should be used to protect and provide for family, while the phrase "Allah willing" demonstrates that even in moments of triumph, one should maintain humility and acknowledge divine providence.
orig: فلما دخلوا على يوسف آوى إليه أبويه وقال ادخلوا مصر إن شاء الله آمنين

translation: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration. And he said, "O my father! This is the interpretation of my dream from before. My Lord has made it true. And He has been good to me when He released me from prison and brought you [here] from bedouin life after Satan had caused discord between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, He is the Knowing, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine plan's perfect completion and Allah's wisdom in orchestrating events over time. Prophet Yusuf's childhood dream finally manifests, showing how Allah's plans unfold gradually but perfectly. The prostration wasn't worship but a cultural gesture of respect, demonstrating how seemingly negative events (imprisonment, family separation) can ultimately lead to positive outcomes through Allah's subtle planning. It teaches us about patience during hardship and trust in Allah's wisdom, as every difficulty may be part of a greater divine plan we cannot yet see.
orig: ورفع أبويه على العرش وخروا له سجدا وقال يا أبت هذا تأويل رؤياي من قبل قد جعلها ربي حقا وقد أحسن بي إذ أخرجني من السجن وجاء بكم من البدو من بعد أن نزغ الشيطان بيني وبين إخوتي إن ربي لطيف لما يشاء إنه هو العليم الحكيم

translation: My Lord, You have given me [something] of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector in this world and in the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse reflects Prophet Yusuf's profound gratitude and humility despite his elevated status. Despite being granted power and special abilities, he acknowledges that these gifts are from Allah and seeks an ending that prioritizes spiritual success over worldly achievements. His prayer demonstrates that even those blessed with authority and knowledge should ultimately aspire to die in a state of submission to Allah and be among the righteous, rather than being attached to worldly position.
orig: رب قد آتيتني من الملك وعلمتني من تأويل الأحاديث فاطر السماوات والأرض أنت وليي في الدنيا والآخرة توفني مسلما وألحقني بالصالحين

translation: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. And you were not with them when they agreed on their plan while they were conspiring.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of Prophet Muhammad's knowledge about historical events, particularly the story of Prophet Yusuf. It serves as a proof of Muhammad's prophethood since he couldn't have known these detailed accounts without divine revelation, as he wasn't present during these historical events. The verse also highlights how Allah's truth prevails over human schemes and conspiracies, even when plotted in secret.
orig: ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك وما كنت لديهم إذ أجمعوا أمرهم وهم يمكرون

translation: And most people will not believe even if you desire it eagerly
interpretation: This verse conveys a profound truth about human nature and free will, indicating that guidance and faith cannot be forced upon people, even by those who most earnestly wish to guide them. It serves as a consolation to those who strive to spread truth, reminding them that their responsibility lies in conveying the message, not in ensuring its acceptance.
orig: وما أكثر الناس ولو حرصت بمؤمنين

translation: And you do not ask them for any reward for it. It is nothing but a reminder for all the worlds
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the pure intention and sincerity of Prophet Muhammad's mission. By highlighting that he seeks no worldly compensation for conveying Allah's message, it establishes that his sole motivation is to guide humanity toward divine truth. The message of Islam is presented as a universal reminder, not limited by time, place, or culture, but accessible to all of creation.
orig: وما تسألهم عليه من أجر إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: And how many signs in the heavens and earth do they pass by while they are turning away from them
interpretation: This verse highlights humanity's tendency to overlook the abundant signs of Allah's existence and power that surround us in creation. Despite being immersed in a universe filled with remarkable phenomena and perfect order - from celestial bodies to Earth's ecosystems - people often remain heedless, choosing to ignore these clear indicators of divine design and purpose.
orig: وكأين من آية في السماوات والأرض يمرون عليها وهم عنها معرضون

translation: And most of them do not believe in Allah except while associating others with Him
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound psychological insight into human nature, where people may claim belief in God while their actions and attitudes reflect a form of hidden polytheism. This could manifest in placing ultimate trust in worldly means, following desires as if they were deities, or attributing divine qualities to other entities. It points to the subtle nature of shirk (polytheism) that can infiltrate one's faith even while claiming monotheism.
orig: وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون

translation: Do they feel secure that an overwhelming punishment from Allah will not come to them, or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?
interpretation: This verse serves as a powerful reminder about the danger of complacency in faith. It warns that those who live in heedlessness, feeling secure in their ways without genuine consciousness of Allah, are in a precarious position. Their false sense of security might be shattered at any moment by divine punishment or the sudden arrival of the Day of Judgment, catching them completely unprepared for the ultimate reckoning that awaits all souls.
orig: أفأمنوا أن تأتيهم غاشية من عذاب الله أو تأتيهم الساعة بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: Say, "This is my way: I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah; and I am not of those who associate others with Him."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of spreading Islam with wisdom and clear understanding, rather than blind following. It highlights that true da'wah (invitation to Islam) must be based on knowledge and insight (basirah), suggesting that one should understand what they're calling others to. The mention of "I and those who follow me" establishes a chain of responsibility where each believer becomes a carrier of this message, but only when equipped with proper understanding.
orig: قل هذه سبيلي أدعو إلى الله على بصيرة أنا ومن اتبعني وسبحان الله وما أنا من المشركين

translation: And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed [Our message] from among the people of cities. Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine messengers have always been human beings, not supernatural entities, chosen from among ordinary people living in communities. It challenges skeptics to study history and learn from the fate of previous civilizations that rejected their prophets. The verse concludes by highlighting that eternal success in the afterlife, achieved through God-consciousness, is far superior to any worldly achievements, urging people to use their intellect to understand this fundamental truth.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك إلا رجالا نوحي إليهم من أهل القرى أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم ولدار الآخرة خير للذين اتقوا أفلا تعقلون

translation: Until when the messengers despaired and thought that they were denied, Our help came to them, and whoever We willed was saved. And Our punishment cannot be repelled from the criminal people
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound test of faith that even prophets endured, highlighting that divine help often comes at the moment of greatest despair. It teaches that moments of extreme hardship are not signs of abandonment by Allah, but rather the prelude to divine intervention, though this deliverance is selective based on Allah's wisdom and justice. The verse also emphasizes that when divine punishment is decreed for those who persist in wrongdoing, it becomes inevitable.
orig: حتى إذا استيأس الرسل وظنوا أنهم قد كذبوا جاءهم نصرنا فنجي من نشاء ولا يرد بأسنا عن القوم المجرمين

translation: Indeed, in their stories is a lesson for people of understanding. This [Qur'an] is not a fabricated narration, but a confirmation of what came before it and a detailed explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy for people who believe.
interpretation: The stories of past prophets and nations serve as profound spiritual mirrors, reflecting timeless patterns of human behavior and divine interaction. These accounts aren't merely historical narratives but contain deep wisdom that resonates with those who reflect deeply. Their authenticity is reinforced by their consistency with previous divine revelations, demonstrating a continuous thread of divine guidance throughout human history.
orig: لقد كان في قصصهم عبرة لأولي الألباب ما كان حديثا يفترى ولكن تصديق الذي بين يديه وتفصيل كل شيء وهدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Alif Lam Mim Ra. These are the verses of the Book; and that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most people do not believe
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine authenticity of the Qur'an by asserting that its source is directly from Allah. The mysterious letters at the beginning serve as a reminder of the miraculous nature of the Qur'an's language, while also highlighting that despite the clear evidence of its divine origin, human nature tends to resist accepting truth even when it's presented clearly before them.
orig: المر تلك آيات الكتاب والذي أنزل إليك من ربك الحق ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: It is Allah who raised the heavens without pillars that you [can] see; then He established Himself above the Throne and made subject the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. He arranges [each] matter; He details the signs that you may, of the meeting with your Lord, be certain.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute power over the cosmos, demonstrating His engineering of a universe that defies human comprehension. The invisible forces holding up the heavens suggest scientific principles like gravity, which weren't known at the time of revelation. The mention of celestial bodies following precise orbits points to the perfect mathematical precision in the universe, while the reference to "arranging matters" indicates Allah's continuous involvement in sustaining and managing creation rather than a one-time act of creation.
orig: الله الذي رفع السماوات بغير عمد ترونها ثم استوى على العرش وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى يدبر الأمر يفصل الآيات لعلكم بلقاء ربكم توقنون

translation: And it is He who spread the earth and placed therein firmly set mountains and rivers; and from all of the fruits He made therein two mates. He causes the night to cover the day. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's perfect design of Earth's ecosystem and the principle of duality in creation. The mention of mountains, rivers, and fruits growing in pairs points to the intricate balance in nature that sustains life. The alternation of day and night further emphasizes this divine orchestration, suggesting that nothing in creation is random but rather carefully planned to maintain life and provide evidence of Allah's existence for those who contemplate deeply.
orig: وهو الذي مد الأرض وجعل فيها رواسي وأنهارا ومن كل الثمرات جعل فيها زوجين اثنين يغشي الليل النهار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: And in the land are neighboring tracts, and gardens of vines and crops and palm trees, growing in clusters or standing alone, watered with one water; but We favor some of them above others in taste. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's perfect wisdom and power through agricultural diversity. Despite sharing the same soil and water, plants produce different fruits and yields, demonstrating that external factors alone don't determine outcomes. This serves as a metaphor for human diversity - how people, given the same opportunities and guidance, can develop differently based on their individual responses and choices. It's a profound lesson about divine wisdom in creation and the importance of using our intellect to reflect on these natural phenomena.
orig: وفي الأرض قطع متجاورات وجنات من أعناب وزرع ونخيل صنوان وغير صنوان يسقى بماء واحد ونفضل بعضها على بعض في الأكل إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يعقلون

translation: And if you are astonished, then astonishing is their saying: "When we are dust, will we indeed be in a new creation?" Those are the ones who have disbelieved in their Lord, and those will have shackles upon their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound spiritual blindness of those who reject the concept of resurrection. Their skepticism about being recreated after death reveals their limited understanding of Allah's infinite power. Just as Allah created them from nothing the first time, He can certainly restore them from dust. Their disbelief in resurrection is portrayed as a form of mental and spiritual bondage, symbolized by the shackles around their necks, which will ultimately lead them to eternal suffering.
orig: وإن تعجب فعجب قولهم أإذا كنا ترابا أإنا لفي خلق جديد أولئك الذين كفروا بربهم وأولئك الأغلال في أعناقهم وأولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

translation: They seek to hasten the bad before the good, while similar examples have already passed before them. And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing, and indeed your Lord is severe in punishment
interpretation: This verse reveals the paradoxical nature of human impatience, where people often rush to challenge divine warnings and mock the threat of punishment, rather than hastening towards good deeds and mercy. It reflects how humans, despite historical lessons of those who doubted before them, continue to test Allah's patience. The verse also beautifully balances Allah's dual nature - His vast mercy and forgiveness even towards those who wrong themselves, alongside His capability for severe punishment, suggesting that while His mercy is expansive, it shouldn't be taken for granted.
orig: ويستعجلونك بالسيئة قبل الحسنة وقد خلت من قبلهم المثلات وإن ربك لذو مغفرة للناس على ظلمهم وإن ربك لشديد العقاب

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" You are only a warner, and for every people is a guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the eternal pattern of denial where skeptics demand miraculous signs as proof of divine message. However, the role of a prophet or messenger is primarily to warn and guide, not to perform miracles on demand. Just as different communities have had their own guides throughout history, each suited to their specific context and needs, the universal message adapts to reach different peoples while maintaining its core truth.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه إنما أنت منذر ولكل قوم هاد

translation: Allah knows what every female carries and what the wombs lose [prematurely] or exceed. And everything with Him is by due measure
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite and precise knowledge of creation, particularly highlighting His awareness of the intricate details of pregnancy and fetal development. It suggests that nothing in existence, no matter how minute or concealed, escapes Allah's knowledge, and every occurrence - whether it's a miscarriage, a full-term pregnancy, or an extended gestation - happens according to His divine plan and measure.
orig: الله يعلم ما تحمل كل أنثى وما تغيض الأرحام وما تزداد وكل شيء عنده بمقدار

translation: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Most Great, the Most High
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete and comprehensive knowledge that encompasses both what is hidden from creation and what is apparent, while also highlighting His supreme status above all creation. The pairing of "unseen and witnessed" suggests that nothing escapes Allah's knowledge, whether it's hidden in hearts, buried in the earth, or visible to all.
orig: عالم الغيب والشهادة الكبير المتعال

translation: It is the same [to Him] whether any of you conceals his speech or declares it openly, whether he lies hidden by night or walks forth freely by day
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's complete and comprehensive knowledge of all human affairs, emphasizing that nothing can be hidden from divine awareness. The mention of different states - secrecy and openness, night and day - demonstrates that Allah's knowledge transcends all temporal and physical barriers, rendering any attempt at concealment futile. It serves as both a warning to those who think they can hide their misdeeds and a comfort to those who suffer in silence, knowing that Allah is fully aware of their situation.
orig: سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار

translation: For each one there are successive [angels] before and behind him who protect him by the decree of Allah. Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah intends for a people ill, there is no repelling it. And there is not for them besides Him any patron.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound relationship between divine protection and human responsibility. While Allah provides guardianship through His angels, the verse establishes a fundamental principle of social and personal change: transformation begins from within. God's help and protection are constant, but positive change requires human initiative and self-improvement. Conversely, when a society persists in wrongdoing and corruption to the point where divine punishment becomes decreed, no force can prevent it, highlighting the importance of maintaining moral and spiritual integrity before reaching a point of no return.
orig: له معقبات من بين يديه ومن خلفه يحفظونه من أمر الله إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم وإذا أراد الله بقوم سوءا فلا مرد له وما لهم من دونه من وال

translation: He is the One Who shows you lightning, inspiring fear and hope, and produces heavy clouds.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's absolute power over nature and its dual impact on human psychology. The lightning serves as a metaphor for divine signs, creating simultaneous feelings of fear (of destruction) and hope (for life-giving rain) in human hearts. This duality reminds us that Allah's manifestations in nature carry both warning and mercy, teaching us to maintain a balance between fear of His punishment and hope in His benevolence.
orig: هو الذي يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا وينشئ السحاب الثقال

translation: The thunder glorifies His praises, as do the angels in awe of Him, and He sends thunderbolts striking with them whom He wills, yet they dispute about Allah while He is severe in might
interpretation: This verse illustrates the paradox between divine power and human arrogance. While even the mightiest forces of nature, symbolized by thunder, submit to Allah's will and recognize His greatness, and the celestial beings tremble in His presence, humans persist in their skepticism and argumentation. The thunderbolts serve as a reminder that Allah's power can manifest at any moment, demonstrating that despite human denial or debate, divine authority remains absolute and uncontested.
orig: ويسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته ويرسل الصواعق فيصيب بها من يشاء وهم يجادلون في الله وهو شديد المحال

translation: To Him belongs the call of truth. Those whom they call upon besides Him do not respond to them with anything, except like one who stretches his hands toward water to reach his mouth, but it cannot reach it. And the supplication of the disbelievers is nothing but in error.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of praying to false deities through a powerful metaphor. Just as someone cannot quench their thirst by merely gesturing at water from a distance without actually bringing it to their mouth, similarly those who pray to false gods or idols will never have their prayers answered. It's an exercise in futility, like trying to grasp water without actually being able to drink it. The verse emphasizes that true prayer and worship should be directed only to Allah, as He alone has the power to respond and fulfill supplications.
orig: له دعوة الحق والذين يدعون من دونه لا يستجيبون لهم بشيء إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه وما هو ببالغه وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and so do their shadows in the mornings and the afternoons
interpretation: This verse illustrates the universal submission to Allah's divine laws, both in the physical and spiritual realms. Even those who deny God's existence are unconsciously submitting to His natural laws, while their shadows' prostration represents how every particle in existence follows divine patterns without choice. The mention of mornings and afternoons signifies the continuous nature of this cosmic submission throughout time.
orig: ولله يسجد من في السماوات والأرض طوعا وكرها وظلالهم بالغدو والآصال

translation: Say, "Who is the Lord of the heavens and earth?" Say, "Allah." Say, "Have you then taken besides Him allies who do not possess for themselves benefit or harm?" Say, "Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Or is darkness equivalent to light? Or have they attributed to Allah partners who created like His creation so that the creation seemed similar to them?" Say, "Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing."
interpretation: This verse establishes a powerful argument for monotheism by highlighting the logical inconsistency in associating partners with Allah. It uses contrasting pairs (blind/seeing, darkness/light) to illustrate the stark difference between true divine authority and false deities. The verse challenges those who worship other deities by pointing out that these supposed partners cannot even benefit or harm themselves, let alone others. It emphasizes Allah's unique position as the sole Creator through a rhetorical question about creation, suggesting that if there were other gods, they would need to demonstrate creative powers equal to Allah's, which they cannot.
orig: قل من رب السماوات والأرض قل الله قل أفاتخذتم من دونه أولياء لا يملكون لأنفسهم نفعا ولا ضرا قل هل يستوي الأعمى والبصير أم هل تستوي الظلمات والنور أم جعلوا لله شركاء خلقوا كخلقه فتشابه الخلق عليهم قل الله خالق كل شيء وهو الواحد القهار

translation: He sends down water from the sky, causing valleys to flow according to their capacity, and the torrent carries rising foam. And from that [ore] which they heat in the fire, desiring adornments and utensils, is a foam like it. Thus Allah presents [the example of] truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it vanishes, being cast off; but as for that which benefits the people, it remains on the earth.
interpretation: This verse presents a profound metaphor comparing truth and falsehood to natural phenomena. Just as pure water remains while foam disappears, and pure metal endures while dross is discarded, divine truth persists while falsehood eventually vanishes. The metaphor suggests that although falsehood may temporarily appear prominent or overwhelming, like foam on water or dross on metal, it lacks substance and permanence. Only what is genuinely beneficial and true will endure, just as pure water sustains life and refined metal serves useful purposes.
orig: أنزل من السماء ماء فسالت أودية بقدرها فاحتمل السيل زبدا رابيا ومما يوقدون عليه في النار ابتغاء حلية أو متاع زبد مثله كذلك يضرب الله الحق والباطل فأما الزبد فيذهب جفاء وأما ما ينفع الناس فيمكث في الأرض كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال

translation: For those who respond to their Lord is the best [reward], but those who do not respond to Him - if they had all that is in the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would [attempt to] ransom themselves with it. Those will have the worst account, and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stark contrast between the ultimate outcomes of faith and rejection, emphasizing that material wealth, no matter how vast, cannot substitute for spiritual accountability. It suggests that when facing divine judgment, even those who rejected faith would desperately offer everything they own to escape punishment, but such attempts at redemption would be futile at that point, highlighting the importance of responding to divine guidance during one's lifetime rather than facing regret in the afterlife.
orig: للذين استجابوا لربهم الحسنى والذين لم يستجيبوا له لو أن لهم ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه لافتدوا به أولئك لهم سوء الحساب ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المهاد

translation: Is one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? Only those of understanding will be reminded.
interpretation: This verse draws a stark distinction between spiritual insight and spiritual blindness, suggesting that true knowledge leads to recognition of divine truth. Those who possess intellectual and spiritual discernment ("people of understanding") can perceive the authenticity of divine revelation, while others remain in a state of spiritual blindness, unable to recognize or accept the truth despite its clarity.
orig: أفمن يعلم أنما أنزل إليك من ربك الحق كمن هو أعمى إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the contract
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic virtue of trustworthiness and keeping one's word. It suggests that true believers are characterized by their unwavering commitment to their promises, whether these are explicit contracts or implicit moral obligations. The use of both "covenant" and "contract" indicates that this applies to our spiritual commitment to Allah as well as our worldly dealings with fellow humans.
orig: الذين يوفون بعهد الله ولا ينقضون الميثاق

translation: And those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined, and fear their Lord, and dread the terrible reckoning
interpretation: This verse speaks to the profound importance of maintaining strong bonds and relationships that Allah has ordained, particularly family ties and social connections. The emphasis on fearing Allah and dreading accountability suggests that nurturing these connections isn't merely a social obligation but a divine mandate that carries spiritual consequences. The combination of joining what Allah commands and fear of accountability indicates that genuine relationships should be maintained with sincere intentions and consciousness of divine oversight.
orig: والذين يصلون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويخشون ربهم ويخافون سوء الحساب

translation: And those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord, and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them secretly and publicly and prevent evil with good - those will have the good consequence of [this] home
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound spiritual principle that true success comes through maintaining patience and steadfastness in faith while actively contributing to society's betterment. The mention of both secret and public charity suggests that sincere actions, regardless of visibility, contribute to spiritual growth. The concept of repelling evil with good indicates that positive actions have a transformative power that can break cycles of negativity and create lasting positive change in both individual lives and society.
orig: والذين صبروا ابتغاء وجه ربهم وأقاموا الصلاة وأنفقوا مما رزقناهم سرا وعلانية ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة أولئك لهم عقبى الدار

translation: Gardens of Eden, which they will enter along with the righteous among their ancestors, spouses, and descendants. And angels will enter upon them from every gate.
interpretation: This verse paints a beautiful picture of the interconnectedness of family bonds in Paradise, suggesting that righteousness can create a spiritual legacy that unites families eternally. The mention of angels entering from every gate indicates both honor and complete divine protection, symbolizing that the inhabitants will receive endless hospitality and care from all directions in their eternal abode.
orig: جنات عدن يدخلونها ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم والملائكة يدخلون عليهم من كل باب

translation: Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that patience and perseverance in faith will be rewarded with eternal peace in the afterlife. The divine greeting of "peace" represents not just a mere salutation, but a comprehensive state of tranquility and contentment bestowed upon those who remained steadfast through life's trials. The phrase "excellent is the final home" suggests that whatever hardships were endured in the worldly life pale in comparison to the ultimate reward of Paradise.
orig: سلام عليكم بما صبرتم فنعم عقبى الدار

translation: Those who break Allah's covenant after its ratification, and sever what Allah has ordered to be joined, and cause corruption on earth - for them is the curse, and they will have the worst home
interpretation: This verse warns against three destructive behaviors that lead to divine punishment: breaking sacred promises, severing relationships that Allah commands us to maintain (such as family ties), and spreading corruption. The severity of these actions is highlighted by the fact that they contradict the fundamental Islamic principles of trustworthiness, maintaining social bonds, and promoting goodness. The mention of "worst home" refers to their ultimate destination in the Hereafter, emphasizing the lasting consequences of such destructive behavior.
orig: والذين ينقضون عهد الله من بعد ميثاقه ويقطعون ما أمر الله به أن يوصل ويفسدون في الأرض أولئك لهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. And they rejoice in the worldly life, while the worldly life is not, compared to the Hereafter, except [brief] enjoyment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the temporary nature of material success and how it can deceive people. While some may have abundance and others scarcity - both conditions being divine tests - many become deluded by worldly prosperity, forgetting that it's merely a passing pleasure compared to the eternal life to come. The verse serves as a reminder that we shouldn't become overly attached to or prideful about worldly possessions, as they're insignificant compared to what awaits in the Hereafter.
orig: الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر وفرحوا بالحياة الدنيا وما الحياة الدنيا في الآخرة إلا متاع

translation: And those who disbelieve say: "Why is not a sign sent down to him from his Lord?" Say: "Indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him]"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine principle of guidance and misguidance, emphasizing that spiritual guidance is not merely about external signs or miracles, but rather about one's inner disposition and willingness to turn towards Allah. Those who sincerely seek truth with an open heart will find guidance, while those who remain obstinate in their disbelief will continue to demand signs yet remain astray, regardless of how many proofs they are shown.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه قل إن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي إليه من أناب

translation: Those who believe and whose hearts find comfort in the remembrance of Allah. Truly, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find comfort
interpretation: This verse reveals the profound psychological and spiritual truth that genuine peace and tranquility can only be achieved through maintaining a constant connection with the Divine. Just as a compass needle becomes unstable when moved away from magnetic north, the human heart experiences anxiety and restlessness when disconnected from its spiritual center. The repetition of "remembrance of Allah" emphasizes that no worldly solution, material possession, or human relationship can provide the deep, lasting comfort that comes from divine consciousness.
orig: الذين آمنوا وتطمئن قلوبهم بذكر الله ألا بذكر الله تطمئن القلوب

translation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds - blessed are they and beautiful is their final return
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine promise of ultimate success, indicating that true fulfillment and happiness aren't just about worldly achievements but rather the combination of sincere faith and positive action. The word "طوبى" (tuba) suggests a state of perfect contentment and joy that awaits those who align their beliefs with righteous conduct, pointing to the inseparable nature of faith and good deeds in Islamic spirituality.
orig: الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات طوبى لهم وحسن مآب

translation: Thus We have sent you to a nation before which other nations have passed away, so that you may recite to them what We revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say: "He is my Lord; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I rely, and to Him is my return."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine guidance throughout human history, showing how each messenger faces similar challenges of resistance and disbelief. The Prophet's mission is placed within this historical context, highlighting that despite people's rejection of Allah's mercy, the messenger's role is to maintain unwavering faith and complete reliance on Allah, serving as a model of steadfast devotion amidst opposition.
orig: كذلك أرسلناك في أمة قد خلت من قبلها أمم لتتلو عليهم الذي أوحينا إليك وهم يكفرون بالرحمن قل هو ربي لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وإليه متاب

translation: And if there were a Qur'an by which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be cleft, or the dead could be made to speak - but to Allah belongs all affairs. Have not those who believe known that if Allah had willed, He would have guided all people? And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by calamity for what they have done, or it will descend near their homes, until Allah's promise comes. Indeed, Allah never fails in His promise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the supreme power of Allah and the limitations of human expectations. Even if people demand miraculous signs, the true purpose of the Qur'an is spiritual guidance rather than supernatural demonstrations. The verse consoles believers who might feel frustrated by others' rejection of faith, reminding them that guidance ultimately comes from Allah's will. It also warns disbelievers that their rejection has consequences, with divine retribution manifesting either through direct calamities or nearby events, serving as continuous reminders until Allah's final judgment arrives.
orig: ولو أن قرآنا سيرت به الجبال أو قطعت به الأرض أو كلم به الموتى بل لله الأمر جميعا أفلم ييأس الذين آمنوا أن لو يشاء الله لهدى الناس جميعا ولا يزال الذين كفروا تصيبهم بما صنعوا قارعة أو تحل قريبا من دارهم حتى يأتي وعد الله إن الله لا يخلف الميعاد

translation: And messengers before you were ridiculed, but I gave respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them - and how [terrible] was My punishment
interpretation: This verse offers divine consolation to Prophet Muhammad by highlighting a recurring pattern in the history of prophetic missions, where initial mockery and rejection ultimately lead to divine justice. It emphasizes that divine patience shouldn't be mistaken for divine neglect, as Allah's eventual response to persistent disbelief and mockery is both decisive and severe.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فأمليت للذين كفروا ثم أخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب

translation: Is He who is maintaining every soul [in accordance with] what it has earned [like any other]? Yet they ascribe partners to Allah. Say, "Name them! Or do you inform Him of something He does not know on the earth, or [is it] an outward statement?" Rather, their plotting has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they have been averted from the path. And whoever Allah sends astray - there will be for him no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's unique position as the ultimate overseer of all souls and their deeds, while criticizing the illogical nature of polytheism. It challenges those who associate partners with Allah to justify their beliefs, pointing out that they cannot inform Allah of anything He doesn't already know. The verse suggests that such false beliefs are merely superficial statements that have been made to seem appealing through deception, leading people away from truth. When someone chooses to reject divine guidance, they lose their way permanently.
orig: أفمن هو قائم على كل نفس بما كسبت وجعلوا لله شركاء قل سموهم أم تنبئونه بما لا يعلم في الأرض أم بظاهر من القول بل زين للذين كفروا مكرهم وصدوا عن السبيل ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: For them is a punishment in the worldly life, but the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe, and they will not have any protector against Allah
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the dual nature of consequences for those who reject divine guidance, indicating that while they may face hardships and difficulties in this world as a result of their choices, these challenges pale in comparison to what awaits in the afterlife. The absence of a protector against Allah's judgment highlights human vulnerability and the futility of seeking refuge in anything other than divine mercy.
orig: لهم عذاب في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أشق وما لهم من الله من واق

translation: The example of Paradise which is promised to the righteous: beneath it rivers flow, its food is everlasting, and its shade. Such is the end for those who are righteous, while the end of the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stark contrast between eternal rewards and consequences, emphasizing how the righteous will receive a paradise that provides perpetual sustenance and comfort, symbolized by flowing rivers and constant shade, while suggesting that true prosperity isn't just material but includes spiritual peace and lasting contentment.
orig: مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون تجري من تحتها الأنهار أكلها دائم وظلها تلك عقبى الذين اتقوا وعقبى الكافرين النار

translation: And those to whom We have given the Book rejoice in what has been revealed to you, but among the factions are those who deny part of it. Say, "I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate [anything] with Him. To Him I invite, and to Him is my return."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the dichotomy in how divine revelation is received by different groups. Those who possess true understanding of previous scriptures recognize and celebrate the truth in the Qur'an because it confirms their existing knowledge. However, human tendency toward selective acceptance of truth is highlighted by those who reject parts that don't align with their preferences. The verse emphasizes that the core message of all divine revelation is the pure monotheistic worship of Allah, without any partners or intermediaries.
orig: والذين آتيناهم الكتاب يفرحون بما أنزل إليك ومن الأحزاب من ينكر بعضه قل إنما أمرت أن أعبد الله ولا أشرك به إليه أدعو وإليه مآب

translation: And thus We have revealed it as an Arabic legislation. And if you follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would not have against Allah any ally or any protector.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom in revealing the Qur'an in Arabic and serves as a stern warning against compromising divine truth for human desires. It indicates that following personal inclinations or societal pressures after receiving clear divine guidance severs one's connection with Allah's protection and support. The verse establishes that true knowledge requires steadfast adherence to divine guidance rather than human preferences.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه حكما عربيا ولئن اتبعت أهواءهم بعدما جاءك من العلم ما لك من الله من ولي ولا واق

translation: And We have already sent messengers before you and assigned to them wives and descendants. And it was not for a messenger to come with a sign except by permission of Allah. For every term is a decree.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the human nature of prophets and messengers, showing that they lived normal lives with families like other humans. It counters those who might object to prophets having wives and children, while also establishing that miraculous signs come only through divine authorization, not at the prophet's personal discretion. This maintains the balance between the prophets' human attributes and their divine mission.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك وجعلنا لهم أزواجا وذرية وما كان لرسول أن يأتي بآية إلا بإذن الله لكل أجل كتاب

translation: Allah eliminates what He wills or confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book
interpretation: This verse speaks to the divine power of modification and the concept of destiny. While Allah has written all matters in the preserved tablet (Umm al-Kitab), He maintains the authority to alter certain decrees based on His wisdom. This demonstrates that while some matters are fixed and unchangeable, others are subject to modification through factors such as prayer, good deeds, and repentance. It's a profound statement about the dynamic nature of divine will while maintaining absolute divine knowledge.
orig: يمحو الله ما يشاء ويثبت وعنده أم الكتاب

translation: And whether We show you some of what We promise them or cause you to die - upon you is only the [duty of] notification, and upon Us is the account.
interpretation: This verse reassures Prophet Muhammad that his sole responsibility is to convey Allah's message faithfully, regardless of whether he witnesses the promised consequences for the disbelievers during his lifetime. The ultimate judgment and accountability of people's actions rest exclusively with Allah, relieving the Prophet from the burden of ensuring people's acceptance or worrying about the final outcome.
orig: وإن ما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإنما عليك البلاغ وعلينا الحساب

translation: Do they not see that We come to the land and reduce it from its borders? And Allah decides; there is no adjuster of His decision, and He is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse conveys Allah's absolute power over all worldly dominions and empires. It suggests that no matter how mighty or permanent earthly powers may seem, Allah gradually diminishes their influence and territory, demonstrating that all authority ultimately belongs to Him. The reference to reducing land from its borders can be understood as the natural process of how civilizations and powers rise and fall, reminding believers that worldly power is temporary and only Allah's authority is permanent and uncontestable.
orig: أولم يروا أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها والله يحكم لا معقب لحكمه وهو سريع الحساب

translation: Those before them did scheme, but all scheming belongs to Allah. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will soon know who gets the final home.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes divine sovereignty over human plots and schemes, highlighting that no matter how people may plan against truth and justice, Allah's ultimate plan supersedes all. It serves as both a warning to those who oppose divine guidance and a reassurance to believers that wrongdoers' temporary success doesn't negate Allah's overarching control. The mention of "final home" points to the ultimate accountability in the hereafter, where the true consequences of one's actions become evident.
orig: وقد مكر الذين من قبلهم فلله المكر جميعا يعلم ما تكسب كل نفس وسيعلم الكفار لمن عقبى الدار

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger." Say, "Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you, and [so is] whoever has knowledge of the Book."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine authentication doesn't require human validation. When faced with denial of his prophethood, Muhammad is instructed to rely on Allah's testimony and those with genuine scriptural knowledge, suggesting that truth stands firm regardless of opposition and that authentic spiritual wisdom recognizes divine authority without needing external proof.
orig: ويقول الذين كفروا لست مرسلا قل كفى بالله شهيدا بيني وبينكم ومن عنده علم الكتاب

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. [This is] a Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that you might bring mankind out of darknesses into the light by permission of their Lord - to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transformative power of divine guidance, where darkness symbolizes ignorance, disbelief, and moral confusion, while light represents knowledge, faith, and spiritual clarity. The Prophet's mission is portrayed as a divine mandate to guide humanity from a state of spiritual blindness to enlightenment, though this transformation can only occur with Allah's permission, highlighting both human free will and divine sovereignty
orig: الر كتاب أنزلناه إليك لتخرج الناس من الظلمات إلى النور بإذن ربهم إلى صراط العزيز الحميد

translation: Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on earth, and woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and ownership over all creation, both seen and unseen, while simultaneously serving as a stern warning about the consequences of rejecting this fundamental truth. It establishes that everything in existence operates under Allah's dominion, and those who deny this reality are setting themselves up for severe consequences due to their rejection of such a clear and fundamental truth.
orig: الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وويل للكافرين من عذاب شديد

translation: Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter and prevent others from the path of Allah, seeking to make it crooked - they are in extreme error
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual blindness of those who prioritize temporary worldly pleasures and gains over eternal salvation. By actively discouraging others from following Allah's path and attempting to distort religious truths to suit their desires, they demonstrate a profound misunderstanding of life's true purpose. Their actions reflect a deep-seated spiritual confusion that leads them far from divine guidance and ultimate success.
orig: الذين يستحبون الحياة الدنيا على الآخرة ويصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا أولئك في ضلال بعيد

translation: And We did not send any messenger except [speaking] in the language of his people to make clear to them, and Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's divine wisdom in choosing messengers who could effectively communicate with their own people, highlighting that true guidance is a matter of divine will rather than merely understanding the message. The use of familiar language removes any barriers to comprehension, making people fully accountable for their choices, while ultimate guidance remains in Allah's hands according to His perfect wisdom and justice.
orig: وما أرسلنا من رسول إلا بلسان قومه ليبين لهم فيضل الله من يشاء ويهدي من يشاء وهو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs, [saying], "Bring out your people from darkness into light and remind them of the days of Allah." Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how divine guidance serves as a transformative force, with Moses's mission representing the universal journey from spiritual ignorance to enlightenment. The "days of Allah" refers to historical moments of divine intervention that serve as lessons, suggesting that spiritual growth requires both patience during hardship and gratitude during prosperity. The transformation from darkness to light symbolizes not just a one-time event but an ongoing process of spiritual awakening that requires active remembrance of God's presence in human history.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا أن أخرج قومك من الظلمات إلى النور وذكرهم بأيام الله إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: And when Moses said to his people: "Remember Allah's favor upon you when He saved you from Pharaoh's people, who subjected you to terrible torment, slaughtering your sons and sparing your women. In that was a great trial from your Lord."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining historical memory of divine intervention and liberation. It suggests that gratitude is enhanced through conscious remembrance of past hardships overcome through Allah's help. The mention of the specific forms of persecution serves to illustrate how oppression often targets the most vulnerable and aims to destroy community continuity. The description of this as a "trial" indicates that even severe hardships serve a divine purpose in testing and strengthening faith and character.
orig: وإذ قال موسى لقومه اذكروا نعمة الله عليكم إذ أنجاكم من آل فرعون يسومونكم سوء العذاب ويذبحون أبناءكم ويستحيون نساءكم وفي ذلكم بلاء من ربكم عظيم

translation: And when your Lord proclaimed: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you [in favor]; but if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe
interpretation: This verse establishes a divine principle of reciprocity, highlighting that gratitude is a catalyst for increased blessings and abundance in one's life. When people recognize Allah's favors and express genuine thankfulness through both words and deeds, Allah promises to multiply His bounties. This gratitude isn't merely verbal acknowledgment but encompasses using Allah's blessings in ways that please Him. Conversely, the warning of severe punishment for ingratitude emphasizes how denying or being ungrateful for Allah's favors is a serious spiritual transgression that distances one from divine mercy.
orig: وإذ تأذن ربكم لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم ولئن كفرتم إن عذابي لشديد

translation: And Moses said: "If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on earth all together, then indeed Allah is Free of need, Praiseworthy"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute independence from His creation, highlighting that even if every being on Earth were to reject faith, it wouldn't diminish Allah's glory or power in any way. Moses is reminding his people that their belief or disbelief affects only themselves, not Allah, who remains eternally self-sufficient and worthy of praise regardless of human choices.
orig: وقال موسى إن تكفروا أنتم ومن في الأرض جميعا فإن الله لغني حميد

translation: Has not the news reached you of those who were before you - the people of Noah and 'Aad and Thamud and those after them? None knows them but Allah. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they put their hands in their mouths and said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed, we are in doubt about that to which you invite us."
interpretation: This verse illustrates a recurring pattern in human resistance to divine guidance, where even in the face of clear evidence, people choose denial. The gesture of putting hands in mouths symbolizes mockery and stubborn rejection, highlighting how pride and skepticism can blind people from accepting truth even when it's presented with clear signs. This serves as a warning to later generations about the consequences of arrogant dismissal of divine messages.
orig: ألم يأتكم نبأ الذين من قبلكم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود والذين من بعدهم لا يعلمهم إلا الله جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فردوا أيديهم في أفواههم وقالوا إنا كفرنا بما أرسلتم به وإنا لفي شك مما تدعوننا إليه مريب

translation: Their messengers said, "Can there be doubt about Allah, Creator of the heavens and earth? He invites you that He may forgive you of your sins, and He delays your term for a specified time." They said, "You are not but men like us who wish to avert us from what our fathers were worshipping. So bring us a clear authority."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the eternal struggle between faith and skepticism, where divine messengers confront the paradox of human resistance to spiritual truth. The messengers' rhetorical question about doubting Allah emphasizes the illogical nature of denying the Creator when surrounded by the evidence of creation. The rejection by their people, demanding "clear authority," reveals how deeply ingrained cultural and ancestral practices can blind people to spiritual truth, even when offered divine forgiveness and mercy. It's a profound commentary on how humans often prefer familiar traditions over transformative spiritual change.
orig: قالت رسلهم أفي الله شك فاطر السماوات والأرض يدعوكم ليغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى قالوا إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا تريدون أن تصدونا عما كان يعبد آباؤنا فأتونا بسلطان مبين

translation: Their messengers said to them, "We are only human like you, but Allah bestows His grace upon whom He wills among His servants. And it is not for us to bring you any authority except by Allah's permission. And upon Allah let the believers rely."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humility of divine messengers while highlighting the special relationship between God and His chosen representatives. While prophets acknowledge their human nature, their distinction lies not in their inherent superiority but in God's selective grace. This teaches us that true authority comes only through divine permission, not human capability, and that success in any divine mission requires complete reliance on Allah rather than personal abilities.
orig: قالت لهم رسلهم إن نحن إلا بشر مثلكم ولكن الله يمن على من يشاء من عباده وما كان لنا أن نأتيكم بسلطان إلا بإذن الله وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

translation: And why should we not rely upon Allah while He has guided us to our ways? And we will surely be patient against whatever harm you should cause us. And upon Allah let those who would rely [indeed] rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the deep spiritual truth that when Allah has already shown us guidance, trusting in Him becomes a natural and logical response to life's challenges. It particularly resonates in situations of adversity, teaching that true reliance on Allah (tawakkul) isn't merely passive trust, but an active state of faith that gives believers the strength to endure hardships and persecution while remaining steadfast in their principles.
orig: وما لنا ألا نتوكل على الله وقد هدانا سبلنا ولنصبرن على ما آذيتمونا وعلى الله فليتوكل المتوكلون

translation: And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, "We will surely drive you out of our land, or you must return to our religion." So their Lord inspired to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the timeless pattern of how power structures react when their authority is challenged by divine truth. The disbelievers' ultimatum - either exile or conformity - reveals how established systems often view religious freedom as a threat to their control. The divine response shows that ultimate victory belongs to truth over oppression, even when the truth-bearers appear powerless in worldly terms.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لرسلهم لنخرجنكم من أرضنا أو لتعودن في ملتنا فأوحى إليهم ربهم لنهلكن الظالمين

translation: And We will surely cause you to dwell in the land after them. That is for those who fear My position and fear My threat
interpretation: This verse conveys Allah's divine promise of empowerment and succession, indicating that righteous behavior and God-consciousness are prerequisites for divine favor and authority on earth. It emphasizes that true success and establishment come to those who maintain a healthy fear of Allah's majesty and remain mindful of His warnings, suggesting that power and authority should be coupled with spiritual awareness and moral responsibility.
orig: ولنسكننكم الأرض من بعدهم ذلك لمن خاف مقامي وخاف وعيد

translation: And they sought victory, but every obstinate tyrant was disappointed
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate futility of those who oppose truth and justice with arrogance. Despite their attempts to achieve victory through oppression and force, their efforts are destined to fail. The divine law ensures that those who maintain stubborn opposition to righteousness while wielding power unjustly will eventually face disappointment and defeat.
orig: واستفتحوا وخاب كل جبار عنيد

translation: Beyond him lies Hell, and he will be given to drink of purulent water
interpretation: The verse paints a vivid picture of divine justice, suggesting that those who reject truth and guidance will face consequences beyond this life. The mention of "purulent water" symbolizes the most repugnant form of punishment, indicating that the choices we make in this life have profound implications in the hereafter. It serves as a powerful warning about accountability and the importance of making righteous choices while we have the opportunity.
orig: من ورائه جهنم ويسقى من ماء صديد

translation: He will sip it but can hardly swallow it. Death will come to him from every direction, yet he cannot die, and before him is a massive punishment.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the eternal nature of Hell's torment, where the punishment is both physical and psychological. The inability to swallow symbolizes the perpetual state of agony, while death's constant presence without relief represents the ultimate form of suffering - the desire for extinction that never comes. The "massive punishment" suggests that this is merely the beginning of a series of escalating torments, highlighting divine justice's comprehensive nature for those who rejected truth in their worldly life.
orig: يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان وما هو بميت ومن ورائه عذاب غليظ

translation: The deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord are like ashes that the wind blows forcefully on a stormy day; they cannot benefit from what they earned. That is the extreme misguidance.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how the actions of disbelievers, despite appearing substantial, lack lasting value and spiritual weight. Just as ashes are scattered and rendered worthless by strong winds, their deeds, though potentially impressive in worldly terms, hold no value in the eternal sphere because they weren't founded on faith and divine guidance. The metaphor of ashes also suggests the fragility and impermanence of works done without divine purpose, highlighting how actions disconnected from faith ultimately leave no lasting benefit or reward.
orig: مثل الذين كفروا بربهم أعمالهم كرماد اشتدت به الريح في يوم عاصف لا يقدرون مما كسبوا على شيء ذلك هو الضلال البعيد

translation: Do you not see that Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth? If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over creation, reminding humans of their contingent nature. It suggests that despite humanity's achievements and perceived importance, they are ultimately replaceable in Allah's grand scheme. This serves as both a warning against arrogance and a reminder of our complete dependence on Allah's will, encouraging humility and conscious awareness of our position as created beings.
orig: ألم تر أن الله خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق إن يشأ يذهبكم ويأت بخلق جديد

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and capability, indicating that nothing is beyond His ability or control. It serves as a reminder that what might seem impossible or challenging to humans is completely feasible for Allah, highlighting the limitless nature of divine power and the futility of doubting Allah's ability to accomplish anything He wills.
orig: وما ذلك على الله بعزيز

translation: And they will come forth before Allah all together, then the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers, so can you avail us anything against Allah's punishment?" They will say, "If Allah had guided us, we would have guided you. It makes no difference whether we rage or bear patiently; there is no escape for us."
interpretation: This verse reveals the ultimate futility of worldly power dynamics and false leadership in the face of divine judgment. On the Day of Judgment, those who blindly followed corrupt leaders will confront their former masters, desperately seeking help, only to discover that these once-powerful figures are equally helpless before Allah's justice. It serves as a warning against placing trust in human authority over divine guidance, and demonstrates how earthly hierarchies become meaningless in the ultimate reckoning.
orig: وبرزوا لله جميعا فقال الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا من عذاب الله من شيء قالوا لو هدانا الله لهديناكم سواء علينا أجزعنا أم صبرنا ما لنا من محيص

translation: And Satan will say when the matter has been concluded, "Indeed, Allah had promised you the promise of truth. And I promised you, but I betrayed you. But I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot be called to your aid, nor can you be called to my aid. Indeed, I deny your association of me [with Allah] before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers there is a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse reveals the true nature of Satan's relationship with humans and his ultimate betrayal. On the Day of Judgment, Satan will abandon his followers and expose his deception, admitting that he had no real power over them except through their own willingness to follow him. This demonstrates the importance of personal responsibility in our spiritual choices and warns against following misleading influences that draw us away from divine guidance. The verse emphasizes that each person bears the ultimate responsibility for their own choices and cannot shift blame onto external influences, even Satan himself.
orig: وقال الشيطان لما قضي الأمر إن الله وعدكم وعد الحق ووعدتكم فأخلفتكم وما كان لي عليكم من سلطان إلا أن دعوتكم فاستجبتم لي فلا تلوموني ولوموا أنفسكم ما أنا بمصرخكم وما أنتم بمصرخي إني كفرت بما أشركتمون من قبل إن الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم
