orig: وله من في السماوات والأرض ومن عنده لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ولا يستحسرون

translation: They glorify Him night and day, and they never tire
interpretation: This verse illustrates the unwavering devotion of the angels, who maintain constant worship without fatigue or interruption. Their perpetual state of worship serves as an ideal model of dedication to Allah, contrasting with human limitations and highlighting the special nature of angelic creation. It reminds us that true devotion transcends physical limitations and temporal constraints.
orig: يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون

translation: Or have they taken gods from the earth who can raise (the dead)?
interpretation: This verse challenges polytheistic beliefs by highlighting the logical fallacy of worshipping earthly deities that lack divine power. It emphasizes that created beings from earth cannot possess the ultimate power of resurrection, which is exclusively a divine attribute. The rhetorical question serves to demonstrate the absurdity of attributing godlike powers to earthly objects or beings that are themselves created and limited.
orig: أم اتخذوا آلهة من الأرض هم ينشرون

translation: If there were other gods besides Allah in them (the heavens and earth), they would have been ruined. So glory be to Allah, Lord of the Throne, far above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse presents a powerful logical argument for monotheism known as the "argument of exclusion." If multiple deities existed, each with their own will and power, the universe would descend into chaos as these gods would compete and conflict with each other's decisions and authority. The perfect order and harmony we observe in the cosmos is evidence that it must be governed by a single, supreme authority.
orig: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا فسبحان الله رب العرش عما يصفون

translation: He cannot be questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and supreme authority. Unlike His creation, Allah is not accountable to anyone for His actions because His wisdom and justice are perfect and beyond human comprehension. This highlights the fundamental difference between the Creator and the created, reminding humans of their position as servants who will be held accountable for their deeds.
orig: لا يسأل عما يفعل وهم يسألون

translation: Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, "Bring your proof. This is the message for those with me and the message of those before me." But most of them do not know the truth, so they turn away.
interpretation: This verse challenges the fundamental error of polytheism by demanding evidence for the worship of multiple deities. It emphasizes that throughout history, divine revelation has consistently proclaimed monotheism, and those who reject this truth do so not from rational evidence but from willful ignorance and aversion to the truth that contradicts their inherited beliefs.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دونه آلهة قل هاتوا برهانكم هذا ذكر من معي وذكر من قبلي بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون الحق فهم معرضون

translation: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity and consistency of God's most fundamental message throughout human history. Every prophet, without exception, was given the same core truth of monotheism (tawhid), indicating that the belief in One God isn't a new concept introduced by Islam but rather the eternal, unchanging divine truth that has been consistently communicated to humanity through all prophets. It serves as a powerful reminder that despite different times, places, and peoples, God's essential message has remained unchanged: acknowledge His uniqueness and direct worship solely to Him.
orig: وما أرسلنا من قبلك من رسول إلا نوحي إليه أنه لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدون

translation: And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they are honored servants.
interpretation: This verse refutes the notion of divine offspring, emphasizing that those whom some mistakenly call God's children are actually noble servants. It particularly addresses the misconception about angels being God's daughters, highlighting how such claims diminish the transcendent nature of Allah's existence. The use of "subhanahu" (Exalted is He) serves as an immediate and emphatic rejection of this false belief, establishing a clear boundary between the Creator and His creation.
orig: وقالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا سبحانه بل عباد مكرمون

translation: They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete submission and obedience of the angels to Allah. Their devotion is so perfect that they never speak before Allah has spoken, showing ultimate respect and discipline. They don't make independent decisions or take actions without divine authorization, reflecting the ideal model of servitude and submission to divine authority.
orig: لا يسبقونه بالقول وهم بأمره يعملون

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot intercede except for one whom He approves, and they, from fear of Him, are apprehensive
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete knowledge and control over His creation, particularly regarding the angels. The angels' ability to intercede is strictly limited by divine permission, showing that even these mighty celestial beings operate under Allah's authority. Their constant state of reverent fear, despite their elevated status, demonstrates that true knowledge of Allah naturally leads to deep humility and awe.
orig: يعلم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم ولا يشفعون إلا لمن ارتضى وهم من خشيته مشفقون

translation: And whoever of them says, "Indeed, I am a god besides Him"- that one We will recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of claiming divinity, highlighting that any creation who dares to elevate themselves to the status of godhood commits the gravest form of transgression. The mention of Hell as recompense indicates that self-deification represents the ultimate corruption of the soul and the most extreme form of injustice, as it attempts to usurp the unique position that belongs exclusively to Allah.
orig: ومن يقل منهم إني إله من دونه فذلك نجزيه جهنم كذلك نجزي الظالمين

translation: Have those who disbelieved not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, then We separated them and made from water every living thing? Then will they not believe?
interpretation: This verse points to the scientific miracle of the "Big Bang" theory, where the universe began as a single point before expanding. It also emphasizes water's fundamental role as the basis of all life, a fact unknown to humans at the time of revelation. The verse challenges skeptics to recognize these signs of Allah's power and creative design in the natural world as evidence of divine truth.
orig: أولم ير الذين كفروا أن السماوات والأرض كانتا رتقا ففتقناهما وجعلنا من الماء كل شيء حي أفلا يؤمنون

translation: And We placed on the earth firmly set mountains, lest it should shake with them, and We made therein broad passes as ways that they might be guided.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine engineering in Earth's creation, where mountains serve as stabilizing anchors that prevent excessive geological movement, much like how tent pegs secure a tent. The mention of mountain passes shows how Allah's design simultaneously provides stability while ensuring human mobility and commerce, demonstrating His perfect balance between security and accessibility in creation.
orig: وجعلنا في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بهم وجعلنا فيها فجاجا سبلا لعلهم يهتدون

translation: And We made the sky a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs, are turning away
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's divine engineering of the universe, specifically how the atmosphere serves as a protective shield for Earth, safeguarding life from harmful cosmic radiation and meteorites. The verse critiques human ingratitude, as people often fail to reflect on this remarkable cosmic protection system despite its crucial role in sustaining life.
orig: وجعلنا السماء سقفا محفوظا وهم عن آياتها معرضون

translation: And He is the One Who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon; each floating in an orbit
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's supreme power over the cosmos and His intricate design of the universe. The use of "floating" (yasbahun) suggests a harmonious, continuous motion, indicating that the celestial bodies follow precise, divinely ordained paths. This scientific allusion in the Qur'an, revealed over 1400 years ago, demonstrates divine knowledge of celestial mechanics before humans discovered these astronomical principles.
orig: وهو الذي خلق الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر كل في فلك يسبحون

translation: And We did not grant immortality to any human being before you. Then if you die, would they live forever?
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of the universal truth of mortality, addressing human arrogance and delusion about permanence in this world. It emphasizes that even the greatest of God's creation, including prophets, are subject to death, thereby establishing death as an inevitable reality that no one can escape. The rhetorical question at the end highlights the absurdity of those who might behave as though they're immune to death while even the Prophet isn't exempt from it.
orig: وما جعلنا لبشر من قبلك الخلد أفإن مت فهم الخالدون

translation: Every soul shall taste death, and We test you with evil and good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned
interpretation: This verse illustrates the universal truth that mortality is an equalizing force that affects all living beings without exception. The mention of testing through both good and bad circumstances suggests that life's experiences, whether positive or negative, serve as a divine assessment of human character and faith. This testing process reveals how individuals respond to both blessings and hardships, with the ultimate purpose being to prepare souls for their inevitable return to their Creator for accountability.
orig: كل نفس ذائقة الموت ونبلوكم بالشر والخير فتنة وإلينا ترجعون

translation: And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in ridicule, [saying], "Is this the one who mentions your deities?" While they are, at the mention of the Most Merciful, disbelievers
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound irony in the behavior of the disbelievers, who mock the Prophet's criticism of their false deities while they themselves reject the worship of Allah, the true source of all mercy. Their mockery reveals their spiritual blindness, as they fail to recognize that their derision of one who calls to truth while they deny the Supreme Creator is the height of misguided judgment.
orig: وإذا رآك الذين كفروا إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي يذكر آلهتكم وهم بذكر الرحمن هم كافرون

translation: Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten.
interpretation: This verse reflects the inherent impatient nature of humans, who often rush to judgment or demand immediate results. Allah reminds us that while humans are naturally hasty and impulsive, divine wisdom operates on its own timeline. The verse teaches us to cultivate patience and trust in Allah's plan, understanding that everything will be revealed at its appointed time rather than according to our rushed desires.
orig: خلق الإنسان من عجل سأريكم آياتي فلا تستعجلون

translation: And they say: "When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and mockery of disbelievers who challenge the truthfulness of divine promises, particularly regarding the Day of Judgment. Their questioning isn't genuine seeking of knowledge, but rather stems from disbelief and arrogance. The use of "if you are truthful" indicates their underlying doubt in the message itself, revealing a pattern of denial that has been common throughout human history when confronted with divine warnings.
orig: ويقولون متى هذا الوعد إن كنتم صادقين

translation: If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces nor from their backs, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: This verse conveys a powerful warning about the consequences of disbelief by highlighting the helplessness of disbelievers in the hereafter. It suggests that if people could truly comprehend the severity of their future punishment while still in this world, they would make different choices. The imagery of fire touching both front and back emphasizes the complete and inescapable nature of divine justice, indicating that no amount of worldly power or assistance can protect someone from the consequences of their rejection of faith.
orig: لو يعلم الذين كفروا حين لا يكفون عن وجوههم النار ولا عن ظهورهم ولا هم ينصرون

translation: Rather, it will come to them unexpectedly and bewilder them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be given respite
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sudden and inevitable nature of divine judgment, highlighting how humans often live in heedlessness until the moment of reckoning arrives. When it does come, it will be so overwhelming that even those who denied or doubted it will be left in a state of complete bewilderment, unable to defend themselves or negotiate for more time. This serves as a powerful reminder that one should always be prepared spiritually and morally, as the moment of accountability can come without warning.
orig: بل تأتيهم بغتة فتبهتهم فلا يستطيعون ردها ولا هم ينظرون

translation: And messengers before you were certainly ridiculed, but those who mocked them were enveloped by what they used to ridicule
interpretation: This verse offers divine consolation to Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing that rejection and mockery are not unique to his mission but are part of a historical pattern faced by all prophets. It also serves as a warning that those who mock divine guidance ultimately face the consequences of their derision, often being destroyed by the very things they ridiculed.
orig: ولقد استهزئ برسل من قبلك فحاق بالذين سخروا منهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Say, "Who can protect you in the night and the day from the Most Merciful?" Yet they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes humanity's complete dependence on Allah's protection, highlighting how even those who deny Him benefit from His constant mercy and guardianship. The rhetorical question serves to make people reflect on their vulnerability and the fact that no force other than Allah can truly protect them through all times. The irony lies in how people continue to turn away from acknowledging the very source of their security and protection, demonstrating the extent of human ingratitude and heedlessness.
orig: قل من يكلؤكم بالليل والنهار من الرحمن بل هم عن ذكر ربهم معرضون

translation: Or do they have gods who can protect them from Us? They cannot help themselves, nor can they be protected from Us.
interpretation: This verse challenges the logic of polytheism by highlighting the powerlessness of false deities. It points out the fundamental flaw in worshipping entities that lack even the basic ability to protect themselves, let alone offer protection to their worshippers. The divine rhetoric emphasizes that true power and protection lie exclusively with Allah, making reliance on other deities not only futile but illogical.
orig: أم لهم آلهة تمنعهم من دوننا لا يستطيعون نصر أنفسهم ولا هم منا يصحبون

translation: Rather, We have provided for these people and their fathers until life grew long for them. Then do they not see that We set upon the land, reducing it from its borders? So is it they who will overcome?
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's strategic approach to those who deny the truth. By granting them and their ancestors extended periods of comfort and prosperity, Allah tests their response to His blessings. The gradual reduction of land from its borders symbolizes the inevitable decline of earthly power and serves as a warning that no matter how secure people feel in their position, Allah's plan will ultimately prevail. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes the futility of human resistance against divine will.
orig: بل متعنا هؤلاء وآباءهم حتى طال عليهم العمر أفلا يرون أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها أفهم الغالبون

translation: Say, "I warn you only through divine revelation." But the deaf cannot hear the call when they are warned
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that spiritual guidance and understanding require more than just physical hearing. Just as a deaf person cannot hear a warning call, those who are spiritually unreceptive - whose hearts are closed - cannot benefit from divine warnings even when they're directly presented with them. The "deafness" here refers to a willful spiritual condition rather than a physical disability.
orig: قل إنما أنذركم بالوحي ولا يسمع الصم الدعاء إذا ما ينذرون

translation: And if even a breath of your Lord's punishment were to touch them, they would surely cry, "Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers!"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the fragile nature of human conviction and how quickly people's attitudes can change when faced with divine consequences. Those who were previously arrogant and dismissive of divine warnings immediately acknowledge their wrongdoing when experiencing even the slightest taste of God's punishment, highlighting humanity's tendency to only recognize truth and admit fault when confronted with dire consequences rather than heeding warnings beforehand.
orig: ولئن مستهم نفحة من عذاب ربك ليقولن يا ويلنا إنا كنا ظالمين

translation: And We shall set up scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be dealt with unjustly at all. And if there be the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and sufficient are We as accounters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute justice and the precision of divine accountability. It illustrates that on the Day of Judgment, every action, regardless of how minuscule, will be accounted for with perfect accuracy. The metaphor of the mustard seed, being one of the smallest known objects to the verse's original audience, drives home the point that nothing escapes divine knowledge and judgment. This serves as both a warning to the wrongdoers and a reassurance to the righteous that no good deed will go unrewarded, nor any injustice unaddressed.
orig: ونضع الموازين القسط ليوم القيامة فلا تظلم نفس شيئا وإن كان مثقال حبة من خردل أتينا بها وكفى بنا حاسبين

translation: And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light and a reminder for the righteous
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine support given to prophets Moses and Aaron through the Torah, which served as a means of distinguishing truth from falsehood. The "light" refers to the spiritual illumination it provided, guiding people from darkness to enlightenment. The mention of it being "for the righteous" suggests that true benefit from divine guidance comes to those who approach it with consciousness and sincerity, maintaining their duty to God.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى وهارون الفرقان وضياء وذكرا للمتقين

translation: Those who fear their Lord in the unseen, and they are apprehensive of the Hour
interpretation: This verse speaks to the quality of true believers who maintain consciousness of Allah even when they are alone, highlighting that genuine faith manifests in private moments when no one is watching. Their fear of the Day of Judgment demonstrates their deep understanding that all actions have consequences, motivating them to live righteously not out of public display but from sincere conviction.
orig: الذين يخشون ربهم بالغيب وهم من الساعة مشفقون

translation: And this is a blessed message which We have sent down. Will you then deny it?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and sanctity of the Qur'an, challenging those who reject it by highlighting their illogical position of denying something that brings such evident blessings and guidance to humanity. The use of the term "blessed" (mubarak) suggests that this revelation is a continuous source of spiritual and practical benefits, making its rejection particularly unreasonable.
orig: وهذا ذكر مبارك أنزلناه أفأنتم له منكرون

translation: And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgement before, and We were of him well-Knowing
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's special favor upon Abraham by granting him wisdom and mature understanding from an early age. The divine bestowal of "rushd" (sound judgment) indicates that Abraham was uniquely qualified for his role as a prophet even before receiving revelation, suggesting that Allah prepares His chosen servants through divine guidance long before their formal mission begins.
orig: ولقد آتينا إبراهيم رشده من قبل وكنا به عالمين

translation: When he said to his father and his people: "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates Ibrahim's rational approach to challenging idolatry by questioning the fundamental logic behind worshipping man-made objects. His question wasn't merely seeking information, but was a strategic method to make his people reflect on the futility of their practices and recognize the absurdity of dedicating themselves to lifeless sculptures that they themselves had crafted.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ما هذه التماثيل التي أنتم لها عاكفون

translation: They said, "We found our forefathers worshipping them."
interpretation: This verse reveals how blind imitation of ancestral practices can hinder spiritual growth and critical thinking. Rather than questioning or seeking truth independently, people often justify their beliefs and actions simply by pointing to tradition, even when those traditions lack logical or spiritual foundation. This mentality represents a significant obstacle to religious reform and spiritual enlightenment.
orig: قالوا وجدنا آباءنا لها عابدين

translation: He said: "You and your forefathers have indeed been in manifest error."
interpretation: This verse highlights the cyclical nature of inherited misconceptions, suggesting that false beliefs and misguided practices can be passed down through generations, creating a chain of spiritual blindness that requires courage to break free from. It emphasizes the importance of questioning traditional beliefs when they contradict divine truth, even if they come from our ancestors.
orig: قال لقد كنتم أنتم وآباؤكم في ضلال مبين

translation: They said: "Have you come to us with truth, or are you one of those who jest?"
interpretation: This verse reflects humanity's common skepticism towards divine messages. When confronted with profound truth that challenges their established beliefs, people often resort to questioning the messenger's sincerity, suggesting that the natural human response to revolutionary spiritual guidance is often doubt and suspicion rather than immediate acceptance.
orig: قالوا أجئتنا بالحق أم أنت من اللاعبين

translation: He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth who created them, and I am, to that, a witness."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of absolute monotheism by asserting that the true sovereign is not any earthly power or idol, but rather the Creator of the entire universe. The speaker's testimony adds a personal dimension of certainty and conviction, suggesting that the truth of God's sovereignty is so evident that it can be personally witnessed and attested to through observation of creation.
orig: قال بل ربكم رب السماوات والأرض الذي فطرهن وأنا على ذلكم من الشاهدين

translation: "And by Allah, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned and gone away."
interpretation: "This verse reveals Ibrahim's strategic approach to challenging idolatry, demonstrating that sometimes indirect methods of exposing falsehood are more effective than direct confrontation. It shows that wisdom in da'wah (calling to truth) may require careful timing and planning, rather than immediate or aggressive approaches."
orig: وتالله لأكيدن أصنامكم بعد أن تولوا مدبرين

translation: So he broke them into pieces, except for their largest one, that they might return to it.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Ibrahim's strategic wisdom in challenging idolatry. By destroying the idols but leaving the largest one intact, he created an opportunity to demonstrate the powerlessness of these false deities. When people would return and question what happened, they would be forced to confront the logical impossibility of idols protecting themselves, leading them to question their beliefs and potentially recognize the truth of monotheism.
orig: فجعلهم جذاذا إلا كبيرا لهم لعلهم إليه يرجعون

translation: They said, "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he must be one of the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse reflects how people's attachment to false beliefs can make them react with hostility toward those who challenge their worldview. When their idols were destroyed, instead of questioning the powerlessness of these deities that couldn't protect themselves, they immediately sought to punish the one who exposed their fallacy. It demonstrates how deeply ingrained false beliefs can become in society, to the point where those who speak truth are labeled as wrongdoers.
orig: قالوا من فعل هذا بآلهتنا إنه لمن الظالمين

translation: They said, "We heard a young man speaking against them, he is called Ibrahim"
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment when the disbelievers identified Prophet Ibrahim as the one who challenged their idolatry, showing how a single courageous voice of truth can create ripples in an established system of falsehood, even when coming from a young person
orig: قالوا سمعنا فتى يذكرهم يقال له إبراهيم

translation: They said: "Bring him before the eyes of the people, that they may witness"
interpretation: This verse reflects the public nature of justice and accountability in society. The call to bring someone before the public eye suggests the importance of transparency in judicial matters and communal decision-making. It emphasizes that matters of significance should not be dealt with in secret, but rather with public witnessing to ensure fairness and prevent injustice.
orig: قالوا فأتوا به على أعين الناس لعلهم يشهدون

translation: They said: "Are you the one who did this to our gods, O Ibrahim?"
interpretation: This verse reveals the confrontational nature of truth versus falsehood, where Prophet Ibrahim's challenge to idolatry led to a direct accusation from his people, highlighting how those invested in false beliefs often respond with hostility when their worldview is threatened rather than examining the logical fallacies in their beliefs.
orig: قالوا أأنت فعلت هذا بآلهتنا يا إبراهيم

translation: He said, "Rather, this - their largest one - did it, so ask them, if they should [be able to] speak."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Ibrahim's clever strategy to expose the logical fallacy of idol worship. By suggesting that the largest idol destroyed the others, he's forcing his people to confront the obvious truth that idols are powerless objects. His statement is a form of educational irony meant to lead people to realize through their own reasoning that worshipping man-made statues that can neither benefit nor harm is absurd.
orig: قال بل فعله كبيرهم هذا فاسألوهم إن كانوا ينطقون

translation: So they turned to themselves and said, "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moment of self-realization and conscience awakening, where people finally confront their own misdeeds and acknowledge their moral failings. Rather than continuing to blame others or justify their actions, they face the truth of their own injustice, marking a crucial step in moral and spiritual growth through honest self-reflection.
orig: فرجعوا إلى أنفسهم فقالوا إنكم أنتم الظالمون

translation: Then they were turned upside down on their heads [and said], "You have already known that these do not speak"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the inner conflict and embarrassment of those who knowingly persist in false beliefs. When confronted with the truth, they revert to irrational arguments, acknowledging in their hearts that their idols are powerless and speechless, yet they continue to defend their misguided practices out of stubbornness and pride.
orig: ثم نكسوا على رءوسهم لقد علمت ما هؤلاء ينطقون

translation: He said, 'Do you worship besides Allah that which can neither benefit you nor harm you?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of worshipping false deities by presenting a logical argument: if something cannot help or harm you, it is inherently powerless and therefore unworthy of worship. It challenges people to reflect on the irrational nature of dedicating devotion to objects or beings that lack any real influence over their lives, while the true God, Allah, holds complete power over benefit and harm.
orig: قال أفتعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعكم شيئا ولا يضركم

translation: Fie upon you and upon what you worship besides Allah! Do you not use your reason?
interpretation: This verse expresses profound frustration with those who persist in worshipping false deities despite having the capacity for rational thought. The use of "uff" (fie) indicates divine exasperation at humanity's failure to recognize the logical inconsistency of worshipping created objects or beings instead of their Creator. The verse challenges people to engage their intellect and reflect on the absurdity of elevating mundane objects or beings to divine status.
orig: أف لكم ولما تعبدون من دون الله أفلا تعقلون

translation: They said, "Burn him and support your gods, if you are to act."
interpretation: This verse reveals the extreme measures people will take to defend their false beliefs when confronted with truth. Rather than engaging in rational dialogue or considering Abraham's message, they resorted to violence, showing how deeply entrenched beliefs can lead to irrational and cruel responses when challenged. The command to "burn him" also demonstrates how those in power often attempt to silence dissenting voices through intimidation and force rather than addressing the substance of their arguments.
orig: قالوا حرقوه وانصروا آلهتكم إن كنتم فاعلين

translation: We said, "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham"
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's absolute power over His creation, showing how He can transform the very nature of elements at His command. The fire, which normally burns and destroys, was commanded to become a source of comfort for Prophet Ibrahim, demonstrating that natural laws exist only by Allah's will and can be suspended when He wishes.
orig: قلنا يا نار كوني بردا وسلاما على إبراهيم

translation: And they intended for him a plan, but We made them the greatest losers
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine protection and vindication of truth against conspiracies. When enemies plot against those who uphold God's message, their schemes ultimately backfire, leading to their own downfall. It's a reassurance that divine justice prevails over human machinations, and those who plot against righteousness will face the consequences of their actions.
orig: وأرادوا به كيدا فجعلناهم الأخسرين

translation: And We saved him and Lot to the land which We had blessed for all people
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's divine intervention in saving Prophet Ibrahim and his nephew Lot from persecution, guiding them to the blessed land of Palestine. The blessing mentioned refers to both spiritual and material abundance, as this region became the cradle of many prophets and divine messages. The phrase "for all people" suggests that this land's blessings were not meant exclusively for one group but were intended to benefit humanity as a whole through its spiritual heritage and religious significance.
orig: ونجيناه ولوطا إلى الأرض التي باركنا فيها للعالمين

translation: And We granted him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift, and We made all of them righteous
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's generosity in bestowing multiple blessings upon Ibrahim (Abraham). While he prayed for one righteous son, Allah not only gave him Isaac but also blessed him with a grandson, Jacob, demonstrating that divine gifts often exceed our expectations and initial requests. The term "nafilah" (additional gift) suggests that Jacob was an unexpected bonus blessing, teaching us that Allah's generosity knows no bounds when we remain faithful and devoted.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب نافلة وكلا جعلنا صالحين

translation: And We made them leaders guiding by Our command, and We inspired them to do good works, establish prayer, and give zakah, and they were worshippers of Us alone
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine selection and grooming of spiritual leaders who embody both religious authority and moral excellence. Their leadership isn't based on worldly criteria but stems from their deep connection with divine guidance and their exemplary character. These leaders don't just preach but actively demonstrate righteous conduct through charitable acts, regular worship, and financial generosity, serving as living models of holistic spiritual devotion.
orig: وجعلناهم أئمة يهدون بأمرنا وأوحينا إليهم فعل الخيرات وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة وكانوا لنا عابدين

translation: And to Lot We gave wisdom and knowledge, and We saved him from the city that practiced abominations. Indeed, they were an evil people who were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and justice by showing how He protects and elevates those who remain righteous even in the midst of widespread corruption. Lot's rescue demonstrates that divine intervention comes to those who maintain their moral integrity despite living among people who have normalized immoral behavior. The mention of wisdom and knowledge bestowed upon Lot indicates that spiritual enlightenment is a protection against societal degradation.
orig: ولوطا آتيناه حكما وعلما ونجيناه من القرية التي كانت تعمل الخبائث إنهم كانوا قوم سوء فاسقين

translation: And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's special favor upon His chosen servants, indicating that righteousness is a path to divine mercy. When one consistently maintains good character and performs righteous deeds, they become worthy of Allah's special compassion and care, which encompasses both worldly success and spiritual elevation.
orig: وأدخلناه في رحمتنا إنه من الصالحين

translation: And Noah, when he called [upon Us] before, so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great distress
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and responsiveness to sincere supplication, showing that even in the darkest moments of human history, divine intervention comes to those who maintain unwavering faith. Noah's story serves as a testament that patience and persistent prayer during severe trials will ultimately lead to deliverance and salvation for the believers.
orig: ونوحا إذ نادى من قبل فاستجبنا له فنجيناه وأهله من الكرب العظيم

translation: And We granted him victory over the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were an evil people, so We drowned them all.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine pattern of protecting His prophets and punishing those who persistently reject truth. When a community reaches a point of complete rejection and hostility towards divine guidance, Allah's intervention becomes a necessity to establish justice and preserve the mission of truth. The complete drowning signifies that divine punishment, when it comes, is absolute and inescapable for those who cross the boundaries of rejection and oppression.
orig: ونصرناه من القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا إنهم كانوا قوم سوء فأغرقناهم أجمعين

translation: And [recall] David and Solomon when they passed judgment concerning the field, when the sheep of a people overran it [at night], and We were witness to their judgment.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the importance of wisdom and fairness in judicial matters, showing how even prophets could have different approaches to justice. The incident demonstrates that Allah guides those in authority to make just decisions, and that judicial reasoning can vary while still remaining within divine guidance. It also emphasizes that Allah is always watching over the judgments of those who rule, ensuring accountability in leadership.
orig: وداوود وسليمان إذ يحكمان في الحرث إذ نفشت فيه غنم القوم وكنا لحكمهم شاهدين

translation: And We gave understanding of it to Solomon, and to each [of them] We gave judgement and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to exalt [Us], along with David and the birds. And We were doing [that]
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's divine wisdom in distributing unique gifts among His prophets. While both David and Solomon were presented with the same case, Solomon was granted special insight into the matter, demonstrating that Allah bestows different strengths upon different individuals. The mention of mountains and birds joining in David's praise shows that spiritual leadership transcends human boundaries, extending into the natural world, and suggests that true wisdom includes harmony with all of God's creation.
orig: ففهمناها سليمان وكلا آتينا حكما وعلما وسخرنا مع داوود الجبال يسبحن والطير وكنا فاعلين

translation: And We taught him the making of armor for you, to protect you from your violence. So will you be grateful?
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy in teaching Prophet David the skill of crafting armor, illustrating how divine knowledge extends beyond spiritual matters to practical innovations that benefit humanity. It emphasizes that technological advancement and practical skills are also gifts from God that deserve gratitude, while simultaneously reminding us that humans need protection from their own violent tendencies.
orig: وعلمناه صنعة لبوس لكم لتحصنكم من بأسكم فهل أنتم شاكرون

translation: And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully, proceeding by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's extraordinary favor upon Prophet Solomon, granting him control over powerful natural forces as a divine gift. The ability to command the wind represents both literal and metaphorical power, suggesting that when Allah bestows authority upon a righteous leader, even the elements of nature can become tools for establishing justice and prosperity. The reference to the "blessed land" likely indicates Jerusalem and its surroundings, highlighting the sacred connection between divine power and sacred geography.
orig: ولسليمان الريح عاصفة تجري بأمره إلى الأرض التي باركنا فيها وكنا بكل شيء عالمين

translation: And of the devils (subdued by Solomon) were some who dived (into the sea) for him and did other work besides that; and We were watching over them
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's extraordinary favor upon Prophet Solomon, granting him authority not just over humans but also over supernatural beings. The devils' submission to Solomon's command demonstrates how even powerful spiritual entities can be subjugated to serve divine purposes when Allah wills it, highlighting that all creation ultimately falls under Allah's supreme control and can be made to serve His chosen servants.
orig: ومن الشياطين من يغوصون له ويعملون عملا دون ذلك وكنا لهم حافظين

translation: And (remember) Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound spiritual principle that even in our deepest moments of suffering, maintaining a positive perception of Allah's mercy is essential. Job's statement demonstrates that acknowledging our pain while simultaneously affirming Allah's compassionate nature is the ideal approach to handling tribulation, as it combines both honest vulnerability and unwavering faith.
orig: وأيوب إذ نادى ربه أني مسني الضر وأنت أرحم الراحمين

translation: So We responded to him and removed what afflicted him of adversity. And We gave him [back] his family and the like thereof with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for the worshippers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's infinite mercy and responsiveness to sincere prayers, showing that relief always follows hardship for those who remain patient and devoted. Job's story serves as a powerful reminder that maintaining faith through difficulties will ultimately lead to rewards far greater than what was lost, as Allah not only restored Job's family but doubled his blessings. This divine response pattern encourages believers to remain steadfast in worship during their own trials.
orig: فاستجبنا له فكشفنا ما به من ضر وآتيناه أهله ومثلهم معهم رحمة من عندنا وذكرى للعابدين

translation: And Ishmael and Idris and Dhul-Kifl - all were of the patient ones
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of patience by grouping three prophets known for their exceptional endurance. Their inclusion in the same verse suggests that patience was their defining characteristic, teaching us that spiritual elevation and success in divine mission are intrinsically linked to one's ability to remain steadfast in the face of difficulties.
orig: وإسماعيل وإدريس وذا الكفل كل من الصابرين

translation: And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's boundless compassion towards those who live righteously. It shows that divine mercy isn't arbitrary but is a direct response to living a life of virtue and good deeds. The use of "admitted" suggests an active divine involvement in elevating the status of the righteous, indicating that spiritual elevation is both a divine gift and a reward for righteous conduct.
orig: وأدخلناهم في رحمتنا إنهم من الصالحين

translation: And [mention] the man of the fish, when he went off in anger and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him. And he called out within the darknesses, "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound lesson that even in our darkest moments of despair and self-imposed exile, sincere repentance and acknowledgment of our mistakes can lead to divine mercy. Prophet Yunus's experience teaches us that no matter how far we think we've strayed or how justified we believe our anger to be, true salvation lies in recognizing our limitations as humans and turning back to Allah with complete humility and recognition of His supreme authority.
orig: وذا النون إذ ذهب مغاضبا فظن أن لن نقدر عليه فنادى في الظلمات أن لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين

translation: So We responded to him and saved him from distress, and thus We save the believers
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's consistent pattern of responding to sincere prayers and delivering His faithful servants from hardship, using Prophet Yunus's rescue from the whale's belly as an example of divine mercy. It establishes a timeless principle that genuine faith and sincere supplication will always be met with Allah's support and deliverance from difficulties.
orig: فاستجبنا له ونجيناه من الغم وكذلك ننجي المؤمنين

translation: And [mention] Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone [with no heir], while you are the best of inheritors"
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep trust in Allah's mercy and timing, even in moments of personal despair. Zechariah's prayer demonstrates that even prophets experience human concerns about legacy and continuity, but they channel these anxieties through faithful supplication rather than despair. His acknowledgment of Allah as "the best of inheritors" shows his understanding that all possessions and lineage ultimately belong to Allah, yet he humbly asks for a successor to carry on his prophetic mission.
orig: وزكريا إذ نادى ربه رب لا تذرني فردا وأنت خير الوارثين

translation: So We answered him and bestowed upon him John, and We cured his wife for him. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate Us in hope and fear, and they were humble before Us.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine response to sincere devotion and persistent faith. When righteous servants maintain both hope and fear in their relationship with Allah, consistently performing good deeds while remaining humble, Allah may grant them what seems impossible by worldly standards. The cure of Zakariya's wife's infertility and the gift of a son in old age serves as a powerful reminder that divine intervention can overcome natural limitations when coupled with genuine submission and continuous good works.
orig: فاستجبنا له ووهبنا له يحيى وأصلحنا له زوجه إنهم كانوا يسارعون في الخيرات ويدعوننا رغبا ورهبا وكانوا لنا خاشعين

translation: And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit and made her and her son a sign for all peoples
interpretation: This verse speaks to the miraculous nature of Mary's immaculate conception, highlighting how her unwavering faith and moral purity made her worthy of being chosen for this divine miracle. Her story serves as a powerful testament to God's ability to transcend natural laws and create extraordinary circumstances to demonstrate His power, while also establishing both Mary and Jesus as profound signs of God's existence and might for humanity across time.
orig: والتي أحصنت فرجها فنفخنا فيها من روحنا وجعلناها وابنها آية للعالمين

translation: Indeed this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so worship Me
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic concept of unity among believers, indicating that despite cultural, ethnic, or geographical differences, all Muslims constitute a single spiritual family bound by their common faith and devotion to Allah. The directive to worship Allah exclusively follows this declaration of unity, suggesting that shared worship and devotion to one God is the binding force that maintains this unity.
orig: إن هذه أمتكم أمة واحدة وأنا ربكم فاعبدون

translation: But they have divided their religion among themselves into sects, each group rejoicing in its beliefs. Yet all will return to Us.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to create divisions and sects within faith, where each group becomes self-satisfied with their own interpretation while forgetting that ultimately all souls will return to Allah for judgment. It serves as a warning against religious sectarianism and a reminder that our differences will be resolved when we face divine accountability.
orig: وتقطعوا أمرهم بينهم كل إلينا راجعون

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds while being a believer, there will be no denial of his effort, and We are recorders of it
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine principle of perfect justice and recognition, highlighting that any good deed performed with sincere faith will never go unnoticed or unrewarded. It provides reassurance that Allah's system of record-keeping is infallible, and every righteous action, no matter how small, is documented and will be acknowledged, as long as it's coupled with genuine belief. This serves as both a motivation for believers to persist in good deeds and a comfort that their efforts are being preserved by divine decree.
orig: فمن يعمل من الصالحات وهو مؤمن فلا كفران لسعيه وإنا له كاتبون

translation: And [there is] prohibition upon [the people of] any city which We have destroyed that they will [ever] return
interpretation: This verse conveys the divine law of irreversibility for civilizations that have faced complete destruction due to their transgressions. Once Allah has decreed destruction upon a people for their persistent wrongdoing, there is no possibility of them returning to their former state of power or existence. This serves as a warning about the finality of divine punishment and emphasizes the importance of heeding divine guidance before reaching a point of no return.
orig: وحرام على قرية أهلكناها أنهم لا يرجعون

translation: Until when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they swiftly swarm from every elevation
interpretation: This verse points to a future time of great tribulation when powerful forces of chaos and destruction will be unleashed upon the world. The imagery of these forces emerging from every elevation suggests a widespread and overwhelming nature of this event, indicating a period of significant global turmoil that will serve as one of the major signs before the Day of Judgment.
orig: حتى إذا فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج وهم من كل حدب ينسلون

translation: And the true promise draws near; then behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare in horror, [while they say], "O woe to us; we had been unmindful of this; rather, we were wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound psychological and spiritual awakening that occurs when people finally confront the reality they've been denying. The "true promise" refers to the Day of Judgment, and the verse captures the moment of devastating realization when those who rejected faith suddenly understand the truth. Their wide-eyed horror and self-recrimination reflect not just fear, but the deeper anguish of recognizing that they deliberately chose to ignore clear signs and warnings throughout their lives.
orig: واقترب الوعد الحق فإذا هي شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا يا ويلنا قد كنا في غفلة من هذا بل كنا ظالمين

translation: Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah will be the firewood of Hell; you will enter it.
interpretation: This verse delivers a stern warning to polytheists, emphasizing that false deities and their worshippers will serve as fuel for hellfire, highlighting the severe consequences of associating partners with Allah and the futility of idol worship. The use of "what" instead of "who" in reference to the deities suggests their powerlessness and lack of divine attributes.
orig: إنكم وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم أنتم لها واردون

translation: If these had been gods, they would not have entered it, but all of them will abide therein forever.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the concept of false deities by presenting a logical argument: if the idols and false gods that people worship were truly divine, they wouldn't be suffering in Hell alongside their worshippers. Their presence in Hell proves their powerlessness and false nature, highlighting the futility of polytheistic beliefs.
orig: لو كان هؤلاء آلهة ما وردوها وكل فيها خالدون

translation: For them therein is [violent] exhaling and they will not be able to hear
interpretation: This verse depicts the severe punishment of the disbelievers in Hell, where their painful sighs and moans will be so intense that they will lose their ability to hear. The loss of hearing symbolizes their complete isolation and disconnection from any form of relief or comfort, emphasizing the totality of their suffering as a consequence of their rejection of truth in worldly life.
orig: لهم فيها زفير وهم فيها لا يسمعون

translation: Indeed, those for whom the best (reward) has already been promised by Us - they will be far removed from it (Hell)
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's absolute justice and mercy, highlighting that those who have earned His favor through their sincere faith and righteous deeds are already guaranteed protection from Hellfire. It emphasizes the divine promise's certainty and suggests that true believers need not live in constant fear, as their ultimate destination has been predetermined by their devotion and good works.
orig: إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى أولئك عنها مبعدون

translation: They will not hear its [Hell's] whisper, while they are, in that which their souls desire, abiding eternally
interpretation: This verse paints a picture of ultimate contentment in Paradise, where the blessed souls are so far removed from Hell's torment that not even its faintest sound reaches them. They exist in a state of perpetual fulfillment, where every desire of their heart is eternally satisfied, highlighting the complete peace and security of Paradise as a contrast to the anxiety and fear that characterizes earthly life.
orig: لا يسمعون حسيسها وهم في ما اشتهت أنفسهم خالدون

translation: The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will meet them [saying], "This is your Day which you have been promised"
interpretation: This verse speaks of the profound spiritual security and tranquility that the righteous believers will experience on the Day of Judgment. While others will be terrified by the events of that momentous day, these faithful souls will remain at peace, having lived their lives in accordance with divine guidance. The welcoming reception by angels represents divine recognition of their righteousness and serves as a fulfillment of Allah's promise to those who maintained their faith and performed good deeds during their worldly existence.
orig: لا يحزنهم الفزع الأكبر وتتلقاهم الملائكة هذا يومكم الذي كنتم توعدون

translation: The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a scroll for records. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [That is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the impermanence of our physical universe and Allah's absolute power over creation. The metaphor of folding the heavens like a scroll emphasizes how what seems vast and permanent to us is easily manipulated by divine will. The promise of recreation mirrors Islamic teachings about resurrection, suggesting that just as Allah had the power to create everything from nothing initially, He can and will restore life after death with equal ease. This demonstrates both Allah's omnipotence and His commitment to justice through the Day of Judgment.
orig: يوم نطوي السماء كطي السجل للكتب كما بدأنا أول خلق نعيده وعدا علينا إنا كنا فاعلين

translation: And We have already written in the Scripture [Az-Zabur] after the [previous] mention that My righteous servants shall inherit the earth
interpretation: This verse conveys Allah's divine promise that ultimately, the righteous and morally upright people will prevail and establish themselves on earth. It suggests that despite temporary setbacks or challenges, those who maintain righteousness and follow Allah's guidance will eventually be granted authority and stewardship over the earth, reflecting a cosmic law of justice where virtue ultimately triumphs
orig: ولقد كتبنا في الزبور من بعد الذكر أن الأرض يرثها عبادي الصالحون

translation: Indeed, in this is notification for a worshipping people
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine messages and signs are most meaningful to those who have cultivated a genuine spirit of worship and devotion. Those who maintain a consistent practice of worship develop a heightened spiritual awareness that allows them to recognize and benefit from Allah's signs and guidance more readily than others.
orig: إن في هذا لبلاغا لقوم عابدين

translation: And We have not sent you [O Muhammad] except as a mercy to the worlds
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Prophet Muhammad's mission was fundamentally one of compassion and mercy, not just for Muslims or humans alone, but for all creation including animals, plants, and every realm of existence. His teachings and guidance were meant to bring benefit and upliftment to all aspects of life, establishing a universal framework of mercy that transcends religious, ethnic, and temporal boundaries.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا رحمة للعالمين

translation: Say, "It is revealed to me that your God is one God; so will you submit [to Him]?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the core foundation of Islamic monotheism by instructing the Prophet to declare the divine truth revealed to him. The rhetorical question at the end serves as a powerful invitation to logical reasoning - if there is indeed only one God, the natural consequence should be submission to His will. It challenges people to align their beliefs with this fundamental truth, suggesting that pure monotheism naturally leads to submission (Islam).
orig: قل إنما يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فهل أنتم مسلمون

translation: But if they turn away, then say, "I have announced to you all alike. And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet's role as a clear warner, highlighting that his responsibility is merely to convey the message equally to all people. The uncertainty about the timing of divine judgment serves as a constant reminder to remain vigilant and prepared, as the promised accountability could come at any moment. This creates a sense of spiritual urgency while acknowledging human limitation in knowing divine timing.
orig: فإن تولوا فقل آذنتكم على سواء وإن أدري أقريب أم بعيد ما توعدون

translation: Indeed, He knows what is declared in speech and He knows what you conceal
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience, highlighting that nothing can be hidden from His knowledge. Whether we express our thoughts openly or keep them secret in our hearts, Allah is fully aware of them. This serves as a reminder that we should be mindful of both our outward actions and inner thoughts, as both are equally visible to our Creator.
orig: إنه يعلم الجهر من القول ويعلم ما تكتمون

translation: And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time
interpretation: This verse suggests that even seemingly favorable circumstances or temporary pleasures might be divine tests to evaluate our faith and character. Allah may grant people worldly comforts or delays punishment not as a blessing, but as a means of testing their gratitude, patience, and adherence to divine guidance.
orig: وإن أدري لعله فتنة لكم ومتاع إلى حين

translation: He said, "My Lord, judge with truth. And our Lord, the Most Merciful, is the one whose help is sought against what you describe."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking divine justice rather than human judgment, acknowledging that only Allah's judgment is perfect and unbiased. The mention of Allah's mercy alongside the request for judgment suggests that even when seeking justice, one should remember that mercy is an essential aspect of divine wisdom. The phrase "what you describe" refers to false accusations or misrepresentations, indicating that when faced with untruths, one should rely on Allah's support rather than engaging in defensive arguments.
orig: قال رب احكم بالحق وربنا الرحمن المستعان على ما تصفون

translation: O mankind! Fear your Lord. Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining God-consciousness in light of the impending Day of Judgment. The use of earthquake as a metaphor for the Day of Judgment suggests that the current world order will be completely disrupted and transformed, much like how an earthquake fundamentally alters the landscape. The directive to "fear your Lord" is not about terror, but rather about maintaining a state of mindful awareness that guides one's actions in preparation for this momentous event.
orig: يا أيها الناس اتقوا ربكم إن زلزلة الساعة شيء عظيم

translation: The Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget her nursling, and every pregnant woman will abort her pregnancy, and you will see mankind as intoxicated, yet they will not be intoxicated; but the punishment of Allah will be severe.
interpretation: This verse paints a vivid picture of the sheer terror and psychological impact of the Day of Judgment, where even the strongest of human bonds - that between a mother and her child - will be severed due to overwhelming fear. The comparison to intoxication suggests a state of complete mental disorientation where people lose their normal faculties and rational behavior, not due to alcohol but due to the horrifying nature of divine judgment. It serves as a powerful reminder that the Day of Reckoning will be so monumentally terrifying that it will override even our most basic human instincts and attachments.
orig: يوم ترونها تذهل كل مرضعة عما أرضعت وتضع كل ذات حمل حملها وترى الناس سكارى وما هم بسكارى ولكن عذاب الله شديد

translation: And among people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil
interpretation: This verse warns against those who engage in theological arguments without proper knowledge or understanding, blindly following misguided ideologies. It critiques individuals who reject divine guidance based on unfounded opinions rather than authentic knowledge, essentially becoming followers of destructive paths that lead away from truth.
orig: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ويتبع كل شيطان مريد

translation: It is decreed for him that whoever takes him as an ally - he will mislead him and will guide him to the punishment of the Blaze
interpretation: This verse reveals a divine warning about the consequences of choosing Satan as an ally. The use of "kutiba" (it is decreed) suggests this is an unchangeable spiritual law, emphasizing that aligning with evil forces inevitably leads to spiritual corruption and ultimately eternal punishment. The progression from "misleading" to "guiding to punishment" shows how Satan's influence gradually transforms from subtle deception to outright destruction.
orig: كتب عليه أنه من تولاه فأنه يضله ويهديه إلى عذاب السعير

translation: O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then [consider that] indeed, We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed - that We may show you. And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as a child, and then [We develop you] that you may reach your [time of] maturity. And among you is he who is taken in death, and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age so that he knows nothing after having known. And you see the earth barren, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells and grows every beautiful kind.
interpretation: This verse presents a profound argument for resurrection by drawing parallels with human embryological development and nature's revival. Just as humans develop from simple dust to complex beings through distinct stages, and just as barren land springs to life with rain, Allah demonstrates His power to bring life from apparent lifelessness. The detailed description of human development stages serves as evidence of divine precision and planning, while the mention of aging and death reminds us of life's temporary nature. The transformation of barren earth into vibrant life serves as a tangible metaphor for resurrection, showing that the Power that accomplishes these everyday "resurrections" can surely accomplish the final Resurrection.
orig: يا أيها الناس إن كنتم في ريب من البعث فإنا خلقناكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم من مضغة مخلقة وغير مخلقة لنبين لكم ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء إلى أجل مسمى ثم نخرجكم طفلا ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ومنكم من يتوفى ومنكم من يرد إلى أرذل العمر لكيلا يعلم من بعد علم شيئا وترى الأرض هامدة فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and He gives life to the dead, and He has power over all things
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty by highlighting three fundamental attributes. First, Allah embodies ultimate truth, meaning all reality stems from Him and His existence is the most certain fact. Second, His power over life and death demonstrates His supreme authority over existence itself, suggesting that just as He can revive the dead, He can transform any situation or state. Third, His unlimited power indicates that nothing in creation is beyond His capability or control, reinforcing the futility of seeking ultimate refuge or assistance from any other source.
orig: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق وأنه يحيي الموتى وأنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: And indeed, the Hour is coming - no doubt about it - and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute certainty of the Day of Judgment and the resurrection, addressing a fundamental aspect of Islamic belief. It serves as both a warning and a comfort, indicating that divine justice will ultimately prevail, and every soul will be held accountable for their deeds. The use of present continuous tense ("is coming") suggests the Hour's continuous approach, making it an imminent reality that should influence believers' current actions and choices.
orig: وأن الساعة آتية لا ريب فيها وأن الله يبعث من في القبور

translation: And among the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book
interpretation: This verse critiques those who engage in theological arguments and make claims about divine matters without proper knowledge, authentic guidance, or scriptural basis. It warns against the dangerous practice of speaking about religious matters based on mere speculation, personal opinions, or unsubstantiated beliefs, suggesting that authentic religious discourse must be grounded in valid knowledge and divine revelation.
orig: ومن الناس من يجادل في الله بغير علم ولا هدى ولا كتاب منير

translation: Turning his side [in pride] to mislead from the way of Allah. For him in this world is disgrace, and We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the Burning Fire
interpretation: This verse illustrates the dangerous nature of arrogance and how it leads people to reject divine guidance. When someone becomes so proud that they physically turn away from the truth with disdain, they not only harm themselves but also mislead others. The immediate consequence is humiliation in this worldly life, as arrogance ultimately leads to downfall and loss of respect. This temporal punishment is followed by a more severe eternal punishment, highlighting how spiritual arrogance is among the gravest of sins in Allah's sight.
orig: ثاني عطفه ليضل عن سبيل الله له في الدنيا خزي ونذيقه يوم القيامة عذاب الحريق

translation: That is because of what your hands have put forth and because Allah is not ever unjust to [His] servants
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability and divine justice, indicating that any hardship or consequence we face is a direct result of our own actions and choices, not divine oppression. It refutes any notion that Allah treats His creation unfairly, establishing that He is the ultimate embodiment of justice who never wrongs His servants.
orig: ذلك بما قدمت يداك وأن الله ليس بظلام للعبيد

translation: And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge. If he is touched by good, he is reassured by it; but if he is struck by trial, he turns on his face [to disbelief]. He has lost [this] world and the Hereafter. That is what is the manifest loss.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the superficial and conditional nature of some people's faith, who maintain their worship only when circumstances are favorable. Their relationship with Allah lacks depth and conviction, being based merely on material benefits rather than genuine devotion. When faced with trials or hardships, they quickly abandon their faith, revealing their weak spiritual foundation. This opportunistic approach to faith leads to loss in both worldly life and the afterlife, as true faith requires steadfastness in both ease and hardship.
orig: ومن الناس من يعبد الله على حرف فإن أصابه خير اطمأن به وإن أصابته فتنة انقلب على وجهه خسر الدنيا والآخرة ذلك هو الخسران المبين

translation: He invokes besides Allah that which neither harms him nor benefits him. That is the extreme misguidance.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of polytheism by highlighting how illogical it is to worship entities that possess no power to help or harm. The emphasis on "neither harms nor benefits" underscores that true power lies exclusively with Allah, making the act of seeking assistance from powerless deities an act of profound spiritual blindness and deviation from reason.
orig: يدعو من دون الله ما لا يضره وما لا ينفعه ذلك هو الضلال البعيد

translation: He calls to that which harms him more than it benefits him. Evil indeed is the patron, and evil indeed is the companion.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of seeking protection from false deities or worldly powers, as they bring more harm than good to those who rely on them. It warns against misplacing one's trust and loyalty in entities that cannot truly help, suggesting that choosing the wrong allies or sources of guidance leads to spiritual and practical detriment.
orig: يدعو لمن ضره أقرب من نفعه لبئس المولى ولبئس العشير

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, Allah does what He intends.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine justice system and Allah's absolute power over reward and punishment. It indicates that faith alone is insufficient; it must be accompanied by good actions to earn Paradise. The description of rivers flowing beneath gardens symbolizes perpetual abundance, freshness, and life-giving sustenance in the afterlife. The closing statement about Allah doing what He intends reinforces His complete sovereignty and reminds us that His promises are certain and unalterable.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار إن الله يفعل ما يريد

translation: Whoever thinks that Allah will not help him in this world and the Hereafter - let him extend a rope to the ceiling, then cut off [his breath], and let him see whether his effort will remove that which enrages [him]
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of doubting Allah's support and assistance. It suggests that if someone is so consumed by despair that they think Allah won't help them, then even the most extreme measures they might take (metaphorically hanging themselves) won't solve their problems or alleviate their distress. The verse serves as a powerful reminder that true solutions and relief come only through trust in Allah's support, not through desperate acts of frustration.
orig: من كان يظن أن لن ينصره الله في الدنيا والآخرة فليمدد بسبب إلى السماء ثم ليقطع فلينظر هل يذهبن كيده ما يغيظ

translation: And thus We have revealed it with clear signs, and surely Allah guides whom He wills
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's divine wisdom in revelation, highlighting that spiritual guidance is a two-way process. While Allah provides clear signs and evidence through His revelation, the ultimate acceptance of guidance depends on an individual's sincere desire and willingness to be guided. The term "whom He wills" refers to those who genuinely seek truth with an open heart and mind.
orig: وكذلك أنزلناه آيات بينات وأن الله يهدي من يريد

translation: Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians, and the Magians, and those who associate others with Allah - Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is witness over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's ultimate role as the supreme judge of all religious communities and belief systems. It suggests that rather than humans passing judgment on different faiths, the final verdict about who was right or wrong in their beliefs and practices is reserved exclusively for Allah on the Day of Judgment. This teaches Muslims to focus on their own relationship with Allah rather than condemning others, while also affirming Allah's complete knowledge and authority over all matters of faith.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئين والنصارى والمجوس والذين أشركوا إن الله يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة إن الله على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Do you not see that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the sun, the moon, the stars, mountains, trees, moving creatures and many of the people? But upon many the punishment has been justified. And he whom Allah humiliates - for him there is no bestower of honor. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse reveals the profound truth that everything in existence submits to Allah's will, whether consciously or unconsciously. The natural elements like the sun, moon, and mountains follow divine laws without deviation, while humans have been given free will to choose submission. Those who refuse to recognize this universal prostration and reject Allah's authority bring upon themselves humiliation, as true honor can only come through alignment with the divine order.
orig: ألم تر أن الله يسجد له من في السماوات ومن في الأرض والشمس والقمر والنجوم والجبال والشجر والدواب وكثير من الناس وكثير حق عليه العذاب ومن يهن الله فما له من مكرم إن الله يفعل ما يشاء

translation: These are two adversaries who have disputed about their Lord. But those who disbelieved will have cut out for them garments of fire. Poured upon their heads will be scalding water.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the eternal spiritual battle between truth and falsehood, believers and non-believers. The imagery of garments of fire suggests that disbelief becomes an inseparable part of one's identity, like clothing that envelops the body, while the scalding water represents the all-encompassing nature of divine punishment that penetrates both body and soul.
orig: هذان خصمان اختصموا في ربهم فالذين كفروا قطعت لهم ثياب من نار يصب من فوق رءوسهم الحميم

translation: With it will be melted what is within their bellies and [their] skins
interpretation: This verse illustrates the severe consequences of divine punishment, where intense heat penetrates to the deepest parts of one's being, suggesting that accountability for our actions affects us both internally and externally, leaving no refuge from the results of our misdeeds
orig: يصهر به ما في بطونهم والجلود

translation: And for them are maces of iron
interpretation: This verse speaks to the severe and lasting nature of punishment in Hell, where the iron maces symbolize both the physical torment and the psychological weight of divine justice. The use of iron specifically indicates the unbreakable and unyielding nature of this punishment, emphasizing that there is no escape or relief from the consequences of one's misdeeds.
orig: ولهم مقامع من حديد

translation: Every time they try to get out of it from anguish, they will be returned to it, and [it will be said], 'Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the eternal nature of Hell's punishment, emphasizing that there's no escape from divine justice once it's enacted. The continuous cycle of attempting to flee and being forced back represents the perpetual state of despair that awaits those who rejected truth, highlighting that accountability for one's actions in this life has permanent consequences in the hereafter.
orig: كلما أرادوا أن يخرجوا منها من غم أعيدوا فيها وذوقوا عذاب الحريق

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearl, and their garments therein will be silk
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine justice and reward, illustrating that spiritual achievement must be accompanied by practical good actions. The physical descriptions of Paradise - gold, pearls, and silk - represent the ultimate elevation of status, as these items were considered the height of luxury in 7th century Arabia. The flowing rivers symbolize perpetual renewal and life, suggesting that the rewards of Paradise are both eternal and ever-fresh. The verse also implies that what was often restricted in worldly life (such as silk for men) becomes permissible in Paradise, indicating a transformation of earthly limitations.
orig: إن الله يدخل الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار يحلون فيها من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤا ولباسهم فيها حرير

translation: And they were guided to good words, and they were guided to the path of the Praiseworthy
interpretation: This verse speaks to the spiritual transformation of believers who are divinely guided to speak with wisdom, kindness, and truth. They are blessed with the ability to recognize and follow the path that leads to Allah, the One worthy of all praise. The repetition of "guided" emphasizes that both pure speech and righteous conduct are divine gifts, not merely human achievements.
orig: وهدوا إلى الطيب من القول وهدوا إلى صراط الحميد

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and prevent [others] from the way of Allah and [from] al-Masjid al-Haram, which We made for the people - equal are the resident therein and one from outside; and whoever intends [a deed] therein of deviation [in religion] or wrongdoing - We will make him taste of a painful punishment
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of the Sacred Mosque (Masjid al-Haram) as a universal place of worship, warning against those who attempt to obstruct access to it or corrupt its sacred purpose. It establishes the principle of religious equality in that all believers, whether local residents or visitors from afar, have equal rights to worship there. The divine warning against wrongdoing within its premises underscores God's protection of sacred spaces and the severe consequences for those who violate their sanctity.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ويصدون عن سبيل الله والمسجد الحرام الذي جعلناه للناس سواء العاكف فيه والباد ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد بظلم نذقه من عذاب أليم

translation: And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House, [saying], "Do not associate anything with Me and purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who stand [in prayer] and those who bow and prostrate."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine trust in Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) as the appointed custodian of the Ka'bah, emphasizing the fundamental principle of monotheism. The command to "purify" the House extends beyond physical cleanliness to spiritual purity, establishing the Ka'bah as a sanctuary dedicated solely to the worship of One God. This appointment marked the beginning of Makkah's sacred status and established a perpetual spiritual center that would unite believers in their devotion through various forms of worship.
orig: وإذ بوأنا لإبراهيم مكان البيت أن لا تشرك بي شيئا وطهر بيتي للطائفين والقائمين والركع السجود

translation: And proclaim to mankind the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, coming from every distant path
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal appeal and magnetic pull of the Ka'bah, showing how Allah's call to Hajj transcends all physical and geographical barriers. The mention of people coming by foot and on lean camels symbolizes the devotees' willingness to endure hardship and fatigue, demonstrating that spiritual commitment outweighs physical comfort. The phrase "every distant path" suggests the global unity of the Muslim ummah, as believers from all corners of the earth respond to this divine invitation, making the Hajj a powerful symbol of Islamic brotherhood and equality.
orig: وأذن في الناس بالحج يأتوك رجالا وعلى كل ضامر يأتين من كل فج عميق
