translation: There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the ill, nor upon yourselves if you eat from your houses, or your fathers' houses, or your mothers' houses, or your brothers' houses, or your sisters' houses, or your paternal uncles' houses, or your paternal aunts' houses, or your maternal uncles' houses, or your maternal aunts' houses, or from houses whose keys you possess, or from your friend's house. There is no blame upon you whether you eat together or separately. But when you enter houses, give greetings of peace upon each other - a greeting from Allah, blessed and good. Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses that you might use reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Islamic principle of social inclusion and family bonds, particularly regarding shared meals and hospitality. It first removes any stigma or restrictions from people with disabilities, establishing their full social equality. The verse then outlines an extensive network of familial and social relationships where people can feel comfortable sharing meals without formal invitation or restriction. This reflects Islam's emphasis on maintaining strong family ties and social bonds through the sharing of food. The mention of greeting with peace when entering homes establishes the etiquette of fostering warmth and blessing in social interactions, making every visit an opportunity for spiritual reward and strengthening community bonds.
orig: ليس على الأعمى حرج ولا على الأعرج حرج ولا على المريض حرج ولا على أنفسكم أن تأكلوا من بيوتكم أو بيوت آبائكم أو بيوت أمهاتكم أو بيوت إخوانكم أو بيوت أخواتكم أو بيوت أعمامكم أو بيوت عماتكم أو بيوت أخوالكم أو بيوت خالاتكم أو ما ملكتم مفاتحه أو صديقكم ليس عليكم جناح أن تأكلوا جميعا أو أشتاتا فإذا دخلتم بيوتا فسلموا على أنفسكم تحية من عند الله مباركة طيبة كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تعقلون

translation: The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter requiring collective action, they do not depart until they have asked his permission. Indeed, those who ask your permission are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they ask your permission for some affair of theirs, give permission to whom you will among them and ask forgiveness for them from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity, discipline, and respect for leadership in the Muslim community. It establishes a fundamental principle of organizational behavior where collective matters require proper consultation and permission from authority. The practice of seeking permission before leaving demonstrates commitment to the community's interests over individual convenience, and shows that true faith manifests in practical actions, not just verbal declarations. The verse also highlights the leader's discretionary power to grant or withhold permission based on circumstances, while maintaining a spirit of mercy and forgiveness.
orig: إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله وإذا كانوا معه على أمر جامع لم يذهبوا حتى يستأذنوه إن الذين يستأذنونك أولئك الذين يؤمنون بالله ورسوله فإذا استأذنوك لبعض شأنهم فأذن لمن شئت منهم واستغفر لهم الله إن الله غفور رحيم

translation: Make not the calling of the Messenger among you as your calling one another. Allah knows those of you who slip away secretly. So let those who oppose his command beware, lest some trial befall them or a painful torment be inflicted on them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique status of the Prophet Muhammad and the proper etiquette in addressing him. It warns against treating his call or summons with the same casualness as one would treat calls from ordinary people. The divine instruction implies that when the Prophet calls, it carries special significance and authority as it represents divine guidance. Those who try to evade his commands or slip away from his gatherings without proper permission are warned of serious consequences, as disobedience to the Prophet's authority is equivalent to opposing divine will, which could result in spiritual or worldly afflictions.
orig: لا تجعلوا دعاء الرسول بينكم كدعاء بعضكم بعضا قد يعلم الله الذين يتسللون منكم لواذا فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره أن تصيبهم فتنة أو يصيبهم عذاب أليم

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth. He knows that upon which you stand, and [He will know] the Day when they will be returned to Him and He will inform them of what they have done. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete sovereignty and omniscience, highlighting that He maintains a continuous awareness of our beliefs, intentions, and actions in this world. It serves as both a warning and a reminder that we are ultimately accountable for our choices, as every deed is recorded and will be revealed on the Day of Judgment. The certainty of this future reckoning should motivate believers to align their actions with divine guidance.
orig: ألا إن لله ما في السماوات والأرض قد يعلم ما أنتم عليه ويوم يرجعون إليه فينبئهم بما عملوا والله بكل شيء عليم

translation: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant that he may be a warner to all worlds
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite mercy in choosing Prophet Muhammad as His messenger and providing him with the Qur'an (the Criterion) to distinguish truth from falsehood. The use of "blessed" indicates the sacred nature of divine revelation, while "warner to all worlds" highlights the universal scope of Islam's message, transcending time, place, and cultural boundaries.
orig: تبارك الذي نزل الفرقان على عبده ليكون للعالمين نذيرا

translation: He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has not taken a son and has not had a partner in dominion and has created each thing and determined it with precise determination
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute uniqueness and sovereignty, refuting any notion of divine partnership or offspring. It establishes that Allah's power is complete and singular, with no division or sharing of authority. The mention of precise determination indicates that everything in existence follows a carefully designed plan, with nothing occurring randomly but rather according to Allah's exact measure and wisdom.
orig: الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض ولم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك وخلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا

translation: Yet they have taken besides Him gods who create nothing but are themselves created, and who have no power to harm or benefit themselves, and who have no power over death, life, or resurrection.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental flaw in polytheistic worship by emphasizing the complete powerlessness of false deities. It points to the logical contradiction of worshipping entities that lack the most basic attributes of divinity - they cannot create, protect themselves, or control the fundamental aspects of existence. The true Divine nature must possess absolute power over creation, life, and death, suggesting that only the One who possesses these qualities deserves worship.
orig: واتخذوا من دونه آلهة لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون ولا يملكون لأنفسهم ضرا ولا نفعا ولا يملكون موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "This [Qur'an] is not except a falsehood he invented, and another people assisted him in it." But they have committed an injustice and a lie.
interpretation: This verse reveals the psychological state of those who reject truth - when faced with something they cannot rationally deny, they resort to baseless accusations of fabrication. The disbelievers' claim that Muhammad had help in composing the Qur'an demonstrates their desperate attempt to discredit divine revelation through conspiracy theories rather than engaging with its actual message and content.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا إفك افتراه وأعانه عليه قوم آخرون فقد جاءوا ظلما وزورا

translation: And they say, "[The Qur'an] is nothing but legends of the former peoples which he has written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."
interpretation: This verse reveals the skeptics' dismissive attitude towards divine revelation, suggesting their inability to accept supernatural truth. By claiming the Qur'an was merely copied from old tales, they attempted to discredit its divine origin, yet their accusation inadvertently highlights a paradox since Prophet Muhammad was known to be unlettered. Their allegation of morning and evening dictation also demonstrates their desperate attempt to find a mundane explanation for what was clearly beyond ordinary human capability.
orig: وقالوا أساطير الأولين اكتتبها فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا

translation: Say, "It has been sent down by Him who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience as a proof of the Qur'an's divine origin, highlighting that the One who revealed it possesses complete knowledge of all hidden matters in the universe. The mention of His forgiveness and mercy alongside His all-encompassing knowledge suggests that this divine knowledge is not used to condemn but rather to guide and show mercy to His creation.
orig: قل أنزله الذي يعلم السر في السماوات والأرض إنه كان غفورا رحيما

translation: And they say, "What is this messenger who eats food and walks in the markets? Why has an angel not been sent down to him to be a warner with him?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the shallow materialistic thinking of those who rejected the Prophet Muhammad's message, as they failed to understand that prophets are meant to be relatable human beings who serve as practical examples for humanity, not supernatural beings detached from human experience. Their demand for an angel companion shows their misunderstanding of the divine wisdom in choosing human messengers who can demonstrate how to implement divine guidance in daily life.
orig: وقالوا مال هذا الرسول يأكل الطعام ويمشي في الأسواق لولا أنزل إليه ملك فيكون معه نذيرا

translation: "Or [why is not] a treasure sent down to him, or why does he [not] have a garden from which he eats?" And the wrongdoers say, "You follow not but a man affected by magic."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the persistent pattern of skeptics demanding material proof of prophethood, reflecting their inability to recognize spiritual authority without worldly displays of wealth or power. The accusation of being "affected by magic" reveals how people often dismiss divine truth by attributing it to supernatural manipulation rather than accepting its authentic divine source.
orig: أو يلقى إليه كنز أو تكون له جنة يأكل منها وقال الظالمون إن تتبعون إلا رجلا مسحورا

translation: See how they strike comparisons for you, but they have gone astray and cannot find a way
interpretation: This verse illustrates how those who oppose the truth often create false analogies and arguments to discredit divine guidance, but their flawed reasoning leads them further from the right path. Their attempts to undermine the message only reveal their own confusion and inability to find genuine spiritual direction.
orig: انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال فضلوا فلا يستطيعون سبيلا

translation: Blessed is He who, if He wills, could give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He could give you palaces.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's boundless power and generosity, suggesting that divine rewards can far exceed our earthly expectations. The mention of gardens and palaces symbolizes not just material abundance, but the ultimate reward of Paradise, indicating that trust and patience in Allah's plan can lead to rewards beyond our imagination.
orig: تبارك الذي إن شاء جعل لك خيرا من ذلك جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار ويجعل لك قصورا

translation: But they deny the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blazing Fire
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of rejecting the fundamental belief in the Day of Judgment. The use of "Sa'ir" (blazing fire) indicates that denial of accountability in the afterlife is a grave spiritual error that leads to intense divine punishment, as accepting the reality of the Final Hour is essential for moral responsibility and righteous conduct in this world.
orig: بل كذبوا بالساعة وأعتدنا لمن كذب بالساعة سعيرا

translation: When it [Hell] sees them from a distant place, they will hear its fury and roaring
interpretation: This verse portrays Hell as a conscious, living entity that expresses intense anger and hostility towards sinners even before they reach it, highlighting the severe consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing. The personification of Hell's rage through sounds of fury and roaring emphasizes the terrifying nature of divine punishment and serves as a powerful warning to humanity about the gravity of their choices in this life.
orig: إذا رأتهم من مكان بعيد سمعوا لها تغيظا وزفيرا

translation: And when they are thrown into a narrow place therein bound in chains, they will cry out thereupon for destruction
interpretation: This verse illustrates the intense psychological and physical torment of Hell, where the confinement and restraint symbolize not only physical imprisonment but also the spiritual bondage that results from one's misdeeds. The cry for destruction represents the ultimate despair and regret, as the souls realize that their eternal fate is sealed by their own choices in worldly life.
orig: وإذا ألقوا منها مكانا ضيقا مقرنين دعوا هنالك ثبورا

translation: Do not cry out today for one destruction, but cry out for many destructions
interpretation: This verse illustrates the intensity of regret and suffering that wrongdoers will face in the afterlife. The call for multiple destructions rather than just one suggests that their anguish will be so overwhelming that a single cry of despair won't be sufficient to express their torment, highlighting the severe consequences of rejecting faith and truth during worldly life.
orig: لا تدعوا اليوم ثبورا واحدا وادعوا ثبورا كثيرا

translation: Say, "Is that better or the Garden of Eternity which is promised to the righteous? It will be for them a reward and destination."
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the stark contrast between worldly pleasures and eternal paradise, challenging people to reflect on their priorities. It suggests that while temporary gains might seem attractive, they pale in comparison to the everlasting rewards Allah has prepared for those who live righteously. The use of the comparative question format serves to prompt deep introspection about what truly holds lasting value.
orig: قل أذلك خير أم جنة الخلد التي وعد المتقون كانت لهم جزاء ومصيرا

translation: Wherein they shall dwell forever, having whatever they desire - it is a promise binding upon your Lord
interpretation: This verse speaks to the eternal nature of divine reward, emphasizing that Allah's promise of paradise isn't just about temporary pleasure but about complete fulfillment where every legitimate desire finds its answer. The term "binding promise" suggests that Allah has made this reward a self-imposed obligation upon Himself, demonstrating His absolute commitment to rewarding the faithful with perfect contentment.
orig: لهم فيها ما يشاءون خالدين كان على ربك وعدا مسئولا

translation: And [mention] the Day He will gather them and that which they worship besides Allah and will say, "Did you mislead these, My servants, or did they [themselves] stray from the way?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's supreme justice and the accountability of false deities. On the Day of Judgment, even the objects or beings that people wrongfully worshipped will be confronted, highlighting the futility of idol worship. The rhetorical question posed serves to demonstrate that these false gods never had any real power to misguide people, and that humans bear full responsibility for their choice to deviate from monotheism.
orig: ويوم يحشرهم وما يعبدون من دون الله فيقول أأنتم أضللتم عبادي هؤلاء أم هم ضلوا السبيل

translation: They will say: "Glory be to You! It was not proper for us to take protectors besides You. But You provided comforts for them and their forefathers until they forgot the Message and became a lost people."
interpretation: This verse reveals the profound regret of those who took others as protectors instead of Allah. Their confession highlights how worldly comforts and generational inheritance of misguided practices can lead people astray from divine remembrance. The term "bura" (lost people) suggests a complete spiritual and moral bankruptcy, indicating that material comfort without divine guidance leads to spiritual destruction.
orig: قالوا سبحانك ما كان ينبغي لنا أن نتخذ من دونك من أولياء ولكن متعتهم وآباءهم حتى نسوا الذكر وكانوا قوما بورا

translation: For they have denied you in what you say, so you cannot avert [punishment] or [find] help. And whoever among you commits injustice, We will make him taste a great punishment
interpretation: This verse emphasizes divine justice and personal accountability, warning that those who reject truth and commit oppression will face inevitable consequences. The inability to escape or find assistance against divine judgment highlights the absolute nature of Allah's authority and the futility of seeking refuge from His justice through worldly means.
orig: فقد كذبوكم بما تقولون فما تستطيعون صرفا ولا نصرا ومن يظلم منكم نذقه عذابا كبيرا

translation: And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets. And We have made some of you as trial for others - will you have patience? And ever is your Lord, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the human nature of prophets and messengers, countering those who questioned why a prophet would engage in ordinary human activities. It teaches that spiritual excellence doesn't require supernatural existence, but rather lies in how one handles life's challenges while maintaining divine guidance. The mention of some being trials for others suggests that social and economic differences among people serve as tests of character, patience, and faith, challenging both the privileged and underprivileged to respond righteously to their circumstances.
orig: وما أرسلنا قبلك من المرسلين إلا إنهم ليأكلون الطعام ويمشون في الأسواق وجعلنا بعضكم لبعض فتنة أتصبرون وكان ربك بصيرا

translation: And those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Why are angels not sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?" They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed with great insolence.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deep-rooted skepticism and arrogance of those who reject faith, demanding physical proof of divine existence. Their request to see angels or God directly reflects not a genuine desire for truth, but rather their presumptuous attitude that they deserve such extraordinary manifestations. This mindset demonstrates how spiritual blindness often stems from pride and an inflated sense of self-importance rather than from a lack of evidence.
orig: وقال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا لولا أنزل علينا الملائكة أو نرى ربنا لقد استكبروا في أنفسهم وعتوا عتوا كبيرا

translation: The Day they will see the angels, no glad tidings will there be for the criminals that Day, and they will say, "(We seek) a ban (of refuge, protection)."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the terror and despair that wrongdoers will experience on the Day of Judgment. When they finally witness the angels, likely the angels of death or punishment, they will attempt to seek protection using a phrase that Arabs traditionally used for seeking refuge. However, this attempt at finding sanctuary will be futile, as the time for redemption will have passed. The denial of "glad tidings" emphasizes that all hope will be lost for those who lived their lives in sin and transgression.
orig: يوم يرون الملائكة لا بشرى يومئذ للمجرمين ويقولون حجرا محجورا

translation: And We will approach what they have done of deeds and make them as scattered dust.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's treatment of the deeds of disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, suggesting that actions performed without faith, despite appearing meaningful in worldly terms, will have no spiritual value and will dissipate like particles of dust in the wind. It emphasizes that good deeds must be accompanied by true faith to have lasting significance in the afterlife.
orig: وقدمنا إلى ما عملوا من عمل فجعلناه هباء منثورا

translation: The companions of Paradise, that Day, are [in] a better settlement and better resting place
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate reward for the righteous, highlighting that their eternal abode in Paradise represents not just physical comfort but a state of perfect contentment and spiritual fulfillment that surpasses any earthly pleasure or rest. The comparison implied in "better" suggests that whatever comforts or achievements people might have had in worldly life pale in comparison to the divine hospitality in Paradise.
orig: أصحاب الجنة يومئذ خير مستقرا وأحسن مقيلا

translation: And [mention] the Day when the heaven will split open with [emerging] clouds, and the angels will descend in successive descent
interpretation: This verse paints a vivid picture of the dramatic events of the Day of Judgment, where the familiar blue sky we know will be transformed as it splits apart, revealing clouds unlike any we've seen. The descent of angels in ranks signifies the transition from the unseen realm to the visible world, marking the moment when the spiritual and physical realms merge, and divine authority becomes directly manifest to all creation.
orig: ويوم تشقق السماء بالغمام ونزل الملائكة تنزيلا

translation: The true sovereignty on that Day will belong to the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate reality of Allah's absolute authority on the Day of Judgment, when all worldly power structures and claims to sovereignty will dissolve. The difficulty faced by disbelievers stems from their realization that their rejection of divine authority in worldly life led them to a position of complete powerlessness when true sovereignty is revealed.
orig: الملك يومئذ الحق للرحمن وكان يوما على الكافرين عسيرا

translation: And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands [in regret] saying, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way"
interpretation: This verse portrays the profound regret and anguish that will be experienced on the Day of Judgment by those who rejected the path of truth. The act of biting one's hands symbolizes extreme remorse and helplessness, highlighting how the realization of one's mistakes comes too late when the opportunity for redemption has passed. The wrongdoer's wish to have followed the Messenger's path represents humanity's ultimate recognition that salvation lies in following divine guidance.
orig: ويوم يعض الظالم على يديه يقول يا ليتني اتخذت مع الرسول سبيلا

translation: Oh, woe to me! I wish I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend!
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning about the profound impact of choosing our close companions, highlighting how on the Day of Judgment some will deeply regret their choice of friends who led them away from divine guidance. It emphasizes the importance of selecting friends who strengthen our faith rather than those who weaken it.
orig: يا ويلتى ليتني لم أتخذ فلانا خليلا

translation: For he led me away from the Reminder after it had reached me. And Satan is ever to mankind a deserter.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound regret of someone who allowed themselves to be misguided by a bad companion who diverted them from Allah's guidance. The use of "Satan" here could refer to both the literal devil and metaphorically to any negative influence that leads one astray. The term "khazula" (deserter) emphasizes how Satan or evil influences will ultimately abandon humans after leading them to destruction, leaving them to face the consequences alone.
orig: لقد أضلني عن الذكر بعد إذ جاءني وكان الشيطان للإنسان خذولا

translation: And the Messenger said, "O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as [a thing] abandoned"
interpretation: This verse reveals the deep anguish of Prophet Muhammad over his people's neglect of the Qur'an's teachings. It points to how people might physically possess the Qur'an but abandon its practical implementation in their lives, either by not studying it, not reflecting upon it, not following its guidance, or not giving it the reverence it deserves as divine revelation. The Prophet's complaint to Allah shows that true devotion to the Qur'an means actively engaging with it, understanding it, and living by its principles rather than treating it as a mere ceremonial object.
orig: وقال الرسول يا رب إن قومي اتخذوا هذا القرآن مهجورا

translation: And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. And sufficient is your Lord as a guide and a helper.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the universal pattern of resistance faced by those who carry divine messages. Just as previous prophets encountered opposition from wrongdoers, this verse serves as a consolation to Prophet Muhammad, reminding him that such resistance is natural and expected. The concluding statement affirms that Allah's guidance and support are ultimately sufficient to overcome any opposition, suggesting that while earthly adversaries may exist, divine assistance ensures the eventual triumph of truth.
orig: وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا من المجرمين وكفى بربك هاديا ونصيرا

translation: And those who disbelieve say: "Why was the Qur'an not revealed to him all at once?" Thus [it is] that We may strengthen your heart thereby, and We have revealed it gradually.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine wisdom in the gradual revelation of the Qur'an, showing how this method served to strengthen Prophet Muhammad's heart and mission. Like a teacher who presents lessons in digestible portions, the gradual revelation allowed for deeper understanding, better implementation, and stronger spiritual growth. This approach also helped address real-time situations and challenges faced by the early Muslim community, making the guidance more relevant and practical.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن جملة واحدة كذلك لنثبت به فؤادك ورتلناه ترتيلا

translation: And they do not come to you with an argument except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's complete support for Prophet Muhammad in his mission, assuring him that for every objection or argument raised by his opponents, Allah would provide him with the perfect counter-argument and superior explanation. It emphasizes divine backing in intellectual discourse and demonstrates that truth, when properly explained, will always prevail over falsehood.
orig: ولا يأتونك بمثل إلا جئناك بالحق وأحسن تفسيرا

translation: Those who will be gathered on their faces to Hell - those are the worst in position and farthest astray in way
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine justice and warns about the severe consequences of rejecting truth and guidance. The imagery of people being dragged on their faces symbolizes ultimate humiliation and powerlessness, reflecting how their arrogance and defiance in worldly life is transformed into complete degradation in the afterlife. Their position is described as the worst because they chose to turn away from divine guidance despite having been given the capacity to recognize and follow truth.
orig: الذين يحشرون على وجوههم إلى جهنم أولئك شر مكانا وأضل سبيلا

translation: And We gave Moses the Book and made with him his brother Aaron as a minister
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's mercy in providing prophets with support systems. Just as Moses needed assistance in his monumental task of leading the Israelites and confronting Pharaoh, Allah appointed his brother Aaron as his helper and minister, showing that even great leaders need trusted allies and that divine missions often require collaborative effort rather than solitary struggle.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب وجعلنا معه أخاه هارون وزيرا

translation: So We said: "Go both of you to the people who have denied Our signs." Then We destroyed them completely.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine justice and the severe consequences of rejecting truth after it has been clearly presented. When a community persistently denies and rejects divine guidance despite clear evidence and warnings, they become subject to divine punishment. The complete destruction mentioned serves as a powerful warning about the gravity of denying God's signs and the importance of heeding divine messages when they come through appointed messengers.
orig: فقلنا اذهبا إلى القوم الذين كذبوا بآياتنا فدمرناهم تدميرا

translation: And the people of Noah - when they denied the messengers, We drowned them, and We made them a sign for mankind. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's consistent pattern of justice throughout history, showing that rejection of divine guidance leads to consequences that serve as eternal lessons. The specific mention of Noah's people being made a "sign" suggests that their story was preserved as a universal warning about the dangers of persistent disbelief and the importance of heeding divine messages. The punishment wasn't merely punitive but educational, designed to serve as a lasting reminder for future generations about the gravity of rejecting divine truth.
orig: وقوم نوح لما كذبوا الرسل أغرقناهم وجعلناهم للناس آية وأعتدنا للظالمين عذابا أليما

translation: And [We destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud and the companions of the well and many generations between them
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's consistent pattern of dealing with civilizations that reject divine guidance. The mention of these specific nations - 'Aad, Thamud, and the mysterious people of the well (Ar-Rass) - serves as a powerful reminder that no matter how mighty or established a civilization might be, their fate is sealed when they persistently deny truth and engage in wrongdoing. It's a historical lesson emphasizing that divine justice operates across time and geography, warning contemporary societies about the consequences of moral corruption and rejection of divine guidance.
orig: وعادا وثمود وأصحاب الرس وقرونا بين ذلك كثيرا

translation: And to each [of them] We presented examples, and each [of them] We destroyed with [total] destruction
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's consistent pattern in dealing with those who reject truth: He first provides clear signs, examples, and warnings through various means, but when these are persistently ignored, divine justice ultimately prevails through decisive consequences. It's a reminder that rejection of divine guidance after clear demonstration leads to spiritual or physical destruction.
orig: وكلا ضربنا له الأمثال وكلا تبرنا تتبيرا

translation: And they had already come upon the city which was showered with a rain of evil. So did they not see it? Rather, they were not expecting resurrection.
interpretation: This verse highlights humanity's tendency to ignore clear warnings and signs from past civilizations' destruction. The reference to Sodom and Gomorrah serves as a powerful reminder that even when confronted with physical evidence of divine punishment, some people remain willfully blind, primarily because they don't believe in accountability in the afterlife. Their disbelief in resurrection leads them to dismiss historical lessons that could guide them to righteousness.
orig: ولقد أتوا على القرية التي أمطرت مطر السوء أفلم يكونوا يرونها بل كانوا لا يرجون نشورا

translation: And when they see you, they take you not except in ridicule [saying], 'Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?'
interpretation: This verse reveals the arrogance and mockery of the disbelievers who couldn't accept that Allah would choose Muhammad, a "regular" person, as His messenger. Their ridicule stems from their materialistic worldview, expecting a messenger to possess worldly status or supernatural qualities, failing to understand that Allah's wisdom in choosing His messengers transcends superficial human criteria.
orig: وإذا رأوك إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا

translation: He would have nearly led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in [worship of] them. And they will know, when they see the punishment, who is more astray in way.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stubborn mindset of those who reject truth, clinging to falsehood despite clear guidance. Their statement reveals a tragic irony - they view steadfastness in error as a virtue, while rejecting the path to salvation. The divine warning at the verse's end carries a profound message about accountability, suggesting that ultimate clarity comes when facing consequences, though by then it's too late for redemption.
orig: إن كاد ليضلنا عن آلهتنا لولا أن صبرنا عليها وسوف يعلمون حين يرون العذاب من أضل سبيلا

translation: Have you seen the one who takes his own desires as his god? Would you then be a guardian over him?
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound spiritual danger of allowing one's personal desires and whims to become the ultimate authority in life, essentially replacing divine guidance. When someone elevates their desires to the status of worship, making decisions based solely on what they want rather than what is right or divinely ordained, they have essentially created their own false deity. The rhetorical question at the end emphasizes that even the Prophet cannot guide those who have consciously chosen to worship their desires over Allah's guidance.
orig: أرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه أفأنت تكون عليه وكيلا

translation: Or do you think that most of them hear or understand? They are only like cattle - nay, they are even more astray from the path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual blindness that can afflict people who refuse to engage their faculties of reason and understanding. By comparing such individuals to cattle, and then stating they are even more astray, the verse suggests that rejecting conscious spiritual and intellectual engagement is worse than natural animal instinct, as humans have been given the capacity for higher reasoning but choose not to use it.
orig: أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون إن هم إلا كالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا

translation: Have you not seen how your Lord extends the shadow? If He willed, He could have made it still. Then We made the sun its indicator.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's absolute power over natural phenomena and His intricate design of the universe. The gradual movement of shadows throughout the day serves as a subtle reminder of divine precision and control. The fact that shadows could have been made stationary but weren't demonstrates Allah's purposeful choice in creating dynamic systems that benefit humanity, such as helping us mark time and understand celestial movements.
orig: ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل ولو شاء لجعله ساكنا ثم جعلنا الشمس عليه دليلا

translation: Then We draw it to Us, an easy drawing
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's absolute control over all creation, showing how He can effortlessly retract or withdraw whatever He has created or extended. Just as He extends shadows and other phenomena, He can withdraw them with perfect ease, demonstrating His supreme power and authority over the natural world without any difficulty or strain.
orig: ثم قبضناه إلينا قبضا يسيرا

translation: And it is He who has made the night a covering for you, and sleep [a means for] rest, and made the day a resurrection.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine wisdom in creating a natural cycle that sustains both physical and spiritual well-being. The darkness of night serves as a protective blanket, offering privacy and security, while sleep is presented as a minor death that allows for mental and physical rejuvenation. The breaking of dawn symbolizes daily resurrection, giving humans renewed energy and opportunities for productivity, reminding us of the greater resurrection to come.
orig: وهو الذي جعل لكم الليل لباسا والنوم سباتا وجعل النهار نشورا

translation: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, and We send down from the sky pure water
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's perfect design in the natural water cycle, where winds carry clouds laden with rain as harbingers of divine mercy. The description of rain as "pure water" points to its role not just in physical cleansing but also in spiritual purification, highlighting how Allah's mercy manifests through natural phenomena that sustain both our material and spiritual existence.
orig: وهو الذي أرسل الرياح بشرا بين يدي رحمته وأنزلنا من السماء ماء طهورا

translation: That We may give life thereby to a dead land and give it as drink to those We created of grazing livestock and mankind, many [of them]
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's perfect system of water distribution and its role in sustaining life. The metaphor of reviving dead land symbolizes how divine mercy brings hope and sustenance even in seemingly hopeless situations. Just as rain transforms barren earth into flourishing landscapes, Allah's guidance can transform spiritually dead hearts into vibrant centers of faith and productivity.
orig: لنحيي به بلدة ميتا ونسقيه مما خلقنا أنعاما وأناسي كثيرا

translation: And We have certainly distributed it among them that they might be reminded, but most of the people refuse except disbelief
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's continuous effort to guide humanity by presenting His message in various ways and forms, yet despite this divine consideration and care, human beings often choose to reject faith. It points to the paradox of human nature where, even when truth is made clear and accessible, many people persist in denial, showing ingratitude towards Allah's guidance.
orig: ولقد صرفناه بينهم ليذكروا فأبى أكثر الناس إلا كفورا

translation: And if We had willed, We would have sent a warner to every town
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's mercy in choosing Muhammad as a universal messenger rather than sending multiple warners to different locations. It emphasizes that the decision to send one comprehensive message through one prophet was a divine choice meant to unify humanity under a single guidance, rather than fragmenting religious leadership across different regions.
orig: ولو شئنا لبعثنا في كل قرية نذيرا

translation: So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it (the Qur'an) a great striving
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual and intellectual nature of Islamic resistance, where the Qur'an itself serves as the primary tool for confronting falsehood. The "great striving" mentioned refers to using divine knowledge, wisdom, and truth to counter disbelief rather than physical confrontation, highlighting the importance of ideological and peaceful discourse in spreading the message of Islam.
orig: فلا تطع الكافرين وجاهدهم به جهادا كبيرا

translation: And it is He who has released [simultaneously] the two seas, one fresh and sweet and one salty and bitter, and He placed between them a barrier and a prohibiting partition
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's perfect design and control over natural phenomena, specifically highlighting how He maintains the distinct properties of different water bodies. The metaphysical barrier between fresh and salt water represents Allah's divine laws that maintain order in the universe, preventing chaos and preserving the unique characteristics of each element. This natural phenomenon serves as a sign of Allah's wisdom and power in creating balance and harmony in nature.
orig: وهو الذي مرج البحرين هذا عذب فرات وهذا ملح أجاج وجعل بينهما برزخا وحجرا محجورا

translation: And it is He who has created from water a human being and made him [a relative by] lineage and marriage. And ever is your Lord competent
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's infinite wisdom in creating complex human relationships and social structures from a simple element - water. It highlights how He established two fundamental types of human bonds: blood relations and marriage ties, demonstrating His power in creating intricate social systems from basic physical matter. This speaks to the divine design in human civilization and family structures.
orig: وهو الذي خلق من الماء بشرا فجعله نسبا وصهرا وكان ربك قديرا

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them, and the disbeliever is ever a helper against his Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of idolatry and false worship, emphasizing how humans often direct their devotion to powerless objects or deities that can neither help nor harm them. The deeper message suggests that by engaging in such meaningless worship, disbelievers are actively working against their own spiritual interests and opposing Allah's truth, effectively becoming adversaries to their own Creator's purpose.
orig: ويعبدون من دون الله ما لا ينفعهم ولا يضرهم وكان الكافر على ربه ظهيرا

translation: And We have not sent you except as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of Prophet Muhammad's mission: to give hope to those who seek righteousness by promising them divine rewards, while also cautioning humanity about the consequences of rejecting divine guidance. It defines the Prophet's role as a messenger whose primary duty is to convey the message, not to force people to accept it or to be responsible for their choices.
orig: وما أرسلناك إلا مبشرا ونذيرا

translation: Say, "I do not ask you for any reward for it except that whoever wills might take a path to his Lord."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's sincerity and selflessness in his mission. He seeks no worldly compensation for delivering Allah's message. The only "payment" he would accept is for people to choose guidance and establish a connection with their Creator, which ultimately benefits them, not him. This reflects the pure intention behind prophetic teachings, focusing solely on spiritual elevation rather than material gain.
orig: قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر إلا من شاء أن يتخذ إلى ربه سبيلا

translation: And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt Him with His praise. And sufficient is He to be aware of the sins of His servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of placing complete trust in Allah's eternal nature, highlighting that unlike all creation, He alone is immortal and ever-living. It teaches that true security and reliance can only be found in the Divine, as all other dependencies are temporary. The mention of Allah's awareness of sins serves as both a warning and comfort - warning for those who transgress and comfort for those who seek justice, knowing that nothing escapes His knowledge.
orig: وتوكل على الحي الذي لا يموت وسبح بحمده وكفى به بذنوب عباده خبيرا

translation: Who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days and then established Himself above the Throne - the Most Merciful, so ask about Him one [well] informed
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's supreme authority and control over creation while highlighting His attributes of mercy. The mention of "six days" demonstrates that Allah created the universe in a deliberate, planned manner rather than instantaneously, teaching us the value of patience and process. The reference to establishing Himself above the Throne indicates His dominion and sovereignty, while directing people to seek knowledge about Him from those who are well-informed suggests the importance of learning about Allah through authentic sources and knowledgeable scholars.
orig: الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام ثم استوى على العرش الرحمن فاسأل به خبيرا

translation: And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Should we prostrate to that which you command us?" And it increases them in aversion.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deep-rooted arrogance and spiritual blindness of those who reject faith, as they question even the basic concept of submitting to Allah's mercy. Their response shows not just ignorance, but a willful defiance and pride that prevents them from accepting divine guidance. The mention of their increasing aversion suggests that their rejection becomes more entrenched with each invitation to faith, demonstrating how continued resistance to truth can harden one's heart progressively.
orig: وإذا قيل لهم اسجدوا للرحمن قالوا وما الرحمن أنسجد لما تأمرنا وزادهم نفورا

translation: Blessed is He who has placed in the sky constellations and placed therein a lamp and a luminous moon
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's infinite power and wisdom in creating celestial bodies that serve multiple purposes. The constellations act as navigational guides, while the sun (referred to as a "lamp") and moon provide essential light and energy that sustain life on Earth. The deliberate use of the word "blessed" emphasizes that these cosmic arrangements are not random but carefully designed blessings from the Creator for humanity's benefit.
orig: تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا وجعل فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا

translation: And it is He who made the night and day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's divine wisdom in creating a cosmic system of alternating day and night, offering humanity distinct opportunities for spiritual growth. The contrast between light and darkness serves as a perpetual reminder of God's presence, where nighttime offers solitude for reflection and worship, while daylight presents chances to demonstrate gratitude through active service and good deeds.
orig: وهو الذي جعل الليل والنهار خلفة لمن أراد أن يذكر أو أراد شكورا

translation: And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say words of peace
interpretation: This verse describes one of the fundamental characteristics of true believers - their humility and dignified response to provocation. When they walk, they do so without arrogance or showing off, demonstrating their understanding that all humans are equal before Allah. More significantly, when faced with ignorance or hostility, they choose peace over confrontation, showing emotional maturity and self-restraint. This reflects the Islamic principle of responding to negativity with positivity, choosing the higher moral ground even in difficult situations.
orig: وعباد الرحمن الذين يمشون على الأرض هونا وإذا خاطبهم الجاهلون قالوا سلاما

translation: And those who spend the night prostrating and standing before their Lord
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual excellence of those believers who maintain a deep connection with Allah through voluntary night prayers (Tahajjud). Their dedication to worship during hours when others sleep demonstrates their sincerity, as they choose devotion over comfort when no one is watching. The alternation between prostration and standing signifies their complete submission, combining physical humility with spiritual alertness in their worship.
orig: والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما

translation: And those who say, "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell. Indeed, its punishment is ever adhering"
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound consciousness of true believers who recognize the gravity of divine punishment. Their earnest supplication demonstrates that they live in a state of hopeful fear, understanding that Hell's torment is a permanent, inescapable affliction that clings to its inhabitants. Their prayer shows both humility and awareness that salvation comes only through Allah's mercy, not through their deeds alone.
orig: والذين يقولون ربنا اصرف عنا عذاب جهنم إن عذابها كان غراما

translation: Indeed, it is an evil place of settlement and residence
interpretation: This verse speaks to the ultimate consequence of wrongdoing and disbelief, describing Hell as a permanent dwelling. The emphasis on both "settlement" and "residence" reinforces the eternal nature of this punishment, suggesting that those who choose evil in this life will find themselves in a state of perpetual torment that serves as both their immediate resting place and their eternal home.
orig: إنها ساءت مستقرا ومقاما

translation: And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but maintain a balance between the two
interpretation: This verse establishes the Islamic principle of moderation in financial matters, teaching that true believers should strike a balance between excessive spending and miserliness. It suggests that financial wisdom lies in maintaining a middle path that avoids the extremes of wasteful consumption and harmful withholding, reflecting Allah's preference for measured and thoughtful management of resources.
orig: والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا وكان بين ذلك قواما

translation: And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity or kill the soul which Allah has forbidden [to be killed], except by right, and do not commit adultery. And whoever does that will meet a penalty
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental principles of moral behavior in Islam, highlighting that true believers maintain absolute monotheism and respect the sanctity of human life and marriage. The mention of these three specific prohibitions together suggests that they represent some of the most serious violations against divine law and human dignity. The warning of punishment serves as a powerful deterrent, indicating that these actions not only harm society but also have severe spiritual consequences in the afterlife.
orig: والذين لا يدعون مع الله إلها آخر ولا يقتلون النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق ولا يزنون ومن يفعل ذلك يلق أثاما

translation: The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in disgrace
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of persistent wrongdoing, particularly for those who knowingly commit sins. The doubling of punishment suggests that those who had knowledge and understanding yet chose to transgress will face greater accountability. The element of eternal disgrace indicates that the spiritual and moral corruption one chooses in this life has lasting implications that extend beyond mere physical punishment.
orig: يضاعف له العذاب يوم القيامة ويخلد فيه مهانا

translation: Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work. For them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good ones. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's infinite mercy and the transformative power of sincere repentance. It suggests that when someone genuinely turns away from their past sins with true remorse, embraces faith, and actively pursues good deeds, Allah doesn't just forgive their sins but actually converts their previous misdeeds into rewards. This divine transformation symbolizes the complete renewal of a person's spiritual record, encouraging hope and highlighting that no one is beyond redemption if they sincerely seek it.
orig: إلا من تاب وآمن وعمل عملا صالحا فأولئك يبدل الله سيئاتهم حسنات وكان الله غفورا رحيما

translation: And whoever repents and does righteous deeds, then indeed, he turns to Allah with true repentance
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transformative power of sincere repentance when coupled with positive action. It suggests that true repentance isn't merely feeling remorse or verbal acknowledgment of wrongdoing, but must be accompanied by concrete steps toward righteousness. The phrase "turns to Allah" implies a complete reorientation of one's life toward divine guidance, indicating that genuine repentance is a journey back to one's spiritual nature.
orig: ومن تاب وعمل صالحا فإنه يتوب إلى الله متابا

translation: And those who do not bear witness to falsehood, and when they pass by futility, they pass by with dignity
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining moral integrity and personal dignity in the face of falsehood and frivolity. It suggests that true believers should neither participate in nor validate dishonest activities, and when confronted with meaningless or trivial matters, they should maintain their composure and dignity rather than engaging with or being drawn into them. This reflects the Islamic principle of rising above base behavior and maintaining one's ethical standards even when surrounded by impropriety.
orig: والذين لا يشهدون الزور وإذا مروا باللغو مروا كراما

translation: And those who, when reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinguishing quality of true believers who engage with divine guidance consciously and actively. Unlike those who merely hear without understanding or see without insight, genuine believers interact with God's revelations with full awareness, reflection, and emotional engagement. They approach scripture with an alert mind and an open heart, ready to understand, implement, and be transformed by its teachings.
orig: والذين إذا ذكروا بآيات ربهم لم يخروا عليها صما وعميانا

translation: And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes and make us an example for the righteous"
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep spiritual aspiration of believers who seek not just personal piety, but wish to establish righteous families that bring joy and spiritual fulfillment. The request to be made "leaders for the righteous" shows their desire to positively influence others, suggesting that true spirituality includes being an inspiration and guide for others in their journey of faith.
orig: والذين يقولون ربنا هب لنا من أزواجنا وذرياتنا قرة أعين واجعلنا للمتقين إماما

translation: Those will be awarded the Chamber for what they patiently endured, and they will be received therein with greetings and [words of] peace
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound spiritual principle that patience and perseverance in faith are rewarded with the highest stations in Paradise. The "Chamber" (Al-Ghurfa) symbolizes an elevated spiritual status, suggesting that those who maintain steadfast faith despite life's trials attain special honor in the afterlife. The greeting of peace they receive represents the ultimate state of tranquility and divine acceptance, marking their complete liberation from worldly anxieties and struggles.
orig: أولئك يجزون الغرفة بما صبروا ويلقون فيها تحية وسلاما

translation: They will abide therein forever - how excellent a place of settlement and residence
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of Paradise, highlighting that it's not just a temporary dwelling but a permanent home. The use of "excellent" (حسنت) suggests that this eternal abode surpasses all human expectations of comfort and satisfaction, offering a state of complete contentment that makes it the ultimate destination for the righteous.
orig: خالدين فيها حسنت مستقرا ومقاما

translation: Say, "What would my Lord care for you if not for your supplication? For you have denied, so your denial will be adherent (to you)."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound significance of human prayer and devotion in their relationship with Allah. It suggests that our value in Allah's sight is deeply connected to our sincere seeking of Him through prayer. The divine attention and care we receive is contingent upon our conscious effort to connect with our Creator. Those who reject this connection and deny the truth will face the natural consequences of their denial, which will become an inseparable part of their fate.
orig: قل ما يعبأ بكم ربي لولا دعاؤكم فقد كذبتم فسوف يكون لزاما

translation: Ta. Sin. Mim.
interpretation: These mystical letters at the beginning of Surah Al-Qasas are believed to signify Allah's unique knowledge of their true meaning, serving as a reminder of the divine origin of the Qur'an and the limitless nature of Allah's wisdom that humans cannot fully comprehend
orig: طسم

translation: These are the verses of the clear Book
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine clarity and unambiguous nature of the Qur'an, indicating that its teachings and guidance are accessible and comprehensible to those who sincerely seek understanding, leaving no room for confusion about its divine origin and purpose.
orig: تلك آيات الكتاب المبين

translation: Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they will not become believers
interpretation: This verse reflects Allah's compassionate address to Prophet Muhammad, acknowledging his deep emotional distress over people's rejection of faith. It suggests that while the Prophet's concern for humanity's guidance is admirable, he shouldn't let it consume him to the point of self-destruction, as ultimate guidance rests with Allah.
orig: لعلك باخع نفسك ألا يكونوا مؤمنين

translation: If We willed, We could send down upon them a sign from the sky, and their necks would remain bent in submission to it
interpretation: The verse illustrates Allah's complete power and ability to compel belief through overwhelming signs, but He chooses not to do so because true faith must come through free will and conscious choice rather than forced submission. The imagery of bent necks suggests that such a sign would be so powerful that even the most stubborn disbelievers would have no choice but to submit, though this submission would not represent genuine faith.
orig: إن نشأ ننزل عليهم من السماء آية فظلت أعناقهم لها خاضعين

translation: And no new revelation comes to them from the Most Merciful except that they turn away from it
interpretation: This verse highlights a recurring pattern in human behavior where people often resist and reject divine guidance when it reaches them, even though it comes from Allah's mercy. This resistance to new spiritual truths reflects a deep-seated tendency in human nature to cling to familiar beliefs and practices, even when presented with clear signs and revelations that could lead to their betterment.
orig: وما يأتيهم من ذكر من الرحمن محدث إلا كانوا عنه معرضين

translation: So they have denied, and there will come to them the news of what they used to ridicule
interpretation: This verse warns those who mock divine truth that their derision will ultimately backfire, as the reality of what they dismissed will manifest itself in ways they cannot deny. It points to the universal principle that truth prevails over falsehood, even if it takes time, and those who reject it will face the consequences of their denial.
orig: فقد كذبوا فسيأتيهم أنباء ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: Do they not see the earth - how much We have produced therein from every noble kind?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on Allah's creative power and generosity through the diversity of plant life. The use of "noble kind" (zawj kareem) suggests that each plant species has inherent value, dignity, and purpose in Allah's grand design. The verse challenges human beings to recognize divine craftsmanship in the natural world as evidence of Allah's existence and wisdom.
orig: أولم يروا إلى الأرض كم أنبتنا فيها من كل زوج كريم

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers
interpretation: This verse highlights a recurring theme in the Qur'an about human nature's resistance to divine signs. Despite clear evidence of Allah's power and existence being presented, the majority of people tend to remain skeptical or disbelieving, choosing to ignore or reject these signs due to their attachment to worldly beliefs or their unwillingness to change their established ways of thinking.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of Allah's attributes, combining absolute power with infinite mercy. It suggests that true strength and mercy are not contradictory but complementary qualities, teaching us that those in positions of power should temper their authority with compassion, following the divine example.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: And when your Lord called to Moses, "Go to the wrongdoing people"
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's direct communication with Moses, demonstrating the special relationship between the divine and His chosen prophet. The command to confront the "wrongdoing people" shows that prophets are tasked with challenging oppression and injustice, even when facing powerful adversaries. The use of "wrongdoing people" rather than specifically naming them emphasizes that the divine message stands against injustice regardless of who the perpetrators are.
orig: وإذ نادى ربك موسى أن ائت القوم الظالمين

translation: The people of Pharaoh, will they not fear [Allah]?
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual blindness and arrogance of those in power who refuse to acknowledge divine authority. It suggests that true security and wisdom lie in maintaining consciousness of God, which Pharaoh's people fatally lacked despite witnessing clear signs.
orig: قوم فرعون ألا يتقون

translation: He said, "My Lord, I fear that they will deny me"
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep human anxiety and vulnerability felt by prophets in their divine mission. It shows that even God's chosen messengers experienced natural human fears about rejection, highlighting the emotional and psychological challenges involved in conveying divine messages to resistant communities. The prophet's candid expression of fear to Allah also demonstrates the intimate relationship between a believer and their Creator, where one can openly share their concerns and seek divine support.
orig: قال رب إني أخاف أن يكذبون

translation: "And my breast becomes tight, and my tongue will not loosen, so send for Aaron"
interpretation: "This verse reflects Moses' deep anxiety and speech impediment when Allah commanded him to confront Pharaoh. It reveals how even great prophets experienced human vulnerabilities, and shows the wisdom in acknowledging one's limitations and seeking support from others when undertaking difficult tasks."
orig: ويضيق صدري ولا ينطلق لساني فأرسل إلى هارون

translation: And they have against me a crime, so I fear they will kill me
interpretation: This verse reflects Prophet Moses's deep anxiety about returning to Egypt where he had accidentally killed a man. It shows how even prophets experienced human emotions like fear, and demonstrates the importance of seeking Allah's protection when facing dangerous situations. The verse also illustrates how past actions can create obstacles in fulfilling divine missions, yet with Allah's help, these challenges can be overcome.
orig: ولهم علي ذنب فأخاف أن يقتلون

translation: He said: "By no means! Go forth, both of you, with Our Signs; We are with you, listening."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's divine support and protection for His messengers. When Moses and Aaron expressed their fears about confronting Pharaoh, Allah reassured them of His constant presence and vigilance. The verse illustrates that when we act in accordance with divine guidance, we are never truly alone, as Allah watches over those who carry out His mission. It teaches us that with divine support, we can overcome even the most daunting challenges.
orig: قال كلا فاذهبا بآياتنا إنا معكم مستمعون

translation: So go to Pharaoh and say, "Indeed, we are messengers from the Lord of the worlds"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine authority and courage required in speaking truth to power, as Moses and Aaron were commanded to confront one of history's most powerful rulers with unwavering conviction in their divine mission. It illustrates how God empowers His chosen messengers to challenge oppression and injustice, regardless of the worldly status of those they must confront.
orig: فأتيا فرعون فقولا إنا رسول رب العالمين

translation: Send with us the Children of Israel
interpretation: This verse reflects the divine command to Pharaoh through Moses to release the Israelites from bondage, emphasizing God's role as protector of the oppressed and His intervention in human history to establish justice and freedom for persecuted peoples
orig: أن أرسل معنا بني إسرائيل

translation: [Pharaoh] said, "Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life?"
interpretation: This verse reveals the manipulative nature of those in power, as Pharaoh attempts to use past kindness as a tool of emotional manipulation and control. By reminding Moses of his upbringing in the palace, Pharaoh tries to create a sense of obligation and guilt, illustrating how oppressors often use psychological tactics to maintain their authority and suppress opposition to their rule.
orig: قال ألم نربك فينا وليدا ولبثت فينا من عمرك سنين

translation: And you did your deed which you did while you were of the disbelievers
interpretation: This verse refers to Moses' past action of killing an Egyptian before receiving divine guidance, highlighting how even great prophets had moments of imperfection before their spiritual awakening. It teaches us that what matters is not our past mistakes but our journey toward righteousness and acceptance of divine truth.
orig: وفعلت فعلتك التي فعلت وأنت من الكافرين

translation: He said, "I did it then, when I was one of those who are astray."
interpretation: This verse reflects the humility and self-awareness of Prophet Moses as he acknowledges his past mistake, demonstrating that even great prophets went through periods of spiritual development before receiving divine guidance. It teaches us the importance of recognizing our past errors and showing remorse as part of personal growth and spiritual evolution.
orig: قال فعلتها إذا وأنا من الضالين

translation: So I fled from you when I feared you. Then my Lord granted me wisdom and made me one of the messengers
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine pattern of transforming adversity into opportunity. Moses's initial act of fleeing from danger, driven by fear, became the catalyst for his spiritual elevation and prophetic appointment, demonstrating how apparent setbacks in one's life can be stepping stones to greater spiritual heights and divine purpose
orig: ففررت منكم لما خفتكم فوهب لي ربي حكما وجعلني من المرسلين

translation: And this is the favor with which you reproach me - that you have enslaved the Children of Israel
interpretation: This verse reveals the complex power dynamics between Moses and Pharaoh, where Pharaoh attempts to manipulate Moses by suggesting that his upbringing in the palace was a favor, while simultaneously using this "favor" to justify the oppression of Moses's people. It exposes how oppressors often use their "benevolence" as a tool to maintain control and justify their unjust actions.
orig: وتلك نعمة تمنها علي أن عبدت بني إسرائيل

translation: Pharaoh said: "And what is the Lord of the worlds?"
interpretation: This verse reveals the arrogance and defiance of those in power who deny divine authority. Pharaoh's question isn't seeking knowledge but rather demonstrates his skepticism and pride, challenging the very concept of a universal deity above his claimed divinity. It shows how absolute power can blind rulers to spiritual truths and lead them to question even the most fundamental aspects of faith.
orig: قال فرعون وما رب العالمين

translation: He said, "[He is] the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you would be certain"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true certainty in faith comes through recognizing Allah's absolute sovereignty over all existence, from the highest heavens to the earth and everything in between. It suggests that contemplating the vastness and interconnectedness of creation should naturally lead to conviction about the Creator's power and authority.
orig: قال رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما إن كنتم موقنين

translation: He said to those around him, "Do you not hear?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of active listening and attentiveness in spiritual and moral matters. The rhetorical question suggests frustration with those who are physically present but mentally disconnected from important truths being conveyed to them.
orig: قال لمن حوله ألا تستمعون

translation: He is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine sovereignty across generations, highlighting that Allah's lordship isn't confined to the present but extends throughout human history. It serves to remind people that their ancestors were also under the same divine authority, establishing a spiritual connection between past and present generations under one supreme authority.
orig: قال ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين

translation: He said, "Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the common tactic used by those in power to discredit prophets and reformers by questioning their sanity, rather than addressing their message. It reflects how truth-bearers throughout history have faced character assassination as a means to undermine their divine message.
orig: قال إن رسولكم الذي أرسل إليكم لمجنون

translation: He said, "[He is] the Lord of the East and the West and what is between them, if you would reason."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty over all directions and spaces, highlighting that His dominion isn't limited to specific regions but encompasses everything in existence. The phrase "if you would reason" suggests that recognizing Allah's complete authority is a matter of logical contemplation, inviting humans to use their intellect to understand the vastness of divine power.
orig: قال رب المشرق والمغرب وما بينهما إن كنتم تعقلون

translation: [Pharaoh] said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely place you among those imprisoned."
interpretation: This verse reveals the extreme arrogance and tyranny of those in power who demand absolute loyalty and submission, even to the point of claiming divine status. It shows how authoritarian rulers often respond to spiritual and ideological challenges with threats of violence and persecution, demonstrating their fear of losing control over people's minds and hearts.
orig: قال لئن اتخذت إلها غيري لأجعلنك من المسجونين

translation: He said: "Even if I brought you something manifest (clear)?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the challenge faced by those who bring truth to those in power or authority. It reflects how even when presented with clear evidence or proof, some people might still resist accepting the truth due to their prejudices or vested interests.
orig: قال أولو جئتك بشيء مبين

translation: He said, "Then bring it, if you are truthful."
interpretation: This verse illustrates a common challenge posed to those who make claims without evidence. It emphasizes the Islamic principle that truth requires substantiation, not mere assertion. The demand for proof serves as a powerful rhetorical device that exposes empty claims and establishes the importance of backing one's statements with concrete evidence.
orig: قال فأت به إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: So he threw down his staff, and suddenly it was a clear serpent
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's absolute power to transform reality and perform miracles beyond human comprehension, as demonstrated when Moses' staff turned into a real serpent. It serves as a reminder that divine miracles occur to strengthen the faith of believers and establish the authenticity of prophetic missions.
orig: فألقى عصاه فإذا هي ثعبان مبين

translation: And he drew out his hand, and behold! it was white to all beholders
interpretation: This verse describes one of Prophet Moses's miracles where his hand became luminously white without any illness, symbolizing divine light and guidance. The miracle served as a powerful sign of his prophethood, demonstrating that seemingly impossible transformations are possible through Allah's will, and that ordinary things can become extraordinary manifestations of divine power when Allah wills it.
orig: ونزع يده فإذا هي بيضاء للناظرين

translation: He said to the chiefs around him, "Indeed, this is a learned magician"
interpretation: This verse illustrates how those in power often attempt to discredit divine truth by labeling its bearers with derogatory terms. By calling a messenger of truth a "magician," the speaker reveals their strategy of undermining authentic spiritual guidance by attributing it to mere trickery or deception, showing how established authorities frequently resist messages that challenge their power structure.
orig: قال للملإ حوله إن هذا لساحر عليم

translation: He wants to drive you out of your land with his magic, so what do you command?
interpretation: This verse reveals the defensive mindset of those in power who feel threatened by truth and divine guidance. They attempt to discredit authentic spiritual leadership by attributing it to sorcery, showing how established authorities often try to maintain their control by portraying reformers as threats to social stability and territorial sovereignty.
orig: يريد أن يخرجكم من أرضكم بسحره فماذا تأمرون

translation: They said: "Put him and his brother off (for a time), and send callers to the cities"
interpretation: This verse reflects the Pharaoh's advisors' fear of Moses's growing influence, suggesting a strategic delay tactic while mobilizing forces throughout Egypt. Their response shows how authoritarian systems often react to perceived threats by buying time and gathering resources to maintain their power structure.
orig: قالوا أرجه وأخاه وابعث في المدائن حاشرين

translation: They will bring you every learned, skilled magician
interpretation: This verse highlights the competitive nature of truth versus falsehood, where those who oppose divine guidance often rely on deception and illusion. The "learned magicians" represent those who use their knowledge and skills to mislead others, rather than seeking and supporting truth. It warns believers to be vigilant against sophisticated forms of deception, even when presented by those who appear knowledgeable.
orig: يأتوك بكل سحار عليم

translation: So the magicians were assembled for the appointment on a specified day
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's perfect timing and control over events. The gathering of Pharaoh's magicians wasn't a random occurrence but a divinely orchestrated moment to demonstrate His supreme power through Moses. It shows how even the schemes of disbelievers ultimately serve Allah's greater plan to establish truth over falsehood.
orig: فجمع السحرة لميقات يوم معلوم

translation: And it was said to the people, "Are you all gathered?"
interpretation: This verse reflects Allah's emphasis on collective accountability and the gathering of humanity for judgment. It suggests a moment of universal assembly where all souls must face their actions, highlighting the equality of all humans before divine justice regardless of their worldly status.
orig: وقيل للناس هل أنتم مجتمعون

translation: Perhaps we will follow the magicians if they are the predominant ones
interpretation: This verse reflects the fickle nature of faith based on worldly success rather than genuine conviction. The people's willingness to follow whoever appears victorious shows how superficial allegiance can be when it's based on power and dominance rather than truth and principles.
orig: لعلنا نتبع السحرة إن كانوا هم الغالبين

translation: And when the magicians came, they said to Pharaoh, "Will there indeed be a reward for us if we are the victors?"
interpretation: This verse reveals the materialistic and opportunistic nature of those who sell their skills and services to support falsehood. The magicians' first concern was securing payment, showing how those who align with oppressive powers often prioritize personal gain over truth and justice. Their question also demonstrates how tyrannical systems maintain power through transactional relationships rather than genuine loyalty or belief.
orig: فلما جاء السحرة قالوا لفرعون أئن لنا لأجرا إن كنا نحن الغالبين

translation: He said, "Yes, and indeed, you will then be among those near [to me]"
interpretation: This verse reveals the manipulative nature of power dynamics, where Pharaoh uses the promise of status and proximity to authority as a tool to win loyalty. It demonstrates how privilege and social position are often used as rewards to influence people's choices and allegiances, particularly in hierarchical systems.
orig: قال نعم وإنكم إذا لمن المقربين

translation: Moses said to them, "Cast whatever you are going to cast."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Moses's supreme confidence in Allah's power over the magicians' illusions. Rather than showing fear or hesitation, he challenges them directly, demonstrating that truth has nothing to fear from falsehood, and genuine divine power surpasses all human deception.
orig: قال لهم موسى ألقوا ما أنتم ملقون

translation: So they threw their ropes and their staffs and said, "By the might of Pharaoh, indeed we will be the victors"
interpretation: This verse illustrates how pride and blind allegiance to worldly power can lead people to challenge divine truth. The magicians' declaration of victory in Pharaoh's name, rather than acknowledging a higher power, demonstrates how earthly authority can corrupt one's spiritual judgment and lead to misplaced confidence.
orig: فألقوا حبالهم وعصيهم وقالوا بعزة فرعون إنا لنحن الغالبون

translation: So Moses threw down his staff, and suddenly it swallowed up all their deceptions
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine truth's ultimate triumph over falsehood. When Moses confronts the magicians, his genuine miracle, empowered by Allah, completely overwhelms and nullifies their illusions and trickery. It demonstrates how authentic divine power will always prevail over human deception and artificial displays, no matter how impressive they might initially appear.
orig: فألقى موسى عصاه فإذا هي تلقف ما يأفكون

translation: So the magicians fell down in prostration
interpretation: This verse illustrates a profound moment of divine truth overcoming falsehood, where even those who were initially opposed to the truth (the magicians) recognized and submitted to divine authority when confronted with genuine miraculous power. Their immediate prostration symbolizes how truth, when manifested clearly, can transform even the strongest opponents into devoted believers.
orig: فألقي السحرة ساجدين

translation: They said: "We believe in the Lord of the Worlds"
interpretation: This declaration represents a profound moment of spiritual awakening and surrender, where individuals consciously choose to submit to the universal truth. It signifies the recognition that there is one supreme authority governing all existence, transcending cultural, geographical, and temporal boundaries. The use of "Lord of the Worlds" rather than a specific divine name emphasizes the all-encompassing nature of God's sovereignty over every realm of existence.
orig: قالوا آمنا برب العالمين

translation: The Lord of Moses and Aaron
