interpretation: This phrase emphasizes the universal nature of divine authority, reminding us that the same God who guided these great prophets remains sovereign over all creation. It establishes a continuity of divine guidance across different prophetic traditions and underscores the unity of monotheistic faith.
orig: رب موسى وهارون

translation: He (Pharaoh) said: "You have believed in him before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your chief who has taught you magic. So you will surely know. I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you all."
interpretation: This verse reveals the deep-seated insecurity and tyrannical nature of absolute power, where Pharaoh's response to his magicians' conversion demonstrates how authoritarian leaders view independent faith as a threat to their control. The verse also illustrates how truth, when recognized, can transform even those who were once opponents into believers, regardless of the consequences they may face.
orig: قال آمنتم له قبل أن آذن لكم إنه لكبيركم الذي علمكم السحر فلسوف تعلمون لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم أجمعين

translation: They said, "No harm! Indeed, to our Lord we will return."
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound faith and unwavering trust of believers in the face of adversity. When threatened with punishment or harm, they demonstrate complete reliance on Allah, showing that worldly threats hold no power over those who are certain of their ultimate return to their Creator. Their response indicates that any temporary suffering in this world is insignificant compared to the eternal reward that awaits them in the hereafter.
orig: قالوا لا ضير إنا إلى ربنا منقلبون

translation: Indeed, we hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins because we were the first of the believers
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound spiritual aspiration of true believers who, despite their shortcomings, maintain unwavering hope in Allah's mercy. It particularly emphasizes how being among the forerunners in faith demonstrates genuine conviction and courage, suggesting that such pioneering faith might serve as grounds for special divine consideration and forgiveness.
orig: إنا نطمع أن يغفر لنا ربنا خطايانا أن كنا أول المؤمنين

translation: And We revealed to Moses, "Travel by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued."
interpretation: This verse reflects Allah's divine protection and strategic guidance during times of persecution. It shows how Allah provides precise instructions to His chosen leaders at critical moments, demonstrating that even in seemingly impossible situations, He has already planned an escape route for the believers. The night journey symbolizes how liberation sometimes requires moving through periods of darkness with complete trust in divine guidance.
orig: وأوحينا إلى موسى أن أسر بعبادي إنكم متبعون

translation: So Pharaoh sent gatherers throughout the cities
interpretation: This verse illustrates Pharaoh's panic and defensive reaction to Moses's message, showing how tyrannical leaders often mobilize their resources and military might when they feel their authority is threatened. The act of sending gatherers throughout cities demonstrates the systematic nature of oppression and how autocratic power structures respond to challenges to their rule.
orig: فأرسل فرعون في المدائن حاشرين

translation: Indeed these are but a small band
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogant mindset of those in power who underestimate their opponents based on numbers alone, failing to recognize that strength lies not in quantity but in faith, determination, and divine support
orig: إن هؤلاء لشرذمة قليلون

translation: And indeed, they are causing us rage
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep-seated frustration and anger of the disbelievers towards the believers, highlighting how the mere existence and steadfastness of the faithful provokes hostility in those who oppose the truth. It demonstrates that success and unity of believers often triggers resentment in their opponents, yet this opposition serves as a testament to the believers' effectiveness in their mission.
orig: وإنهم لنا لغائظون

translation: And indeed, we are all cautious
interpretation: This verse reflects the natural human instinct for self-preservation and vigilance. It suggests that maintaining a state of alertness and preparedness is not just prudent but divinely acknowledged as a legitimate aspect of human behavior. The collective "we" implies that cautiousness is a shared human trait, essential for survival and protection against potential threats.
orig: وإنا لجميع حاذرون

translation: So We drove them out from gardens and springs
interpretation: The verse speaks to divine retribution, showing how Allah's punishment can transform a state of luxury and abundance into one of deprivation. It illustrates that no matter how secure or prosperous one's position may seem, divine justice can swiftly alter circumstances when people persist in wrongdoing or reject truth.
orig: فأخرجناهم من جنات وعيون

translation: And treasures and noble dwellings
interpretation: This verse speaks to the impermanence of worldly possessions and status. Even the most precious treasures and prestigious positions we might attain in this life are temporary and will be left behind. It serves as a reminder that we shouldn't become overly attached to material wealth or social standing, as these are not what define our true worth in the sight of Allah.
orig: وكنوز ومقام كريم

translation: Thus, and We made the Children of Israel inherit it
interpretation: This verse signifies God's fulfillment of His divine promise to the Israelites, granting them authority over the land after their persecution. It demonstrates how God elevates those who remain patient and steadfast in their faith through times of hardship, ultimately rewarding their perseverance with empowerment and sovereignty.
orig: كذلك وأورثناها بني إسرائيل

translation: So they pursued them at sunrise
interpretation: This verse from Surah Ash-Shu'ara speaks of Pharaoh's army pursuing Moses and the Children of Israel, highlighting how oppressors often act with haste and aggression in their pursuit of those they wish to subjugate. The timing of sunrise symbolizes the critical moment when truth and falsehood would meet for a decisive confrontation.
orig: فأتبعوهم مشرقين

translation: And when the two groups saw each other, the companions of Moses said, "Indeed, we are to be overtaken."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the human tendency to succumb to fear and despair when facing seemingly insurmountable challenges, despite having witnessed divine miracles. The followers of Moses momentarily lost faith in Allah's protection, forgetting His previous demonstrations of power and support, which teaches us about the importance of maintaining unwavering trust in Allah's help even in the most difficult circumstances.
orig: فلما تراءى الجمعان قال أصحاب موسى إنا لمدركون

translation: He said: "By no means! For surely my Lord is with me; He will guide me"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound trust and unwavering faith in divine guidance. It reflects the understanding that when one maintains a conscious connection with Allah, fear dissipates as His guidance becomes a constant source of direction and protection through life's challenges.
orig: قال كلا إن معي ربي سيهدين

translation: So We inspired Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff." Then it parted, and each part was like a great mountain.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how divine miracles can manifest through seemingly ordinary objects when wielded with absolute faith. The staff, a humble shepherd's tool, became an instrument of extraordinary power through Allah's will, teaching us that what matters is not the grandeur of our resources but the depth of our trust in divine guidance and intervention.
orig: فأوحينا إلى موسى أن اضرب بعصاك البحر فانفلق فكان كل فرق كالطود العظيم

translation: And We brought the others [the pursuers] near
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine control over circumstances, specifically referring to how He brought Pharaoh's army close to the Israelites at the sea. It demonstrates how Allah sometimes brings opposing forces into proximity to manifest His power and execute His plan, even when such closeness appears threatening to believers.
orig: وأزلفنا ثم الآخرين

translation: And We saved Moses and all who were with him
interpretation: This verse demonstrates Allah's divine protection and intervention for His faithful servants. It shows that when believers remain steadfast in their faith and mission, despite facing overwhelming odds or powerful opposition, Allah will provide a way out and ensure their safety. The collective salvation of Moses and his followers also illustrates that divine protection extends to the community of believers as a whole, not just individual prophets.
orig: وأنجينا موسى ومن معه أجمعين

translation: Then We drowned the others
interpretation: This verse demonstrates Allah's power and justice in dealing with those who reject His message and oppose His messengers. It likely refers to the drowning of Pharaoh and his army, serving as a reminder that ultimate accountability awaits those who persist in defiance against divine guidance.
orig: ثم أغرقنا الآخرين

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers
interpretation: This verse highlights a recurring theme in the Qur'an about human nature's resistance to divine signs. Despite clear evidence of Allah's power and existence being presented, the majority of people tend to remain skeptical or dismissive, choosing not to believe due to their attachment to worldly perspectives or preconceived notions.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of Allah's attributes, combining absolute power with infinite mercy. It teaches us that true strength and mercy are not contradictory but complementary qualities, suggesting that those in positions of power should temper their authority with compassion, following the divine example.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: And recite to them the news of Abraham
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of storytelling as a method of teaching moral lessons, specifically directing the Prophet Muhammad to share the narrative of Abraham with his followers. The use of the word "news" (naba') suggests that these are not mere stories but significant historical accounts with profound spiritual implications.
orig: واتل عليهم نبأ إبراهيم

translation: When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates Ibrahim's courageous confrontation of idolatry, demonstrating that questioning established beliefs is essential for discovering truth. His direct challenge to his father and community shows that seeking truth sometimes requires us to respectfully question even our closest family members and societal norms.
orig: إذ قال لأبيه وقومه ما تعبدون

translation: They said, "We worship idols and remain devoted to them."
interpretation: This verse reveals the deep-rooted psychological attachment people can develop to false beliefs and practices, even when they lack logical foundation. The use of the word "remain" (nathal) suggests a conscious choice to persist in this behavior, highlighting how comfort in familiar practices, even misguided ones, can prevent spiritual growth and acceptance of truth.
orig: قالوا نعبد أصناما فنظل لها عاكفين

translation: He said: "Do they hear you when you call?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of idol worship by questioning whether these false deities possess even the basic ability to hear their worshippers' prayers. It's a rhetorical device used to make people reflect on the absurdity of praying to objects or beings that lack the fundamental capacity to respond or interact with their supplicants.
orig: قال هل يسمعونكم إذ تدعون

translation: Or benefit you or harm you
interpretation: This verse highlights the powerlessness of false deities and idols, emphasizing that only Allah has true power over benefit and harm. It challenges the logic of idol worship by pointing out that these objects or entities that people worship besides Allah can neither help them in times of need nor cause them any real harm, making their worship futile and meaningless.
orig: أو ينفعونكم أو يضرون

translation: They said, "But we found our forefathers doing so."
interpretation: This verse reveals the deep-rooted challenge of blind imitation in human societies, where people justify their actions not through rational thought or divine guidance, but through ancestral traditions. It critiques the mindset of those who resist change and truth merely because they are comfortable with inherited customs, even if these customs are wrong or harmful.
orig: قالوا بل وجدنا آباءنا كذلك يفعلون

translation: He said: "Do you see what you have been worshipping?"
interpretation: This verse challenges idolaters to critically examine their beliefs by prompting them to reflect on the true nature and powerlessness of their objects of worship, inviting them to recognize the futility of worshipping entities that can neither benefit nor harm them.
orig: قال أفرأيتم ما كنتم تعبدون

translation: You and your ancient forefathers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of human behavior across generations, suggesting that current practices and beliefs are often inherited from ancestors. It serves as a reminder that blindly following ancestral traditions without questioning their validity or alignment with truth isn't justified, as both present and past generations are equally capable of error.
orig: أنتم وآباؤكم الأقدمون

translation: "Indeed, they are enemies to me, except for the Lord of the worlds"
interpretation: "This verse highlights the fundamental principle of absolute loyalty to Allah above all else. Even when surrounded by those who may oppose or mislead us, our ultimate allegiance and trust should be placed solely in Allah, the Lord of all creation. It teaches us to be discerning in our relationships and to recognize that true friendship and guidance come only from our Creator."
orig: فإنهم عدو لي إلا رب العالمين

translation: The One who created me, and He guides me
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound connection between divine creation and guidance, suggesting that the Creator who brought us into existence continues to actively guide us through life. The One who designed our physical, mental, and spiritual faculties is best positioned to guide us toward our purpose and ultimate fulfillment.
orig: الذي خلقني فهو يهدين

translation: And it is He who feeds me and gives me drink
interpretation: This verse emphasizes our complete dependence on Allah for our most basic needs. While we may work to earn money and prepare food, the ultimate provider of our sustenance is Allah. It reminds us to be grateful and humble, acknowledging that even our ability to eat and drink comes from His mercy and provision, not solely from our own efforts.
orig: والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين

translation: And when I am ill, it is He who cures me
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute dependence of humans on Allah for healing and recovery. While we may seek medical treatment and take medicines, the ultimate power of healing lies solely with Allah. It teaches us to turn to Allah in times of illness with complete trust, knowing that no cure is possible without His will and mercy
orig: وإذا مرضت فهو يشفين

translation: And the One Who causes me to die, then brings me back to life
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power of Allah over life and death, and points to the reality of resurrection. It shows that death is not the end but rather a transition, demonstrating Allah's ability to restore life after death just as He initiates it in the first place. This serves as a powerful reminder of our accountability and the temporary nature of our worldly existence.
orig: والذي يميتني ثم يحيين

translation: And Who, I hope, will forgive my sins on the Day of Judgment
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound hope and reliance on Allah's mercy, emphasizing that true believers maintain a balance between fear and hope. While acknowledging their sins and shortcomings, they never despair of Allah's forgiveness, recognizing that His mercy encompasses everything. The mention of "Day of Judgment" underscores that ultimate accountability lies with Allah alone, and His pardon is what every soul should earnestly seek.
orig: والذي أطمع أن يغفر لي خطيئتي يوم الدين

translation: My Lord, grant me wisdom and join me with the righteous
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep yearning of a believer for spiritual elevation, specifically asking for wisdom which encompasses both knowledge and the ability to act upon it correctly. The supplication to be joined with the righteous shows humility and recognition that spiritual growth is best achieved in the company of virtuous people who can serve as guides and companions on the path of righteousness.
orig: رب هب لي حكما وألحقني بالصالحين

translation: And grant me a reputation of honor among later generations
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound human desire for lasting positive impact and legacy. It suggests that a noble reputation that endures after one's death is a valuable spiritual asset, as it continues to inspire and benefit others, thereby extending one's good influence beyond their earthly life. The concept of "tongue of truth" or honorable mention indicates that true legacy isn't about fame, but about being remembered for sincerity, honesty, and beneficial contributions to humanity.
orig: واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين

translation: And place me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss
interpretation: This verse reflects the ultimate aspiration of a believer to attain eternal paradise through sincere devotion and righteous deeds. The use of the word "inheritors" suggests that paradise is a divine gift that one can claim through faith and good actions, not something that can be purchased or earned solely through human effort. The emphasis on "Garden of Bliss" indicates that true happiness and contentment can only be found in the eternal reward that Allah has prepared for His devoted servants.
orig: واجعلني من ورثة جنة النعيم

translation: "And forgive my father, for he was among those who went astray"
interpretation: "This verse reflects the deep compassion and mercy that exists in the human heart, even towards those who may not share our beliefs. It demonstrates that we can maintain love for our family while acknowledging their spiritual state, and teaches us the importance of seeking divine mercy for others, regardless of their choices."
orig: واغفر لأبي إنه كان من الضالين

translation: And do not disgrace me on the Day when they are resurrected
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep spiritual anxiety about the Day of Judgment, expressing a profound understanding that true humiliation comes not from worldly shame but from moral and spiritual failure in the eyes of Allah. It's a recognition that one's standing on the Day of Resurrection is the ultimate measure of success or failure, surpassing any worldly achievements or setbacks.
orig: ولا تخزني يوم يبعثون

translation: The Day when neither wealth nor children will be of benefit
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that on the Day of Judgment, the material possessions and familial connections that people often rely upon in worldly life will have no value. The only thing that will truly matter is one's spiritual state and righteous deeds, highlighting the importance of focusing on eternal values rather than temporary worldly attachments.
orig: يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون

translation: Except one who comes to Allah with a sound heart
interpretation: True salvation lies in maintaining a pure heart that is free from spiritual diseases like envy, hatred, and arrogance. This "sound heart" refers to a spiritual state where one's inner being is solely devoted to Allah, untainted by worldly attachments and negative emotions that could corrupt one's connection with the Divine.
orig: إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم

translation: And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous
interpretation: This verse paints a vivid picture of divine reward, suggesting that Paradise isn't merely a distant promise but will be made accessible and immediate for those who lived their lives in consciousness of Allah. The use of the word "uzlifat" (brought near) implies a transformation of Paradise from an abstract concept to a tangible reality, emphasizing the immediacy and certainty of Allah's reward for the righteous.
orig: وأزلفت الجنة للمتقين

translation: And Hellfire will be brought forth for the deviators
interpretation: This verse portrays a powerful moment of accountability where the reality of Hell becomes visible to those who deliberately chose to stray from truth and righteousness. The use of the word "brought forth" (burizat) suggests a dramatic unveiling, implying that Hell was always present but hidden from view in worldly life, and now its reality becomes unmistakably clear to those who chose the path of deviation.
orig: وبرزت الجحيم للغاوين

translation: And it will be said to them, "Where are those whom you used to worship?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility and abandonment that polytheists will face on the Day of Judgment, when their false deities will be nowhere to help them. It portrays a moment of profound realization where those who worshipped other than Allah will be confronted with the emptiness of their former beliefs and the absence of their supposed protectors.
orig: وقيل لهم أين ما كنتم تعبدون

translation: Besides Allah, can they help you or help themselves?
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of relying on false deities or powers other than Allah. It poses a rhetorical question to emphasize that these supposed helpers or gods are themselves powerless and cannot offer assistance to their worshippers, nor can they even help themselves. The verse serves to demonstrate the absolute dependence of all creation on Allah's power and the meaninglessness of seeking protection or aid from any other source.
orig: من دون الله هل ينصرونكم أو ينتصرون

translation: They will be thrown headlong into Hell, they and the deviators
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine justice and the ultimate consequence of leading others astray. Those who misguide others will not face punishment alone but will be accompanied by their followers, emphasizing the shared accountability between misleading leaders and their willing followers in the afterlife. The forceful word "kubkibu" (thrown headlong) suggests a violent and humiliating entry into Hell, reflecting the severity of the punishment for those who deceive others and lead them away from truth.
orig: فكبكبوا فيها هم والغاوون

translation: And the soldiers of Iblis all together
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes the vast army of evil forces that work under Satan's command, suggesting that negative influences and temptations don't operate in isolation but rather as part of a coordinated effort to lead people astray from their spiritual path
orig: وجنود إبليس أجمعون

translation: They will say, while they dispute with each other therein
interpretation: This verse reflects the eternal regret and blame-shifting that will occur among the inhabitants of Hell. The disputants will engage in heated arguments, each trying to hold others responsible for their mutual misguidance, showing how earthly relationships and influences can lead to shared misfortune in the afterlife.
orig: قالوا وهم فيها يختصمون

translation: By Allah, we were indeed in manifest error
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound moment of self-realization and acknowledgment of past misconceptions. It represents the transformative power of truth when it finally becomes clear, showing how people can recognize their previous errors with complete honesty when divine guidance illuminates their understanding.
orig: تالله إن كنا لفي ضلال مبين

translation: When we equated you with the Lord of the Worlds
interpretation: This verse reveals the profound error of idol worshippers who elevated false deities to the status of Allah. It points to humanity's tendency to create equivalences where none exist, highlighting the fundamental mistake of polytheism in placing created beings on par with the Creator. The use of "we" here refers to the confessions of those who led others astray, acknowledging their grave error in the afterlife.
orig: إذ نسويكم برب العالمين

translation: And none led us astray except the criminals
interpretation: This verse reveals the regret and blame-shifting that will occur on the Day of Judgment, where the misguided followers will point fingers at their corrupt leaders and influencers who led them away from the truth. It highlights how influential figures who commit evil can lead others into misguidance, emphasizing the importance of choosing righteous role models and being cautious of who we follow.
orig: وما أضلنا إلا المجرمون

translation: Now we have no intercessors
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep regret and despair felt by those who rejected faith when facing judgment, realizing that no one will come to their defense or plead their case before Allah. It emphasizes the individual's ultimate responsibility for their choices and the futility of seeking help after the time for action has passed.
orig: فما لنا من شافعين

translation: And no close friend
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound loneliness and isolation that sinners will experience on the Day of Judgment, highlighting how even the deepest earthly friendships will dissolve when each soul faces its own reckoning. It emphasizes the ultimate individual nature of spiritual accountability.
orig: ولا صديق حميم

translation: "If only we had another chance, we would be among the believers"
interpretation: "This verse reflects the deep regret of disbelievers in the afterlife, who, upon seeing the reality of divine truth, wish they could return to earthly life to make different choices. However, this desire comes too late, emphasizing the importance of embracing faith during our worldly existence rather than postponing it until it's no longer possible to change course."
orig: فلو أن لنا كرة فنكون من المؤمنين

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes how despite clear evidence of Allah's power and existence being presented, human nature often resists accepting divine truth. Even when confronted with unmistakable signs, many people choose to remain in disbelief, highlighting the persistent challenge between divine guidance and human free will.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of Allah's attributes, combining absolute power with infinite mercy. It suggests that true strength and mercy are not contradictory but complementary qualities, teaching us that those in positions of power should temper their authority with compassion, following the divine example.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The people of Noah denied the messengers
interpretation: This verse highlights a recurring theme in human history where people reject divine guidance. Although Noah was specifically their messenger, by denying him, they effectively denied all messengers since the message of monotheism and moral righteousness is universal. Their rejection wasn't just of Noah as a person, but of the entire concept of divine guidance and moral accountability.
orig: كذبت قوم نوح المرسلين

translation: When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep familial connection between prophets and their people, as Noah is referred to as their "brother" despite their rejection of his message. It emphasizes that guidance often comes from within our own communities, making the rejection of divine messages even more poignant as it involves turning away from someone who genuinely cares for their welfare like a brother.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم نوح ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental quality of trustworthiness (amanah) that all prophets possess, highlighting how divine messengers must embody complete honesty and reliability to effectively convey God's message to humanity. The messenger's self-declaration of trustworthiness serves as both a reassurance to the recipients of the message and a demonstration that truthfulness is an essential prerequisite for spiritual guidance.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me
interpretation: This recurring phrase emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of combining inner consciousness of God (taqwa) with outward obedience to divine guidance. The fear mentioned here isn't about terror, but rather a respectful awareness that leads to mindful actions. The command to obey follows naturally from this God-consciousness, suggesting that true spiritual fear naturally leads to righteous conduct.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the pure intentions of the Prophet in delivering Allah's message, highlighting that true dawah (calling to Islam) should be done solely for Allah's pleasure, not for material gain or worldly benefits. It sets a standard for sincerity in religious teaching and leadership, showing that guidance should be offered without expectation of worldly compensation.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me
interpretation: The divine command emphasizes the interconnected nature of spiritual consciousness and practical obedience. By fearing Allah, one develops an inner moral compass that naturally leads to following divine guidance through His messengers. This establishes a complete system of spiritual and practical devotion.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: They said: "Should we believe in you while the lowest of people follow you?"
interpretation: This verse reveals a common prejudice among the elite where they reject truth based on social status rather than merit. The disbelievers' objection stems from their arrogance and false notion that truth and guidance should be exclusive to the wealthy and socially prominent, showing how worldly status can become a barrier to accepting divine guidance.
orig: قالوا أنؤمن لك واتبعك الأرذلون

translation: He said, "And what knowledge do I have of what they used to do?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the principle of individual responsibility and the limitations of human knowledge. Even those in positions of authority or leadership cannot truly know the complete reality of others' actions or intentions, emphasizing that ultimate judgment belongs to Allah alone.
orig: قال وما علمي بما كانوا يعملون

translation: Their account is only with my Lord, if you could but know
interpretation: This verse emphasizes divine justice and accountability, indicating that Allah alone has the ultimate authority to judge people's deeds and intentions. It suggests that humans should refrain from making hasty judgments about others, as the true assessment of one's worth and actions lies exclusively within Allah's domain. The phrase "if you could but know" implies that humans have limited understanding of divine wisdom and the complexities of divine judgment.
orig: إن حسابهم إلا على ربي لو تشعرون

translation: And I am not one to drive away the believers
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound principle of equality and dignity in Islam. It was revealed when some elite members of society suggested to Prophet Muhammad that he should dismiss poor believers from his gatherings to accommodate influential people. The verse emphasizes that true faith transcends social status, wealth, or worldly position, and that all believers deserve equal respect and inclusion in the community regardless of their social standing.
orig: وما أنا بطارد المؤمنين

translation: I am but a clear warner
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's core mission as a messenger whose primary duty is to convey Allah's message clearly and warn humanity of the consequences of their actions, without having supernatural powers or divine attributes. It reflects the humility and straightforwardness of prophetic duty, focused on delivering divine guidance rather than performing miracles or forcing people to believe.
orig: إن أنا إلا نذير مبين

translation: They said, "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be of those who are stoned."
interpretation: This verse illustrates how the powerful often resort to threats and intimidation when faced with messages of truth that challenge their established order. The threat of stoning represents not just physical violence, but the ultimate attempt to silence and eliminate voices of reform and divine guidance. It shows how prophets faced severe opposition and death threats for simply delivering God's message, highlighting the heavy price of standing up for truth in the face of entrenched corruption and disbelief.
orig: قالوا لئن لم تنته يا نوح لتكونن من المرجومين

translation: He said, "My Lord! Indeed, my people have denied me."
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep anguish of a prophet facing rejection from his own community, highlighting the emotional and spiritual struggle of those who stand for truth in the face of widespread opposition. It demonstrates how even divine messengers experience moments of human vulnerability, turning to Allah for support and validation when faced with communal rejection.
orig: قال رب إن قومي كذبون

translation: So judge between me and them with decisive justice and save me and those believers who are with me
interpretation: This verse reflects the universal plea for divine intervention in times of conflict and persecution. It emphasizes the believer's trust in God's justice and protection, acknowledging that true deliverance comes from divine judgment rather than human means. The verse also highlights the importance of communal solidarity, as the prayer extends beyond individual salvation to include all believers, suggesting that spiritual welfare is interconnected within the community of faith.
orig: فافتح بيني وبينهم فتحا ونجني ومن معي من المؤمنين

translation: So We saved him and those with him in the laden ark
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's mercy and protection for those who remain faithful and righteous, even in times of overwhelming adversity. The "laden ark" symbolizes not just physical salvation but also spiritual preservation, showing how Allah provides a way out for the believers when they seem surrounded by destruction. It emphasizes that divine protection extends beyond the individual to encompass those who associate themselves with the righteous path.
orig: فأنجيناه ومن معه في الفلك المشحون

translation: Then We drowned the others who remained
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and justice in dealing with those who persistently reject divine guidance. It refers to the fate of those who opposed their prophets, particularly in the context of Noah's people, showing that divine punishment ultimately comes to those who remain adamant in their disbelief after being given ample opportunity to accept the truth.
orig: ثم أغرقنا بعد الباقين

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers
interpretation: This verse highlights a recurring theme in the Qur'an about human nature's resistance to divine signs. Despite being presented with clear evidence of Allah's power and existence, the majority of people tend to remain skeptical or dismissive, choosing disbelief over faith even when confronted with manifest proofs. This reflects the deep-rooted challenge of human stubbornness in accepting truth when it conflicts with their established beliefs or desires.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of Allah's attributes, combining absolute power with infinite mercy. It suggests that true strength and authority are inherently linked with compassion, teaching us that those in positions of power should temper their might with mercy and kindness. The verse also offers reassurance that despite Allah's overwhelming power, His mercy is a fundamental aspect of His relationship with creation.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The people of 'Ad denied the messengers
interpretation: This verse highlights a recurring pattern in human history where communities reject divine guidance. The people of 'Ad's rejection wasn't just of one messenger but represents a denial of the fundamental message of all divine messengers, suggesting that rejecting one prophet is equivalent to rejecting all prophets as they all came with the same essential truth.
orig: كذبت عاد المرسلين

translation: When their brother Hud said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental role of prophets in calling their people to God-consciousness. Hud's addressing of his people as "brother" shows the compassionate approach taken by divine messengers, attempting to reform their communities through familial bonds rather than alienation, while simultaneously emphasizing the universal human need for spiritual awareness and moral accountability.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم هود ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the essential quality of trustworthiness (amanah) in divine messengers, highlighting how credibility and reliability are fundamental prerequisites for anyone who carries God's message. The speaker's self-declaration of being trustworthy suggests that truth and honesty are inseparable from authentic spiritual guidance.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me
interpretation: This recurring phrase emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of combining inner consciousness of God (taqwa) with outward obedience to divine guidance through His messengers. The fear mentioned here isn't about terror, but rather a mindful awareness that leads to spiritual and moral responsibility.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the pure intention and sincerity of the prophets in their mission, showing that they seek no worldly gain or compensation for spreading divine guidance. Their sole motivation is to fulfill their duty to Allah, trusting that He alone will reward them. This principle establishes the credibility of their message, as it removes any suspicion of personal benefit or material interest in their preaching.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: Do you build upon every elevation a sign, amusing yourselves?
interpretation: The verse criticizes those who build lavish monuments and structures for vanity and pride rather than necessity, suggesting that such actions reflect misplaced priorities and wasteful behavior that diverts attention from more meaningful spiritual pursuits
orig: أتبنون بكل ريع آية تعبثون

translation: And you construct fortresses that you might live eternally?
interpretation: The verse critiques human arrogance in building grand structures and fortifications with the false hope of achieving immortality. It points to humanity's tendency to seek permanence through material achievements, while overlooking their inherent mortality and temporary existence in this world.
orig: وتتخذون مصانع لعلكم تخلدون

translation: And when you strike, you strike as tyrants
interpretation: This verse warns against the abuse of power and authority, highlighting how human beings can become oppressive when they possess strength or control over others. It serves as a divine reminder that wielding power should be done with justice and mercy, not with tyranny or excessive force.
orig: وإذا بطشتم بطشتم جبارين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me
interpretation: This recurring phrase emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle that true piety combines both inner consciousness of God (taqwa) and outward obedience to divine guidance through His messengers. The fear mentioned here isn't about terror, but rather a respectful awareness that shapes one's moral compass and actions.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And fear Him who has provided you with what you know
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining consciousness of Allah's generosity in bestowing upon us knowledge, understanding, and awareness. It suggests that our intellectual capabilities and accumulated knowledge are divine gifts that create a responsibility to use them wisely and acknowledge their true source. This recognition should lead to a deeper sense of accountability and gratitude toward Allah.
orig: واتقوا الذي أمدكم بما تعلمون

translation: He has aided you with cattle and children
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's continuous blessings upon humanity, highlighting how He provides sustenance both through livestock, which offers multiple benefits like food, transportation, and materials, and through offspring who represent the continuation of human lineage and a source of support and joy. The use of the word "aided" suggests these are tools given to help humans fulfill their purpose on Earth.
orig: أمدكم بأنعام وبنين

translation: And gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse speaks to Allah's promise of eternal rewards, suggesting that the faithful will be granted access to places of ultimate comfort and sustenance. The gardens represent abundance and beauty, while the springs symbolize perpetual refreshment and purity, together painting a picture of complete contentment in the afterlife.
orig: وجنات وعيون

translation: Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day
interpretation: This verse conveys Allah's mercy through His prophets' concern for humanity, warning them out of compassion rather than desire for control. The emphasis on fear suggests that divine punishment is a serious reality, not a mere threat, and the reference to a "tremendous day" points to the gravity of the Day of Judgment where every soul will be held accountable for its choices.
orig: إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: They said, "It is the same to us whether you advise or are not of the advisers"
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and dismissiveness of those who reject guidance. It shows how hardened hearts can become when they deliberately choose to ignore truth, reaching a state where they treat sincere advice with complete indifference. Their response indicates a dangerous level of spiritual blindness where they've lost the ability to distinguish between beneficial guidance and its absence.
orig: قالوا سواء علينا أوعظت أم لم تكن من الواعظين

translation: This is not but the custom of the former peoples
interpretation: The verse highlights how people tend to dismiss new truths by claiming they are merely old tales or traditions. It points to humanity's recurring pattern of resistance to divine guidance by attributing it to human invention rather than accepting it as divine revelation.
orig: إن هذا إلا خلق الأولين

translation: And we are not to be punished
interpretation: This verse reflects a dangerous mindset of denial and false security, where individuals convince themselves they are immune to divine accountability. It highlights how people can delude themselves into believing they won't face consequences for their actions, which often leads to moral negligence and spiritual complacency.
orig: وما نحن بمعذبين

translation: They denied him, so We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's consistent pattern of divine justice, showing that persistent rejection of truth and guidance, despite clear signs and warnings, ultimately leads to consequences. The destruction mentioned serves as a historical lesson and warning for future generations, emphasizing that denial of divine messages carries serious repercussions.
orig: فكذبوه فأهلكناهم إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of Allah's attributes, showing how He perfectly combines seemingly opposite qualities: absolute power and complete mercy. This pairing teaches us that true strength lies not just in having power, but in knowing when to exercise mercy, and that genuine mercy comes from a position of strength, not weakness.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The Thamud denied the messengers
interpretation: Though the verse specifically mentions Thamud's rejection of messengers in plural form, historically they primarily rejected their prophet Salih. This implies that rejecting one messenger is equivalent to rejecting all divine messengers, as the core message and source of their teachings are the same. It also demonstrates how denying divine guidance isn't just a simple rejection but a deeper pattern of disbelief in the very concept of divine communication with humanity.
orig: كذبت ثمود المرسلين

translation: When their brother Salih said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the universal nature of divine guidance, where prophets emerge from within communities as familiar figures, addressing their people as family. Salih's question isn't merely about fear, but about moral consciousness and spiritual awareness, challenging his people to recognize their accountability to their Creator.
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم صالح ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the essential quality of trustworthiness in divine messengers, highlighting how credibility and reliability are fundamental prerequisites for anyone who carries God's message. The speaker's self-declaration of being "trustworthy" suggests that truth and honesty are inseparable from genuine spiritual guidance.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me
interpretation: This recurring phrase emphasizes the interconnected nature of spiritual consciousness and practical obedience. True God-consciousness (taqwa) naturally leads to following divine guidance through His messengers, while genuine obedience stems from a deep reverence for Allah. It's a call for holistic faith that combines inner spirituality with outward compliance.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the pure intentions and sincerity of the prophets in their divine mission. The prophet's declaration that he seeks no worldly compensation for his guidance shows that spiritual leadership and divine guidance should be free from material motivations, ensuring that the message remains untainted by personal gain or ulterior motives.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: Will you be left secure in what is here?
interpretation: The verse serves as a divine reminder that worldly security and comfort are temporary illusions. It challenges those who become overly attached to their current state of ease and material possessions, warning that such perceived safety can be stripped away at any moment. This interpretation emphasizes the importance of not taking God's blessings for granted and maintaining spiritual vigilance despite temporal comfort.
orig: أتتركون في ما هاهنا آمنين

translation: In gardens and springs
interpretation: This verse paints an image of the eternal rewards awaiting the righteous in Paradise, where they will dwell amidst lush, verdant gardens with flowing springs. The combination of gardens and springs symbolizes complete sustenance, as gardens provide food and beauty while springs ensure endless pure water, representing Allah's perfect and complete provision for the blessed souls in the afterlife.
orig: في جنات وعيون

translation: And plantations and date palms with soft spadix
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's mercy in providing sustenance through agriculture, specifically highlighting how He created date palms with tender, easily accessible fruit clusters. It symbolizes divine precision in creating food sources that are perfectly suited for human consumption and harvesting, demonstrating both God's generosity and His attention to practical details in sustaining human life.
orig: وزروع ونخل طلعها هضيم

translation: And you carve houses from the mountains with great skill
interpretation: The verse highlights how human ingenuity and craftsmanship are gifts from Allah. The ability to transform solid mountain rock into comfortable dwellings demonstrates mankind's creative potential when using the resources Allah has provided. However, it also serves as a reminder that such achievements shouldn't lead to arrogance or excessive pride, as these abilities are ultimately divine endowments.
orig: وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا فارهين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me
interpretation: This recurring phrase emphasizes the fundamental connection between genuine God-consciousness and following divine guidance through His messengers. True fear of Allah naturally leads to obedience of His appointed guides, as they represent the practical implementation of divine will. The verse suggests that spiritual awareness and practical submission are inseparable aspects of faith.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And do not obey the command of the transgressors
interpretation: This verse warns against following those who exceed proper limits in their behavior and choices. It emphasizes the importance of discernment in choosing whose guidance to follow, cautioning against those who are wasteful, excessive, or transgress moral and ethical boundaries. The term "musrifin" (transgressors) refers to those who have lost their moral compass and whose judgment cannot be trusted.
orig: ولا تطيعوا أمر المسرفين

translation: Those who spread corruption on earth and do not make amends
interpretation: This verse highlights the destructive nature of those who actively work against the moral and social fabric of society. It refers not only to physical corruption but also to moral, spiritual, and social degradation. The emphasis on "not making amends" suggests that true evil lies not in making mistakes, but in the deliberate choice to persist in harmful behavior without any attempt at reform or correction.
orig: الذين يفسدون في الأرض ولا يصلحون

translation: They said, "You are only one of those bewitched"
interpretation: This verse reflects how people often dismiss divine messages by attributing them to madness or supernatural influence, rather than engaging with the actual message. It demonstrates a common defense mechanism used by those who feel threatened by truth - they attempt to discredit the messenger instead of addressing the message itself.
orig: قالوا إنما أنت من المسحرين

translation: You are but a human like us, so bring a sign if you are among the truthful
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism of disbelievers who challenged prophets by dismissing their divine message solely based on their human nature. It demonstrates how people often struggle to accept extraordinary truths from ordinary sources, demanding supernatural proof rather than examining the message itself. The verse highlights humanity's tendency to seek spectacular validation rather than contemplating the wisdom and truth in the message being conveyed.
orig: ما أنت إلا بشر مثلنا فأت بآية إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, "This is a she-camel: she has a right to drink, and you have a right to drink, each on a day appointed."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine principle of equitable resource sharing and respect for established rights. It points to the importance of fair distribution and organized scheduling in managing limited resources, teaching us that even those with competing interests can coexist peacefully through proper arrangement and mutual respect for each other's rights.
orig: قال هذه ناقة لها شرب ولكم شرب يوم معلوم

translation: And do not touch her with harm, lest the punishment of a terrible day seize you
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound spiritual and moral consequences of harming Allah's creation. It specifically refers to the she-camel sent as a sign to the people of Thamud, but extends to a broader principle about respecting divine signs and treating all of God's creatures with kindness. The warning of punishment suggests that acts of cruelty or disregard for sacred boundaries carry severe spiritual repercussions, affecting not just the individual but potentially the entire community.
orig: ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: So they slaughtered her, and they became regretful
interpretation: This verse illustrates how immediate actions driven by defiance and anger often lead to deep remorse, highlighting the universal pattern of human behavior where hasty decisions made against divine guidance result in profound regret and spiritual loss
orig: فعقروها فأصبحوا نادمين

translation: So the punishment seized them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's consistent pattern of divine justice, where persistent rejection of truth despite clear evidence leads to eventual consequences. The mention of "most of them were not believers" suggests that even witnessing divine signs doesn't guarantee faith, as belief requires an open heart and willingness to accept the truth rather than just intellectual acknowledgment.
orig: فأخذهم العذاب إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of Allah's attributes, combining both strength and compassion. It teaches us that true power and mercy are not contradictory but complementary qualities, suggesting that those in positions of authority should emulate these divine characteristics by being both firm and merciful in their dealings.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The people of Lot rejected the messengers
interpretation: This verse highlights a recurring pattern in human history where communities reject divine guidance. The people of Lot's rejection wasn't just of him personally, but represented a broader rejection of moral and spiritual truth. Their rejection stemmed from their deep-rooted attachment to their immoral practices and their unwillingness to accept reform, showing how entrenched behaviors can blind people to divine guidance.
orig: كذبت قوم لوط المرسلين

translation: When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral courage of Prophet Lot in confronting his people about their sinful behavior, emphasizing the fundamental Islamic principle that true faith requires standing up for righteousness even when facing societal opposition
orig: إذ قال لهم أخوهم لوط ألا تتقون

translation: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental quality of trustworthiness (amanah) that is essential for divine messengers. The speaker's self-declaration of being "amin" (trustworthy) suggests that credibility and reliability are prerequisites for anyone who claims to convey divine messages, as truth can only be effectively delivered by someone who has earned people's trust through their character and actions.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

interpretation: This recurring phrase emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle that true piety combines both inner consciousness of God (taqwa) and outward obedience to His messengers. The fear mentioned here isn't about terror, but rather a reverent awareness that shapes one's moral compass and leads to righteous conduct.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the pure intentions and sincerity of the Prophet's mission, showing that true guidance and spiritual leadership should be free from worldly gains. The Prophet's sole motivation is seeking Allah's pleasure and reward, which establishes a model of selfless dedication to divine work. This approach removes any suspicion of personal benefit or material motivation in spreading the message of Islam.
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: Do you approach males among the worlds?
interpretation: This verse condemns the unnatural practice of homosexuality among men, highlighting how this behavior deviates from the divine natural order where intimate relationships are meant to be between men and women. It emphasizes that this practice was unprecedented in all of creation, making it particularly egregious.
orig: أتأتون الذكران من العالمين

translation: And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your wives. Rather, you are a transgressing people
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who engage in unnatural sexual practices while abandoning the lawful intimate relationship with their spouses. It emphasizes that marriage is divinely ordained and going against this natural order by seeking alternative outlets represents a violation of God's intended design for human relationships
orig: وتذرون ما خلق لكم ربكم من أزواجكم بل أنتم قوم عادون

translation: They said, "If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be of those evicted."
interpretation: This verse reveals the hostile response of the people of Sodom to Prophet Lot's moral guidance, demonstrating how societies often react with threats and intimidation when their established but immoral practices are challenged. The threat of exile was used as a tool of suppression against religious and moral reformation, showing how power structures resist change even when it's for their own good.
orig: قالوا لئن لم تنته يا لوط لتكونن من المخرجين

translation: He said: "I am among those who detest your conduct"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the moral courage required to stand against wrongdoing, even when it means opposing the majority. It illustrates that true faith sometimes demands taking a firm stance against practices that contradict divine guidance, regardless of social pressures or cultural norms.
orig: قال إني لعملكم من القالين

translation: My Lord, save me and my family from what they do
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound anxiety of a believer living among those who commit evil deeds, showing how corruption and immorality in society can pose a spiritual and moral threat to one's family. It emphasizes the importance of seeking divine protection not just for oneself but also for loved ones, acknowledging that negative societal influences can impact family values and spiritual well-being.
orig: رب نجني وأهلي مما يعملون

translation: So We saved him and his family all together
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's mercy and reward for the faithful, showing how He protects and preserves those who remain steadfast in their belief and righteousness, extending His protection not only to His chosen servants but also to their families as a complete blessing
orig: فنجيناه وأهله أجمعين

translation: Except for an old woman among those who remained behind
interpretation: This verse highlights divine justice and mercy. While punishment befalls those who transgress, there are always exceptions for the righteous. The old woman represents those who, despite being among wrongdoers, maintain their faith and moral standing, thus earning divine protection from calamity.
orig: إلا عجوزا في الغابرين

translation: Then We destroyed the others
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine justice and the inevitable consequences that befall those who persistently reject truth and guidance. It serves as a powerful reminder that no matter how mighty or numerous a people may be, their fate is sealed when they choose to persist in wrongdoing and denial of divine messages.
orig: ثم دمرنا الآخرين

translation: And We rained upon them a rain, and evil was the rain of those who were warned
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine punishment of those who persistently rejected His message despite clear warnings. The repetition of "rain" emphasizes that what appeared to be a natural phenomenon was actually a deliberate, powerful form of divine retribution, transforming what is typically a blessing (rain) into a means of destruction for those who refused to heed the warnings of their prophet.
orig: وأمطرنا عليهم مطرا فساء مطر المنذرين

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the paradox of human nature, where despite clear divine signs and evidence of Allah's power and existence, the majority of people still choose disbelief. It reflects on the persistent pattern throughout history where humans, despite being presented with undeniable proofs, often resist faith due to pride, stubbornness, or attachment to worldly matters.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of Allah's attributes, combining absolute power with infinite mercy. It suggests that true strength and authority are inherently linked with compassion, teaching us that those in positions of power should temper their might with mercy and kindness. The pairing of these attributes also offers comfort to believers, assuring them that the same God who possesses unlimited power chooses to exercise it with mercy and loving-kindness towards His creation.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: The companions of the thicket (Madyan) denied the messengers
interpretation: This verse highlights a recurring pattern in human history where communities reject divine guidance. The people of Madyan, who lived in a densely wooded area, demonstrated the same arrogance and disbelief that many other nations showed when confronted with prophetic messages. Their rejection of Prophet Shu'ayb wasn't just a rejection of one individual, but a rejection of the entire concept of divine guidance, showing how spiritual blindness often stems from societal pride and established corrupt practices.
orig: كذب أصحاب الأيكة المرسلين

translation: When Shu'ayb said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the perpetual struggle between divine guidance and human resistance to moral accountability. Shu'ayb's question isn't merely about fear, but rather calls for a deep, conscious awareness of divine presence that should naturally lead to ethical behavior and social justice. His appeal to their sense of taqwa (God-consciousness) suggests that the root of their societal problems was their disconnection from divine moral principles.
orig: إذ قال لهم شعيب ألا تتقون

interpretation: This verse emphasizes the essential quality of trustworthiness in divine messengers, highlighting how integrity and reliability are fundamental prerequisites for anyone tasked with delivering God's message. The speaker's self-declaration of being "trustworthy" suggests that truth and honesty are inseparable from genuine spiritual guidance.
orig: إني لكم رسول أمين

translation: So fear Allah and obey me
interpretation: This recurring phrase in the Qur'an emphasizes the dual nature of faith: having consciousness of God's presence and following divine guidance through His messengers. The fear mentioned here isn't about terror but rather a reverent awareness that shapes one's moral compass and leads to righteous conduct.
orig: فاتقوا الله وأطيعون

translation: "And I do not ask you for any reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds"
interpretation: "This verse emphasizes the pure intentions and sincerity of the prophetic mission, highlighting that true spiritual guidance and divine message-bearing should be free from worldly compensation. The prophet's dedication is solely for Allah's pleasure, demonstrating that spiritual leadership and guidance should be motivated by divine love rather than material gain or personal benefit."
orig: وما أسألكم عليه من أجر إن أجري إلا على رب العالمين

translation: Give full measure and do not be among those who cause loss
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of honesty and fairness in business transactions. It suggests that ethical conduct in commerce is not merely a social obligation but a divine command, warning against the temptation to shortchange others for personal gain. The deeper meaning extends beyond literal measurement to encompass all forms of giving others their due rights, whether in business, relationships, or social interactions.
orig: أوفوا الكيل ولا تكونوا من المخسرين

translation: And weigh with the straight balance
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of absolute fairness and honesty in business dealings. The use of "qistas" (balance) specifically refers to the most precise and accurate measuring tool, suggesting that Muslims should strive for the utmost precision and fairness in all their transactions, leaving no room for deception or approximation.
orig: وزنوا بالقسطاس المستقيم

translation: And do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on earth, spreading corruption
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of economic and social justice. It warns against two interconnected forms of moral corruption: depriving others of their rightful dues through cheating, fraud, or exploitation, and causing general disorder in society through destructive behavior. The verse suggests that economic injustice and social corruption are closely linked, as unfair economic practices often lead to broader societal breakdown and moral decay.
orig: ولا تبخسوا الناس أشياءهم ولا تعثوا في الأرض مفسدين

translation: And fear Him who created you and the former generations
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining consciousness of Allah's authority by reminding us that our very existence, along with all those who came before us, stems from His creative power. The mention of "former generations" serves to highlight the historical continuity of human accountability to their Creator, suggesting that just as previous peoples were answerable for their deeds, we too must recognize our responsibility to the One who brought us into being.
orig: واتقوا الذي خلقكم والجبلة الأولين

translation: They said, "You are only one of those bewitched"
interpretation: This verse reflects how people often dismiss divine messages by attributing them to madness or supernatural manipulation, rather than engaging with the actual message. It shows a common defense mechanism where people discredit the messenger to avoid confronting uncomfortable truths that challenge their established beliefs and way of life.
orig: قالوا إنما أنت من المسحرين

translation: And you are not but a human like us, and indeed, we think you are among the liars
interpretation: This verse reflects the common response of disbelievers to prophets throughout history, highlighting humanity's tendency to reject divine guidance based on the messenger's ordinary human nature. It demonstrates how people often struggle to accept that God would choose regular humans as His messengers, expecting instead that divine messages should come through supernatural beings.
orig: وما أنت إلا بشر مثلنا وإن نظنك لمن الكاذبين

translation: So cause to fall upon us fragments of the sky, if you are among the truthful
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogant challenge posed by disbelievers to prophets, demanding miraculous signs as proof. It demonstrates how skeptics often demand destructive or spectacular signs rather than contemplating existing evidence, showing their unwillingness to accept the truth unless it comes in the form they dictate.
orig: فأسقط علينا كسفا من السماء إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, "My Lord knows best what you do."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete and perfect knowledge of all human actions, both visible and hidden. It serves as both a warning to wrongdoers and a comfort to the righteous, reminding us that no deed escapes divine awareness and ultimate accountability.
orig: قال ربي أعلم بما تعملون

translation: So they denied him, and the punishment of the day of the dark cloud seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine justice and the severe consequences of rejecting His messengers. The "day of the dark cloud" refers to a specific punishment sent to the people of Prophet Shu'ayb, where Allah made them suffer through what appeared to be a relieving cloud during intense heat, but instead brought devastating torment. This demonstrates how divine punishment can come in deceptive forms, where what appears to be mercy can become a source of destruction for those who persist in denying the truth.
orig: فكذبوه فأخذهم عذاب يوم الظلة إنه كان عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers
interpretation: This verse highlights a recurring theme in the Qur'an about human nature's resistance to divine guidance. Despite being presented with clear signs and evidence of Allah's power and truth, the majority of people tend to remain skeptical or disbelieving, choosing to reject faith even when confronted with compelling proofs.
orig: إن في ذلك لآية وما كان أكثرهم مؤمنين

translation: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of Allah's attributes, combining both strength and compassion. It teaches us that true power is balanced with mercy, suggesting that those in positions of authority should emulate these divine qualities by being both firm and compassionate. The use of "your Lord" creates a personal connection, indicating that this all-powerful yet merciful God maintains a close relationship with each believer.
orig: وإن ربك لهو العزيز الرحيم

translation: And indeed, it is the revelation of the Lord of the worlds
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine authenticity of the Qur'an by affirming that its source is directly from Allah, the Supreme Creator of all existence, rather than being a human creation or inspired by lesser beings. The use of the word "tanzil" (revelation) specifically implies a gradual, deliberate descent of knowledge from the highest authority in existence, emphasizing both the Qur'an's sacred nature and its purposeful delivery method.
orig: وإنه لتنزيل رب العالمين

translation: The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down
interpretation: This verse refers to Angel Gabriel's role as the divine messenger who delivered the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad. The title "Trustworthy Spirit" emphasizes Gabriel's absolute reliability and integrity in conveying Allah's message without any alteration, highlighting the authenticity and preservation of divine revelation.
orig: نزل به الروح الأمين

translation: Upon your heart, so that you may be among the warners
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature of revelation, indicating that Allah's message was imprinted directly upon Prophet Muhammad's heart. The intimate nature of this spiritual connection enabled him to internalize the divine message completely, making him a genuine and effective warner to humanity. The heart's mention, rather than the mind, signifies that true guidance requires both spiritual receptivity and emotional intelligence, not just intellectual understanding.
orig: على قلبك لتكون من المنذرين

translation: In clear Arabic language
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom in delivering the Qur'an in Arabic, a language known for its eloquence and precision, to ensure clear communication and eliminate ambiguity in conveying Allah's message to humanity.
orig: بلسان عربي مبين

translation: And indeed, it is [mentioned] in the scriptures of the former peoples
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine revelation throughout human history, indicating that the message of Islam wasn't entirely new but rather a confirmation of truths that had been previously revealed to earlier communities through their prophets and preserved in their sacred texts
orig: وإنه لفي زبر الأولين

translation: Is it not a sign for them that the learned men of the Children of Israel know it?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the validity of Prophet Muhammad's message by pointing out that Jewish scholars recognized the truth of his prophethood based on the descriptions in their scriptures. Their recognition serves as a powerful testament since they, as people of earlier revelation, could verify the authenticity of Islam's message through their own religious knowledge and texts.
orig: أولم يكن لهم آية أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل

translation: And if We had revealed it to a non-Arab
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature of the Qur'an by suggesting that even if it had been revealed to someone who wasn't an Arab, its miraculous nature would still be evident. It highlights that the message's power transcends language barriers and cultural boundaries, demonstrating that the Qur'an's divine origin isn't dependent on the recipient's linguistic background.
orig: ولو نزلناه على بعض الأعجمين

translation: So he recited it to them, but they would not believe in it
interpretation: This verse illustrates the persistent rejection of divine truth even when it is clearly presented. Despite having the message conveyed to them directly, some hearts remain closed due to pride, stubbornness, or attachment to existing beliefs, highlighting how faith is ultimately a matter of personal willingness to accept guidance rather than merely being exposed to it.
orig: فقرأه عليهم ما كانوا به مؤمنين

translation: Thus do We make it traverse the hearts of the criminals
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine law regarding how disbelief and rejection become deeply embedded in the hearts of persistent wrongdoers. Just as a thread is woven through fabric, Allah allows their denial to penetrate their hearts as a consequence of their continuous choice to reject faith and truth.
orig: كذلك سلكناه في قلوب المجرمين

translation: They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the stubborn nature of those who reject faith, indicating that some people are so deeply entrenched in their disbelief that only the stark reality of divine punishment will finally convince them of the truth. However, such belated recognition will be futile, as belief under duress or when facing inevitable consequences does not constitute genuine faith.
orig: لا يؤمنون به حتى يروا العذاب الأليم

translation: And it will come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning about the unpredictable nature of Allah's judgment or consequences, emphasizing how people often remain heedless and unprepared while continuing their daily lives, only to be caught off guard when the moment of reckoning arrives. It reflects the human tendency to live in a state of forgetfulness about ultimate accountability.
orig: فيأتيهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون

translation: And they will say, "Are we to be given respite?"
interpretation: This verse reflects humanity's tendency to procrastinate in matters of faith and moral responsibility, often seeking delays when faced with divine accountability. It portrays the regretful realization that comes too late, when people finally understand the consequences of their actions but wish for more time to make amends.
orig: فيقولوا هل نحن منظرون

translation: Are they trying to hasten Our punishment?
interpretation: This verse reflects Allah's response to those who mockingly demand divine punishment, highlighting human arrogance in challenging divine wisdom and timing. It serves as a warning that seeking to expedite divine judgment stems from a lack of understanding of its severe consequences.
orig: أفبعذابنا يستعجلون

translation: Have you considered if We let them enjoy life for some years
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder about the temporary nature of worldly pleasures, suggesting that even lengthy periods of comfort and enjoyment in this life should not be mistaken for true success or divine favor. It prompts reflection on how people often become deluded by temporary worldly comforts, forgetting their ultimate accountability before Allah.
orig: أفرأيت إن متعناهم سنين

translation: Then there came to them what they were promised
interpretation: This verse speaks to the profound reality that divine promises, whether of reward or consequence, inevitably materialize. It serves as a reminder that all warnings and promises from Allah will ultimately come to pass, emphasizing the importance of heeding divine guidance before the promised outcome becomes a present reality.
orig: ثم جاءهم ما كانوا يوعدون

translation: Of no avail to them was all that they used to enjoy
interpretation: This verse reflects on the temporary nature of worldly pleasures and luxuries, highlighting how material comforts and enjoyments ultimately provide no protection or benefit when divine judgment comes. It serves as a reminder that earthly indulgences, no matter how extensive or prolonged, cannot shield one from accountability or substitute for spiritual righteousness.
orig: ما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يمتعون

translation: And We did not destroy any city except that it had warners
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's perfect justice and mercy, highlighting that divine punishment never comes without prior warning. Before any community faced destruction, they were first sent messengers or warners who explained the truth and called them to righteousness. This demonstrates that Allah gives ample opportunity for repentance and reform before implementing consequences, establishing that destruction comes only after clear warning and persistent defiance.
orig: وما أهلكنا من قرية إلا لها منذرون

translation: A reminder, and We were not unjust
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and justice in sending reminders to humanity before holding them accountable. It affirms that divine punishment never comes without prior warning through messengers and revelations, demonstrating Allah's perfect fairness in dealing with His creation.
orig: ذكرى وما كنا ظالمين

translation: And the devils did not bring it [the Qur'an] down
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an by explicitly rejecting any demonic influence in its revelation, countering accusations that Muhammad was receiving information from dark forces.
