Indeed, he is a manifest, misleading enemy."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the human tendency to act impulsively when emotions run high, even among those who are righteous. Moses' intervention, though intended to help someone from his own people, led to an unintended death, showing how even prophets can make mistakes in moments of haste. The immediate recognition of this act as "Satan's work" demonstrates the importance of self-reflection and acknowledging our errors rather than justifying them. It serves as a reminder that violence, even when seemingly justified, can lead to regrettable consequences and that Satan's influence often works through our moments of emotional impulse.
orig: ودخل المدينة على حين غفلة من أهلها فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان هذا من شيعته وهذا من عدوه فاستغاثه الذي من شيعته على الذي من عدوه فوكزه موسى فقضى عليه قال هذا من عمل الشيطان إنه عدو مضل مبين

translation: He said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me," and He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound relationship between divine mercy and sincere repentance, showing that when one acknowledges their mistakes with genuine remorse and humility before Allah, forgiveness is readily granted. The immediate response to the prayer demonstrates Allah's eagerness to forgive those who turn to Him with sincerity, regardless of the magnitude of their transgression.
orig: قال رب إني ظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي فغفر له إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: He said, "My Lord, because of the favor You have bestowed upon me, I will never be an assistant to the criminals."
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound commitment to moral integrity and gratitude. When someone recognizes God's blessings in their life, it creates a moral obligation to use these blessings righteously and stand against wrongdoing, rather than using one's abilities or position to aid those who commit evil acts.
orig: قال رب بما أنعمت علي فلن أكون ظهيرا للمجرمين

translation: So he became fearful in the city, vigilant, when suddenly the one who had sought his help the previous day cried out to him for help. Moses said to him, "Indeed, you are clearly a troublemaker."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the psychological and moral consequences of impulsive actions. Moses's fear and vigilance after the unintended killing shows how a single act can transform one's sense of security into constant anxiety. His harsh response to the same person seeking help again reflects how past experiences can lead us to recognize toxic patterns in relationships and the wisdom in distancing ourselves from those who repeatedly draw us into conflict.
orig: فأصبح في المدينة خائفا يترقب فإذا الذي استنصره بالأمس يستصرخه قال له موسى إنك لغوي مبين

translation: But when he was about to strike the one who was their enemy, he said, "O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed a man yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land and do not wish to be of those who reform."
interpretation: This verse illustrates how past actions can haunt and undermine one's present credibility and authority. Even when attempting to do right, previous mistakes can be used against us, making it harder to effect positive change. The accuser's words also reveal how people often attribute the worst motives to others' actions, even when the intentions might be noble.
orig: فلما أن أراد أن يبطش بالذي هو عدو لهما قال يا موسى أتريد أن تقتلني كما قتلت نفسا بالأمس إن تريد إلا أن تكون جبارا في الأرض وما تريد أن تكون من المصلحين

translation: A man came running from the farthest part of the city, saying, "O Moses! The chiefs are conspiring against you to kill you, so leave [the city]. I am truly one of your well-wishers."
interpretation: This verse illustrates how Allah often sends help through unexpected sources in times of danger. The anonymous man's urgency and sincerity in warning Moses demonstrates that divine protection can manifest through ordinary people who act on their moral conscience, even when they might risk their own safety to help others. It shows that standing up for justice and protecting the innocent is a noble act that transcends social status or tribal affiliations.
orig: وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى قال يا موسى إن الملأ يأتمرون بك ليقتلوك فاخرج إني لك من الناصحين

translation: So he left it [the city], fearful and vigilant, saying, "My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound human experience of seeking divine protection in moments of vulnerability. Moses's prayer reflects the universal human need to turn to a higher power when facing oppression, showing that even prophets experienced fear and relied on divine intervention for safety. His state of vigilance while escaping highlights how faith can coexist with practical caution, teaching us that trust in God doesn't negate the need for prudent action.
orig: فخرج منها خائفا يترقب قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين

translation: And when he headed towards Madyan, he said: "I hope my Lord will guide me to the right path"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound trust and reliance (tawakkul) that Prophet Musa placed in Allah during times of uncertainty. Despite fleeing from danger without a clear destination, his immediate thought was to seek divine guidance, showing that true believers prioritize spiritual direction over physical safety. His supplication demonstrates that even prophets actively sought Allah's guidance, teaching us that seeking direction from Allah should be our first resort, not our last.
orig: ولما توجه تلقاء مدين قال عسى ربي أن يهديني سواء السبيل

translation: And when he came to the water of Madyan, he found there a group of people watering [their flocks], and he found beside them two women keeping back [their flocks]. He said, "What is your concern?" They said, "We cannot water until the shepherds dispatch [their flocks], and our father is a very old man."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the moral obligation to help those in vulnerable positions, particularly women who face societal barriers. Moses's immediate response to help the women demonstrates that social justice and chivalry are integral parts of prophetic conduct. The women's situation also highlights how circumstances sometimes force people to take on roles they wouldn't normally choose, as these women had to tend to flocks due to their father's old age, challenging traditional gender roles when necessity demands.
orig: ولما ورد ماء مدين وجد عليه أمة من الناس يسقون ووجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان قال ما خطبكما قالتا لا نسقي حتى يصدر الرعاء وأبونا شيخ كبير

translation: So he watered [their flocks] for them, then turned to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the beautiful combination of taking practical action while maintaining complete reliance on Allah. Even after performing a good deed (helping the women), Moses demonstrates perfect servitude by acknowledging his continuous need for Allah's assistance, showing that no matter how capable or helpful we may be, we remain in constant need of divine support and guidance.
orig: فسقى لهما ثم تولى إلى الظل فقال رب إني لما أنزلت إلي من خير فقير

translation: Then one of the two women came to him, walking with shyness. She said, "Indeed, my father invites you that he may reward you for having watered [our flocks] for us." So when he came to him and narrated the story, he said, "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the delicate balance between modesty and necessity in Islamic ethics. The woman's shy demeanor while fulfilling her duty demonstrates that modesty shouldn't prevent one from conducting necessary affairs. It also shows how divine providence works through seemingly ordinary circumstances - Moses' act of kindness in watering their flocks led to his safety and eventual employment, proving that good deeds often lead to unexpected blessings. The father's response "Fear not" indicates how providing sanctuary to those fleeing injustice is a noble Islamic principle.
orig: فجاءته إحداهما تمشي على استحياء قالت إن أبي يدعوك ليجزيك أجر ما سقيت لنا فلما جاءه وقص عليه القصص قال لا تخف نجوت من القوم الظالمين

translation: One of them said, "O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of two fundamental qualities in leadership and employment: strength and trustworthiness. It suggests that when selecting someone for a position or responsibility, one should look for individuals who possess both physical or mental capability (strength) and moral integrity (trustworthiness). The woman's observation demonstrates wisdom in recognizing that competence without character, or character without competence, is insufficient for true excellence in service.
orig: قالت إحداهما يا أبت استأجره إن خير من استأجرت القوي الأمين

translation: He said, "I wish to wed one of these two daughters of mine to you, on condition that you serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be (a favor) from you. I do not want to make it difficult for you. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the righteous."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of marriage as a dignified contractual arrangement in Islam, where transparency and clear terms are essential. The father's offer demonstrates wisdom in establishing a fair exchange of marriage for service, while showing flexibility and consideration for the prospective son-in-law's circumstances. It also exemplifies how marriage arrangements in Islamic tradition can incorporate both spiritual and practical considerations, with the emphasis on righteousness and mutual benefit rather than purely material gains.
orig: قال إني أريد أن أنكحك إحدى ابنتي هاتين على أن تأجرني ثماني حجج فإن أتممت عشرا فمن عندك وما أريد أن أشق عليك ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين

translation: He said, "That is [settled] between you and me. Whichever of the two terms I complete, there shall be no injustice to me, and Allah is witness over what we say."
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the importance of clear contractual agreements and mutual consent in business dealings. Moses's response to his future father-in-law shows how Islam emphasizes the need for transparency and fairness in agreements, with both parties having clear terms and God serving as the ultimate witness to their covenant. It teaches us that when we make agreements, we should be explicit about terms, fulfill our obligations honorably, and remember that God oversees all our dealings and promises.
orig: قال ذلك بيني وبينك أيما الأجلين قضيت فلا عدوان علي والله على ما نقول وكيل

translation: When Moses had fulfilled the term and was traveling with his family, he noticed a fire from the direction of Mount Tur. He said to his family, "Stay here, I have spotted a fire. Perhaps I can bring you some news from there, or a burning torch so that you may warm yourselves."
interpretation: This verse illustrates a pivotal moment of divine guidance, where ordinary circumstances lead to extraordinary spiritual encounters. Moses's journey, initially mundane, becomes the prelude to his prophethood. The fire symbolizes divine light and guidance, appearing when Moses had fulfilled his worldly obligations, suggesting that spiritual enlightenment often comes after fulfilling our responsibilities and commitments. His concern for his family's comfort, shown by seeking fire for warmth, demonstrates how divine intervention can manifest through simple acts of human care and responsibility.
orig: فلما قضى موسى الأجل وسار بأهله آنس من جانب الطور نارا قال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر أو جذوة من النار لعلكم تصطلون

translation: When he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley in the blessed spot, from the tree: "O Moses, indeed I am Allah, Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse illustrates a pivotal moment of divine manifestation, where the boundary between the physical and spiritual realms momentarily dissolved. The sacred location and the medium of communication through a tree emphasize that Allah can manifest His signs through any means He chooses, demonstrating that divine presence isn't confined to traditional places of worship but can occur in unexpected locations when He wills it.
orig: فلما أتاها نودي من شاطئ الواد الأيمن في البقعة المباركة من الشجرة أن يا موسى إني أنا الله رب العالمين

translation: "And [he was told], 'Throw down your staff.' But when he saw it writhing as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not return. [Allah said], 'O Moses, approach and fear not. Indeed, you are of the safe.'"
interpretation: "This verse illustrates how Allah transforms the ordinary into the extraordinary to build faith and confidence in His messengers. Moses's fear was a natural human reaction, but Allah's reassurance teaches us that when we act under divine guidance, we need not fear the seemingly impossible tasks before us. The transformation of the staff also symbolizes how Allah can convert our simple, everyday resources into powerful instruments of His will."
orig: وأن ألق عصاك فلما رآها تهتز كأنها جان ولى مدبرا ولم يعقب يا موسى أقبل ولا تخف إنك من الآمنين

translation: Put your hand into your bosom, it will come forth white without any harm. And draw your hand close to your side to be free from fear. These are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Indeed, they have been a rebellious people.
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine empowerment through miraculous signs, specifically showing how Allah equipped Moses with supernatural abilities to confront tyranny. The "white hand" miracle and the calming gesture represent how divine support can transform ordinary human capabilities into extraordinary powers when one is acting in service of truth. These signs were not merely for display but were tools of spiritual and social revolution, demonstrating that when Allah commissions someone for a mission, He provides them with the necessary means to accomplish it despite facing powerful opposition.
orig: اسلك يدك في جيبك تخرج بيضاء من غير سوء واضمم إليك جناحك من الرهب فذانك برهانان من ربك إلى فرعون وملئه إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين

translation: He said, "My Lord, I have killed one of them, and I fear they will kill me"
interpretation: This verse reveals the human vulnerability and emotional honesty of Prophet Musa (Moses) in his relationship with Allah. Despite being chosen as a prophet, he acknowledges his past mistakes and expresses his natural human fears. It demonstrates that even great leaders and prophets experience fear and seek divine protection, teaching us the importance of being truthful about our weaknesses when turning to Allah for help.
orig: قال رب إني قتلت منهم نفسا فأخاف أن يقتلون

translation: And my brother Aaron is more eloquent in speech than I am, so send him with me as a helper to confirm me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me.
interpretation: This verse reflects Moses' humility and strategic thinking in requesting divine assistance. By acknowledging his brother's superior communication skills, Moses demonstrates that effective leadership sometimes requires recognizing others' strengths and delegating responsibilities accordingly. The request also shows how familial bonds can be utilized in service of a greater divine mission, highlighting the importance of complementary partnerships in achieving spiritual goals.
orig: وأخي هارون هو أفصح مني لسانا فأرسله معي ردءا يصدقني إني أخاف أن يكذبون

translation: He said, "We will strengthen your arm through your brother, and grant you both authority, so they will not be able to harm you with Our signs. You two and those who follow you will be the victors."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine strategy of empowering His messengers through companionship and mutual support. When Moses expressed his concerns about confronting Pharaoh alone, Allah assured him by pairing him with his brother Aaron, teaching us that even prophets benefit from partnership and emotional support. The promise of authority and protection demonstrates how divine backing manifests not just spiritually but through practical means, suggesting that when we work in righteous collaboration for Allah's cause, we are granted both tangible and intangible strength to overcome opposition.
orig: قال سنشد عضدك بأخيك ونجعل لكما سلطانا فلا يصلون إليكما بآياتنا أنتما ومن اتبعكما الغالبون

translation: When Moses came to them with Our clear signs, they said: "This is nothing but invented magic, and we never heard of this among our ancient forefathers"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the persistent pattern of denial and skepticism that prophets face when presenting divine truth. The rejection of Moses's message by his people, despite clear evidence, shows how deeply entrenched traditions and inherited beliefs can blind people from accepting new truths, even when they come with undeniable proofs. Their accusation of "magic" reflects a common defensive mechanism used by those who encounter truths that challenge their established worldview.
orig: فلما جاءهم موسى بآياتنا بينات قالوا ما هذا إلا سحر مفترى وما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين

translation: And Moses said, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance from Him and who will have the best outcome in the Hereafter. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in judgment and ultimate justice. Moses is expressing complete trust in Allah's knowledge and judgment, acknowledging that only God can truly determine who is genuinely guided and who is misguided. The statement reflects a profound understanding that worldly success or temporary power doesn't equate to true success, as the final outcome in the Hereafter is what truly matters. Those who persist in oppression and wrongdoing, despite their apparent worldly achievements, will ultimately face failure in the eternal realm.
orig: وقال موسى ربي أعلم بمن جاء بالهدى من عنده ومن تكون له عاقبة الدار إنه لا يفلح الظالمون

translation: And Pharaoh said, "O chiefs, I do not know of any god for you other than me. So, O Haman, light a fire upon clay and make for me a tower that I may look at the god of Moses. And indeed, I think he is among the liars."
interpretation: This verse reveals the extreme arrogance and delusion of power that can corrupt human beings. Pharaoh's claim to divinity demonstrates how absolute power can lead to a complete disconnection from reality and spiritual truth. His command to build a tower to "reach" Moses's God shows a materialistic understanding of divinity, failing to grasp that the Divine cannot be confined to physical space or discovered through worldly constructions. The verse serves as a warning about the dangers of unchecked ego and the folly of those who reject faith based on their limited physical understanding of existence.
orig: وقال فرعون يا أيها الملأ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري فأوقد لي يا هامان على الطين فاجعل لي صرحا لعلي أطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه من الكاذبين

translation: And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us
interpretation: This verse illustrates the dangerous combination of power and denial of accountability, showing how temporal authority can blind people to their ultimate responsibility before God. Pharaoh's arrogance stemmed from his failure to recognize that all power is temporary and borrowed from God, teaching us that true wisdom lies in remaining humble regardless of our worldly position
orig: واستكبر هو وجنوده في الأرض بغير الحق وظنوا أنهم إلينا لا يرجعون

translation: So We seized him and his soldiers and cast them into the sea. See then what was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine justice and the inevitable consequences of tyranny and oppression. It serves as a powerful reminder that no matter how mighty or powerful oppressors may become, they ultimately face divine retribution. The use of Pharaoh's fate as an example demonstrates that those who abuse their power and persist in wrongdoing will eventually meet a dramatic downfall, serving as a lesson for future generations.
orig: فأخذناه وجنوده فنبذناهم في اليم فانظر كيف كان عاقبة الظالمين

translation: And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped
interpretation: This verse speaks to the profound responsibility that comes with leadership and the severe consequences of misguiding others. Those who lead people away from divine guidance and towards destructive paths become architects of their own downfall, as their influence multiplies their accountability before Allah. Their temporary power in this world contrasts sharply with their ultimate powerlessness in the hereafter, where they'll face the consequences of their misguiding leadership without any assistance or intercession.
orig: وجعلناهم أئمة يدعون إلى النار ويوم القيامة لا ينصرون

translation: And We caused a curse to follow them in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among those made hideous.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the enduring nature of divine justice, where those who persistently reject truth and commit wrongdoing face consequences that extend beyond their earthly existence. The "curse" represents a state of spiritual and moral degradation that accompanies the wrongdoers in this life, while their ultimate fate on the Day of Judgment will be one of disgrace and disfigurement, reflecting their inner spiritual corruption.
orig: وأتبعناهم في هذه الدنيا لعنة ويوم القيامة هم من المقبوحين

translation: And We gave Moses the Book, after We had destroyed the former generations, as enlightenment for mankind and guidance and mercy, that they might be reminded
interpretation: This verse highlights how Allah's mercy operates even after periods of divine punishment. The Torah was given to Moses not merely as a law book, but as a means of spiritual and moral regeneration for humanity after previous civilizations had been destroyed due to their transgressions. It suggests that divine guidance is Allah's way of giving humanity new opportunities for redemption and spiritual growth, even after periods of severe divine judgment.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب من بعد ما أهلكنا القرون الأولى بصائر للناس وهدى ورحمة لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And you were not on the western side when We decreed the commandment to Moses, nor were you among the witnesses
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature of the Prophet Muhammad's knowledge about Moses's story, as he wasn't physically present during these historical events. It serves as evidence that Muhammad's revelations came directly from Allah, since he couldn't have known such detailed accounts of past events without divine inspiration, thus validating his prophethood and the authenticity of the Qur'anic message.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الغربي إذ قضينا إلى موسى الأمر وما كنت من الشاهدين

translation: But We produced [many] generations [after Moses], and prolonged was their duration. And you were not a resident among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were senders [of this message]
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's divine plan in preserving and transmitting religious knowledge across generations. It points out that Prophet Muhammad's knowledge of past events wasn't from direct experience or learning from those communities, but rather through divine revelation. This serves as evidence of the Qur'an's divine origin, as Muhammad couldn't have known these historical details about Moses and Madyan without Allah's guidance.
orig: ولكنا أنشأنا قرونا فتطاول عليهم العمر وما كنت ثاويا في أهل مدين تتلو عليهم آياتنا ولكنا كنا مرسلين

translation: And you were not at the side of the Mount when We called [to Moses], but [you were sent] as a mercy from your Lord to warn a people to whom no warner had come before you that they might be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the miraculous nature of Prophet Muhammad's knowledge of past events, highlighting that his message wasn't derived from direct witnessing but through divine revelation. It demonstrates Allah's mercy in sending Muhammad as a messenger to people who had not received previous guidance, suggesting that divine knowledge transcends physical presence and temporal boundaries.
orig: وما كنت بجانب الطور إذ نادينا ولكن رحمة من ربك لتنذر قوما ما أتاهم من نذير من قبلك لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: And if not for [their] fear that a calamity would strike them for what their hands have put forth, they would say, "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so we could follow Your verses and become among the believers?"
interpretation: This verse reveals Allah's wisdom in sending messengers before holding people accountable, preventing them from making excuses on the Day of Judgment. It shows that divine justice includes giving clear warnings and guidance before punishment, demonstrating Allah's mercy in establishing proof against those who reject faith. The mention of "what their hands have put forth" indicates that people's actions and choices have consequences, and divine guidance through messengers is a safeguard against claiming ignorance of truth.
orig: ولولا أن تصيبهم مصيبة بما قدمت أيديهم فيقولوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا فنتبع آياتك ونكون من المؤمنين

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given like what was given to Moses?" Did they not also reject what was given to Moses before? They said, "Two works of magic supporting each other," and they said, "Indeed, we are disbelievers in all."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the perpetual pattern of human resistance to divine guidance, showing how skeptics often use inconsistent arguments to justify their rejection. When presented with new truth, they demand credentials similar to previous prophets, yet they had already rejected those previous prophets. Their claim that Moses and Muhammad's messages were "two forms of magic" reveals their desperate attempt to rationalize their disbelief, ultimately admitting their predetermined stance to reject all divine guidance regardless of its authenticity.
orig: فلما جاءهم الحق من عندنا قالوا لولا أوتي مثل ما أوتي موسى أولم يكفروا بما أوتي موسى من قبل قالوا سحران تظاهرا وقالوا إنا بكل كافرون

translation: Say, "Then bring a scripture from Allah which is more guiding than either of them that I may follow it, if you are truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who doubt divine revelation by asking them to present a better source of guidance than what Allah has provided. It emphasizes that if critics claim to have superior wisdom or guidance, they should be able to produce something that surpasses divine scripture in terms of moral and spiritual direction. The challenge remains unanswered, highlighting the Qur'an's unique position as the ultimate source of guidance.
orig: قل فأتوا بكتاب من عند الله هو أهدى منهما أتبعه إن كنتم صادقين

translation: And if they do not respond to you, then know that they only follow their desires. And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental conflict between divine guidance and personal desires, suggesting that those who reject divine truth often do so not based on rational grounds, but because they are enslaved to their own preferences and inclinations. It points to the spiritual blindness that occurs when one prioritizes personal whims over divine guidance, indicating that such a choice represents the deepest form of misguidance.
orig: فإن لم يستجيبوا لك فاعلم أنما يتبعون أهواءهم ومن أضل ممن اتبع هواه بغير هدى من الله إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين

translation: And We have conveyed to them the Word in succession, that they might give heed.
interpretation: Allah's continuous revelation of divine guidance throughout history serves as a manifestation of His mercy, ensuring that each generation has the opportunity to receive and reflect upon His message. This ongoing process of revelation demonstrates Allah's commitment to human guidance, giving people multiple chances to remember their purpose and return to the right path.
orig: ولقد وصلنا لهم القول لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of divine revelation and the recognition of truth by sincere followers of previous scriptures. It suggests that genuine scholars and believers from among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who truly understood their own scriptures would naturally recognize and accept the truth of the Qur'an, as it confirms and completes the message they already possessed.
orig: الذين آتيناهم الكتاب من قبله هم به يؤمنون

translation: And when it is recited to them, they say, "We believe in it; indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were, before it, Muslims [submitting to Allah]"
interpretation: This verse reveals the sincere response of true believers who recognize divine truth when they encounter it. Their immediate acceptance shows that their hearts were already prepared and aligned with Allah's guidance, indicating that genuine faith often resonates with an inner truth that existed within believers even before their formal declaration of faith. Their statement of being "Muslims before it" suggests that the natural disposition of humans is inclined towards divine truth and submission to the Creator.
orig: وإذا يتلى عليهم قالوا آمنا به إنه الحق من ربنا إنا كنا من قبله مسلمين

translation: Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured, and they repel evil with good, and from what We have provided them, they spend
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine recognition of those who maintain steadfast faith despite hardships, particularly those who converted from previous faiths to Islam. Their double reward symbolizes both their adherence to their previous scripture and their acceptance of the new truth. Their character is marked by responding to negativity with positive actions, demonstrating emotional maturity and spiritual elevation. Their generosity in spending from their provisions reflects a deep trust in divine sustenance and a detachment from material possessions.
orig: أولئك يؤتون أجرهم مرتين بما صبروا ويدرءون بالحسنة السيئة ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it and say, "For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace be upon you; we seek not the ignorant."
interpretation: This verse teaches the noble Islamic principle of maintaining dignity and composure when faced with offensive behavior. Rather than engaging in hostile exchanges or seeking revenge, believers are encouraged to respond with graceful detachment, choosing peace over confrontation while making it clear they won't be drawn into ignorant behavior. It establishes a practical approach to conflict resolution that prevents escalation while preserving one's moral high ground.
orig: وإذا سمعوا اللغو أعرضوا عنه وقالوا لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم سلام عليكم لا نبتغي الجاهلين

translation: Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitations of human influence in matters of spiritual guidance, teaching that even the most sincere efforts to guide loved ones to faith cannot guarantee their acceptance of truth. True guidance comes solely from Allah's divine will and wisdom, reminding us that our role is merely to convey the message while the outcome rests entirely in Allah's hands.
orig: إنك لا تهدي من أحببت ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء وهو أعلم بالمهتدين

translation: And they say, "If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be swept from our land." Have We not established for them a safe sanctuary to which are brought fruits of all kinds as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the common human tendency to prioritize immediate worldly security over spiritual truth, even when divine protection is evident. The Meccans' excuse for rejecting guidance was fear of losing their position and security, yet they failed to recognize that their very safety and prosperity in Mecca was already a divine gift, demonstrating Allah's ability to protect those who follow His path.
orig: وقالوا إن نتبع الهدى معك نتخطف من أرضنا أولم نمكن لهم حرما آمنا يجبى إليه ثمرات كل شيء رزقا من لدنا ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: And how many a city We have destroyed that was insolent in its [way of] living, and those are their dwellings which have not been inhabited after them except briefly. And it is We who were the inheritors.
interpretation: This verse serves as a powerful reminder of the transient nature of worldly power and the consequences of ingratitude and excess. It specifically warns against the arrogance that comes with prosperity, suggesting that when societies become overly comfortable and ungrateful, taking their blessings for granted, they risk divine retribution. The empty dwellings serve as silent witnesses to the futility of worldly accumulation without spiritual consciousness, emphasizing that all possessions ultimately return to Allah, the true and permanent inheritor of everything.
orig: وكم أهلكنا من قرية بطرت معيشتها فتلك مساكنهم لم تسكن من بعدهم إلا قليلا وكنا نحن الوارثين

translation: And your Lord would not destroy the cities until He sends to their mother city a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not destroy the cities except while their people were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's perfect justice and mercy, showing that divine punishment never comes arbitrarily. Before any civilization faces destruction, they must first receive clear guidance through a messenger. This principle demonstrates that Allah gives people ample opportunity to reform and choose the right path before facing consequences for their persistent wrongdoing. The reference to the "mother city" suggests that guidance typically spreads from major urban centers to surrounding areas, reflecting how religious and social reform often follows this pattern.
orig: وما كان ربك مهلك القرى حتى يبعث في أمها رسولا يتلو عليهم آياتنا وما كنا مهلكي القرى إلا وأهلها ظالمون

translation: Whatever you have been given is only the enjoyment and adornment of worldly life, but what is with Allah is better and more lasting. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient nature of material possessions and worldly pleasures, contrasting them with the eternal rewards of the divine. It suggests that humans often become attached to temporary worldly gains, while failing to recognize that spiritual wealth and divine rewards are far more valuable and permanent. The rhetorical question at the end serves as a wake-up call, urging people to use their intellect to discern between fleeting worldly pleasures and lasting spiritual fulfillment.
orig: وما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وزينتها وما عند الله خير وأبقى أفلا تعقلون

translation: Is one to whom We have made a good promise which he will meet [in the Hereafter] like he whom We have provided with the enjoyment of worldly life, then he is, on the Day of Resurrection, among those presented [for punishment]?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between two types of people: those who prioritize eternal rewards through faith and good deeds, and those who are consumed by temporary worldly pleasures. It suggests that true success isn't measured by material wealth or worldly status, but by one's spiritual investment in the hereafter. The verse serves as a reminder that those who choose immediate gratification over eternal salvation will ultimately face accountability.
orig: أفمن وعدناه وعدا حسنا فهو لاقيه كمن متعناه متاع الحياة الدنيا ثم هو يوم القيامة من المحضرين

translation: And [mention] the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' whom you used to claim?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's challenge to those who associated partners with Him, highlighting the futility and falseness of polytheism. On the Day of Judgment, those who worshipped false deities will face a moment of profound realization when their supposed "partners" of Allah will be completely absent, unable to help or intercede for them. The questioning tone carries divine sarcasm, emphasizing how these false gods will abandon their worshippers when they need them most.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: Those against whom the Word has been fulfilled will say: "Our Lord! These are the ones whom we led astray. We led them astray just as we ourselves were astray. We declare our innocence before You; it was not us they worshipped."
interpretation: This verse reveals the futile attempt of misleading leaders to absolve themselves of responsibility on the Day of Judgment. It shows how those who led others astray will try to distance themselves from their followers, demonstrating that relationships built on falsehood will dissolve when accountability arrives. The confession "we led them astray just as we ourselves were astray" indicates that misguidance often perpetuates itself, with the misguided becoming agents of further misguidance.
orig: قال الذين حق عليهم القول ربنا هؤلاء الذين أغوينا أغويناهم كما غوينا تبرأنا إليك ما كانوا إيانا يعبدون

translation: And it will be said: "Call upon your partners!" So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had been guided!
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate futility and desperation of polytheism, as on the Day of Judgment, those who associated partners with Allah will discover that their false deities are powerless to help them. When faced with divine punishment, they'll realize the grave error of their ways, experiencing deep regret for not having followed true guidance when they had the chance.
orig: وقيل ادعوا شركاءكم فدعوهم فلم يستجيبوا لهم ورأوا العذاب لو أنهم كانوا يهتدون

translation: And on the Day when He will call them and say, "What answer did you give to the Messengers?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accountability that awaits humanity on the Day of Judgment, highlighting how each person will be questioned about their response to divine guidance. The interrogative nature of Allah's question suggests that the responsibility to accept or reject the message of the prophets lies squarely with the recipients, and they must bear the consequences of their choice.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول ماذا أجبتم المرسلين

translation: And all information will be obscured from them that Day, so they will not [be able to] ask one another
interpretation: This verse highlights the state of overwhelming confusion and isolation that sinners will experience on the Day of Judgment. The inability to seek information from one another reflects the complete breakdown of worldly social connections and mutual support systems, as each person will be solely focused on their own fate. The "blindness" to information symbolizes how all the excuses and false arguments people used in worldly life will become useless, leaving them unable to defend or justify their past actions.
orig: فعميت عليهم الأنباء يومئذ فهم لا يتساءلون

translation: But whoever repents, believes and does righteous deeds - perhaps he will be among the successful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine principle of second chances and spiritual redemption, suggesting that genuine transformation requires three essential elements: internal change through repentance, spiritual conviction through faith, and external manifestation through good actions. The use of "perhaps" (عسى) doesn't indicate doubt but rather encourages humility and continuous striving, as true success lies in maintaining this transformative path rather than achieving a single moment of change.
orig: فأما من تاب وآمن وعمل صالحا فعسى أن يكون من المفلحين

translation: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; they have no choice. Exalted is Allah and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah in all matters of creation and selection. It refutes the human tendency to question divine wisdom or claim authority in matters that belong solely to Allah's domain. Just as an artist has complete freedom over their artwork, Allah's choices in creation, guidance, and selection are based on His perfect wisdom, beyond human comprehension or interference. The verse serves as a reminder of human limitations and the importance of submitting to divine will rather than imposing our preferences on God's decisions.
orig: وربك يخلق ما يشاء ويختار ما كان لهم الخيرة سبحان الله وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they declare
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's omniscience, highlighting that He has complete knowledge of both our inner thoughts and outward actions, serving as a reminder that we cannot hide anything from our Creator, which should motivate us to maintain sincerity and authenticity in our beliefs and actions.
orig: وربك يعلم ما تكن صدورهم وما يعلنون

translation: And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him is [due all] praise in the first [life] and the Hereafter. And His is the [final] decision, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute uniqueness of Allah's sovereignty, highlighting that His authority transcends both worldly existence and the afterlife. The mention of praise in both realms suggests that all creation, whether aware or unaware, willingly or unwillingly, submits to His glory. The final return to Him implies ultimate accountability, where His judgment will be the only judgment that matters, emphasizing the temporary nature of worldly power and authority.
orig: وهو الله لا إله إلا هو له الحمد في الأولى والآخرة وله الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear?"
interpretation: This verse challenges people to reflect on Allah's absolute power and humanity's complete dependence on Him by presenting a hypothetical scenario that demonstrates His control over natural phenomena. It emphasizes that no other deity could provide light if Allah were to make darkness permanent, highlighting the futility of polytheism and the necessity of recognizing Allah's unique authority over creation.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم الليل سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بضياء أفلا تسمعون

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the day continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you a night in which you may rest? Then will you not see?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes humanity's complete dependence on Allah's divine system by highlighting how the alternation of day and night is a mercy that we often take for granted. It challenges people to recognize that no other power could provide the essential rest period of night if Allah were to make daylight permanent, thus demonstrating Allah's unique authority over natural phenomena and His wisdom in creating a balanced universe that sustains life.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن جعل الله عليكم النهار سرمدا إلى يوم القيامة من إله غير الله يأتيكم بليل تسكنون فيه أفلا تبصرون

translation: And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty and that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's compassionate design of the universe, where the alternation of night and day serves humanity's physical, economic, and spiritual needs. The night's darkness is a divine gift for rest and recuperation, while daylight enables the pursuit of livelihood and prosperity. This dual system reflects Allah's deep understanding of human nature, providing both the necessity of rest and the opportunity for productivity, ultimately calling for human gratitude in recognizing this perfect balance.
orig: ومن رحمته جعل لكم الليل والنهار لتسكنوا فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله ولعلكم تشكرون

translation: And [mention] the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' whom you used to claim?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's challenge to those who associated partners with Him, highlighting the futility and falseness of polytheistic beliefs. On the Day of Judgment, when all illusions are stripped away, those who worshipped false deities will face the stark reality that their objects of worship were powerless and non-existent. The questioning tone emphasizes the absurdity of their previous beliefs and serves as a powerful reminder that only Allah deserves worship.
orig: ويوم يناديهم فيقول أين شركائي الذين كنتم تزعمون

translation: And We will extract from every nation a witness and say, "Produce your proof," and they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and lost from them is what they used to invent
interpretation: This verse paints a powerful scene of the Day of Judgment where Allah will bring forth from each community a witness - typically their prophet or leader - to testify about how their people responded to divine guidance. The demand for proof represents the ultimate moment of accountability where all false beliefs and fabricated deities will be exposed as mere inventions, leaving people to confront the undeniable reality of Allah's absolute truth and sovereignty
orig: ونزعنا من كل أمة شهيدا فقلنا هاتوا برهانكم فعلموا أن الحق لله وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

translation: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he behaved arrogantly towards them. And We had given him such treasures that their very keys would weigh down a band of strong men. When his people said to him, "Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like the exultant."
interpretation: This verse illustrates how material wealth can corrupt the human soul and lead to spiritual downfall. Qarun's story serves as a warning about the dangers of allowing wealth to breed arrogance and disconnection from one's community. Despite being blessed with extraordinary wealth by Allah, instead of showing gratitude and using it for good, he became prideful and oppressive. The mention of the heavy keys symbolizes how excessive wealth can become a burden rather than a blessing when not handled with humility and social responsibility.
orig: إن قارون كان من قوم موسى فبغى عليهم وآتيناه من الكنوز ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة أولي القوة إذ قال له قومه لا تفرح إن الله لا يحب الفرحين

translation: But seek, through that which Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and do not forget your share of the world. And do good as Allah has done good to you. And desire not corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not like corrupters.
interpretation: This verse teaches the principle of balanced living in Islam, emphasizing that worldly success and spiritual fulfillment aren't mutually exclusive. It encourages believers to use their God-given resources to secure their eternal life while maintaining a healthy engagement with worldly affairs. The verse suggests that one's approach to life should mirror Allah's generosity, indicating that prosperity should be channeled towards beneficial causes rather than destructive or corrupt practices.
orig: وابتغ فيما آتاك الله الدار الآخرة ولا تنس نصيبك من الدنيا وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك ولا تبغ الفساد في الأرض إن الله لا يحب المفسدين

translation: He said, "I was only given it [wealth] because of knowledge I possess." Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him of generations those who were greater than him in power and greater in accumulation [of wealth]? But the criminals will not be asked about their sins.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the dangerous mindset of attributing success solely to one's own abilities while forgetting Allah's role, exemplifying how wealth and power can lead to arrogance and ingratitude. It reminds us that no matter how powerful or wealthy someone becomes, they are not immune to Allah's judgment, as demonstrated by the fate of previous, more powerful civilizations. The final statement about criminals not being questioned is particularly poignant, suggesting that some sins are so evident they require no interrogation before judgment.
orig: قال إنما أوتيته على علم عندي أولم يعلم أن الله قد أهلك من قبله من القرون من هو أشد منه قوة وأكثر جمعا ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون

translation: So he came out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the worldly life said, "Oh, would that we had like what was given to Qarun! Indeed, he is one of great fortune."
interpretation: This verse illustrates how material wealth can deceive people into equating prosperity with success and divine favor. The admiration of Qarun's wealth by his people demonstrates humanity's persistent weakness in being dazzled by worldly possessions, failing to recognize that true fortune lies in spiritual wealth and divine contentment rather than material abundance.
orig: فخرج على قومه في زينته قال الذين يريدون الحياة الدنيا يا ليت لنا مثل ما أوتي قارون إنه لذو حظ عظيم

translation: But those who had been given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds. And none are granted this [reward] except the patient."
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound understanding of those who possess true knowledge, as they recognize that material wealth and worldly success are fleeting compared to the eternal rewards from Allah. Their insight stems from spiritual wisdom, emphasizing that lasting fulfillment comes through faith and good deeds, though achieving this requires patience and perseverance through life's trials.
orig: وقال الذين أوتوا العلم ويلكم ثواب الله خير لمن آمن وعمل صالحا ولا يلقاها إلا الصابرون

translation: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. And there was no company to help him against Allah, nor was he among those who could help themselves.
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine justice and the ultimate powerlessness of worldly might, showing how material wealth and earthly power offer no protection against Allah's will. It serves as a reminder that arrogance and self-sufficiency, exemplified by Qarun's story, lead to downfall, while true security lies only in humble submission to Allah.
orig: فخسفنا به وبداره الأرض فما كان له من فئة ينصرونه من دون الله وما كان من المنتصرين

translation: And those who had wished for his position the day before began to say, "Ah! It is indeed Allah Who enlarges the provision or restricts it, to any of His servants He pleases! Had it not been that Allah was gracious to us, He could have caused the earth to swallow us up! Ah! Those who reject Allah will assuredly never prosper."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound transformation in people's understanding when they witness divine intervention. Those who initially envied Qarun's wealth and status experienced a spiritual awakening upon seeing his downfall, recognizing that material success is entirely at Allah's discretion and not a sign of divine favor. Their reflection reveals the mature realization that true prosperity lies not in wealth but in divine grace, and that ingratitude and denial of Allah's authority leads to ultimate failure.
orig: وأصبح الذين تمنوا مكانه بالأمس يقولون ويكأن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء من عباده ويقدر لولا أن من الله علينا لخسف بنا ويكأنه لا يفلح الكافرون

translation: That home of the Hereafter We assign to those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth or corruption. And the best outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that eternal success is reserved for those who maintain humility and ethical conduct. It suggests that true achievement in God's eyes isn't measured by worldly status or power, but rather by one's ability to resist the temptations of arrogance and corruption. The promise of the Hereafter serves as a divine incentive for maintaining moral integrity and practicing self-restraint in the face of worldly temptations.
orig: تلك الدار الآخرة نجعلها للذين لا يريدون علوا في الأرض ولا فسادا والعاقبة للمتقين

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it, and whoever comes with an evil deed - then those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except for what they used to do
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's perfect justice and boundless generosity. While good deeds are multiplied and rewarded beyond their actual worth, evil deeds receive only their equivalent punishment, demonstrating how Allah's mercy outweighs His punishment. This divine principle encourages believers to strive for righteousness by showing that God's rewards are always more generous than what we actually deserve.
orig: من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى الذين عملوا السيئات إلا ما كانوا يعملون

translation: Indeed, He who imposed upon you the Qur'an will return you to a place of return. Say, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in clear error."
interpretation: This verse offers a divine promise of comfort to the Prophet Muhammad during his challenging time in Mecca, assuring him that his eventual return to Mecca would be triumphant. The "place of return" symbolizes both the physical return to Mecca and the spiritual return to Allah. It reinforces the idea that those who stay true to their divine mission will ultimately be vindicated, even if they face temporary displacement or hardship.
orig: إن الذي فرض عليك القرآن لرادك إلى معاد قل ربي أعلم من جاء بالهدى ومن هو في ضلال مبين

translation: And you (O Muhammad) were not expecting that the Book would be conveyed to you, but it is a mercy from your Lord. So never be a supporter to the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and highlights that its revelation was an unexpected mercy bestowed upon Prophet Muhammad. It underscores that the Prophet's mission wasn't self-initiated but rather a divine intervention, suggesting that true guidance comes as a gift from Allah rather than through human planning. The concluding warning against supporting disbelievers indicates the serious responsibility that comes with receiving divine guidance, emphasizing the need to maintain unwavering commitment to divine truth over worldly alliances.
orig: وما كنت ترجو أن يلقى إليك الكتاب إلا رحمة من ربك فلا تكونن ظهيرا للكافرين

translation: And let them not avert you from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you. And invite to your Lord and do not be among the polytheists
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remaining steadfast in one's commitment to divine guidance despite external pressures or opposition. It suggests that once a person has received spiritual truth, they have a dual responsibility: to personally maintain their dedication to these truths without letting others dissuade them, and to actively share this guidance with others through peaceful invitation. The warning against polytheism at the end indicates that compromising one's monotheistic beliefs for social acceptance or external pressure is a serious spiritual danger.
orig: ولا يصدنك عن آيات الله بعد إذ أنزلت إليك وادع إلى ربك ولا تكونن من المشركين

translation: And do not invoke with Allah another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will perish except His Face. His is the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental concept of pure monotheism by warning against associating any partners with Allah, while also highlighting the temporary nature of all creation. The mention of Allah's "Face" remaining while everything else perishes symbolizes His eternal essence and attributes, reminding us that all power, authority, and permanence belong exclusively to Him. The verse serves as a profound reminder of human mortality and accountability, contrasted with Divine permanence and sovereignty.
orig: ولا تدع مع الله إلها آخر لا إله إلا هو كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه له الحكم وإليه ترجعون

translation: Alif, Lam, Meem
interpretation: These mysterious letters at the beginning of several Qur'anic chapters symbolize the miraculous nature of the Qur'an's language, demonstrating that despite being composed of the same letters that Arabs used in everyday speech, they could not replicate its divine eloquence and perfection
orig: الم

translation: Do people think they will be left alone to say "We believe" without being tested?
interpretation: This verse teaches us that true faith requires more than mere verbal declaration. Allah subjects believers to various trials and difficulties to distinguish genuine believers from those who merely claim faith without conviction. These tests serve to strengthen one's faith, purify the heart, and elevate the believer's spiritual status through patience and perseverance.
orig: أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يفتنون

translation: And We have certainly tested those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's divine wisdom in testing people's faith through various trials and tribulations. The purpose is not merely to cause hardship, but to distinguish genuine believers from pretenders. Just as gold is purified through fire, a person's true character and sincerity in faith becomes apparent through challenges. These tests serve as a means of spiritual growth and self-discovery, revealing one's true nature and level of commitment to their beliefs.
orig: ولقد فتنا الذين من قبلهم فليعلمن الله الذين صدقوا وليعلمن الكاذبين

translation: Or do those who commit evil deeds think they can outrun Us? Evil is what they judge.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of those who believe they can escape divine accountability. It suggests that some people delude themselves into thinking their misdeeds will go unpunished, or that they can somehow evade Allah's justice through their cleverness or resources. The phrase "outrun Us" metaphorically illustrates their misguided attempt to escape consequences, while the final judgment "Evil is what they judge" emphasizes the poor reasoning behind such thinking, as no one can escape Allah's all-encompassing knowledge and justice.
orig: أم حسب الذين يعملون السيئات أن يسبقونا ساء ما يحكمون

translation: Whoever hopes to meet Allah - indeed, Allah's appointed time will come. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere anticipation of meeting Allah in the afterlife, suggesting that one's actions and faith should be driven by this ultimate encounter. The mention of Allah's appointed time serves as both a comfort to believers and a warning to the heedless, reminding us that everything occurs according to divine timing that cannot be hastened or delayed. Allah's attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing indicate that He is fully aware of our innermost hopes, fears, and intentions regarding this anticipated meeting.
orig: من كان يرجو لقاء الله فإن أجل الله لآت وهو السميع العليم

translation: And whoever strives, he strives only for himself. Indeed, Allah is Free of need from the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability and the nature of spiritual struggle, highlighting that when we engage in efforts to improve ourselves or fight against our inner desires, the benefit of such striving returns solely to us. Allah doesn't need our worship or efforts, as He is completely self-sufficient. Our striving is ultimately a means of our own growth, development, and salvation.
orig: ومن جاهد فإنما يجاهد لنفسه إن الله لغني عن العالمين

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's divine justice and mercy, illustrating that sincere faith coupled with good actions leads to spiritual purification. The promise of removing misdeeds suggests that genuine righteousness can serve as an expiation for past sins, while the reward being based on their "best" deeds indicates that Allah judges people by their finest moments and highest achievements rather than their shortcomings.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنكفرن عنهم سيئاتهم ولنجزينهم أحسن الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: And We have enjoined upon man goodness to parents. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the delicate balance between filial duty and religious conviction, emphasizing that while respect and kindness to parents is a divine mandate, one's primary allegiance must be to divine truth. It acknowledges that even the closest family bonds cannot supersede one's relationship with the Divine, establishing a clear hierarchy of loyalties where truth and monotheism take precedence over familial pressures to compromise religious principles.
orig: ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حسنا وإن جاهداك لتشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما إلي مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely admit them among the righteous
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's divine promise of spiritual elevation, indicating that true faith combined with righteous actions leads to a person's inclusion among the company of the virtuous. It suggests that one's ultimate spiritual station isn't determined by lineage or social status, but rather by the combination of sincere belief and practical manifestation of that belief through good deeds.
orig: والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لندخلنهم في الصالحين

translation: And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah," but when they are harmed for [the cause of] Allah, they consider the trial of the people as [if it were] the punishment of Allah. But if victory comes from your Lord, they say, "Indeed, we were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of all creatures?
interpretation: This verse exposes the nature of those whose faith is superficial and opportunistic. It criticizes people who claim to believe but abandon their faith when faced with hardship or persecution, treating social pressure as if it were divine punishment. When success or victory comes, these same individuals quickly switch sides, claiming they were always believers. The verse highlights the phenomenon of fair-weather faith and reminds us that Allah knows the true contents of everyone's hearts, exposing the futility of such hypocrisy.
orig: ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله فإذا أوذي في الله جعل فتنة الناس كعذاب الله ولئن جاء نصر من ربك ليقولن إنا كنا معكم أوليس الله بأعلم بما في صدور العالمين

translation: And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's divine knowledge in distinguishing between true believers and hypocrites through life's trials and challenges. The trials serve as a means of exposing the genuine faith of believers and revealing the false pretenses of hypocrites, showing that one's true nature cannot remain hidden from Allah's wisdom.
orig: وليعلمن الله الذين آمنوا وليعلمن المنافقين

translation: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will carry your sins." But they will not carry anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse exposes the deceptive tactics of those who oppose faith, showing how they attempt to mislead believers by making false promises of bearing their spiritual burden. It highlights the universal principle that each soul is ultimately responsible for its own actions and choices, and no one can truly bear another's spiritual accountability. The verse serves as a warning against following those who make grandiose promises without having any real ability to fulfill them.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا اتبعوا سبيلنا ولنحمل خطاياكم وما هم بحاملين من خطاياهم من شيء إنهم لكاذبون

translation: And they will surely carry their own burdens and burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of moral accountability and the ripple effect of misleading others. Those who lead people astray will bear not only the burden of their own sins but also share in the burden of those whom they misguided. Leaders, influencers, and those in positions of authority have an amplified responsibility as their actions and teachings affect others, making them accountable for both their personal misdeeds and the collective impact of their influence on others' spiritual deviation.
orig: وليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم وليسألن يوم القيامة عما كانوا يفترون

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them for a thousand years minus fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers
interpretation: This verse highlights the extraordinary patience and perseverance of Prophet Noah in his mission, spending an incredibly long time calling his people to the truth. Despite his continuous efforts over 950 years, most of his people remained resistant to his message, demonstrating that success in spiritual calling isn't measured by numbers of converts but by steadfastness in delivering the divine message. Their eventual punishment through the flood came only after they were given an exceptionally long period to reflect and reform.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فلبث فيهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما فأخذهم الطوفان وهم ظالمون

translation: So We saved him and the companions of the ship and made it a sign for all worlds
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and power through the story of Noah, demonstrating how divine intervention protects the faithful while serving as an eternal reminder of both God's justice and mercy. The preservation of Noah's story isn't just historical documentation but stands as a timeless lesson about faith, perseverance, and divine protection in times of overwhelming adversity.
orig: فأنجيناه وأصحاب السفينة وجعلناها آية للعالمين

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said to his people, "Worship Allah and fear Him. That is better for you, if you should know."
interpretation: This verse highlights the timeless essence of Prophet Ibrahim's message, emphasizing that true success and fulfillment can only be achieved through sincere devotion to Allah and maintaining consciousness of His presence in our lives. Ibrahim's approach demonstrates that spiritual guidance should be presented with wisdom and care for people's wellbeing, as he explains that following divine guidance is ultimately for their own benefit.
orig: وإبراهيم إذ قال لقومه اعبدوا الله واتقوه ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون

translation: You worship besides Allah only idols, and you create falsehood. Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess for you [the power of] provision. So seek from Allah provision and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of polytheism by highlighting how created objects or beings cannot provide sustenance or benefit to their worshippers. It points to the fundamental economic and spiritual reality that all provisions ultimately come from Allah alone, establishing a direct connection between economic sustenance and spiritual truth. The command to seek provision from Allah while worshipping Him suggests that material pursuit should be integrated with spiritual devotion, rather than separated from it.
orig: إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون إفكا إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه واشكروا له إليه ترجعون

translation: And if you deny [the message], already nations before you have denied. And there is not upon the Messenger except [the duty of] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that rejection of divine truth is a recurring pattern throughout human history, and prophets cannot be held accountable for people's disbelief. The prophet's sole responsibility is to convey the message with clarity and sincerity, while the choice to accept or reject ultimately lies with the recipients. This relieves the burden of outcome from the messenger's shoulders, highlighting the universal principle of individual accountability in matters of faith.
orig: وإن تكذبوا فقد كذب أمم من قبلكم وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين

translation: Do they not see how Allah originates creation, then repeats it? Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite power over creation and resurrection, drawing attention to the observable cycle of life as evidence. Just as we witness Allah's ability to create life from nothing initially, this same power makes the resurrection of the dead equally feasible. The verse challenges skeptics to reflect on the natural phenomena around them as proof of Allah's capability to bring forth life after death.
orig: أولم يروا كيف يبدئ الله الخلق ثم يعيده إن ذلك على الله يسير

translation: Say, "Travel throughout the earth and see how He began creation. Then Allah will create the final creation. Indeed, Allah has power over all things."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of scientific observation and contemplation of the natural world as a means to strengthen one's faith. By studying Earth's geological history, fossil records, and the origins of life, humans can witness Allah's creative power firsthand. This empirical evidence, combined with the promise of resurrection, demonstrates Allah's unlimited ability to create, recreate, and transform matter in any way He chooses.
orig: قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف بدأ الخلق ثم الله ينشئ النشأة الآخرة إن الله على كل شيء قدير

translation: He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills, and to Him you will be returned
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and divine justice, highlighting that ultimate authority in dispensing both mercy and punishment rests solely with Him. It reminds us that our actions have consequences, but the final judgment lies in Allah's wisdom and discretion, not in human standards or expectations. The mention of return to Him underscores the temporary nature of worldly life and the inevitability of accountability.
orig: يعذب من يشاء ويرحم من يشاء وإليه تقلبون

translation: And you cannot escape [from Allah] on earth or in the heaven, and you have not besides Allah any protector or any helper
interpretation: This verse emphasizes humanity's complete dependence on Allah by highlighting our inability to escape His power or knowledge, whether through earthly means or even if we could reach the heavens. It serves as a reminder that seeking refuge or assistance from any source other than Allah is futile, as He alone possesses true authority and capability to help. This understanding should instill both humility and security in believers - humility in recognizing our limitations, and security in knowing that attaching ourselves to Allah is the only path to real protection.
orig: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض ولا في السماء وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And those who disbelieve in Allah's signs and the meeting with Him - those have despaired of My mercy, and they will have a painful punishment
interpretation: This verse illustrates the spiritual and psychological state of those who reject faith, suggesting that their denial creates a self-imposed barrier between them and divine mercy. Their disbelief isn't just a rejection of religious concepts, but a deeper disconnection that leads to a state of hopelessness regarding Allah's compassion, making their punishment not just a future consequence but also an immediate spiritual deprivation.
orig: والذين كفروا بآيات الله ولقائه أولئك يئسوا من رحمتي وأولئك لهم عذاب أليم

translation: But the answer of his people was only that they said, "Kill him or burn him." But Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how truth-bearers often face extreme opposition from those in power, yet divine protection supersedes human schemes. The attempt to burn Prophet Ibrahim demonstrates that when one stands firm in their convictions of faith, Allah's protection manifests in miraculous ways, turning what was meant for destruction into a sign of divine power.
orig: فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا اقتلوه أو حرقوه فأنجاه الله من النار إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: And he said: "You have taken idols besides Allah, forming bonds of love between yourselves in the worldly life. Then on the Day of Resurrection, you will disown one another and curse one another, and your abode will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers."
interpretation: This verse reveals the temporary and deceptive nature of relationships built on false foundations. Just as people unite in their worship of idols or false deities out of worldly interests and temporary affection, these same bonds will transform into enmity and hatred on the Day of Judgment. The superficial unity they shared in rejecting truth will dissolve, leaving them to face the consequences of their choices without any support or assistance.
orig: وقال إنما اتخذتم من دون الله أوثانا مودة بينكم في الحياة الدنيا ثم يوم القيامة يكفر بعضكم ببعض ويلعن بعضكم بعضا ومأواكم النار وما لكم من ناصرين

translation: So Lot believed in him, and said: "Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound nature of true faith and its demands, showing how genuine belief often requires leaving behind familiar surroundings and comfort zones. Lot's declaration of migration demonstrates that spiritual commitment sometimes necessitates physical relocation, especially when one's current environment becomes hostile to faith and righteousness. His acknowledgment of Allah's might and wisdom suggests complete trust that divine guidance will lead to a better destination, despite the uncertainties of migration.
orig: فآمن له لوط وقال إني مهاجر إلى ربي إنه هو العزيز الحكيم

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and We placed in his descendants prophethood and scripture, and We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, he is in the Hereafter among the righteous
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's abundant blessings upon Ibrahim (Abraham) by establishing a legacy of divine guidance through his lineage. The mention of both worldly and spiritual rewards demonstrates that sincere devotion to Allah's path leads to success in both realms of existence, emphasizing that righteousness can bring fulfillment in this life while securing an elevated position in the hereafter.
orig: ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب وجعلنا في ذريته النبوة والكتاب وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين

translation: And [We sent] Lot when he said to his people, "Indeed, you commit an immorality that no one in the world has committed before you."
interpretation: This verse highlights how moral degradation can lead a society to unprecedented levels of transgression. Lot's people had invented a new form of sin, demonstrating that human beings can devise novel ways of disobedience when they stray from divine guidance. This serves as a warning that societies can normalize behaviors that were previously unthinkable, making it crucial to maintain strong moral boundaries.
orig: ولوطا إذ قال لقومه إنكم لتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد من العالمين

translation: Do you indeed approach men with desire and cut off the road and commit evil in your meetings? But his people's answer was only that they said, "Bring us Allah's punishment, if you are truthful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the depth of moral corruption in the community of Prophet Lut, where their defiance reached such extremes that instead of heeding warnings, they mockingly challenged divine punishment. Their response demonstrates how persistent sinfulness can lead to spiritual blindness, making people so arrogant that they even dare to challenge divine retribution rather than reflect on their wrongdoings.
orig: أئنكم لتأتون الرجال وتقطعون السبيل وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر فما كان جواب قومه إلا أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله إن كنت من الصادقين

translation: He said, "My Lord, help me against the people who spread corruption."
interpretation: This verse reflects the universal struggle between righteousness and corruption, emphasizing that seeking divine assistance is essential when confronting those who actively work to spread evil and disorder in society. It teaches that when faced with overwhelming opposition from wrongdoers, one's primary recourse should be turning to Allah rather than relying solely on human means.
orig: قال رب انصرني على القوم المفسدين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good news, they said, "Indeed, we will destroy the people of this city. Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine justice and mercy working in tandem, where the angels first bring Abraham good news (of a son) before announcing destruction, showing how Allah's mercy precedes His punishment. The mention of the city's destruction due to wrongdoing establishes that divine punishment is never arbitrary but comes as a consequence of persistent transgression and injustice.
orig: ولما جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم بالبشرى قالوا إنا مهلكو أهل هذه القرية إن أهلها كانوا ظالمين

translation: He said, "Indeed, within it is Lot." They said, "We are more knowing of who is within it. We will surely save him and his family, except for his wife; she is to be of those who remain behind."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's mercy and justice operating simultaneously - while divine punishment was decreed for the wicked city, the righteous were guaranteed protection. It shows that familial ties alone don't guarantee salvation; rather, individual faith and conduct determine one's fate, as exemplified by Lot's wife who, despite being married to a prophet, chose disbelief and faced divine punishment.
orig: قال إن فيها لوطا قالوا نحن أعلم بمن فيها لننجينه وأهله إلا امرأته كانت من الغابرين

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt for them great discomfort. They said, "Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is to be of those who remain behind."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound challenge faced by righteous individuals when standing up for divine truth in the face of societal corruption. Lot's distress upon seeing the angels (who appeared as handsome young men) reflects his awareness of his community's depravity and his protective instinct as a host in a morally bankrupt society.
