translation: [This is] a blessed Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that they might reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding would be reminded
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transformative power of deep contemplation and reflection on divine scripture. It suggests that true understanding of the Qur'an comes not from mere reading, but from thoughtful meditation on its meanings. The phrase "those of understanding" indicates that spiritual wisdom requires engaging both intellect and heart, as true comprehension is reserved for those who approach the text with sincere dedication to understanding its deeper implications.
orig: كتاب أنزلناه إليك مبارك ليدبروا آياته وليتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: And to David We gave Solomon - an excellent servant, indeed he was one who constantly turned [to Allah]
interpretation: This verse highlights the special spiritual connection between Prophet Solomon and Allah, emphasizing how true servitude to God manifests in constantly returning to Him in all matters. Solomon's designation as an "excellent servant" despite his immense worldly power as a king demonstrates that genuine greatness lies not in authority or wealth, but in one's devotion and humility before the Divine.
orig: ووهبنا لداوود سليمان نعم العبد إنه أواب

translation: When there were displayed before him in the evening the steeds of the highest breeding and swift of foot
interpretation: This verse speaks to the importance of maintaining balance between worldly responsibilities and spiritual devotion. Solomon's momentary distraction by these magnificent horses represents how even the most pious can be temporarily drawn to worldly beauty, but what matters is returning one's focus to divine remembrance.
orig: إذ عرض عليه بالعشي الصافنات الجياد

translation: And he said, "Indeed, I gave preference to the love of good [things] over the remembrance of my Lord until [the sun] disappeared into the barrier [of darkness]"
interpretation: This verse illustrates how material attachments, even seemingly noble ones like the love of fine horses, can distract us from our spiritual obligations and remembrance of Allah. It serves as a reminder that we must maintain balance and not let worldly attractions, regardless of their nature, overshadow our primary duty to God.
orig: فقال إني أحببت حب الخير عن ذكر ربي حتى توارت بالحجاب

translation: "Return them to me," then he began to strike their legs and necks
interpretation: This verse from Surah Sad illustrates Prophet Solomon's momentary distraction from prayer by fine horses, followed by his realization and subsequent symbolic act. The striking of legs and necks represents his determination to remove worldly distractions that interfere with devotion to Allah, symbolizing the spiritual struggle to maintain focus on divine worship over material attractions.
orig: ردوها علي فطفق مسحا بالسوق والأعناق

translation: And We certainly tried Solomon and placed on his throne a body; then he returned [to his former condition]
interpretation: This verse alludes to a divine test that Solomon faced, possibly involving his temporary loss of authority or spiritual status. The "body" on his throne may represent a period where Solomon's power was diminished or when he faced significant challenges that made him realize his dependence on Allah. Through this trial, Solomon demonstrated humility and returned to a state of sincere devotion, showing that even great kings and prophets are subject to Allah's tests and must maintain their spiritual consciousness.
orig: ولقد فتنا سليمان وألقينا على كرسيه جسدا ثم أناب

translation: He said: "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower."
interpretation: This verse reflects Solomon's profound understanding that true sovereignty comes from divine grace. His request wasn't born of mere worldly ambition, but rather a desire to establish a unique model of righteous governance that would serve as an eternal example. The kingdom he sought was one that would combine both spiritual and temporal authority, demonstrating how divine wisdom could be perfectly integrated with worldly rule.
orig: قال رب اغفر لي وهب لي ملكا لا ينبغي لأحد من بعدي إنك أنت الوهاب

translation: So We subjected to him the wind blowing gently by his command wherever he directed
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's special favor upon Prophet Sulaiman (Solomon), granting him authority over natural elements. The gentle submission of the wind to Sulaiman's command symbolizes how even the mightiest forces of nature yield to divine will, and how true power comes through divine blessing rather than human effort.
orig: فسخرنا له الريح تجري بأمره رخاء حيث أصاب

translation: And (We subjected to him) the devils - every builder and diver
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's favor upon Prophet Sulaiman (Solomon) by granting him authority over supernatural forces. The devils were compelled to serve him in construction and underwater exploration, highlighting how even powerful spiritual beings can be subjected to human authority when Allah wills it, demonstrating that ultimate power belongs to Allah alone.
orig: والشياطين كل بناء وغواص

translation: And others bound together in chains
interpretation: This verse alludes to the divine power over those who reject truth and act in defiance, suggesting that no matter how powerful or rebellious one might be in this world, they are ultimately subject to Allah's authority and justice. The imagery of chains represents the consequences of one's actions and the inability to escape divine judgment.
orig: وآخرين مقرنين في الأصفاد

translation: "This is Our gift, so grant or withhold without account."
interpretation: "This verse emphasizes divine generosity and sovereignty, indicating that when Allah bestows authority or resources upon someone, they have the freedom to distribute or manage these gifts according to their discretion, without being questioned about their decisions. It shows that true authority comes with the privilege of independent decision-making, free from the need to justify one's choices to others."
orig: هذا عطاؤنا فامنن أو أمسك بغير حساب

translation: And indeed, for him is nearness to Us and a good place of return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the special status of those who remain steadfast in their faith and righteousness. The "nearness" mentioned refers to a spiritual proximity to Allah, suggesting an intimate relationship between the Creator and His devoted servants. The "good place of return" indicates that such individuals will be rewarded with an excellent destination in the hereafter, highlighting Allah's promise of eternal contentment to those who stay true to His path.
orig: وإن له عندنا لزلفى وحسن مآب

translation: And remember Our servant Job, when he called upon his Lord: "Indeed, Satan has afflicted me with hardship and torment"
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound spiritual lesson that even the most righteous of believers can face severe trials, and the proper response is to turn directly to Allah in humility and supplication rather than losing faith. Job's example teaches us that attributing our hardships to Satan while maintaining trust in Allah demonstrates both spiritual awareness and steadfast faith.
orig: واذكر عبدنا أيوب إذ نادى ربه أني مسني الشيطان بنصب وعذاب

translation: Strike [the ground] with your foot; this is a [spring for] a cool bath and drink
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's mercy and miraculous response to Prophet Ayyub's suffering, showing that divine relief can come from unexpected sources and that hardship is often followed by ease through simple divine commands
orig: اركض برجلك هذا مغتسل بارد وشراب

translation: And We restored to him his family and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's infinite mercy and reward for patience through the story of Prophet Job (Ayyub). After enduring immense trials with unwavering faith, Allah not only restored Job's family but doubled them, demonstrating that steadfast patience and trust in divine wisdom ultimately leads to greater blessings than what was initially lost.
orig: ووهبنا له أهله ومثلهم معهم رحمة منا وذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: "Take in your hand a bundle of grass and strike with it, and do not break your oath. Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned back [to Allah]."
interpretation: "This verse reveals divine mercy and wisdom in helping Prophet Ayyub fulfill his oath without causing excessive harm. When he had sworn to strike his wife during a moment of frustration, Allah provided him a compassionate solution by allowing him to use a bundle of grass instead of causing actual harm, teaching us that Islam encourages finding merciful solutions even in matters of fulfilling oaths while maintaining justice."
orig: وخذ بيدك ضغثا فاضرب به ولا تحنث إنا وجدناه صابرا نعم العبد إنه أواب

translation: And remember Our servants Ibrahim, Ishaq, and Ya'qub, men of strength and vision
interpretation: The verse highlights that true strength lies not just in physical power but in spiritual insight and moral fortitude. By describing these prophets as possessing both "hands" (strength) and "vision," it suggests that effective leadership and divine service require a combination of practical capability and spiritual wisdom. Their strength was manifested in their unwavering dedication to God's cause, while their vision represented their deep spiritual insight and foresight in guiding their people.
orig: واذكر عبادنا إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب أولي الأيدي والأبصار

translation: Indeed, We chose them for an exclusive quality: the remembrance of the Home [of the Hereafter]
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's special favor upon His chosen servants, who were granted the unique ability to remain constantly mindful of the afterlife. Their hearts were purified to focus on eternal matters rather than worldly distractions, making them truly exceptional in their spiritual consciousness and detachment from material pursuits.
orig: إنا أخلصناهم بخالصة ذكرى الدار

translation: And indeed, they are with Us among the chosen and outstanding [ones]
interpretation: This verse speaks to the elevated spiritual status of certain individuals who have been specially selected by Allah. It suggests that divine selection is based on both inherent qualities and earned merit, indicating that spiritual excellence is a combination of Allah's grace and human effort. The term "chosen" implies a rigorous selection process, suggesting that these individuals demonstrated exceptional devotion, character, and commitment to their spiritual journey.
orig: وإنهم عندنا لمن المصطفين الأخيار

translation: And remember Ismail, Al-Yasa (Elisha), and Dhul-Kifl; they were all among the best
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering and learning from righteous role models. By specifically mentioning these three prophets, Allah highlights how they exemplified exceptional moral character and dedication to their divine mission. Their inclusion in the Qur'an serves as a reminder that spiritual excellence is achieved through consistent righteousness and unwavering commitment to one's faith, rather than through momentary acts of piety.
orig: واذكر إسماعيل واليسع وذا الكفل وكل من الأخيار

translation: This is a reminder, and indeed, for the righteous is a good place of return
interpretation: The verse emphasizes that the teachings and guidance provided in the Qur'an serve as a powerful reminder for humanity, and those who live their lives in consciousness of Allah and maintain righteousness will be rewarded with an excellent destination in the afterlife. This indicates that spiritual success is directly linked to how one responds to divine guidance and implements it in their daily life.
orig: هذا ذكر وإن للمتقين لحسن مآب

translation: Gardens of Eden, whose gates will be opened for them
interpretation: This verse describes the eternal reward of the righteous in Paradise, emphasizing the welcoming and accessible nature of Heaven. The open gates symbolize unconditional acceptance and honor, suggesting that the inhabitants will have complete freedom of movement and unrestricted access to all of Paradise's pleasures, unlike earthly gardens which may have restricted access or closed gates.
orig: جنات عدن مفتحة لهم الأبواب

translation: Reclining therein, calling for abundant fruit and drink
interpretation: This verse paints a picture of complete contentment and luxury in Paradise, where believers can request whatever fruits and drinks they desire while resting in complete comfort. The use of "reclining" suggests a state of ease and honor, as this was traditionally a position of dignity. The ability to call for whatever they wish indicates that Paradise's inhabitants will have their desires instantly fulfilled without effort, highlighting the contrast with worldly life where one must work for sustenance.
orig: متكئين فيها يدعون فيها بفاكهة كثيرة وشراب

translation: And with them will be women of modest gaze, of equal age
interpretation: This verse describes one of the rewards in Paradise, emphasizing the concept of perfect companionship where spouses are matched in spiritual and physical maturity, creating harmonious relationships based on mutual respect and devotion rather than superficial attraction. The modesty mentioned reflects spiritual purity and moral excellence.
orig: وعندهم قاصرات الطرف أتراب

translation: "This is what you are promised for the Day of Account."
interpretation: "This verse emphasizes the certainty of divine accountability, reminding believers that every promise of reward or consequence mentioned in scripture will materialize on the Day of Judgment. It serves as both a warning to the heedless and a reassurance to the righteous that their deeds are being recorded and will be justly evaluated."
orig: هذا ما توعدون ليوم الحساب

translation: Indeed, this is Our provision; it will never cease
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite generosity and the eternal nature of His rewards, particularly in reference to Paradise. It conveys a message of reassurance that divine blessings, once granted, are permanent and inexhaustible, contrasting with the temporary nature of worldly provisions.
orig: إن هذا لرزقنا ما له من نفاد

translation: Indeed, for the transgressors is an evil place of return
interpretation: This verse emphasizes divine justice and accountability, indicating that those who exceed bounds in wrongdoing and rebel against moral and divine laws will face severe consequences in the afterlife. The use of "ma'ab" (place of return) suggests a permanent destination, implying that the outcome of transgression is not temporary but an eternal state of difficulty and punishment.
orig: هذا وإن للطاغين لشر مآب

translation: They will burn in Hell - what a wretched resting place!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of rejecting divine guidance, suggesting that those who consciously choose evil over good create their own spiritual prison. The use of "resting place" (mihad) ironically contrasts with its usual connotation of comfort, highlighting how one's choices can transform what could have been paradise into a self-imposed torment.
orig: جهنم يصلونها فبئس المهاد

translation: This is what they taste: scalding water and pus
interpretation: This verse illustrates the severe consequences of rejecting divine guidance, where those who denied truth will experience intense suffering. The mention of "hamim" (scalding water) and "ghassaq" (pus) symbolizes both physical and spiritual torment, representing the ultimate outcome of one's conscious choice to reject righteousness in worldly life.
orig: هذا فليذوقوه حميم وغساق

translation: And other (torments) of similar nature, in pairs
interpretation: This verse hints at the comprehensive nature of divine punishment, suggesting that afflictions come in complementary forms - both physical and spiritual, internal and external, immediate and lasting - emphasizing the complete justice in divine retribution for those who transgress
orig: وآخر من شكله أزواج

translation: This is a company bursting in with you. No welcome for them. They will indeed burn in the Fire.
interpretation: This verse portrays the scene of mutual blame and hostility between the dwellers of Hell, where one group of sinners rejects association with their followers who led them astray in worldly life. The denial of welcome reflects the dissolution of all worldly bonds and relationships in the afterlife, where each soul bears responsibility for its own choices.
orig: هذا فوج مقتحم معكم لا مرحبا بهم إنهم صالو النار

translation: They will say, "No, it is you who have no welcome. You brought this upon us, so wretched is the settlement."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the bitter exchanges between the followers and their misguiding leaders in Hell, highlighting how blame and resentment manifest in the afterlife. The followers' hostile response reflects their realization that their blind adherence to corrupt leadership led to their damnation, emphasizing the importance of personal responsibility in choosing whom to follow in matters of faith and morality.
orig: قالوا بل أنتم لا مرحبا بكم أنتم قدمتموه لنا فبئس القرار

translation: They will say, "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase them in double punishment in the Fire."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the intense regret and anger felt by the followers towards their misguiding leaders on the Day of Judgment. It reveals how those who were led astray will seek divine justice, requesting that their misleaders receive an amplified punishment for causing their downfall. This demonstrates how the bonds between the misguided and their leaders will transform from loyalty in worldly life to resentment and hostility in the hereafter.
orig: قالوا ربنا من قدم لنا هذا فزده عذابا ضعفا في النار

translation: And they will say, "What is wrong with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the worst?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the confusion and regret of the disbelievers in Hell when they notice the absence of people they once mocked and considered evil. It particularly points to their realization that those they deemed worthless or misguided in worldly life - likely the believers and righteous people - have actually attained salvation and are not with them in Hell, forcing them to confront their grave error in judgment and highlighting how worldly standards of status and worth differ greatly from divine judgment.
orig: وقالوا ما لنا لا نرى رجالا كنا نعدهم من الأشرار

translation: Did we take them in mockery, or have eyes swerved away from them?
interpretation: This verse reflects on human arrogance and misjudgment, highlighting how people often dismiss or mock those they consider beneath them, only to later realize their error in judgment. The question posed serves as a reminder that what we perceive as insignificant or worthy of derision may actually hold great value in divine sight.
orig: أتخذناهم سخريا أم زاغت عنهم الأبصار

translation: Indeed, that is the truth: the quarreling of the people of the Fire
interpretation: This verse reveals the eternal nature of human accountability, showing that even in Hell, people will continue their worldly traits of blame and dispute. The inhabitants will engage in bitter arguments, each trying to hold others responsible for their mutual misfortune, reflecting how denial and refusal to accept responsibility persist even in the afterlife.
orig: إن ذلك لحق تخاصم أهل النار

translation: Say, "I am only a warner, and there is no deity except Allah, the One, the Prevailing."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophet's role as a messenger whose primary duty is to warn humanity about the consequences of their actions, while simultaneously affirming the absolute oneness of Allah's sovereignty. The use of "Qahhar" (Prevailing) alongside "Wahid" (One) suggests that not only is Allah unique in His essence, but He also holds complete and irresistible power over all creation, leaving no room for other deities or powers to share in His authority.
orig: قل إنما أنا منذر وما من إله إلا الله الواحد القهار

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty over all creation, highlighting His dual nature of supreme power and infinite mercy. While He possesses unmatched might that commands the entire universe, He simultaneously maintains an open door of forgiveness for His creation, showing that ultimate power can coexist with boundless compassion.
orig: رب السماوات والأرض وما بينهما العزيز الغفار

translation: Say, "It is a great message"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound significance of the Qur'anic message, indicating that its importance transcends ordinary human concerns and contains universal truths that deserve serious attention and contemplation. The use of "great" suggests that this message has the power to transform lives and societies when properly understood and implemented.
orig: قل هو نبأ عظيم

translation: Yet you are turning away from it
interpretation: This verse highlights humanity's tendency to ignore or reject divine guidance despite its clarity and importance. It points to the paradox of people having access to truth and wisdom, yet consciously choosing to disregard it, suggesting a deep spiritual negligence that stems from either pride, worldly distractions, or willful ignorance.
orig: أنتم عنه معرضون

translation: I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly [of angels] when they were disputing
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature of revelation, showing that Prophet Muhammad's knowledge of heavenly matters could only have come through divine inspiration, not through personal experience or learning. It specifically refers to his receiving information about the angels' discussion regarding Adam's creation, which he couldn't have known about except through divine revelation, thus authenticating his prophethood and the divine source of his message.
orig: ما كان لي من علم بالملإ الأعلى إذ يختصمون

translation: It is revealed to me that I am only a clear warner
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's primary role as a messenger whose main duty is to deliver divine warnings with clarity and sincerity, without any pretense of possessing supernatural powers or divine attributes. It underscores the humility required in spiritual leadership and the importance of clear communication in religious guidance.
orig: إن يوحى إلي إلا أنما أنا نذير مبين

translation: When your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay"
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's divine plan to establish human beings as His representatives on Earth, marking a significant moment in creation. The use of clay symbolizes humankind's connection to Earth and their humble origins, while Allah's direct announcement to the angels emphasizes the special status and purpose intended for humans in the divine scheme.
orig: إذ قال ربك للملائكة إني خالق بشرا من طين

translation: And when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down before him prostrating
interpretation: This verse illustrates the unique honor bestowed upon humans by Allah, marking the moment when the physical form of Adam was elevated by the divine breath. The command for prostration signifies humanity's special status among creation, as even angels were ordered to acknowledge this distinction. The "spirit" mentioned here represents the divine qualities imbued within humans, including consciousness, free will, and moral understanding, making them capable of serving as Allah's representatives on Earth.
orig: فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي فقعوا له ساجدين

translation: So the angels prostrated - all of them entirely
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute obedience and humility of angels to Allah's commands, demonstrating that even these mighty celestial beings submit without hesitation or pride, setting an example of perfect servitude and compliance with divine will
orig: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون

translation: Except for Iblis (Satan); he was arrogant and became one of the disbelievers
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound danger of arrogance, as it was the first sin that led to eternal damnation. Iblis's refusal to bow to Adam wasn't merely disobedience, but stemmed from a deep-seated pride that made him believe he was superior to God's command. His arrogance transformed him from a being of high status to one of the disbelievers, demonstrating how spiritual destruction often begins with the sin of pride.
orig: إلا إبليس استكبر وكان من الكافرين

translation: He (Allah) said: "O Iblis! What prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My Own Hands? Were you arrogant, or were you already among the haughty ones?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the direct confrontation between Allah and Iblis (Satan), emphasizing the severity of Iblis's disobedience. The mention of Allah creating Adam with "His Own Hands" signifies a special honor bestowed upon Adam, making Iblis's refusal to prostrate even more egregious. The question posed is rhetorical, exposing Iblis's fundamental flaw of pride and suggesting that his arrogance was a conscious choice rather than an inherent quality, marking the moment when pride first corrupted a creation of Allah.
orig: قال يا إبليس ما منعك أن تسجد لما خلقت بيدي أستكبرت أم كنت من العالين

translation: He (Iblis) said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."
interpretation: This verse reveals the dangerous nature of arrogance and false superiority, as demonstrated by Iblis's response to Allah. His claim of superiority based on his physical composition shows how pride can blind one from recognizing true virtue and divine wisdom, leading to spiritual downfall and disobedience to Allah's commands.
orig: قال أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين

translation: He (Allah) said: "Then get out from here, for you are rejected (outcast)"
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine justice and the consequence of arrogance. When Iblis (Satan) refused to bow to Adam out of pride, Allah expelled him from his position of honor in the heavens, marking him as permanently cursed. This divine banishment serves as a reminder that defiance against Allah's commands due to arrogance leads to spiritual downfall and eternal disgrace.
orig: قال فاخرج منها فإنك رجيم

translation: "And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Judgment"
interpretation: "This verse reflects Allah's absolute rejection of evil and disobedience, specifically directed at Satan after his refusal to bow to Adam. The permanence of the curse until the Day of Judgment demonstrates that unrepentant defiance against divine commands leads to eternal spiritual alienation from Allah's mercy."
orig: وإن عليك لعنتي إلى يوم الدين

translation: He said: "My Lord, then grant me respite until the Day they are resurrected"
interpretation: This verse reveals Satan's cunning nature and long-term strategy, as he seeks not immediate revenge but rather a prolonged opportunity to misguide humanity. By requesting to live until the Day of Resurrection, he demonstrates his determination to prove his assumption that humans are unworthy of God's favor, showing his pride and refusal to accept his own error in disobeying Allah's command.
orig: قال رب فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون

translation: Allah said: "Indeed, you are of those given respite"
interpretation: This verse reflects Allah's response to Iblis (Satan) after his request for postponement until the Day of Resurrection. It demonstrates divine wisdom in allowing evil to exist as a test for humanity, while also highlighting that even Satan's apparent freedom to mislead is ultimately bound by Allah's permission and predetermined limits.
orig: قال فإنك من المنظرين

translation: Until the Day of the appointed time
interpretation: This verse speaks to Allah's complete control over time and destiny, indicating that everything has a predetermined endpoint known only to Him. It reminds us that all matters, whether concerning individual lives or cosmic events, unfold according to Allah's precise schedule, not a moment early or late.
orig: إلى يوم الوقت المعلوم

translation: He said: "Then by Your might, I will surely mislead them all"
interpretation: This verse reveals Satan's arrogant defiance and his sworn mission to lead humanity astray, demonstrating how he uses Allah's own power (by swearing by it) to declare his rebellious intentions, highlighting the ongoing spiritual battle between good and evil in human existence
orig: قال فبعزتك لأغوينهم أجمعين

translation: Except Your chosen servants among them
interpretation: This verse speaks to the profound concept of divine protection and spiritual immunity. The "chosen servants" refers to those who have achieved a state of complete sincerity and devotion to God, making them impervious to evil influences and temptations. Their hearts and minds are so purely focused on divine truth that they remain untouched by corruption and misguidance.
orig: إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين

translation: He said: "The Truth (I say), and the Truth I speak"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute nature of divine truth and sincerity. When Allah makes a statement, it is not just truthful in its immediate context, but represents an eternal, unchangeable truth that transcends time and circumstance. The repetition of "truth" serves to reinforce that both the essence and the expression are purely truthful, without any trace of falsehood or ambiguity.
orig: قال فالحق والحق أقول

translation: I will surely fill Hell with you and those who follow you from among them all together
interpretation: This verse conveys Allah's stern warning to Iblis (Satan) and his followers, emphasizing the absolute justice and consequence of rebellion against divine guidance. It illustrates that choosing to follow Satan's path is a conscious decision that leads to a predetermined fate, highlighting personal accountability in spiritual choices.
orig: لأملأن جهنم منك وممن تبعك منهم أجمعين

translation: Say, "I do not ask you for any payment for this [message], nor am I one of the pretenders."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sincerity and authenticity of the Prophet's mission. By declaring that he seeks no worldly compensation for delivering Allah's message, it demonstrates that his motivation is purely spiritual and divinely guided, not driven by material gain or self-interest. The rejection of being among "the pretenders" further reinforces his genuine commitment to truth and authenticity in conveying divine guidance.
orig: قل ما أسألكم عليه من أجر وما أنا من المتكلفين

translation: It is nothing but a reminder for all the worlds
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal nature of the Qur'an's message, indicating that divine guidance isn't restricted to a specific group or time period but serves as a source of enlightenment and reflection for all creation across time and space
orig: إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين

translation: And you will surely know its message after a time
interpretation: This verse conveys Allah's promise that truth will eventually become manifest, even if not immediately apparent. It suggests that divine wisdom often unfolds gradually, teaching us patience and trust in Allah's timing. The delayed revelation of consequences serves as both a test of faith and a demonstration of Allah's perfect planning.
orig: ولتعلمن نبأه بعد حين

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine knowledge comes exclusively from Allah's authority, highlighting that true wisdom and guidance can only originate from a source that combines absolute power with perfect wisdom. The mention of Allah's attributes "Al-Aziz" (Mighty) and "Al-Hakeem" (Wise) suggests that the Qur'an's teachings are both authoritative and purposeful, designed with divine wisdom for humanity's benefit.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound connection between divine knowledge and sincere worship, indicating that once a person receives authentic guidance from Allah, the natural response should be pure, undiluted devotion. The command for sincerity suggests that worship should be free from any form of showing off, worldly gains, or divided loyalties, focusing solely on pleasing Allah without any intermediaries or partners in worship.
orig: إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق فاعبد الله مخلصا له الدين

translation: Unquestionably, to Allah belongs the pure religion. And those who take protectors besides Him [say], "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position." Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide he who is a liar and [confirmed] disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of intermediaries in worship by addressing a common justification used by polytheists throughout history. It critiques the practice of seeking intermediaries between humans and God, showing that such practices stem from a fundamental misunderstanding of God's direct relationship with His creation. The verse suggests that true faith must be pure and direct, without the need for intercessors or intermediaries, as these only serve to dilute the essential connection between the worshipper and the Divine.
orig: ألا لله الدين الخالص والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى إن الله يحكم بينهم في ما هم فيه يختلفون إن الله لا يهدي من هو كاذب كفار

translation: If Allah had intended to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Exalted is He! He is Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute self-sufficiency and uniqueness by explaining that the concept of having a son is incompatible with His divine nature. If He had wanted offspring, He wouldn't have needed to beget in the human sense but could have simply chosen any of His creations. The fact that He hasn't done so reinforces that He is above such needs, standing alone in His perfect unity and complete authority.
orig: لو أراد الله أن يتخذ ولدا لاصطفى مما يخلق ما يشاء سبحانه هو الله الواحد القهار

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's absolute power over the cosmic system, using the metaphor of "wrapping" to describe the fluid transition between day and night, much like wrapping a turban. The imagery emphasizes the precision and perfection of Allah's natural laws, where celestial bodies follow their ordained paths without deviation. It demonstrates how the universe operates under divine control while simultaneously highlighting Allah's seemingly paradoxical attributes of might and forgiveness - showing He is both powerful enough to control the cosmos yet merciful enough to forgive His creation.
orig: خلق السماوات والأرض بالحق يكور الليل على النهار ويكور النهار على الليل وسخر الشمس والقمر كل يجري لأجل مسمى ألا هو العزيز الغفار

translation: He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate, and sent down for you eight pairs of livestock. He creates you in your mothers' wombs, creation after creation, in three layers of darkness. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound unity of human origin and Allah's intricate design in creation. By mentioning that all humans come from a single soul, it points to our fundamental equality and interconnectedness. The reference to the "three darknesses" (the abdominal wall, uterus, and amniotic membrane) demonstrates Allah's knowledge of embryology long before scientific discoveries, serving as a sign of divine wisdom. This systematic progression from human creation to animal provision to fetal development builds up to establish Allah's absolute authority and uniqueness, challenging those who would turn away from such clear evidence of His existence and power.
orig: خلقكم من نفس واحدة ثم جعل منها زوجها وأنزل لكم من الأنعام ثمانية أزواج يخلقكم في بطون أمهاتكم خلقا من بعد خلق في ظلمات ثلاث ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك لا إله إلا هو فأنى تصرفون

translation: If you disbelieve, then Allah is free from need of you. And He does not approve of disbelief for His servants. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the complete independence of Allah from His creation while highlighting the personal nature of faith and accountability. It teaches that Allah's perfection and self-sufficiency mean He doesn't need our worship, yet He desires what's best for us by preferring our gratitude over disbelief. The mention that no soul bears another's burden establishes the fundamental principle of individual responsibility in faith and actions, rejecting the concept of vicarious atonement or inherited sin.
orig: إن تكفروا فإن الله غني عنكم ولا يرضى لعباده الكفر وإن تشكروا يرضه لكم ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى ثم إلى ربكم مرجعكم فينبئكم بما كنتم تعملون إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And when adversity touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him [alone]; then when He bestows on him a favor from Himself, he forgets Him whom he called upon before, and he sets up rivals to Allah to mislead [others] from His way. Say, "Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire."
interpretation: This verse reveals a fundamental aspect of human psychology and spiritual weakness, where people tend to be sincere in their devotion only during times of hardship. When comfort and ease return, they often forget their moments of desperation and divine dependence, reverting to ingratitude and polytheistic behavior. The verse serves as a warning about the temporary nature of worldly comfort and the severe consequences of such spiritual inconsistency.
orig: وإذا مس الإنسان ضر دعا ربه منيبا إليه ثم إذا خوله نعمة منه نسي ما كان يدعو إليه من قبل وجعل لله أندادا ليضل عن سبيله قل تمتع بكفرك قليلا إنك من أصحاب النار

translation: Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who does not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only they will remember [who are] people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual and intellectual distinction between those who possess knowledge and understanding versus those who don't. The imagery of night worship symbolizes sincere devotion and self-discipline, suggesting that true knowledge is intimately connected with spiritual consciousness and moral awareness. The rhetorical question about equality between the knowledgeable and ignorant implies that genuine knowledge leads to God-consciousness and ethical behavior, making the learned fundamentally different from the unlearned in their approach to life and their understanding of ultimate reality.
orig: أمن هو قانت آناء الليل ساجدا وقائما يحذر الآخرة ويرجو رحمة ربه قل هل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون إنما يتذكر أولو الألباب

translation: Say, "O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world is good, and the earth of Allah is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without measure."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound relationship between faith, righteousness, and divine reward, highlighting that those who maintain their faith and persevere through hardships, even if it means leaving their homeland for Allah's sake, will receive unlimited rewards. The mention of Allah's "spacious earth" suggests that believers should not feel constrained to remain in situations that compromise their faith, as opportunities for practicing their religion can be found elsewhere.
orig: قل يا عباد الذين آمنوا اتقوا ربكم للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنة وأرض الله واسعة إنما يوفى الصابرون أجرهم بغير حساب

translation: Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion"
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of pure monotheism, highlighting that true worship must be dedicated solely to Allah without any intermediaries or partners. The command for sincerity (ikhlas) in worship indicates that our actions should be free from showing off, worldly gains, or any form of polytheistic intentions. This purification of intention is essential for the acceptance of worship and represents the core of spiritual authenticity in Islam.
orig: قل إني أمرت أن أعبد الله مخلصا له الدين

translation: And I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit (to Allah)
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of spiritual leadership through example. The speaker is demonstrating complete readiness to be at the forefront of submission to Allah's will, setting a precedent for others to follow. It reflects the importance of not just believing, but being willing to be the pioneer in demonstrating that belief through action and complete surrender to divine guidance.
orig: وأمرت لأن أكون أول المسلمين

translation: Say: "Indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability and the profound consciousness of divine consequences. It reflects the understanding that even the most righteous individuals must maintain a healthy fear of divine justice, recognizing that disobedience to Allah's commands carries serious implications. The mention of a "tremendous day" points to the gravity of the Day of Judgment, suggesting that our present actions have eternal consequences.
orig: قل إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم

translation: Say, "It is Allah I worship, being sincere to Him in my religion"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of pure monotheism and sincerity in worship. It teaches that true worship requires dedicating one's religious devotion exclusively to Allah, free from any form of showing off, polytheism, or ulterior motives. The command to "say" makes this a public declaration of faith, demonstrating that one should be unashamed and clear about their devotion to Allah alone.
orig: قل الله أعبد مخلصا له ديني

translation: So worship whatever you wish besides Him. Say, "Indeed, the losers are those who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Behold! That is the manifest loss."
interpretation: This verse employs divine irony to highlight the futility of idol worship, suggesting that those who choose to worship false deities are only harming themselves. The true tragedy lies not just in personal loss but in leading one's family astray, resulting in eternal separation from loved ones in the afterlife. The emphasis on "manifest loss" indicates that this spiritual bankruptcy is not hidden but will be evident and undeniable on the Day of Judgment.
orig: فاعبدوا ما شئتم من دونه قل إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ألا ذلك هو الخسران المبين

translation: They shall have layers of fire above them and layers below them. With this Allah warns His servants: "O My servants! Fear Me!"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound consequence of rejecting divine guidance, depicting a complete encompassment by punishment that leaves no escape route. The use of "layers" (ظلل) suggests a comprehensive and inescapable nature of divine justice, while the direct address to servants highlights Allah's mercy in warning humanity before such consequences manifest. The call to fear (فاتقون) is not about terror but rather a loving warning to develop consciousness and mindfulness of divine presence in one's life.
orig: لهم من فوقهم ظلل من النار ومن تحتهم ظلل ذلك يخوف الله به عباده يا عباد فاتقون

translation: And those who avoid false deities, refusing to worship them, and turn back to Allah - for them are good tidings. So give good tidings to My servants
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound spiritual reward that awaits those who consciously reject all forms of false worship and materialistic devotion in favor of sincere devotion to Allah alone. It suggests that the act of turning away from worldly temptations and false ideologies requires both courage and wisdom, and such commitment is met with divine recognition and glad tidings of success in both worlds.
orig: والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها وأنابوا إلى الله لهم البشرى فبشر عباد

translation: Those who listen to the Word and follow the best of it. Those are the ones Allah has guided, and those are people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of critical thinking and discernment in faith. It praises those who don't blindly accept everything they hear, but rather thoughtfully evaluate different viewpoints and consciously choose to follow what is most beneficial and truthful. These individuals are considered truly wise because they exercise their intellectual faculties in their spiritual journey, showing that Islam encourages active engagement with knowledge rather than passive acceptance.
orig: الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه أولئك الذين هداهم الله وأولئك هم أولو الألباب

translation: Then is one who has deserved the sentence of punishment [to be guided]? Then, can you save one who is in the Fire?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limitations of human agency in spiritual guidance, suggesting that even the Prophet Muhammad cannot force salvation upon those who have actively chosen disbelief. It reflects the divine principle that ultimate guidance and redemption rest with Allah, while highlighting the futility of becoming overly distressed about those who persistently reject faith despite clear signs and warnings.
orig: أفمن حق عليه كلمة العذاب أفأنت تنقذ من في النار

translation: But those who fear their Lord - for them will be mansions, above them mansions built high, beneath which rivers flow - the promise of Allah. Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of divine justice and reward, emphasizing that those who maintain God-consciousness (taqwa) through their lives will receive multiple levels of elevation in Paradise. The mention of "mansions above mansions" suggests an infinite vertical progression of rewards, symbolizing both the physical and spiritual heights achievable through piety. The flowing rivers represent perpetual sustenance and life, while the emphasis on Allah's unfailing promise serves to provide absolute certainty and comfort to the believers in their pursuit of righteousness.
orig: لكن الذين اتقوا ربهم لهم غرف من فوقها غرف مبنية تجري من تحتها الأنهار وعد الله لا يخلف الله الميعاد

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth; then He brings forth with it crops of different colors; then they wither and you see them turn yellow; then He makes them [scattered] debris? Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the cyclical nature of life and serves as a metaphor for human existence. Just as plants go through stages of growth, vitality, decline, and death, so too does human life follow a similar pattern. The different colors of crops represent the diversity of human achievements and experiences, while their eventual withering reminds us of the temporary nature of worldly success and material prosperity. This natural cycle is meant to prompt those with deep understanding to reflect on their own mortality and the futility of becoming too attached to worldly matters.
orig: ألم تر أن الله أنزل من السماء ماء فسلكه ينابيع في الأرض ثم يخرج به زرعا مختلفا ألوانه ثم يهيج فتراه مصفرا ثم يجعله حطاما إن في ذلك لذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: Is one whose breast Allah has expanded to [accept] Islam and he is upon a light from his Lord [like one whose heart rejects it]? Then woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in clear error.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound contrast between those who have been blessed with spiritual enlightenment and those who resist divine guidance. When Allah opens one's heart to Islam, it creates an internal illumination that brings clarity, peace, and understanding. This spiritual awakening is compared to being guided by a divine light, suggesting that true faith transforms one's entire perspective on life. The verse warns those who maintain hardened hearts against divine remembrance, indicating that spiritual resistance leads to a self-imposed darkness and separation from divine truth.
orig: أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله أولئك في ضلال مبين

translation: Allah has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book wherein is reiteration. The skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts relax at the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills. And one whom Allah leaves astray - for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound psychological and spiritual impact of the Qur'an on sincere believers. The physical reaction described - the shivering of skin followed by relaxation - represents the transformative journey from fear to peace that occurs when one truly engages with divine revelation. Like a medicine that first causes discomfort before bringing healing, the Qur'an initially confronts people with challenging truths that may unsettle them, but ultimately leads to spiritual tranquility and enlightenment for those who are open to guidance.
orig: الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا متشابها مثاني تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله ذلك هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: Is one who shields himself with his face from the worst of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one secure from it]? And it will be said to the wrongdoers, "Taste what you used to earn."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stark contrast between attempting self-protection and true divine protection, suggesting that those who rejected faith will be so desperate on the Day of Judgment that they'll try to shield themselves with their faces - the most vulnerable part of the body - highlighting the futility of their attempts at self-preservation when facing divine justice. The command to "taste" their deeds implies that consequences are the natural outcome of one's choices, not arbitrary punishment.
orig: أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة وقيل للظالمين ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون

translation: Those before them denied, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning about the pattern of historical consequences, illustrating how past civilizations that rejected truth faced unexpected divine retribution. The suddenness of punishment highlights how human beings often remain oblivious to approaching consequences of their actions, living in a false sense of security until divine judgment manifests in ways they never anticipated.
orig: كذب الذين من قبلهم فأتاهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون

translation: So Allah made them taste humiliation in the worldly life, but the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine principle that rejection of truth and persistence in wrongdoing leads to two levels of consequences: immediate repercussions in this life through disgrace and failure, and a far more severe punishment in the afterlife. The use of the word "taste" suggests that the worldly humiliation is but a small sample of what awaits in the hereafter, serving as a warning and wake-up call for those who might still reflect and change their ways.
orig: فأذاقهم الله الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون

translation: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example that they might remember
interpretation: Allah emphasizes the comprehensive nature of His divine teaching methodology, using diverse parables and examples to make complex spiritual and moral truths accessible to all levels of human understanding. This pedagogical approach reflects Allah's wisdom in knowing that humans learn best through relatable examples, helping them internalize and remember the Qur'an's guidance more effectively.
orig: ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل لعلهم يتذكرون

translation: An Arabic Quran, without any crookedness, that they may become righteous
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfection and clarity of the Qur'an's message, highlighting that its revelation in Arabic is deliberate and purposeful. The absence of 'crookedness' indicates that the divine message is straightforward, free from contradictions, and perfectly aligned with human nature and understanding. The ultimate purpose of this clear, unambiguous revelation is to guide people toward righteousness and God-consciousness.
orig: قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج لعلهم يتقون

translation: Allah presents an example: a man owned by quarreling partners and another belonging exclusively to one man - are they equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah! But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stark contrast between monotheism and polytheism through a powerful metaphor. It compares a person torn between multiple conflicting masters to someone devoted to a single master, highlighting how serving multiple deities leads to inner conflict and confusion, while dedication to the One True God brings clarity and peace. The metaphor demonstrates the logical superiority of monotheism over polytheism, as a unified direction in life is more conducive to spiritual and psychological well-being than trying to please multiple competing authorities.
orig: ضرب الله مثلا رجلا فيه شركاء متشاكسون ورجلا سلما لرجل هل يستويان مثلا الحمد لله بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of the universal truth of mortality, emphasizing that even the Prophet Muhammad, despite his exalted status, and all humanity share the same inevitable fate. It establishes the temporary nature of earthly existence and helps maintain humility by highlighting that death is the great equalizer, making no distinction between prophet and follower, ruler and subject.
orig: إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون

translation: Then, on the Day of Resurrection, you will dispute before your Lord
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate accountability that awaits all people, where they will engage in disputes and arguments to justify their worldly actions and beliefs. It suggests that the differences and conflicts that exist between people in this world will finally be resolved by Allah's perfect judgment, emphasizing the importance of maintaining righteousness and truth in this life rather than engaging in futile disputes.
orig: ثم إنكم يوم القيامة عند ربكم تختصمون

translation: Then who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him? Is not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe spiritual and moral corruption of those who commit two grave offenses: fabricating falsehoods about Allah and rejecting divine truth when it's presented to them. The rhetorical question suggests that these individuals represent the height of injustice, as they not only mislead others with their lies about God but also obstinately refuse to accept truth when confronted with it. The mention of Hell as their dwelling place indicates that deliberately distorting religious truth and rejecting divine guidance are among the most serious spiritual crimes one can commit.
orig: فمن أظلم ممن كذب على الله وكذب بالصدق إذ جاءه أليس في جهنم مثوى للكافرين

translation: And he who brings the truth and he who confirms it - those are the righteous
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of moral excellence - both being truthful oneself and supporting truth when others present it. It suggests that true righteousness isn't just about personal integrity but also about recognizing and affirming truth when others speak it, creating a community of mutual support for what is right and true.
orig: والذي جاء بالصدق وصدق به أولئك هم المتقون

translation: They shall have whatever they wish for with their Lord. Such is the reward of the good-doers
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless generosity of Allah towards those who excel in their faith and actions. The concept of having "whatever they wish" suggests that the rewards in Paradise are not predetermined or limited, but rather tailored to each individual's deepest desires. The term "muhsineen" (good-doers) implies that this reward is specifically for those who reached the highest level of worship - doing good as if they see Allah, and if they don't see Him, knowing that He sees them.
orig: لهم ما يشاءون عند ربهم ذلك جزاء المحسنين

translation: So that Allah may remove from them the worst of what they did and reward them according to the best of what they used to do
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's infinite mercy and justice, showing that He not only forgives the gravest sins of the faithful but also elevates their status by rewarding them based on their best deeds rather than their average or worst actions. It's a manifestation of divine generosity where Allah chooses to overlook our shortcomings and instead focuses on our moments of excellence.
orig: ليكفر الله عنهم أسوأ الذي عملوا ويجزيهم أجرهم بأحسن الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: Is Allah not sufficient for His servant? Yet they threaten you with those besides Him. And whoever Allah leaves astray - for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes absolute trust in Allah's protection and sufficiency. It addresses a profound spiritual truth that when one relies completely on Allah, there is no need to fear any other power or threat. The verse was revealed when the polytheists tried to frighten Prophet Muhammad with their idols and deities, showing that manufactured fears and threats are meaningless against divine protection. It also establishes Allah's ultimate authority over guidance, indicating that true guidance comes only through His will.
orig: أليس الله بكاف عبده ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: And whoever Allah guides, there is none who can lead him astray. Is not Allah Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute authority and power over guidance. When Allah chooses to guide someone to the truth, no force in existence can divert them from that path. The rhetorical question at the end reinforces Allah's supreme might and justice, suggesting that His guidance is based on wisdom and that He has the power to deal with those who reject His guidance.
orig: ومن يهد الله فما له من مضل أليس الله بعزيز ذي انتقام

translation: And if you asked them who created the heavens and earth, they would surely say 'Allah.' Say, 'Then have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended me harm, are they removers of His harm; or if He intended me mercy, are they withholders of His mercy?' Say, 'Sufficient for me is Allah; upon Him rely the reliant.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent contradiction in the behavior of polytheists who acknowledge Allah's supreme power as the Creator yet turn to lesser deities for help. It demonstrates the futility of seeking protection or blessings from anything other than Allah, as no force in existence can override His will or alter His decree. The verse concludes by affirming that complete trust in Allah alone is the wisest course, as He is sufficient for all needs and is the only true source of help and protection.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن الله قل أفرأيتم ما تدعون من دون الله إن أرادني الله بضر هل هن كاشفات ضره أو أرادني برحمة هل هن ممسكات رحمته قل حسبي الله عليه يتوكل المتوكلون

translation: Say, "O my people, work according to your position; I am working. You will soon know"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability and divine justice, suggesting that everyone should proceed with their chosen path while being mindful that ultimate consequences will reveal the truth. It carries a subtle warning that those who reject faith and continue in their ways will eventually face the results of their choices, while the believers who remain steadfast will be vindicated.
orig: قل يا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم إني عامل فسوف تعلمون

translation: Who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him and upon whom will descend an everlasting punishment
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal consequences of rejecting divine guidance, suggesting that those who persist in wrongdoing face not only the immediate shame of punishment but also its permanent nature, reflecting the Islamic concept that actions in this life have lasting implications in the hereafter
orig: من يأتيه عذاب يخزيه ويحل عليه عذاب مقيم

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book for mankind in truth. So whoever is guided - it is for [the benefit of] his soul; and whoever goes astray only goes astray to its detriment. And you are not a guardian over them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of individual responsibility and free will in matters of faith. Allah has provided guidance through divine revelation, but the choice to accept or reject it lies with each person. The Prophet's role is solely to convey the message, not to force people to believe, highlighting that spiritual coercion is incompatible with Islamic teachings.
orig: إنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب للناس بالحق فمن اهتدى فلنفسه ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die [He takes] during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others for a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse reveals the profound connection between sleep and death, teaching us that sleep is a daily reminder of our mortality. When we sleep, our souls temporarily depart from our bodies, similar to what happens at death, but are returned unless Allah decrees otherwise. This temporary separation serves as a metaphor for the final departure of the soul, helping us understand the transient nature of life and encouraging reflection on our ultimate destiny.
orig: الله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها والتي لم تمت في منامها فيمسك التي قضى عليها الموت ويرسل الأخرى إلى أجل مسمى إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يتفكرون

translation: Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah? Say, "[What] even though they do not possess anything, nor do they reason?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the practice of idol worship and seeking intermediaries other than Allah by highlighting the illogical nature of such beliefs. It emphasizes that these false deities are inherently powerless and lack even basic consciousness or intelligence, making it absurd to expect them to intercede or provide any benefit to their worshippers. The verse serves as a rational argument against polytheism by pointing out that one cannot logically seek help from entities that are themselves devoid of power and understanding.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دون الله شفعاء قل أولو كانوا لا يملكون شيئا ولا يعقلون

translation: Say, "To Allah belongs all intercession. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute authority over intercession, highlighting that no one can intercede without His permission, which dismantles the pagan belief in intermediaries. The mention of His dominion over the heavens and earth reinforces His complete sovereignty, while the final return to Him reminds us that all power structures and hierarchies are temporary, as everyone will ultimately be accountable to Allah alone.
orig: قل لله الشفاعة جميعا له ملك السماوات والأرض ثم إليه ترجعون

translation: And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink with aversion, but when those [worshipped] besides Him are mentioned, immediately they rejoice
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound psychological insight into the nature of disbelief, showing how those who reject faith have an inherent resistance to divine unity. Their adverse reaction to monotheism and joy at the mention of false deities indicates a deep-seated preference for beliefs that allow them to maintain their worldly attachments and desires without absolute divine accountability.
orig: وإذا ذكر الله وحده اشمأزت قلوب الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة وإذا ذكر الذين من دونه إذا هم يستبشرون

translation: Say, "O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's ultimate authority as the supreme judge who will resolve all human disagreements and disputes on the Day of Judgment. It acknowledges that while humans may have different interpretations, beliefs, and viewpoints in this world, Allah's perfect knowledge of both the visible and invisible realms qualifies Him alone to make final judgments about truth and falsehood. This serves as a reminder to maintain humility in our convictions and to ultimately trust in divine wisdom rather than becoming overly dogmatic in our positions.
orig: قل اللهم فاطر السماوات والأرض عالم الغيب والشهادة أنت تحكم بين عبادك في ما كانوا فيه يختلفون

translation: And if those who did wrong had all that is in the earth and the like of it with it, they would surely offer it as ransom to save themselves from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allah what they had not taken into account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute futility of worldly wealth and power in the face of divine justice. It illustrates that on the Day of Judgment, when people fully realize the consequences of their wrongdoings, they would be willing to give up everything they own - even if they possessed the entire world's wealth twice over - to escape punishment. However, no amount of material wealth can serve as a substitute for righteousness and good deeds in the afterlife. The verse particularly highlights the element of surprise, as people will encounter aspects of divine judgment they never anticipated during their worldly lives, underscoring the limited nature of human foresight regarding the ultimate consequences of their actions.
orig: ولو أن للذين ظلموا ما في الأرض جميعا ومثله معه لافتدوا به من سوء العذاب يوم القيامة وبدا لهم من الله ما لم يكونوا يحتسبون

translation: And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned, and they will be surrounded by what they used to mock
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine justice and the principle of accountability, showing how people who dismissed or mocked divine warnings will ultimately face the consequences of their actions. Their deeds' true nature will become undeniably clear to them, and the very matters they treated with derision will become their inescapable reality.
orig: وبدا لهم سيئات ما كسبوا وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And when adversity touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, "I have only been given it because of knowledge." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent weakness in human nature where people often display a pattern of spiritual inconsistency. When facing hardship, humans readily turn to God with humility and desperation, but once blessed with prosperity, they attribute their success to their own merits and abilities, forgetting their previous state of dependence on divine mercy. The divine response clarifies that such blessings are actually tests of character, designed to reveal whether the recipient will remain grateful and humble or become arrogant and self-attributing.
orig: فإذا مس الإنسان ضر دعانا ثم إذا خولناه نعمة منا قال إنما أوتيته على علم بل هي فتنة ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون

translation: Those before them had already said it, but all they had earned did not benefit them at all
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of worldly accumulation and denial of divine truth. It points to a recurring pattern in human history where previous nations who rejected faith placed their trust in their wealth and achievements, only to find that these material gains offered no protection or benefit when divine judgment came upon them. The verse serves as a warning that material success alone cannot substitute for spiritual guidance and divine acceptance.
orig: قد قالها الذين من قبلهم فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: So they were struck by the evil consequences of what they earned. And those who have wronged of these [people] will be struck by the evil consequences of what they earned, and they will not cause failure.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the universal principle of divine justice, emphasizing that every individual's actions have consequences. Those who persist in wrongdoing or evil deeds will inevitably face the repercussions of their choices, and no amount of power or influence can prevent Allah's justice from taking its course.
orig: فأصابهم سيئات ما كسبوا والذين ظلموا من هؤلاء سيصيبهم سيئات ما كسبوا وما هم بمعجزين

translation: Do they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's wisdom in distributing wealth and sustenance is beyond human comprehension. Some people are granted abundance while others face restrictions, not necessarily due to their merit or lack thereof, but as part of divine wisdom and testing. This system of unequal distribution serves as a reminder of Allah's absolute control and sovereignty, encouraging believers to trust in His wisdom rather than questioning why some have more than others.
orig: أولم يعلموا أن الله يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

translation: Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."
interpretation: This verse embodies Allah's infinite mercy and compassion, emphasizing that no sin is too great for divine forgiveness. It serves as a powerful message of hope for those who feel overwhelmed by their past mistakes, reassuring them that sincere repentance can wipe away any transgression, no matter how severe. The use of "My servants" shows Allah's close relationship with humanity, even with those who have sinned, indicating that one's mistakes don't sever their connection with their Creator.
orig: قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا إنه هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And turn to your Lord in repentance and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, after which you will not be helped
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency of spiritual transformation and highlights that divine mercy is available through sincere repentance, but there exists a point of no return. The call to "turn" and "submit" suggests that humans have free will to choose their spiritual path, but this window of opportunity isn't endless. It's a reminder that postponing spiritual awakening and submission to divine guidance could lead to a state where redemption becomes impossible.
orig: وأنيبوا إلى ربكم وأسلموا له من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب ثم لا تنصرون

translation: And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of proactive spiritual awareness and making conscious choices in following divine guidance. It suggests that humans shouldn't wait for consequences to motivate their adherence to God's teachings, as divine retribution can come unexpectedly. The mention of "best of what was revealed" indicates that believers should strive for excellence in their practice of faith, choosing the most beneficial and righteous path among the various options presented to them.
orig: واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب بغتة وأنتم لا تشعرون

translation: Lest a soul should say, "Oh, how I regret what I neglected in regard to Allah, and I was among the mockers"
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound warning about the devastating regret that awaits those who realize too late that they wasted their earthly life by neglecting their spiritual duties and relationship with Allah. The use of "Oh, how I regret" (يا حسرتا) emphasizes the intense anguish and remorse that will be felt when one finally recognizes their spiritual negligence, particularly after having adopted a dismissive or mocking attitude toward faith and divine guidance.
orig: أن تقول نفس يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله وإن كنت لمن الساخرين

translation: Or lest you should say, "If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous"
interpretation: This verse addresses the human tendency to shift blame for one's spiritual shortcomings onto divine predestination. It warns against using the lack of guidance as an excuse for not following the right path, as Allah has already provided clear guidance through revelation and natural disposition. The verse emphasizes personal responsibility in choosing righteousness and warns against procrastination in matters of faith.
orig: أو تقول لو أن الله هداني لكنت من المتقين

translation: Or [lest] you would say when you see the punishment, "If only I had another opportunity, then I would be among the doers of good."
interpretation: This verse reveals the deep regret and desperate wishful thinking of sinners in the afterlife. When faced with divine punishment, they yearn for a second chance at life, claiming they would live righteously if given another opportunity. However, this desire for redemption comes too late, highlighting the importance of making righteous choices during one's earthly life rather than postponing good deeds until it's no longer possible.
orig: أو تقول حين ترى العذاب لو أن لي كرة فأكون من المحسنين

translation: Yes indeed, My verses came to you, but you denied them, acted arrogantly, and were among the disbelievers
interpretation: This verse illustrates the tragic pattern of human resistance to divine guidance, where pride and arrogance become the primary barriers between a person and spiritual truth. When someone consciously rejects divine signs despite recognizing their authenticity, it's not due to lack of evidence but rather due to their ego and unwillingness to submit to a higher authority. The verse serves as a reminder that spiritual blindness is often a choice rooted in arrogance rather than genuine disbelief.
orig: بلى قد جاءتك آياتي فكذبت بها واستكبرت وكنت من الكافرين

translation: And on the Day of Resurrection, you will see those who lied about Allah with their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell a residence for the arrogant?
interpretation: This verse illustrates the severe consequences of attributing false things to Allah, showing how spiritual corruption manifests as physical darkness in the afterlife. The blackened faces symbolize the spiritual darkness and shame that engulfs those who fabricated lies about divine truth. The rhetorical question about Hell being a dwelling for the arrogant connects false attribution to Allah with the sin of arrogance, suggesting that those who dare to lie about Allah do so from a position of pride and self-importance.
orig: ويوم القيامة ترى الذين كذبوا على الله وجوههم مسودة أليس في جهنم مثوى للمتكبرين

translation: And Allah will deliver those who feared Him to their place of salvation. No evil will touch them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine promise of protection and emotional security granted to those who maintain God-consciousness (taqwa) in their lives. The use of "mafazah" (place of salvation) suggests not just physical safety but a comprehensive state of success and triumph. The promise of freedom from both external harm ("no evil will touch them") and internal distress ("nor will they grieve") indicates that true God-consciousness leads to complete peace and security in both worldly life and the hereafter.
orig: وينجي الله الذين اتقوا بمفازتهم لا يمسهم السوء ولا هم يحزنون

translation: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is, over all things, Disposer of affairs
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and complete control over creation. It establishes that nothing exists without His will and creative power, and He not only creates but actively manages and oversees everything in existence. The term "wakeel" (disposer of affairs) suggests that Allah is not a distant creator but remains intimately involved with His creation, sustaining and directing all matters according to His wisdom.
orig: الله خالق كل شيء وهو على كل شيء وكيل

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah, it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and control over all creation, symbolized through the metaphor of "keys," suggesting His complete authority over every aspect of existence. The cosmic scope of His dominion serves as a stark contrast to the misguided choice of those who reject His signs, highlighting how their denial of such an evident truth leads to their ultimate loss in both worldly and spiritual terms.
orig: له مقاليد السماوات والأرض والذين كفروا بآيات الله أولئك هم الخاسرون

translation: Say, "Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental principle of monotheism by highlighting the absurdity of worshipping anything besides Allah. It portrays how those who suggest the worship of other deities are acting from a place of ignorance, as they fail to recognize the supreme authority and uniqueness of the Creator. The use of the term "ignorant ones" suggests that polytheism stems from a lack of true knowledge and understanding of divine reality.
orig: قل أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد أيها الجاهلون
