translation: And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you that if you associate [anything] with Allah, your deeds would surely become worthless, and you would surely be among the losers
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental principle of monotheism by highlighting that even prophets, despite their elevated status, are not exempt from the consequences of shirk (polytheism). It serves as a divine warning that associating partners with Allah nullifies all good deeds, suggesting that pure monotheism is the foundation upon which all righteous actions must be built to have any spiritual value.
orig: ولقد أوحي إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك لئن أشركت ليحبطن عملك ولتكونن من الخاسرين

translation: Rather, worship Allah and be among the grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of directing one's devotion exclusively to Allah, rejecting all false objects of worship. The command to "be among the grateful" suggests that true worship is inherently linked to gratitude, as recognizing Allah's blessings naturally leads to sincere devotion and appreciation of His favors.
orig: بل الله فاعبد وكن من الشاكرين

translation: They have not appraised Allah with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be [within] His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the incomprehensible magnitude of Allah's power and dominion, contrasting human limitations in understanding His true nature with His absolute control over the cosmos. The imagery of holding the earth and folding the heavens serves to demonstrate that even the largest entities we know are insignificant in Allah's hands, making human attempts to associate partners with Him or comprehend His full majesty appear foolish and inadequate.
orig: وما قدروا الله حق قدره والأرض جميعا قبضته يوم القيامة والسماوات مطويات بيمينه سبحانه وتعالى عما يشركون

translation: And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute power of Allah over life and death, particularly during the Day of Judgment. The two blows of the Horn represent the complete transition from one phase of existence to another. The first blow signifies the end of worldly life and current universal order, while the second blow marks the beginning of the resurrection and accountability. The exception mentioned ("except whom Allah wills") demonstrates that Allah's power is absolute and that He maintains complete control even during universal destruction, choosing to spare whomever He wishes, possibly referring to certain angels or special servants.
orig: ونفخ في الصور فصعق من في السماوات ومن في الأرض إلا من شاء الله ثم نفخ فيه أخرى فإذا هم قيام ينظرون

translation: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Book will be placed, and the prophets and witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be made between them with truth, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse paints a powerful image of the Day of Judgment, where divine justice illuminates everything with perfect clarity. The "light of its Lord" symbolizes how all truths, deeds, and intentions will become unmistakably clear, leaving no room for deception or ambiguity. The presence of prophets and witnesses suggests complete accountability, where every soul's actions will be testified to by those who witnessed their earthly life. The emphasis on justice being served without wrongdoing indicates Allah's perfect fairness in judgment, where even the smallest deed will be accounted for with absolute precision.
orig: وأشرقت الأرض بنور ربها ووضع الكتاب وجيء بالنبيين والشهداء وقضي بينهم بالحق وهم لا يظلمون

translation: And every soul will be fully compensated for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's perfect justice and omniscience, highlighting that no deed, whether good or bad, will be overlooked in the final reckoning. The use of "wuffiyat" (fully compensated) suggests absolute completeness in the recompense, indicating that divine justice operates with utmost precision and thoroughness, leaving no room for injustice or oversight.
orig: ووفيت كل نفس ما عملت وهو أعلم بما يفعلون

translation: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they arrive there, its gates are opened and its keepers will say, 'Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?' They will say, 'Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound concept of accountability and divine justice, showing how denial of truth in this life leads to inevitable consequences in the afterlife. The group-wise procession to Hell symbolizes how people often follow collective patterns of disbelief, influenced by their social circles and communities. The dialogue between the angels and the disbelievers emphasizes that rejection of faith is a conscious choice made despite clear warnings and guidance, not due to lack of information or understanding.
orig: وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها فتحت أبوابها وقال لهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يتلون عليكم آيات ربكم وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هذا قالوا بلى ولكن حقت كلمة العذاب على الكافرين

translation: It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell to abide therein eternally, and wretched is the residence of the arrogant."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequences of arrogance and pride, showing that those who reject divine guidance due to their ego will face eternal punishment. The use of the word "gates" suggests different levels of punishment corresponding to different manifestations of arrogance in one's life, while the term "abide therein" indicates the permanence of this punishment as a fitting response to those who considered themselves too important to submit to divine truth.
orig: قيل ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: And those who feared their Lord will be led to Paradise in groups until, when they reach it while its gates have been opened and its keepers say, 'Peace be upon you; you have become pure; so enter it to abide eternally therein'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound honor and dignity with which the righteous will be received in Paradise. The use of the word "زمرا" (groups) suggests that people will enter with their spiritual companions and like-minded believers, highlighting the social nature of Paradise. The open gates symbolize welcome and readiness, while the greeting of peace from the angels shows that Paradise is a realm of ultimate tranquility. The phrase "طبتم" (you have become pure) indicates that entering Paradise requires spiritual purification in worldly life, and only those who have achieved this state through God-consciousness will be worthy of eternal residence there.
orig: وسيق الذين اتقوا ربهم إلى الجنة زمرا حتى إذا جاءوها وفتحت أبوابها وقال لهم خزنتها سلام عليكم طبتم فادخلوها خالدين

translation: And they will say, "All praise is due to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the earth, allowing us to settle in Paradise wherever we wish. How excellent is the reward of the workers!"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate triumph and gratitude of the believers in Paradise, highlighting how faith and patience are eventually vindicated. The mention of "inheriting the earth" symbolizes complete freedom and dominion, suggesting that the constraints and limitations of worldly life are replaced by absolute liberty in Paradise. The phrase "wherever we wish" emphasizes the complete autonomy and absence of restrictions in Paradise, contrasting with the limited choices in earthly life.
orig: وقالوا الحمد لله الذي صدقنا وعده وأورثنا الأرض نتبوأ من الجنة حيث نشاء فنعم أجر العاملين

translation: And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying the praises of their Lord. And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, 'All praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse paints a powerful image of the Day of Judgment, where the cosmic hierarchy and ultimate justice are revealed. The angels' encirclement of Allah's Throne represents the complete submission of all spiritual beings to divine authority. Their continuous glorification symbolizes the eternal recognition of Allah's perfection. The judgment "in truth" indicates absolute justice without any possibility of unfairness or bias. The concluding praise suggests that all creation will ultimately acknowledge Allah's sovereignty and perfect wisdom in His judgments, marking the final resolution of all worldly disputes and differences.
orig: وترى الملائكة حافين من حول العرش يسبحون بحمد ربهم وقضي بينهم بالحق وقيل الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Ha Mim
interpretation: These mystical letters at the beginning of the surah point to the miraculous nature of the Qur'an's language and serve as a reminder that Allah's knowledge transcends human understanding, highlighting the divine origin of the revelation
orig: حم

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the All-Knowing
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine knowledge comes directly from its supreme source, highlighting Allah's absolute authority and complete knowledge. The mention of Allah's attributes "Al-Aziz" (Mighty) and "Al-Alim" (All-Knowing) suggests that this revelation is both powerful in its impact and perfect in its wisdom, leaving no room for doubt about its authenticity or questioning its source.
orig: تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم

translation: The Forgiver of sin, Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment, Owner of abundance. There is no deity except Him; to Him is the final destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual nature of Allah's attributes - His infinite mercy and His absolute justice. While He is ever-ready to forgive sins and accept sincere repentance from His servants, He also maintains perfect justice through His punishment of unrepentant wrongdoing. The mention of "Owner of abundance" indicates that all blessings and rewards flow from Him alone, reinforcing why He is the only deity worthy of worship and why all souls will ultimately return to Him for judgment.
orig: غافر الذنب وقابل التوب شديد العقاب ذي الطول لا إله إلا هو إليه المصير

translation: None dispute concerning the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so do not be deceived by their movement throughout the lands
interpretation: This verse warns believers not to be impressed or misled by the apparent success and prosperity of those who reject divine truth. Their worldly achievements and freedom to travel and conduct business should not be seen as a sign of Allah's approval or as validation of their disbelief. Material success is temporary and not a measure of spiritual truth or divine favor.
orig: ما يجادل في آيات الله إلا الذين كفروا فلا يغررك تقلبهم في البلاد

translation: Before them, the people of Noah denied and the factions after them, and every nation intended [harm] for their messenger to seize him, and they disputed by [using] falsehood to invalidate thereby the truth. So I seized them, and how [terrible] was My penalty.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a recurring pattern in human history where communities consistently reject divine guidance through similar methods. The mention of successive nations attempting to "seize" their messengers suggests that opposition to truth often manifests through physical persecution rather than intellectual debate. The use of "falsehood to invalidate truth" points to how those in power typically employ deception and propaganda to maintain their status quo when faced with reformative messages. The divine response - "So I seized them" - emphasizes that ultimate justice prevails over human schemes, serving as both a warning and a reminder of divine sovereignty.
orig: كذبت قبلهم قوم نوح والأحزاب من بعدهم وهمت كل أمة برسولهم ليأخذوه وجادلوا بالباطل ليدحضوا به الحق فأخذتهم فكيف كان عقاب

translation: Thus the word of your Lord has been proven true against those who disbelieved, that they are companions of the Fire
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine justice and its inevitability, emphasizing that those who persistently reject truth and guidance, despite clear evidence, have effectively chosen their fate through their own actions. The term "word of your Lord" refers to God's established decree that deliberate disbelief leads to accountability, reflecting a universal spiritual law rather than arbitrary punishment.
orig: وكذلك حقت كلمت ربك على الذين كفروا أنهم أصحاب النار

translation: Those who carry the Throne and those around it glorify their Lord with praise, believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe: "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way, and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire."
interpretation: This verse reveals the profound relationship between angels and believers, showing how even the highest-ranking angels who bear Allah's throne engage in intercession for the faithful. It demonstrates the interconnected nature of the spiritual realm, where celestial beings actively participate in seeking divine mercy for believing humans. The angels' prayer highlights Allah's all-encompassing mercy and knowledge, suggesting that true repentance and following Allah's path are key factors in receiving divine forgiveness and protection from punishment.
orig: الذين يحملون العرش ومن حوله يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويؤمنون به ويستغفرون للذين آمنوا ربنا وسعت كل شيء رحمة وعلما فاغفر للذين تابوا واتبعوا سبيلك وقهم عذاب الجحيم

translation: Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them and whoever was righteous among their forefathers, their spouses and their offspring. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound Islamic understanding of family bonds extending into the afterlife, suggesting that righteousness can create a ripple effect across generations. It indicates that one's good deeds can benefit their family members, and that believers earnestly desire to be reunited with their virtuous loved ones in Paradise. The mention of Allah's attributes at the end - Al-Aziz (Mighty) and Al-Hakim (Wise) - implies that this divine promise of family reunion in Paradise is both powerful and purposeful in its design.
orig: ربنا وأدخلهم جنات عدن التي وعدتهم ومن صلح من آبائهم وأزواجهم وذرياتهم إنك أنت العزيز الحكيم

translation: And protect them from evil, and whoever You protect from evil that Day - You will have given him mercy. And that is the great success.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's divine protection as the ultimate salvation, suggesting that true success lies not in worldly achievements but in being shielded from spiritual and moral corruption through Allah's mercy. It's a reminder that our greatest victory is earning divine protection from sins and their consequences, particularly on the Day of Judgment.
orig: وقهم السيئات ومن تق السيئات يومئذ فقد رحمته وذلك هو الفوز العظيم

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve will be called out: "Allah's hatred towards you was greater than your hatred of yourselves when you were called to faith but you disbelieved."
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound psychological truth about the state of disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. When they realize the magnitude of their mistake, they will experience intense self-loathing. However, the verse indicates that Allah's displeasure with their rejection of faith during their worldly life was even greater than their own self-hatred. This suggests that Allah's love for His creation is so immense that His disappointment in their rejection of guidance exceeds even their own regret and self-reproach.
orig: إن الذين كفروا ينادون لمقت الله أكبر من مقتكم أنفسكم إذ تدعون إلى الإيمان فتكفرون

translation: They will say: "Our Lord! You have caused us to die twice and given us life twice, and we have acknowledged our sins. So is there any way to get out?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound regret of disbelievers in the afterlife, recognizing two deaths (non-existence before birth and physical death) and two lives (worldly life and resurrection). Their acknowledgment of sins in this state reflects how clarity comes when it's too late, highlighting the importance of recognizing truth and accepting guidance during earthly life rather than waiting until the final judgment when repentance is no longer possible.
orig: قالوا ربنا أمتنا اثنتين وأحييتنا اثنتين فاعترفنا بذنوبنا فهل إلى خروج من سبيل

translation: That is because when Allah alone was called upon, you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed. So the judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological disposition of those who reject monotheism while embracing polytheism, suggesting that their resistance to the concept of One God stems not from rational objection but from an emotional attachment to their traditional polytheistic beliefs. The verse concludes by asserting Allah's supreme authority as the ultimate judge of truth, emphasizing that human preferences or beliefs don't alter the fundamental reality of His uniqueness and sovereignty.
orig: ذلكم بأنه إذا دعي الله وحده كفرتم وإن يشرك به تؤمنوا فالحكم لله العلي الكبير

translation: It is He who shows you His signs and sends down sustenance from the sky for you. Yet none pays heed except those who turn back (to Him)
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual connection between recognizing divine signs and sustenance, suggesting that true understanding of God's providence comes only to those who approach life with humility and a willingness to return to divine guidance. The physical sustenance from the sky (rain) serves as a metaphor for spiritual nourishment, which can only be fully appreciated by those who maintain an open heart and conscious relationship with their Creator.
orig: هو الذي يريكم آياته وينزل لكم من السماء رزقا وما يتذكر إلا من ينيب

translation: So call upon Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, even though the disbelievers dislike it
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental principle of spiritual authenticity, urging believers to maintain pure devotion to Allah regardless of external opposition. The sincerity (ikhlas) mentioned here represents a complete purification of one's intentions and actions from any worldly motives or desire for recognition, focusing solely on seeking Allah's pleasure. The mention of disbelievers' displeasure suggests that true faith often faces resistance, but this opposition should not deter believers from maintaining their sincere devotion.
orig: فادعوا الله مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون

translation: The One who raises the ranks, Owner of the Throne, He places the spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants to warn of the Day of Meeting
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's supreme authority and His method of divine guidance through revelation. The "raising of ranks" suggests that Allah elevates people spiritually and morally through divine knowledge. The mention of the Spirit (often understood as divine revelation or Angel Gabriel) being cast upon chosen servants indicates that spiritual enlightenment and prophetic mission are divine gifts, not acquired attributes. The ultimate purpose of this divine communication is to prepare humanity for the inevitable Day of Meeting, when all creation will gather before their Creator for judgment.
orig: رفيع الدرجات ذو العرش يلقي الروح من أمره على من يشاء من عباده لينذر يوم التلاق

translation: The Day they will emerge - nothing of them will be concealed from Allah. [It will be said], "To whom belongs [all] sovereignty this Day? To Allah, the One, the Prevailing."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the absolute powerlessness of all creation on the Day of Judgment, when every soul will stand exposed before Allah. The rhetorical question emphasizes that all claims to power, authority, and control that existed in worldly life will be stripped away, revealing Allah's complete and undisputed sovereignty. The use of "The One, the Prevailing" emphasizes that Allah's dominion is both unique and overwhelming, crushing all false notions of power that humans might have held.
orig: يوم هم بارزون لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء لمن الملك اليوم لله الواحد القهار

translation: Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. No injustice today! Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's perfect justice and the immediacy of judgment in the Hereafter. The use of "today" creates a sense of immediacy and inevitability, suggesting that all our actions, whether hidden or apparent, will face immediate accountability. The declaration of "no injustice" reinforces that divine judgment is absolutely fair, with each person receiving exactly what they deserve based on their deeds, neither more punishment nor less reward than what is warranted.
orig: اليوم تجزى كل نفس بما كسبت لا ظلم اليوم إن الله سريع الحساب

translation: And warn them of the Day of the approaching (doom), when hearts will be at throats, choking (with anguish). The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend nor any intercessor who will be obeyed.
interpretation: This verse conveys the profound psychological and spiritual state of humanity during the Day of Judgment. The imagery of hearts rising to throats represents the extreme anxiety and terror that people will experience when facing divine justice. It particularly emphasizes that those who committed injustice will find themselves completely isolated, stripped of all worldly connections and support systems they once relied upon. The absence of both friends and effective intercessors highlights the ultimate individual accountability before Allah, where one's actions alone will determine their fate.
orig: وأنذرهم يوم الآزفة إذ القلوب لدى الحناجر كاظمين ما للظالمين من حميم ولا شفيع يطاع

translation: He knows the stealthy looks and what the hearts conceal
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete and perfect knowledge of even the most subtle human actions and thoughts. The reference to "stealthy looks" points to the hidden glances people make when they think no one notices, highlighting that even our smallest visual indiscretions are known to Allah. The mention of what hearts conceal demonstrates that Allah's knowledge extends beyond physical actions to our deepest thoughts, intentions, and emotional states, leaving no room for humans to hide anything from their Creator.
orig: يعلم خائنة الأعين وما تخفي الصدور

translation: And Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him judge not with anything. Indeed, Allah - He is the All-Hearer, the All-Seer.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority and perfect justice of Allah in contrast to the powerlessness of false deities. It highlights that only Allah's judgment carries real weight and consequence, while the judgment or intercession sought from idols, saints, or other objects of worship is meaningless and ineffective. The mention of Allah being All-Hearing and All-Seeing reinforces that His judgments are based on complete knowledge and understanding of all matters, both apparent and hidden.
orig: والله يقضي بالحق والذين يدعون من دونه لا يقضون بشيء إن الله هو السميع البصير

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power and impact on the earth, but Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector against Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder about historical accountability and divine justice. It suggests that material strength and earthly achievements don't guarantee protection from divine judgment. The verse encourages people to learn from the fate of past civilizations who, despite their superior technological and material advancements, were ultimately held accountable for their moral transgressions. It emphasizes that true security lies not in worldly power but in moral and spiritual righteousness.
orig: أولم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين كانوا من قبلهم كانوا هم أشد منهم قوة وآثارا في الأرض فأخذهم الله بذنوبهم وما كان لهم من الله من واق

translation: That was because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Powerful and severe in punishment
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine pattern of justice where people's rejection of clear guidance leads to consequences. When communities persistently deny the truth despite being presented with undeniable evidence, they demonstrate willful defiance rather than genuine ignorance. The use of "seized" implies a sudden and inescapable grasp, highlighting that no one can evade divine accountability when it comes.
orig: ذلك بأنهم كانت تأتيهم رسلهم بالبينات فكفروا فأخذهم الله إنه قوي شديد العقاب

translation: And We sent Moses with Our signs and clear authority
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine empowerment of prophets, specifically highlighting how Allah equipped Moses with both miraculous signs and undeniable spiritual authority to confront Pharaoh's tyranny. The "clear authority" refers to Moses's divinely granted leadership and the absolute certainty of his message, which was backed by tangible miracles to leave no room for doubt about his prophethood.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا وسلطان مبين

translation: To Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun, but they said: "A lying sorcerer"
interpretation: This verse illustrates how people in positions of power and wealth often reject divine guidance out of arrogance. The three figures mentioned represent different forms of corruption: political tyranny (Pharaoh), bureaucratic manipulation (Haman), and economic exploitation (Qarun). Their dismissal of the messenger as a "lying sorcerer" shows how those invested in worldly power systems typically respond to spiritual truth with denial and accusations.
orig: إلى فرعون وهامان وقارون فقالوا ساحر كذاب

translation: But when he came to them with Our truth, they said, "Kill the sons of those who have believed with him and keep their women alive." But the plot of the disbelievers is not except in error.
interpretation: This verse reveals the desperate tactics of tyrannical powers when faced with divine truth. When threatened by the message of faith, oppressors often resort to demographic warfare, targeting the next generation of believers while seeking to exploit women. This pattern of persecution, seen in Pharaoh's response to Moses, demonstrates how those who reject truth often respond with violence and social engineering rather than engaging with the message itself.
orig: فلما جاءهم بالحق من عندنا قالوا اقتلوا أبناء الذين آمنوا معه واستحيوا نساءهم وما كيد الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: And Pharaoh said, "Let me kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will spread corruption in the land."
interpretation: This verse reveals the true nature of tyrannical power structures that feel threatened by messages of truth and justice. Pharaoh's statement exposes how autocratic rulers often mask their fear of losing control under the pretense of protecting society's stability and religious traditions. His claim of wanting to prevent corruption is ironic, as he himself was the source of corruption, demonstrating how oppressors often accuse others of the very crimes they commit.
orig: وقال فرعون ذروني أقتل موسى وليدع ربه إني أخاف أن يبدل دينكم أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد

translation: And Moses said, "Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Account."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the universal nature of seeking divine protection against oppression and tyranny. Moses's declaration shows that true strength lies not in confronting oppressors directly, but in placing one's trust in divine protection. The mention of those who deny the Day of Account suggests that moral corruption and tyranny often stem from a lack of belief in ultimate accountability.
orig: وقال موسى إني عذت بربي وربكم من كل متكبر لا يؤمن بيوم الحساب

translation: A believing man from among the people of Pharaoh who concealed his faith said, "Would you kill a man [merely] because he says, 'My Lord is Allah' while he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord? And if he should be lying, then upon him is his lie; but if he should be truthful, there will strike you some of what he promises you. Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power of moral courage and rational argument in the face of tyranny. The believer's logical defense of Moses demonstrates how faith can coexist with reason, as he presents a risk-assessment argument: if Moses is lying, he alone bears the consequence, but if he's truthful, their persecution of him will lead to their own destruction. The believer's need to conceal his faith while speaking truth to power shows how wisdom and strategic thinking can be used to defend justice even under oppressive conditions.
orig: وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون يكتم إيمانه أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم وإن يك كاذبا فعليه كذبه وإن يك صادقا يصبكم بعض الذي يعدكم إن الله لا يهدي من هو مسرف كذاب

translation: O my people! Yours is the kingdom today, being dominant in the land, but who will help us against Allah's might, should it come upon us? Pharaoh said: I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct.
interpretation: This verse reveals the paradox of worldly power and its ultimate insignificance before divine authority. Pharaoh's statement reflects the common delusion of autocratic rulers who mistake temporal power for absolute authority, failing to recognize their vulnerability before divine will. His claim to show "only what he sees" demonstrates how earthly rulers often mistake their limited perspective for complete truth, while their promise of guidance ironically leads to destruction rather than salvation.
orig: يا قوم لكم الملك اليوم ظاهرين في الأرض فمن ينصرنا من بأس الله إن جاءنا قال فرعون ما أريكم إلا ما أرى وما أهديكم إلا سبيل الرشاد

translation: And he who believed said, "O my people! Indeed, I fear for you something like the day of the confederates"
interpretation: This verse highlights the compassionate warning from a believer to his people, drawing a parallel between their potential fate and historical examples of nations that faced divine punishment. The believer's concern stems from his understanding that rejection of truth and persistence in wrongdoing can lead to consequences similar to those experienced by previous opposing factions who were ultimately destroyed. His warning demonstrates how true faith motivates caring for others' welfare, even when they oppose the truth.
orig: وقال الذي آمن يا قوم إني أخاف عليكم مثل يوم الأحزاب

translation: Similar to the case of the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, and those who came after them. And Allah does not intend injustice for [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse illustrates a divine pattern in dealing with rebellious nations, emphasizing that their downfall was a result of their own actions rather than divine injustice. It serves as a reminder that when societies persistently reject truth and morality, their destruction is a consequence of their choices, not God's desire to harm them. The reference to previous nations serves as a warning that divine laws of justice are consistent throughout history.
orig: مثل دأب قوم نوح وعاد وثمود والذين من بعدهم وما الله يريد ظلما للعباد

translation: And O my people, I fear for you the Day of Calling
interpretation: This verse reflects a deep concern for humanity's ultimate fate, specifically referring to the Day of Judgment when people will call out to one another in distress and panic. The prophet's use of "I fear for you" demonstrates the sincere compassion and worry that spiritual leaders have for their followers, understanding the gravity of accountability that awaits those who reject divine guidance.
orig: ويا قوم إني أخاف عليكم يوم التناد

translation: The Day you will turn to flee - there will be no defender for you from Allah. And whoever Allah sends astray - there will be no guide for him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute powerlessness of humans on the Day of Judgment when faced with divine accountability. The imagery of people turning to flee suggests a moment of overwhelming terror when the reality of their deeds confronts them. The mention that there will be no "defender" or "guide" reinforces the concept that on this ultimate day, all human connections, power, and influence become meaningless, and one's fate rests solely with Allah's judgment. It serves as a powerful reminder that true guidance comes only from Allah, and those who reject His guidance during their worldly life will find no alternative path to salvation.
orig: يوم تولون مدبرين ما لكم من الله من عاصم ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

translation: And Joseph had already come to you before with clear proofs, but you remained in doubt of that which he brought to you, until when he died, you said, 'Never will Allah send a messenger after him.' Thus does Allah leave astray he who is a transgressor and skeptic.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how persistent denial and skepticism can harden hearts against divine guidance. Just as the people rejected Joseph's message despite clear evidence, their skepticism led them to make false assumptions about God's will, believing no more messengers would come. This pattern of doubt and rejection stems from an excessive inclination towards disbelief rather than from a lack of evidence, showing how spiritual corruption begins with a willful choice to remain skeptical despite clear signs.
orig: ولقد جاءكم يوسف من قبل بالبينات فما زلتم في شك مما جاءكم به حتى إذا هلك قلتم لن يبعث الله من بعده رسولا كذلك يضل الله من هو مسرف مرتاب

translation: Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them - it is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe. Thus does Allah seal over every heart [of one who is] arrogant and oppressive
interpretation: This verse warns against intellectual arrogance, particularly in matters of faith. When people argue against divine truths without valid evidence or genuine knowledge, they demonstrate a dangerous form of pride. The divine response to such behavior is a spiritual consequence - their hearts become sealed, preventing them from recognizing truth. This indicates that humility and openness are essential qualities for spiritual growth and understanding of divine wisdom.
orig: الذين يجادلون في آيات الله بغير سلطان أتاهم كبر مقتا عند الله وعند الذين آمنوا كذلك يطبع الله على كل قلب متكبر جبار

translation: And Pharaoh said, "O Haman, build for me a tower that I might reach the ways"
interpretation: This verse reveals Pharaoh's arrogance and delusion of grandeur, as he believed he could challenge God's authority by physically ascending to the heavens. His command to build a tower demonstrates how earthly rulers often attempt to assert their dominance through grand architectural projects, mistaking material height for spiritual elevation. The verse serves as a warning about the futility of human attempts to rival divine power through worldly means.
orig: وقال فرعون يا هامان ابن لي صرحا لعلي أبلغ الأسباب

translation: The ways of the heavens so I may look at the God of Moses, though I surely think he is a liar. And thus was made attractive to Pharaoh his evil deed, and he was averted from the path. And Pharaoh's plot was not except in ruin.
interpretation: This verse reveals the arrogance and psychological state of Pharaoh, who refused to acknowledge a power greater than himself. His desire to physically "reach" God through building shows his materialistic understanding of divinity and his refusal to accept spiritual truths. The verse also demonstrates how one's ego can lead to self-deception, where evil actions become rationalized and appear justified in one's mind, ultimately leading to their own destruction.
orig: أسباب السماوات فأطلع إلى إله موسى وإني لأظنه كاذبا وكذلك زين لفرعون سوء عمله وصد عن السبيل وما كيد فرعون إلا في تباب

translation: And he who believed said, "O my people! Follow me, I will guide you to the right path"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the sincere concern of a true believer for the spiritual welfare of others. The believer's invitation demonstrates that genuine faith naturally compels one to share guidance with others, reflecting how divine wisdom often flows through ordinary people who have embraced truth. The use of the word "guide" suggests that the path to righteousness is not merely theoretical but requires practical leadership and example from those who have already found it.
orig: وقال الذي آمن يا قوم اتبعون أهدكم سبيل الرشاد

translation: O my people! This worldly life is only [temporary] enjoyment, and indeed, the Hereafter is the home of permanent settlement
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transient nature of worldly pleasures and possessions, contrasting them with the eternal significance of the afterlife. It serves as a reminder that our current existence is merely a temporary phase, like a traveler's brief stop, while our ultimate destination is the hereafter where we will permanently reside. This understanding should influence how we prioritize our actions and investments, focusing more on eternal rewards rather than fleeting worldly gains.
orig: يا قوم إنما هذه الحياة الدنيا متاع وإن الآخرة هي دار القرار

translation: Whoever does evil will not be recompensed except with its equivalent, and whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise, being given provision therein without account.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine principle of perfect justice and boundless mercy. While evil deeds are repaid only in equal measure, showing Allah's justice, good deeds from believing men and women are rewarded with unlimited provisions in Paradise, demonstrating how Allah's mercy far outweighs His punishment. The explicit mention of both genders highlights Islam's recognition of spiritual equality between men and women, emphasizing that faith and righteous actions, not gender, determine one's standing before Allah.
orig: من عمل سيئة فلا يجزى إلا مثلها ومن عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن فأولئك يدخلون الجنة يرزقون فيها بغير حساب

translation: And O my people! What is wrong with me that I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?
interpretation: This verse highlights the frustration of a righteous person who earnestly seeks to guide others toward spiritual salvation and moral uprightness, only to be met with resistance and invitation to destructive practices. It reflects the eternal struggle between those who advocate for truth and righteousness against those who persist in harmful ways, showing how people sometimes paradoxically reject what's beneficial for them in favor of what's harmful.
orig: ويا قوم ما لي أدعوكم إلى النجاة وتدعونني إلى النار

translation: You invite me to disbelieve in Allah and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, while I invite you to the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between two paths: one of ignorance leading to polytheism, and another of enlightened monotheism. It emphasizes that true wisdom lies in following clear divine guidance rather than baseless beliefs, while also showing Allah's mercy through the mention of His forgiveness despite people's tendency to stray.
orig: تدعونني لأكفر بالله وأشرك به ما ليس لي به علم وأنا أدعوكم إلى العزيز الغفار

translation: Without doubt, that to which you call me has no claim in this world or in the Hereafter; and our return will be to Allah, and the transgressors will be companions of the Fire
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of false beliefs and idolatry, highlighting that any deity or ideology that diverts from Allah's path has no real power or authority in either this life or the next. It serves as a powerful reminder that excessive deviation from divine guidance leads to spiritual destruction, as those who transgress bounds will ultimately face divine justice in the hellfire.
orig: لا جرم أنما تدعونني إليه ليس له دعوة في الدنيا ولا في الآخرة وأن مردنا إلى الله وأن المسرفين هم أصحاب النار

translation: Soon you will remember what I say to you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Seeing of His servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the power of divine justice and truth's eventual triumph. When someone warns others of their wrongdoing but is ignored, they can find solace in surrendering their concerns to Allah's wisdom. The statement reflects complete trust in Allah's judgment, knowing that He witnesses all actions and will ultimately vindicate those who stand for truth.
orig: فستذكرون ما أقول لكم وأفوض أمري إلى الله إن الله بصير بالعباد

translation: So Allah protected him from the evils that they plotted, and the people of Pharaoh were surrounded by the worst punishment
interpretation: This verse illustrates divine protection and justice, showing how Allah's guardianship over the faithful manifests in real terms. When believers face schemes and plots from their adversaries, Allah's protection serves as an impenetrable shield. The mention of Pharaoh's people receiving punishment demonstrates that those who plot against truth and justice ultimately face the consequences of their actions, while the righteous remain divinely protected.
orig: فوقاه الله سيئات ما مكروا وحاق بآل فرعون سوء العذاب

translation: The Fire, they are exposed to it morning and evening. And on the Day the Hour appears [it will be said], "Make the people of Pharaoh enter the severest punishment"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the continuous nature of punishment in the afterlife, where time as we know it ceases to exist. The morning and evening exposure to fire represents an ongoing torment without respite, suggesting that the souls of wrongdoers experience punishment even before the Day of Judgment in their intermediate state (barzakh). The specific mention of Pharaoh's people serves as a warning that arrogance and oppression against truth and justice will result in the most severe divine retribution.
orig: النار يعرضون عليها غدوا وعشيا ويوم تقوم الساعة أدخلوا آل فرعون أشد العذاب

translation: And when they will dispute in the Fire, and the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers, so will you relieve us of a share of the Fire?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate futility of blind followership and misplaced loyalty in worldly life. On the Day of Judgment, those who followed corrupt leaders and influential figures out of weakness or desire for worldly gain will realize their grave error. Their desperate plea for help from their former leaders demonstrates how earthly hierarchies and power dynamics become meaningless in the face of divine justice, where each soul must bear its own burden.
orig: وإذ يتحاجون في النار فيقول الضعفاء للذين استكبروا إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا نصيبا من النار

translation: Those who were arrogant will say, "Indeed, we are all in it [Hell]. Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants."
interpretation: This verse reveals the ultimate realization of the arrogant when they face divine justice, showing how worldly hierarchies and pride become meaningless in the afterlife. The powerful who once looked down upon others finally acknowledge their equality in punishment, demonstrating how Allah's judgment treats all souls with perfect justice, regardless of their former status or position.
orig: قال الذين استكبروا إنا كل فيها إن الله قد حكم بين العباد

translation: And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell, "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day from the punishment"
interpretation: This verse reflects the utter desperation and regret of those in Hell, showing that even a single day's relief from torment becomes a desperate wish. Their plea to the guards of Hell to intercede on their behalf demonstrates that in the afterlife, the reality of one's choices and their consequences becomes painfully clear, but it is too late for redemption or relief.
orig: وقال الذين في النار لخزنة جهنم ادعوا ربكم يخفف عنا يوما من العذاب

translation: They will say, "Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?" They will reply, "Yes." They will say, "Then pray!" But the prayer of the disbelievers is only in vain.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound regret and helplessness that disbelievers will experience in the afterlife. When they plead for relief from their punishment, they're reminded of how they rejected clear divine guidance in worldly life. Their admission of receiving messengers shows they made conscious choices to reject faith. The final statement about their prayers being in vain demonstrates that after judgment, attempts to seek divine mercy are futile, emphasizing the importance of accepting truth and guidance while still in the worldly life.
orig: قالوا أولم تك تأتيكم رسلكم بالبينات قالوا بلى قالوا فادعوا وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال

translation: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand
interpretation: This verse offers a profound divine guarantee of Allah's unwavering support for both His messengers and the faithful believers, not just in their earthly struggles but extending to the ultimate justice of the Day of Judgment. It serves as a powerful reassurance that despite temporary hardships or apparent setbacks, Allah's protection and victory are assured for those who maintain their faith and persevere in His path.
orig: إنا لننصر رسلنا والذين آمنوا في الحياة الدنيا ويوم يقوم الأشهاد

translation: The Day when their excuses will not benefit the wrongdoers, and they will have the curse and they will have the worst home
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice of the Day of Judgment, where those who committed injustice and oppression in this world will face the consequences of their actions. Their attempts to justify their wrongdoings or offer excuses will be futile, as that Day is one of pure accountability where only one's deeds will speak. The mention of "curse" and "worst home" indicates that the punishment for oppression and injustice is not just physical but includes spiritual alienation from Allah's mercy and an eternal abode of misery.
orig: يوم لا ينفع الظالمين معذرتهم ولهم اللعنة ولهم سوء الدار

translation: And We had certainly given Moses guidance, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's special favor upon Moses and the Children of Israel by bestowing divine guidance and entrusting them with the responsibility of preserving and implementing divine scripture. It highlights the historical significance of the Israelites as bearers of religious knowledge and divine law, though this position also came with great accountability and expectations for their moral and spiritual conduct.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الهدى وأورثنا بني إسرائيل الكتاب

translation: A guidance and reminder for those of understanding
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true wisdom and enlightenment are accessible to those who actively engage their intellect and reasoning capabilities in seeking truth. The term "ulil albab" (those of understanding) refers to individuals who combine both intellectual capacity and spiritual awareness, suggesting that genuine guidance requires both mental discernment and an open heart.
orig: هدى وذكرى لأولي الألباب

translation: So be patient, for the promise of Allah is true, and seek forgiveness for your sin and glorify with praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining steadfast patience while trusting in Allah's divine timing, coupled with continuous spiritual purification through seeking forgiveness. The mention of morning and evening worship suggests that maintaining a consistent spiritual connection throughout the day is essential for achieving inner peace and divine guidance.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق واستغفر لذنبك وسبح بحمد ربك بالعشي والإبكار

translation: Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without [any] authority having come to them - there is not within their breasts except pride, [the extent of] which they cannot reach. So seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological roots of religious denial, suggesting that those who argue against divine truth without valid evidence are primarily motivated by arrogance rather than genuine intellectual objection. Their rejection stems from an inflated sense of self-importance that they can never truly justify. The divine remedy prescribed is seeking Allah's protection from such prideful disposition, reminding us that Allah is fully aware of both outward arguments and inner motivations.
orig: إن الذين يجادلون في آيات الله بغير سلطان أتاهم إن في صدورهم إلا كبر ما هم ببالغيه فاستعذ بالله إنه هو السميع البصير

translation: The creation of the heavens and earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most people do not know
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vast scale of Allah's creative power by comparing the immense creation of the cosmos to that of humans, suggesting that if Allah can create such massive celestial bodies and systems, then the resurrection of humans should not be considered impossible. It also points to human limitations in comprehending the full scope of divine power and creation.
orig: لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون

translation: Not equal are the blind and the seeing, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds and the evildoer. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse establishes a fundamental principle of divine justice and moral discernment. Just as there is a clear distinction between physical blindness and sight, there is an equally significant difference between spiritual blindness and enlightenment. Those who choose faith and act righteously possess spiritual vision that guides them to truth and virtue, while those who persist in wrongdoing are like the blind, unable to perceive the path of righteousness. The verse suggests that humans often fail to reflect deeply on this essential difference, leading them to incorrectly equate fundamentally different moral positions and spiritual states.
orig: وما يستوي الأعمى والبصير والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ولا المسيء قليلا ما تتذكرون

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming - no doubt about it - but most of the people do not believe
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute certainty of the Day of Judgment, presenting it as an inevitable reality rather than a mere possibility. The phrase "no doubt about it" serves to remove any skepticism, making it a matter of absolute truth. The latter part reveals a profound insight into human psychology - despite clear signs and warnings, humanity's tendency is toward denial or disbelief of ultimate accountability, perhaps due to being overly attached to worldly life or reluctant to face the implications of such a momentous event.
orig: إن الساعة لآتية لا ريب فيها ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون

translation: And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you." Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell humiliated.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the direct and personal relationship between Allah and His creation, highlighting that sincere supplication is a form of worship that Allah loves and promises to answer. The divine response is guaranteed, though it may come in different forms or times than expected. The latter part of the verse warns against arrogance in worship, suggesting that true spiritual elevation comes through humility and recognition of our dependence on Allah.
orig: وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي سيدخلون جهنم داخرين

translation: Allah is He who made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day giving sight. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of the people are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine wisdom in the alternation of night and day, where Allah has designed the night as a period of physical and mental rejuvenation, allowing humans to disconnect from their daily struggles and find peace in darkness. The day is described as "giving sight," suggesting that it's not just about illumination, but about clarity, productivity, and the ability to pursue life's purposes. This natural rhythm is presented as evidence of Allah's mercy and thoughtful design for human wellbeing, yet humans often fail to recognize these blessings in their daily lives.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الليل لتسكنوا فيه والنهار مبصرا إن الله لذو فضل على الناس ولكن أكثر الناس لا يشكرون

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, Creator of all things; there is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: The verse emphasizes the futility of turning away from the truth when all evidence points to Allah's supreme authority. By questioning "how are you deluded," it challenges those who reject divine unity despite witnessing Allah's creative power in everything around them, suggesting that denying His uniqueness is a form of self-imposed deception that defies logical reasoning.
orig: ذلكم الله ربكم خالق كل شيء لا إله إلا هو فأنى تؤفكون

translation: Thus are deluded those who used to deny Allah's signs
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound spiritual law: those who consistently and willfully reject divine guidance eventually develop a distorted perception of reality. Their denial becomes a self-reinforcing cycle, where each rejection of truth makes it increasingly difficult to recognize subsequent truths, leading to a state of spiritual blindness.
orig: كذلك يؤفك الذين كانوا بآيات الله يجحدون

translation: Allah is the One Who made for you the earth a place of settlement and the sky a canopy, and formed you—and perfected your form—and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord. So Blessed is Allah, Lord of all worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's comprehensive care for humanity through His intricate design of creation. The metaphor of Earth as a "place of settlement" and sky as a "canopy" illustrates how the universe is purposefully engineered to sustain human life. The mention of human form being perfected suggests that humans are created with divine intent and precision, not by chance. The provision of "good things" points to Allah's role as the ultimate sustainer, providing not just necessities but pleasant and wholesome provisions, demonstrating both His power and mercy.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الأرض قرارا والسماء بناء وصوركم فأحسن صوركم ورزقكم من الطيبات ذلكم الله ربكم فتبارك الله رب العالمين

translation: He is the Ever-Living; there is no deity except Him, so call upon Him, being sincere to Him in religion. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unique attribute of Allah as the eternally living one, highlighting that true life in its perfect form belongs only to Him. The command to call upon Him with sincerity indicates that worship must be free from any form of pretense or divided loyalty, as pure monotheism requires complete dedication of one's spiritual devotion to Allah alone. The closing praise reinforces His absolute sovereignty and authority over all creation.
orig: هو الحي لا إله إلا هو فادعوه مخلصين له الدين الحمد لله رب العالمين

translation: Say: "I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah when clear proofs have come to me from my Lord, and I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental principle of monotheism by highlighting the Prophet's unwavering commitment to pure worship of Allah. It shows that once divine guidance becomes clear through evidence and revelation, there can be no compromise or acceptance of polytheistic practices, regardless of societal pressures or cultural norms. The command to submit to the "Lord of the worlds" specifically indicates that true sovereignty belongs exclusively to Allah, who governs all realms of existence.
orig: قل إني نهيت أن أعبد الذين تدعون من دون الله لما جاءني البينات من ربي وأمرت أن أسلم لرب العالمين

translation: It is He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot; then He brings you out as a child; then [He develops you] that you may reach your [time of] maturity; then [further] that you may become elders. And among you is he who is taken in death before [that], so that you may reach a specified term; and perhaps you will understand.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's complete mastery over the human lifecycle, demonstrating how our existence is a carefully designed journey that proves divine wisdom. The progression from humble origins (dust and sperm) to complex human development serves as a powerful reminder of our dependency on Allah and the temporary nature of our worldly existence. The mention of premature death alongside natural aging emphasizes that our lifespan is predetermined, encouraging contemplation of our purpose and mortality.
orig: هو الذي خلقكم من تراب ثم من نطفة ثم من علقة ثم يخرجكم طفلا ثم لتبلغوا أشدكم ثم لتكونوا شيوخا ومنكم من يتوفى من قبل ولتبلغوا أجلا مسمى ولعلكم تعقلون

translation: He is the One Who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be!" and it is.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power over existence and non-existence, highlighting His unique ability to create and terminate life through a mere command. The phrase "Be! and it is" illustrates the immediacy and effortlessness of divine will, showing that Allah's creative power isn't bound by physical processes or natural laws but operates through direct divine command.
orig: هو الذي يحيي ويميت فإذا قضى أمرا فإنما يقول له كن فيكون

translation: Do you not see those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah - how are they averted?
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of those who argue against divine truth despite clear evidence. It suggests that such people willfully turn away from guidance, indicating that their rejection stems not from lack of proof but from an internal resistance to accept what contradicts their desires or established beliefs. The question "how are they averted?" carries a tone of astonishment at their deliberate choice to ignore clear signs.
orig: ألم تر إلى الذين يجادلون في آيات الله أنى يصرفون

translation: Those who have denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers - they are going to know
interpretation: This verse carries a divine warning to those who reject revealed truth. The use of "soon they will know" (فسوف يعلمون) implies an inevitable future consequence, suggesting that deniers of divine messages will ultimately face the reality of their rejection when they encounter its consequences. It's a powerful statement about accountability and the serious nature of dismissing divine guidance.
orig: الذين كذبوا بالكتاب وبما أرسلنا به رسلنا فسوف يعلمون

translation: When iron collars will be around their necks and chains, they will be dragged
interpretation: This verse paints a vivid picture of the consequences awaiting those who rejected truth and divine guidance. The physical restraints mentioned symbolize how one's own choices and rejection of faith can become spiritual bondages that ultimately lead to a state of perpetual constraint and suffering. The dragging represents the loss of dignity and free will that comes from choosing to remain in spiritual darkness.
orig: إذ الأغلال في أعناقهم والسلاسل يسحبون

translation: In boiling water, then in the Fire they will be burned
interpretation: This verse illustrates the severe consequences of rejecting divine guidance, where the punishment involves a dual torment - first being immersed in scalding water that strips away the flesh, followed by being fuel for the blazing fire, representing a complete and absolute form of suffering that encompasses both liquid and solid states of torture
orig: في الحميم ثم في النار يسجرون

translation: Then it will be said to them, "Where are those you used to associate (with Allah)?"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility and ultimate abandonment of false deities on the Day of Judgment, when polytheists will face the harsh reality that their idols and objects of worship are powerless and absent when they need them most. It's a rhetorical question meant to highlight the foolishness of associating partners with Allah, as these supposed deities vanish when true accountability arrives.
orig: ثم قيل لهم أين ما كنتم تشركون

translation: Instead of Allah they will say, "They have forsaken us. Rather, we did not used to invoke anything before." Thus does Allah put the disbelievers astray
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate abandonment that idol worshippers will face on the Day of Judgment, when their false deities will completely dissociate from them. The profound irony is captured in their confession that their entire basis of worship was essentially meaningless, as they were worshipping "nothing." This realization comes too late, highlighting how spiritual blindness in this life leads to permanent loss in the hereafter.
orig: من دون الله قالوا ضلوا عنا بل لم نكن ندعو من قبل شيئا كذلك يضل الله الكافرين

translation: That is because you used to exult upon the earth without right and behave insolently
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice that befalls those who indulge in arrogant behavior and excessive pride during their worldly life. The term "without right" suggests that their joy was rooted in materialism, oppression, or transgression rather than legitimate achievements or spiritual fulfillment. It serves as a warning that unchecked worldly exuberance and insolent behavior, especially when it comes at the expense of others or moral values, will ultimately lead to accountability.
orig: ذلكم بما كنتم تفرحون في الأرض بغير الحق وبما كنتم تمرحون

translation: Enter the gates of Hell, to remain therein forever. How wretched is the abode of the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate consequence of arrogance and pride, showing that those who reject divine guidance due to their ego will face eternal punishment. The emphasis on "gates" suggests different levels of punishment corresponding to different manifestations of arrogance in one's life. The permanence of this state ("to remain therein") serves as a powerful warning against allowing pride to become a defining characteristic of one's personality.
orig: ادخلوا أبواب جهنم خالدين فيها فبئس مثوى المتكبرين

translation: So be patient, for the promise of Allah is true. And whether We show you part of what We promise them or We take you in death, to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom in the timing of justice and accountability. It suggests that while evildoers may seem to escape consequences in the immediate term, ultimate justice is inevitable, whether witnessed in this life or administered in the hereafter. The command for patience implies that divine timing operates on a scale beyond human perception, and trust in Allah's promise requires steadfast perseverance through challenging times.
orig: فاصبر إن وعد الله حق فإما نرينك بعض الذي نعدهم أو نتوفينك فإلينا يرجعون

translation: And We have certainly sent messengers before you. Among them are those [whose stories] We have related to you, and among them are those [whose stories] We have not related to you. And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign [or verse] except by permission of Allah. So when the command of Allah comes, it will be concluded in truth, and the falsifiers will thereupon lose.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the historical continuity of divine guidance and establishes the proper protocol of prophetic authority. It reveals that Allah's system of sending messengers is well-established, though not all their stories have been preserved. The verse also clarifies that even prophets cannot produce miracles at will, as these are solely under divine discretion. This serves as a reminder that ultimate authority belongs to Allah, and when His judgment comes, those who denied or fabricated falsehoods against His message will face the consequences of their denial.
orig: ولقد أرسلنا رسلا من قبلك منهم من قصصنا عليك ومنهم من لم نقصص عليك وما كان لرسول أن يأتي بآية إلا بإذن الله فإذا جاء أمر الله قضي بالحق وخسر هنالك المبطلون

translation: Allah is the one who made for you livestock, that you may ride upon them, and from them you eat
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's benevolence in creating animals with dual purposes, highlighting how He thoughtfully designed creation to serve humanity's various needs. The mention of riding before eating suggests that transportation and mobility were particularly significant for the early Muslim community, while also emphasizing how a single divine gift can serve multiple essential functions in human civilization.
orig: الله الذي جعل لكم الأنعام لتركبوا منها ومنها تأكلون

translation: And in them are benefits for you and that you may reach upon them a need in your breasts, and upon them and upon ships you are carried
interpretation: This verse emphasizes how Allah's creation of animals, particularly livestock, serves multiple divine purposes in human civilization. The reference to being "carried" on both animals and ships draws a parallel between land and sea transport, highlighting how Allah has provided humans with various means of mobility to facilitate trade, travel, and the fulfillment of their needs. This divine provision demonstrates Allah's comprehensive understanding of humanity's requirements for survival and progress.
orig: ولكم فيها منافع ولتبلغوا عليها حاجة في صدوركم وعليها وعلى الفلك تحملون

translation: And He shows you His signs - so which of the signs of Allah do you deny?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuous manifestation of Allah's presence and power through observable signs in creation, challenging human beings to reflect on their tendency to overlook or reject these evident proofs despite their clarity and abundance in the universe. The rhetorical question implies that denying these signs is illogical given their overwhelming presence in both the natural world and human experience.
orig: ويريكم آياته فأي آيات الله تنكرون

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? They were more numerous than them and greater in strength and impressions on the land, but all that they used to earn did not avail them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of learning from historical precedents and warns against the delusion of worldly power. It suggests that material strength, numerical superiority, and technological advancement are not guarantees of permanence or success. The verse teaches that civilizations that relied solely on their material achievements, while neglecting spiritual and moral development, ultimately faced divine judgment, making their worldly accomplishments futile.
orig: أفلم يسيروا في الأرض فينظروا كيف كان عاقبة الذين من قبلهم كانوا أكثر منهم وأشد قوة وآثارا في الأرض فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون

translation: When their messengers came to them with clear signs, they rejoiced in the knowledge they possessed, but they were overwhelmed by what they used to mock
interpretation: This verse illustrates the tragic irony of human arrogance in the face of divine wisdom. Those who possessed worldly knowledge became so overconfident in their own understanding that they dismissed the greater truths brought by the messengers, only to ultimately face the consequences of their mockery. It serves as a warning about intellectual arrogance and the danger of rejecting divine guidance based on limited human knowledge.
orig: فلما جاءتهم رسلهم بالبينات فرحوا بما عندهم من العلم وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: When they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and reject what we used to associate with Him"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the common human tendency to turn to genuine faith only when faced with severe consequences or divine punishment, showing that such last-minute declarations of faith, born out of desperation rather than sincere conviction, may not be accepted as they come after the opportunity for true repentance has passed
orig: فلما رأوا بأسنا قالوا آمنا بالله وحده وكفرنا بما كنا به مشركين

translation: But their faith was not going to benefit them once they saw Our punishment - [this is] the established way of Allah which has occurred concerning His servants - and there the disbelievers lost
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futile nature of deathbed repentance, highlighting that genuine faith must precede moments of inevitable doom. Just as a student cannot pass by studying only when seeing their failing grade, true faith cannot be established merely at the sight of divine punishment. Allah's unchanging law (sunnah) is that faith must be embraced during times of free will and choice, not when reality becomes undeniable through punishment.
orig: فلم يك ينفعهم إيمانهم لما رأوا بأسنا سنت الله التي قد خلت في عباده وخسر هنالك الكافرون

translation: Ha Mim
interpretation: These mysterious letters at the beginning of this surah symbolize the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, highlighting that despite being composed of regular Arabic letters that people know, its divine composition remains inimitable and serves as a testament to its divine origin.
orig: حم

translation: A revelation from the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine guidance comes from Allah's attributes of mercy, suggesting that His revelation is inherently an act of compassion and care for humanity rather than burden or hardship. The dual mention of mercy (Rahman and Raheem) indicates that this revelation is a manifestation of both Allah's universal mercy that encompasses all creation and His special mercy reserved for the faithful.
orig: تنزيل من الرحمن الرحيم

translation: A Book whose verses have been detailed, an Arabic Quran for a people who know
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom in revealing the Qur'an in Arabic, making it accessible and comprehensible to its immediate audience. The detailed nature of its verses suggests Allah's thoroughness in providing guidance, ensuring that those who sincerely seek knowledge can understand and implement its teachings. The phrase "for a people who know" indicates that true benefit from the Qur'an comes to those who approach it with intellectual engagement and sincere desire to understand.
orig: كتاب فصلت آياته قرآنا عربيا لقوم يعلمون

translation: A bearer of glad tidings and a warner, but most of them turn away, so they do not hear
interpretation: This verse illustrates the dual nature of divine guidance and human resistance. While the message comes with both hope and caution, people's inherent resistance to change and their attachment to familiar ways often leads them to willfully ignore spiritual truths, much like someone who covers their ears to avoid hearing what they don't wish to acknowledge
orig: بشيرا ونذيرا فأعرض أكثرهم فهم لا يسمعون

translation: And they say: "Our hearts are within coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a barrier, so work; indeed, we are working."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stubborn resistance and willful rejection of truth by disbelievers, who create artificial barriers to avoid engaging with divine guidance. Their claim of "coverings" on hearts and "deafness" in ears is not a physical condition but rather a metaphor for their deliberate choice to remain closed to the message. The mention of a "barrier" further emphasizes their self-imposed isolation from truth, while their challenge to "work" reveals their arrogant dismissal of divine warning and persistence in their own misguided ways.
orig: وقالوا قلوبنا في أكنة مما تدعونا إليه وفي آذاننا وقر ومن بيننا وبينك حجاب فاعمل إننا عاملون

translation: Say, "I am only a man like you, to whom it has been revealed that your god is one God. So take a straight course to Him and seek His forgiveness." And woe to those who associate others with Allah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity of Prophet Muhammad while highlighting his divine connection. It teaches that despite being a messenger, he shares the same human nature as others, distinguishing him from those who were wrongly deified by their followers. The prophet's role is to convey the fundamental truth of monotheism, while encouraging direct connection with Allah through righteous conduct and sincere repentance. The stern warning at the end underscores the gravity of associating partners with Allah, as it contradicts the pure monotheistic message.
orig: قل إنما أنا بشر مثلكم يوحى إلي أنما إلهكم إله واحد فاستقيموا إليه واستغفروه وويل للمشركين

translation: Those who do not give Zakah, and regarding the Hereafter, they are disbelievers
interpretation: This verse highlights the intrinsic connection between financial worship and faith. By refusing to pay Zakah, one demonstrates a spiritual deficiency that extends beyond mere monetary withholding - it reflects a deeper rejection of divine social responsibility and accountability in the afterlife. The repetition of "hum" (they) emphasizes their conscious choice in both refusing Zakah and denying the Hereafter, suggesting that neglecting financial obligations to society is a manifestation of disbelief in ultimate divine justice.
orig: الذين لا يؤتون الزكاة وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward uninterrupted
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite generosity, highlighting that the rewards for sincere faith combined with good actions are perpetual and endless. Unlike worldly rewards which may be cut off or diminished, divine compensation flows continuously without limitation or cessation, reflecting Allah's boundless mercy towards those who align their beliefs with righteous conduct.
orig: إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لهم أجر غير ممنون

translation: Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the irrationality of polytheism by highlighting the stark contrast between Allah's supreme power as the Creator and humanity's ingratitude. The mention of creating the earth in "two days" demonstrates Allah's methodical and purposeful creation, suggesting that a being capable of such precise and magnificent creation deserves exclusive worship. The rhetorical question format serves to make polytheists reflect on the contradiction between acknowledging Allah's power to create the universe while still worshipping other deities alongside Him.
orig: قل أئنكم لتكفرون بالذي خلق الأرض في يومين وتجعلون له أندادا ذلك رب العالمين

translation: And He placed therein (the earth) firmly set mountains over its surface, and He blessed it and determined therein its sustenance in four days, equal for all those who ask.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's perfect design and planning in creation, showing how He established a precise ecological and sustenance system on Earth. The mountains serve as stabilizers and regulators of Earth's physical processes, while the predetermined distribution of resources and provisions ensures the survival of all creatures. The mention of "four days" emphasizes the deliberate, measured nature of creation rather than a hasty or random process.
orig: وجعل فيها رواسي من فوقها وبارك فيها وقدر فيها أقواتها في أربعة أيام سواء للسائلين

translation: Then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We have come willingly."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's absolute power over creation and speaks to the fundamental nature of divine will. The metaphorical dialogue between Allah and His creation demonstrates that everything in existence ultimately submits to divine authority. The mention of "smoke" likely refers to the primordial state of the universe, suggesting that even the most basic elements of creation are subject to Allah's command. The willing submission of heaven and earth reflects the inherent disposition of all creation to naturally align with divine order, even though they were given a choice.
orig: ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها قالتا أتينا طائعين

translation: And He completed them as seven heavens within two days and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's absolute power and precision in creation, showing how He meticulously designed the universe in layers, with each heaven having its distinct purpose and function. The mention of "lamps" (stars) serving dual purposes - both as decoration and protection - demonstrates how Allah's creation is both beautiful and practical. The precise nature of this cosmic architecture points to a deliberate design by an All-Powerful, All-Knowing Creator, emphasizing that nothing in the universe is random or without purpose.
orig: فقضاهن سبع سماوات في يومين وأوحى في كل سماء أمرها وزينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح وحفظا ذلك تقدير العزيز العليم

translation: But if they turn away, then say, "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt [that struck] 'Aad and Thamud"
interpretation: This verse serves as a powerful reminder that rejection of divine guidance can lead to severe consequences, drawing a parallel between potential modern-day deniers and the ancient civilizations of 'Aad and Thamud who faced divine punishment. It emphasizes that historical patterns of divine justice remain relevant and applicable to contemporary situations.
orig: فإن أعرضوا فقل أنذرتكم صاعقة مثل صاعقة عاد وثمود

translation: When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them [saying], 'Do not worship except Allah,' they said, 'If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels, so indeed we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the persistent pattern of human resistance to divine guidance, where people reject the message not based on its merit but through arbitrary demands and excuses.
