The disbelievers' response shows how they used divine predestination as a pretext for their rejection, suggesting that if God truly wanted them to believe, He would have sent angels instead of human messengers. This reflects their arrogance and unwillingness to accept guidance through fellow humans, despite the fact that human messengers are more relatable and better suited to guide other humans.
orig: إذ جاءتهم الرسل من بين أيديهم ومن خلفهم ألا تعبدوا إلا الله قالوا لو شاء ربنا لأنزل ملائكة فإنا بما أرسلتم به كافرون

translation: As for 'Ad, they behaved arrogantly in the land without right and said, "Who is mightier than us in strength?" Did they not see that Allah who created them was mightier than them in strength? And they used to reject Our signs.
interpretation: This verse illustrates how material power and technological advancement can lead to spiritual blindness and arrogance. The people of 'Ad's fatal flaw wasn't their strength itself, but their failure to recognize its true source and their inability to see their own limitations as created beings. Their story serves as a warning about the dangers of human pride and the tendency to forget our ultimate dependence on divine power.
orig: فأما عاد فاستكبروا في الأرض بغير الحق وقالوا من أشد منا قوة أولم يروا أن الله الذي خلقهم هو أشد منهم قوة وكانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: So We sent upon them a screaming wind during days of misfortune to make them taste the punishment of disgrace in worldly life; but the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's method of dealing with persistent wrongdoers, showing that divine punishment can manifest in both natural and supernatural forms. The "screaming wind" represents how natural elements can become instruments of divine justice, while the emphasis on disgrace rather than just physical punishment highlights how spiritual and social humiliation often serve as powerful deterrents. The comparison with the Hereafter's punishment reminds us that worldly consequences, however severe, are merely a glimpse of what awaits those who persist in defiance of divine guidance.
orig: فأرسلنا عليهم ريحا صرصرا في أيام نحسات لنذيقهم عذاب الخزي في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أخزى وهم لا ينصرون

translation: And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance, so the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seized them for what they used to earn
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound concept of human free will and its consequences. Despite being given divine guidance, the people of Thamud made a conscious choice to reject truth in favor of spiritual blindness, demonstrating how guidance doesn't guarantee acceptance. Their punishment serves as a testament that willful rejection of truth, when one knows better, carries severe consequences in Allah's justice system.
orig: وأما ثمود فهديناهم فاستحبوا العمى على الهدى فأخذتهم صاعقة العذاب الهون بما كانوا يكسبون

translation: And We saved those who believed and used to fear Allah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine pattern of salvation, where sincere faith combined with God-consciousness (taqwa) becomes a means of deliverance from hardship and destruction. It suggests that true safety and success lie not in worldly power or resources, but in maintaining a strong spiritual connection with Allah through belief and righteous conduct.
orig: ونجينا الذين آمنوا وكانوا يتقون

translation: And the Day when Allah's enemies will be gathered to the Fire, and they will be driven in ranks
interpretation: This verse paints a powerful picture of divine justice, highlighting that those who actively opposed Allah's message and guidance will face a systematic and organized process of accountability. The use of the word "yūzaʿūn" (arranged in ranks) suggests that this gathering isn't chaotic but rather a deliberate and orderly process, emphasizing the absolute control and authority of Allah even in administering judgment to those who denied Him.
orig: ويوم يحشر أعداء الله إلى النار فهم يوزعون

translation: Until, when they reach it, their hearing and their sight and their skins will testify against them about what they used to do
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound concept of divine justice, where even our own body parts will become witnesses to our deeds on the Day of Judgment. It suggests that Allah's system of accountability is so comprehensive that one's own physical faculties, which were used to commit sins or good deeds, will speak the truth about their actions. This implies that there can be no denial or escape from one's deeds, as the very instruments of our actions become testifiers against us.
orig: حتى إذا ما جاءوها شهد عليهم سمعهم وأبصارهم وجلودهم بما كانوا يعملون

translation: And they will say to their skins, "Why have you testified against us?" They will say, "Allah has made us speak, as He makes everything speak, and He created you the first time, and to Him you will return."
interpretation: This verse reveals the profound truth that on the Day of Judgment, even our physical bodies will bear witness to our deeds, highlighting that nothing can be hidden from Allah's knowledge. The dialogue between sinners and their own skin demonstrates that Allah's power extends beyond our comprehension, as He can make inanimate parts of our body speak and testify. This serves as a reminder that our entire existence, from creation to resurrection, is under Allah's complete control, and we cannot escape accountability for our actions.
orig: وقالوا لجلودهم لم شهدتم علينا قالوا أنطقنا الله الذي أنطق كل شيء وهو خلقكم أول مرة وإليه ترجعون

translation: And you did not use to conceal yourselves, lest your hearing and your sight and your skins would testify against you, but you assumed that Allah does not know much of what you do
interpretation: This verse reveals the profound truth about human self-deception, where people engage in sins thinking they can hide from Allah's knowledge. It points to how our own body parts will become witnesses against us, suggesting that the very faculties we use to commit sins will ultimately expose our deeds, highlighting the futility of attempting to conceal our actions from Allah's all-encompassing awareness.
orig: وما كنتم تستترون أن يشهد عليكم سمعكم ولا أبصاركم ولا جلودكم ولكن ظننتم أن الله لا يعلم كثيرا مما تعملون

translation: And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord that has brought you to ruin, and you have become among the losers
interpretation: This verse highlights the grave consequences of having negative or false assumptions about Allah. When people doubt Allah's wisdom, mercy, or justice, these misguided thoughts can lead them to spiritual destruction. The verse serves as a warning that maintaining wrong beliefs about Allah's nature and attributes is not merely a passive error, but an active force that can drive one to spiritual ruin and ultimate loss in both this life and the hereafter.
orig: وذلكم ظنكم الذي ظننتم بربكم أرداكم فأصبحتم من الخاسرين

translation: And if they endure patiently, the Fire will be their residence; and if they ask to appease [Allah], they will not be of those who are allowed to appease.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of seeking redemption after final judgment, emphasizing that once divine justice is enacted, there will be no opportunity for the unrepentant to make amends or seek Allah's pleasure. The mention of patience here is ironic, as their endurance of punishment becomes meaningless since their fate is already sealed.
orig: فإن يصبروا فالنار مثوى لهم وإن يستعتبوا فما هم من المعتبين

translation: And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them, and the word has come into effect upon them among nations which had passed on before them of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound spiritual principle that when people persistently reject divine guidance, Allah allows them to be influenced by companions (whether human or jinn) who encourage their misdeeds and make sin appear attractive. These companions beautify both their past actions and future endeavors, leading them further astray. This divine arrangement serves as a natural consequence of their initial choice to turn away from truth, ultimately resulting in their spiritual loss.
orig: وقيضنا لهم قرناء فزينوا لهم ما بين أيديهم وما خلفهم وحق عليهم القول في أمم قد خلت من قبلهم من الجن والإنس إنهم كانوا خاسرين

translation: And those who disbelieved said, "Do not listen to this Qur'an and speak noisily during it that perhaps you will overcome."
interpretation: This verse reveals a deliberate strategy employed by the opponents of Islam to prevent the Qur'an's message from reaching people's hearts. By creating noise and disruption during its recitation, they hoped to diminish its impact and maintain their influence over others, showing how those who fear truth often resort to suppressing it rather than engaging with it intellectually.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا لا تسمعوا لهذا القرآن والغوا فيه لعلكم تغلبون

translation: So We will surely cause those who disbelieve to taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they used to do
interpretation: This verse emphasizes divine justice and accountability, highlighting that rejection of truth and persistent wrongdoing will ultimately lead to consequences. The use of "taste" suggests that the punishment will be experienced personally and directly, while "worst of what they used to do" indicates that people's most grievous actions will be the basis of their recompense, serving as a warning that our actions have lasting implications.
orig: فلنذيقن الذين كفروا عذابا شديدا ولنجزينهم أسوأ الذي كانوا يعملون

translation: That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah - the Fire. For them therein is the eternal home as recompense for their rejection of Our signs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes divine justice and the concept of accountability, highlighting that persistent denial of truth and opposition to divine guidance leads to spiritual alienation. The metaphor of an "eternal home" suggests that the choices one makes in rejecting divine signs become an integral part of one's permanent spiritual condition.
orig: ذلك جزاء أعداء الله النار لهم فيها دار الخلد جزاء بما كانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

translation: And those who disbelieved will say, "Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and men [so] we may put them under our feet that they will be among the lowest."
interpretation: This verse reveals the deep regret and anger that will consume the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment. Their request to see those who misled them shows how humans often try to shift blame for their own choices onto others. Rather than accepting responsibility for their disbelief, they seek to exact revenge on their misleaders, demonstrating that in the afterlife, all relationships based on falsehood will turn into enmity.
orig: وقال الذين كفروا ربنا أرنا اللذين أضلانا من الجن والإنس نجعلهما تحت أقدامنا ليكونا من الأسفلين

translation: Indeed, those who say "Our Lord is Allah" and then remain steadfast - the angels will descend upon them [saying]: "Do not fear and do not grieve but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised"
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound spiritual reward of unwavering faith and consistency in one's belief. It suggests that true faith isn't merely in declaration but in maintaining steadfastness despite life's challenges. The divine promise of angelic comfort and reassurance comes specifically to those who not only profess their faith but live by it consistently, indicating that genuine spiritual transformation requires both verbal affirmation and practical commitment.
orig: إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا تتنزل عليهم الملائكة ألا تخافوا ولا تحزنوا وأبشروا بالجنة التي كنتم توعدون

translation: We are your protectors in the worldly life and in the Hereafter. And therein you will have whatever your souls desire, and therein you will have whatever you request
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's comprehensive care for the believers, extending beyond mere protection to the fulfillment of their deepest desires. It suggests that true contentment and satisfaction are not found in the temporary pleasures of this world, but in the eternal relationship with Allah that continues into the afterlife. The promise of having "whatever your souls desire" indicates that Paradise is personalized to each individual's pure aspirations, reflecting Allah's intimate understanding of His creation's innermost wishes.
orig: نحن أولياؤكم في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة ولكم فيها ما تشتهي أنفسكم ولكم فيها ما تدعون

translation: A revelation from One who is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine guidance comes from Allah's attributes of forgiveness and mercy, suggesting that His revelations are not meant to burden us but to guide us with compassion and understanding towards salvation
orig: نزلا من غفور رحيم

translation: And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah and does righteous deeds and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"
interpretation: This verse highlights the noble status of those who combine three essential qualities: calling others to the path of Allah, performing good deeds, and proudly identifying themselves with Islam. It suggests that the most excellent form of speech is that which is backed by sincere actions and a clear commitment to one's faith, emphasizing that true da'wah (invitation to Islam) requires consistency between one's words, actions, and identity.
orig: ومن أحسن قولا ممن دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا وقال إنني من المسلمين

translation: Good and evil cannot be equal. Repel evil with what is better, and then the one between whom and yourself was enmity will become like a close friend.
interpretation: This verse teaches a profound spiritual principle about transforming negative relationships through elevated behavior. When we respond to hostility or negativity with kindness, patience, and good character, we have the power to transform our enemies into friends. This approach requires emotional maturity and spiritual strength, as it's challenging to respond positively to those who wrong us. The verse suggests that consistent ethical behavior and forgiveness can break down barriers of hatred and create genuine bonds of friendship where enmity once existed.
orig: ولا تستوي الحسنة ولا السيئة ادفع بالتي هي أحسن فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم

translation: None shall attain it except those who persevere, and none shall attain it except those of great fortune
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that achieving spiritual excellence and moral virtues requires unwavering patience and steadfastness. The "great fortune" mentioned isn't about material wealth, but rather about having the divine blessing of understanding and implementing wisdom in one's life. Those who maintain patience through life's trials are the ones who truly grasp and embody the deeper meanings of faith and wisdom.
orig: وما يلقاها إلا الذين صبروا وما يلقاها إلا ذو حظ عظيم

translation: And if an evil whisper comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge with Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing
interpretation: This verse teaches us that even the most pious individuals are not immune to Satan's subtle influences and negative thoughts. The use of "nazgh" (evil whisper) indicates that Satan's influence often begins with small, seemingly insignificant suggestions that can gradually lead one astray. The immediate recourse to Allah's protection serves as a spiritual shield, acknowledging our human vulnerability while affirming that divine protection is instantly accessible through sincere supplication.
orig: وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله إنه هو السميع العليم

translation: And among His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah who created them, if it is Him you worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental Islamic principle of monotheism by highlighting how celestial bodies, despite their grandeur, are merely signs of Allah's power rather than objects of worship. It directly challenges the pagan practices of sun and moon worship that were common in pre-Islamic Arabia, establishing a clear distinction between the Creator and His creation. The verse teaches that true worship should be directed solely to the One who possesses the power to create these magnificent cosmic phenomena.
orig: ومن آياته الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر لا تسجدوا للشمس ولا للقمر واسجدوا لله الذي خلقهن إن كنتم إياه تعبدون

translation: But if they are arrogant, then those who are with your Lord glorify Him by night and day, and they do not tire
interpretation: This verse conveys a profound message about the insignificance of human arrogance in the face of divine worship. It suggests that Allah's dominion remains unaffected by those who reject Him, as He has countless faithful servants among the angels who maintain constant devotion without fatigue or interruption. The verse serves as both a consolation to believers and a warning to the arrogant, illustrating that divine worship continues eternally regardless of human rejection.
orig: فإن استكبروا فالذين عند ربك يسبحون له بالليل والنهار وهم لا يسأمون

translation: And among His signs is that you see the earth barren, but when We send down upon it water, it stirs and swells. Indeed, He who gives it life is the Giver of life to the dead. Indeed, He is competent over all things.
interpretation: This verse draws a profound parallel between the resurrection of barren land and the resurrection of human beings after death. Just as Allah demonstrates His power by bringing dead soil to life with rain, causing it to vibrate with energy and swell with growth, He will similarly resurrect human beings on the Day of Judgment. The transformation of lifeless earth into vibrant, fertile land serves as a tangible proof of Allah's ability to restore life to what appears completely dead, reinforcing the concept of resurrection and the limitless nature of divine power.
orig: ومن آياته أنك ترى الأرض خاشعة فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت إن الذي أحياها لمحيي الموتى إنه على كل شيء قدير

translation: Indeed, those who distort Our verses are not hidden from Us. So, is he who is cast into the Fire better or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do what you will; indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning about the serious consequences of deliberately misinterpreting or distorting God's revelations. It emphasizes that God's complete awareness of such actions makes escape from accountability impossible. The rhetorical question about who is better - the one punished or the one secure - reinforces the stark contrast between the fates of those who respect versus those who distort divine guidance. The final statement "Do what you will" is not a permission but rather a stern warning, indicating that every action is being monitored and will face its due consequence.
orig: إن الذين يلحدون في آياتنا لا يخفون علينا أفمن يلقى في النار خير أم من يأتي آمنا يوم القيامة اعملوا ما شئتم إنه بما تعملون بصير

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them [are doomed], and indeed, it is a mighty Book
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gravity of rejecting divine guidance when it presents itself. The "mighty Book" refers to the Qur'an's unassailable nature, suggesting that those who reject it are opposing something that is inherently powerful and indestructible in its truth and wisdom. Their rejection doesn't diminish its authority or significance but rather reflects their own spiritual loss.
orig: إن الذين كفروا بالذكر لما جاءهم وإنه لكتاب عزيز

translation: No falsehood can approach it from before or behind it: It is sent down by One Full of Wisdom, Worthy of all Praise
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine protection and perfection of the Qur'an, indicating that it's safeguarded from any form of corruption, distortion, or falsehood throughout time. Its preservation is guaranteed by Allah's wisdom, making it immune to both historical criticism and future challenges to its authenticity. The mention of "before and behind" suggests that the Qur'an's truth is eternal, unaffected by past knowledge or future discoveries.
orig: لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه تنزيل من حكيم حميد

translation: Nothing is said to you except what was already said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness and the possessor of painful punishment
interpretation: This verse offers divine reassurance to Prophet Muhammad by emphasizing the universal pattern of how prophets were received throughout history. It suggests that the opposition, denial, and hardships he faced were not unique to him, but rather a common experience shared by all messengers of God. The mention of God's forgiveness and punishment together indicates the balance between hope and accountability in divine justice, where those who heed the message can find mercy while those who persist in rejection face consequences.
orig: ما يقال لك إلا ما قد قيل للرسل من قبلك إن ربك لذو مغفرة وذو عقاب أليم

translation: And if We had made it a Quran in a foreign language, they would have said, 'Why are its verses not explained in detail? Is it a foreign [recitation] and an Arab [messenger]?' Say, 'It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing. But those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is upon them blindness. Those are being called from a distant place.'
interpretation: The verse illustrates the paradoxical nature of human resistance to divine guidance, showing that skeptics would have found fault with the Quran regardless of its form. If it had been revealed in a non-Arabic language, they would have questioned its accessibility to Arab audiences. This reveals that the real issue isn't the language or format of the message, but rather the spiritual readiness of the recipient. Those who approach the text with faith find in it healing and guidance, while those who approach it with skepticism find themselves unable to access its wisdom, as if they're being called from an impossibly far distance.
orig: ولو جعلناه قرآنا أعجميا لقالوا لولا فصلت آياته أأعجمي وعربي قل هو للذين آمنوا هدى وشفاء والذين لا يؤمنون في آذانهم وقر وهو عليهم عمى أولئك ينادون من مكان بعيد

translation: And We gave Moses the Book, but differences arose therein. Had it not been for a Word that preceded from your Lord, the matter would have been judged between them. Indeed, they are in disquieting doubt concerning it
interpretation: This verse highlights a recurring pattern in human religious history where divine guidance, though clear, becomes a source of disagreement due to human nature. Just as Moses's followers disputed over their scripture despite its divine origin, this pattern of discord continues. The verse suggests that Allah's wisdom and predetermined plan allows these differences to exist until an appointed time, rather than immediately settling all disputes. This divine patience serves as a test of faith and free will, while also emphasizing how humans tend to create doubt and controversy even when presented with clear divine guidance.
orig: ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب فاختلف فيه ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك لقضي بينهم وإنهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: Whoever does righteousness - it is for his [own] soul; and whoever does evil [does so] against it. And your Lord is not ever unjust to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal principle of personal accountability in Islam, highlighting that our actions have direct consequences on our own spiritual well-being. When we perform good deeds, we're ultimately enriching our own souls and securing our future in the Hereafter, while our misdeeds damage our own spiritual state. The verse concludes by affirming Allah's perfect justice, indicating that whatever outcomes we face are purely the result of our own choices, not divine prejudice or unfairness.
orig: من عمل صالحا فلنفسه ومن أساء فعليها وما ربك بظلام للعبيد

translation: To Him is referred knowledge of the Hour. No fruit emerges from its sheath, nor does any female conceive or give birth except with His knowledge. And on the Day when He will call to them, "Where are My partners?" they will say, "We announce to You that none of us bears witness to that."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute and comprehensive knowledge of all things, both seen and unseen. It particularly highlights that even the most minute and hidden details of creation - from the development of fruit within its covering to the conception and gestation of every living being - are under His complete awareness and control. The verse then transitions to show how this all-encompassing knowledge will expose the falsehood of polytheism on the Day of Judgment, when those who attributed partners to Allah will be forced to admit their error, finding themselves without any evidence or witness to support their false beliefs.
orig: إليه يرد علم الساعة وما تخرج من ثمرات من أكمامها وما تحمل من أنثى ولا تضع إلا بعلمه ويوم يناديهم أين شركائي قالوا آذناك ما منا من شهيد

translation: And lost from them are those they used to invoke before, and they will realize there is no place of escape
interpretation: This verse illustrates the ultimate futility of relying on false deities or worldly powers for salvation. On the Day of Judgment, those who placed their trust in anything other than Allah will find themselves completely abandoned by their objects of worship, facing the stark reality that there is nowhere to flee from divine justice. It serves as a powerful warning against the practice of shirk (polytheism) and emphasizes the importance of maintaining pure monotheistic faith.
orig: وضل عنهم ما كانوا يدعون من قبل وظنوا ما لهم من محيص

translation: Man never tires of supplicating for good, but if evil touches him, he becomes hopeless and despondent
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound aspect of human nature: our tendency to be persistently optimistic and demanding when things are going well, yet quick to fall into despair when facing adversity. It highlights humanity's inherent impatience and lack of emotional equilibrium, suggesting that true faith requires maintaining hope and trust in Allah's wisdom regardless of circumstances.
orig: لا يسأم الإنسان من دعاء الخير وإن مسه الشر فيئوس قنوط

translation: And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity which has touched him, he will surely say, 'This is [due] to me, and I do not think the Hour will occur; and [even] if I should be returned to my Lord, indeed, for me there will be with Him the best.' But We will surely inform those who disbelieved about what they did, and We will surely make them taste a massive punishment.
interpretation: This verse reveals the inherent tendency of humans to become arrogant and ungrateful when blessed with prosperity after hardship. Instead of attributing their good fortune to Allah's mercy, they claim it as their own achievement and even begin to doubt the Day of Judgment. Their delusion extends to believing that if there is an afterlife, they deserve only good things there. This attitude reflects spiritual blindness and ingratitude, which Allah warns will be met with severe consequences.
orig: ولئن أذقناه رحمة منا من بعد ضراء مسته ليقولن هذا لي وما أظن الساعة قائمة ولئن رجعت إلى ربي إن لي عنده للحسنى فلننبئن الذين كفروا بما عملوا ولنذيقنهم من عذاب غليظ

translation: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; and when evil touches him, he makes lengthy supplications
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound insight into human psychology and our relationship with Allah. It describes the tendency of humans to become arrogant and distant from Allah during times of prosperity and comfort, forgetting the source of their blessings. However, when hardship strikes, the same person turns to prolonged, desperate prayers, showing how adversity often serves as a reminder of our dependence on divine mercy. This contrast highlights humanity's inconsistent nature and our failure to maintain gratitude and remembrance of Allah in all circumstances.
orig: وإذا أنعمنا على الإنسان أعرض ونأى بجانبه وإذا مسه الشر فذو دعاء عريض

translation: Say, "Have you considered: if the Quran is from Allah and you disbelieved in it, who would be more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?"
interpretation: This verse challenges those who reject divine revelation by highlighting the grave consequences of their denial. If the Quran is indeed from Allah, then those who oppose it are not merely making a simple error, but are positioning themselves in complete opposition to divine truth, placing themselves in a state of profound spiritual loss and separation from guidance.
orig: قل أرأيتم إن كان من عند الله ثم كفرتم به من أضل ممن هو في شقاق بعيد

translation: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?
interpretation: This verse points to Allah's promise of continuous revelation of divine signs through both the external universe and human nature itself. It suggests that scientific discoveries and deeper understanding of human consciousness will progressively validate the truth of divine revelation, indicating that faith and scientific knowledge are complementary paths to recognizing God's existence and power.
orig: سنريهم آياتنا في الآفاق وفي أنفسهم حتى يتبين لهم أنه الحق أولم يكف بربك أنه على كل شيء شهيد

translation: Unquestionably, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. Unquestionably, He encompasses all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights the psychological state of denial that prevents people from accepting accountability in the afterlife. Their doubt stems not from lack of evidence, but from an inner resistance to accept responsibility for their actions. The second part serves as a powerful reminder that Allah's knowledge and power encompass everything, making escape from accountability impossible, thus making their doubt ultimately futile.
orig: ألا إنهم في مرية من لقاء ربهم ألا إنه بكل شيء محيط

translation: Ha Mim
interpretation: These mystical letters at the beginning of this surah symbolize Allah's unique knowledge and serve as a reminder that the Qur'an's divine mysteries are known fully only to Allah, while containing layers of meaning that humans can explore but never fully comprehend
orig: حم

translation: Ain, Seen, Qaf
interpretation: These mystical letters at the beginning of Surah ash-Shura point to Allah's infinite knowledge and wisdom. The specific combination of these letters might symbolize the divine communication between Allah and Prophet Muhammad, emphasizing that the Qur'an's source is divine and beyond human comprehension.
orig: عسق

translation: Thus does Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, reveal to you and to those before you
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the continuity of divine revelation throughout history, highlighting that Muhammad's prophetic experience is part of a larger pattern of Allah's communication with humanity. It affirms that the source of revelation remains constant - the All-Mighty and All-Wise God - indicating that divine wisdom and guidance isn't limited to a single era or messenger but is part of Allah's ongoing relationship with His creation.
orig: كذلك يوحي إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك الله العزيز الحكيم

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute ownership and sovereignty over all creation, both seen and unseen, highlighting His supreme authority and infinite majesty that transcends all limitations of space and time. His attributes of being the Most High (Al-Ali) and the Most Great (Al-Azim) indicate that His power and greatness are beyond human comprehension, yet He maintains complete control and authority over everything He has created.
orig: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض وهو العلي العظيم

translation: The heavens almost rupture from above them while the angels exalt [Allah] with praise of their Lord and ask forgiveness for those on Earth. Unquestionably, it is Allah who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound impact of human disobedience and polytheism on the cosmic order, suggesting that even the mighty heavens can barely contain their distress at such transgressions. Yet, it simultaneously reveals Allah's infinite mercy, as the angels continuously intercede for humanity despite our shortcomings, reflecting the perfect balance between divine justice and compassion.
orig: تكاد السماوات يتفطرن من فوقهن والملائكة يسبحون بحمد ربهم ويستغفرون لمن في الأرض ألا إن الله هو الغفور الرحيم

translation: And those who take protectors besides Him - Allah is Guardian over them, and you are not over them a manager.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's complete sovereignty and oversight over those who seek protection from false deities or powers. It relieves Prophet Muhammad of the burden of responsibility for those who reject true faith, reminding him that his role is merely to convey the message, not to force people's choices or be accountable for their decisions.
orig: والذين اتخذوا من دونه أولياء الله حفيظ عليهم وما أنت عليهم بوكيل

translation: And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an that you may warn the Mother of Cities [Makkah] and those around it and warn of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt. A party will be in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine purpose behind revealing the Qur'an in Arabic, specifically targeting Makkah and its surrounding regions as the initial focal point for spreading Islam's message. The choice of Arabic and Makkah's centrality reflects a strategic divine plan to establish a strong foundation for the message before its global expansion. The mention of the inevitable division of humanity into two groups - Paradise and Hellfire dwellers - serves as a powerful motivator for ethical behavior and spiritual consciousness, highlighting the eternal consequences of one's choices in this world.
orig: وكذلك أوحينا إليك قرآنا عربيا لتنذر أم القرى ومن حولها وتنذر يوم الجمع لا ريب فيه فريق في الجنة وفريق في السعير

translation: And if Allah had willed, He could have made them one community, but He admits whom He wills into His mercy. And the wrongdoers have neither protector nor helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in allowing diversity among humankind rather than forcing uniformity. It teaches that diversity in beliefs and paths is part of Allah's plan, emphasizing human free will while maintaining His absolute power. The mention of His mercy suggests that guidance is a divine gift, while those who choose wrongdoing isolate themselves from divine protection and support.
orig: ولو شاء الله لجعلهم أمة واحدة ولكن يدخل من يشاء في رحمته والظالمون ما لهم من ولي ولا نصير

translation: Or have they taken protectors besides Him? But Allah - He is the [true] Protector, and He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the futility of seeking protection or guidance from any entity other than Allah. It challenges those who place their trust in false deities, human beings, or worldly powers by asserting that true protection can only come from Allah. The mention of giving life to the dead serves as a powerful reminder of Allah's unique and supreme power, indicating that only One who possesses such extraordinary ability deserves to be taken as a protector. The verse concludes by affirming Allah's absolute power over everything, reinforcing that He alone is worthy of being our guardian and protector.
orig: أم اتخذوا من دونه أولياء فالله هو الولي وهو يحيي الموتى وهو على كل شيء قدير

translation: And whatever you differ in, its ruling is with Allah. That is Allah, my Lord; upon Him I rely, and to Him I return
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate authority of Allah in resolving disputes and differences among people, suggesting that when human reasoning and debate reach their limits, divine guidance should be sought. It teaches that true wisdom lies in recognizing Allah's supreme judgment and submitting to His authority rather than becoming entrenched in endless disagreements
orig: وما اختلفتم فيه من شيء فحكمه إلى الله ذلكم الله ربي عليه توكلت وإليه أنيب

translation: Creator of the heavens and earth, He has made for you mates from among yourselves and mates among the cattle; by this means He multiplies you. There is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's unique creative power and His understanding of human nature. By establishing the system of pairs in both humans and animals, Allah demonstrates His wisdom in ensuring the continuation of life through companionship and procreation. The mention that "nothing is like Him" establishes a fundamental principle of Islamic monotheism, asserting Allah's absolute uniqueness and transcendence above His creation, while His attributes of hearing and seeing indicate His constant awareness and intimate knowledge of His creation's needs and actions.
orig: فاطر السماوات والأرض جعل لكم من أنفسكم أزواجا ومن الأنعام أزواجا يذرؤكم فيه ليس كمثله شيء وهو السميع البصير

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. He extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it. Indeed He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty over all resources and sustenance in the universe. The use of "keys" (maqalid) metaphorically indicates His complete control and authority. The variation in provision among people isn't random but stems from divine wisdom, as Allah distributes wealth and resources according to His perfect knowledge of what best serves each individual's spiritual growth and ultimate well-being.
orig: له مقاليد السماوات والأرض يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء ويقدر إنه بكل شيء عليم

translation: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus - to establish the religion and not be divided therein. Difficult for the polytheists is that to which you invite them. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the fundamental unity of divine revelation across all prophetic traditions, highlighting that Islam is not a new religion but a continuation and completion of the same essential message delivered to all major prophets. The divine instruction to maintain religious unity and avoid sectarian division suggests that theological fragmentation is contrary to God's will. The verse also acknowledges the natural resistance of polytheists to monotheistic teaching, while affirming that divine guidance is both a matter of God's selection and human receptivity to truth.
orig: شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا والذي أوحينا إليك وما وصينا به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى أن أقيموا الدين ولا تتفرقوا فيه كبر على المشركين ما تدعوهم إليه الله يجتبي إليه من يشاء ويهدي إليه من ينيب

translation: And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord [postponing the penalty] until a specified time, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, those who were granted inheritance of the Scripture after them are, concerning it, in disquieting doubt.
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound truth about human nature and religious discord. It points out that divisions among people often arise not from lack of knowledge, but rather after they have received clear knowledge. The root cause is identified as "baghy" (jealous animosity), suggesting that personal ego, pride, and worldly ambitions - not genuine theological differences - are often behind religious schisms. The divine wisdom in delaying immediate judgment allows for human free will and the opportunity for repentance, while also warning that inheriting religious knowledge without proper understanding leads to destructive doubt.
orig: وما تفرقوا إلا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم بغيا بينهم ولولا كلمة سبقت من ربك إلى أجل مسمى لقضي بينهم وإن الذين أورثوا الكتاب من بعدهم لفي شك منه مريب

translation: Therefore, to this [religion] invite [people], and be steadfast as you have been commanded, and do not follow their desires. And say, "I have believed in whatever Allah has revealed of scripture, and I have been commanded to do justice among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you. Allah will gather us together, and to Him is the final destination."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal principle of religious tolerance and mutual respect while maintaining firm conviction in one's faith. It instructs believers to invite others to truth with wisdom and steadfastness, without compromising their principles or being swayed by others' desires. The verse acknowledges the fundamental human right to choose one's beliefs while asserting that ultimate judgment rests with Allah, promoting peaceful coexistence despite religious differences.
orig: فلذلك فادع واستقم كما أمرت ولا تتبع أهواءهم وقل آمنت بما أنزل الله من كتاب وأمرت لأعدل بينكم الله ربنا وربكم لنا أعمالنا ولكم أعمالكم لا حجة بيننا وبينكم الله يجمع بيننا وإليه المصير

translation: And those who argue concerning Allah after He has been responded to - their argument is invalid with their Lord, and upon them is [His] wrath, and for them is a severe punishment
interpretation: This verse warns against those who persist in arguing against the truth of Allah's message after clear evidence has been established. It highlights how futile and counterproductive it is to dispute divine guidance once it has been clearly manifested, suggesting that such argumentative behavior stems from arrogance rather than genuine seeking of truth. The mention of Allah's wrath indicates that questioning established divine truths is a serious transgression that distances one from divine mercy.
orig: والذين يحاجون في الله من بعد ما استجيب له حجتهم داحضة عند ربهم وعليهم غضب ولهم عذاب شديد

translation: It is Allah who has sent down the Book in truth and [also] the balance. And what will make you perceive? Perhaps the Hour is near.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's divine wisdom in providing humanity with both spiritual guidance (the Book) and a moral framework (the balance) for establishing justice. The mention of "the Hour" serves as a reminder that accountability is imminent, urging believers to align their actions with these divine standards before the Day of Judgment arrives unexpectedly.
orig: الله الذي أنزل الكتاب بالحق والميزان وما يدريك لعل الساعة قريب

translation: Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in extreme error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrasting attitudes towards the Day of Judgment, revealing a psychological truth about human nature. The disbelievers' rush to mock and challenge its arrival reflects their deep-seated denial and defense mechanism against a reality they fear might be true. Meanwhile, the believers' apprehension stems from their genuine understanding of its gravity and consequences, demonstrating how true knowledge leads to appropriate reverence rather than arrogant dismissal.
orig: يستعجل بها الذين لا يؤمنون بها والذين آمنوا مشفقون منها ويعلمون أنها الحق ألا إن الذين يمارون في الساعة لفي ضلال بعيد

translation: Allah is Subtle with His servants; He gives provision to whom He wills, and He is the All-Strong, the All-Mighty
interpretation: This verse reveals the delicate balance between Allah's gentleness and power. The word "Latif" (Subtle) suggests that Allah's care for His creation operates in ways that are often imperceptible to us, working through intricate and nuanced means to provide for His servants. Just as a gentle breeze can carry a seed to fertile ground, Allah's subtle workings in our lives lead to profound outcomes. The mention of His strength and might alongside His subtlety indicates that true power doesn't always manifest in obvious or forceful ways, but can work through refined and sophisticated means.
orig: الله لطيف بعباده يرزق من يشاء وهو القوي العزيز

translation: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We will increase for him his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world - We will give him thereof, but he will have no share in the Hereafter
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine principle of intention and reward, emphasizing that our ultimate success depends on what we prioritize in life. Those who direct their efforts and intentions toward eternal spiritual rewards will find their good deeds multiplied by Allah's grace. Conversely, those who focus solely on worldly gains may achieve their material goals but will find themselves spiritually bankrupt in the afterlife, having traded eternal bliss for temporary satisfaction.
orig: من كان يريد حرث الآخرة نزد له في حرثه ومن كان يريد حرث الدنيا نؤته منها وما له في الآخرة من نصيب

translation: Or do they have partners who have prescribed for them a religion to which Allah has not consented? And were it not for the decisive word, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse challenges the concept of religious innovation and unauthorized legislation, warning against those who establish religious laws and practices without divine authorization. It emphasizes Allah's exclusive right to legislate religious matters and condemns those who attempt to create their own religious rules or follow man-made laws that contradict divine guidance. The mention of "partners" refers to false deities or human authorities who compete with Allah's legislative authority.
orig: أم لهم شركاء شرعوا لهم من الدين ما لم يأذن به الله ولولا كلمة الفصل لقضي بينهم وإن الظالمين لهم عذاب أليم

translation: You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, and it will [certainly] befall them. And those who have believed and done righteous deeds will be in lush regions of the gardens [in Paradise] having whatever they will in the presence of their Lord. That is [what is] the great bounty.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the stark contrast between divine justice and mercy, showing how those who committed injustice will face inevitable consequences with fear and dread, while the righteous believers will experience complete freedom and fulfillment in Paradise. The mention of "whatever they will" suggests that the rewards of the believers aren't just predetermined gifts, but rather a state of complete empowerment where their very wishes become reality, reflecting God's ultimate generosity and recognition of their faith and good deeds.
orig: ترى الظالمين مشفقين مما كسبوا وهو واقع بهم والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات في روضات الجنات لهم ما يشاءون عند ربهم ذلك هو الفضل الكبير

translation: That is the good news which Allah gives to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say, "I do not ask you for this message any payment except affection among relatives." And whoever commits a good deed - We will increase for him good therein. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine economy of love and reciprocity in Islam, where spiritual rewards are intertwined with maintaining family bonds. The Prophet's request for love among relatives as his only "payment" suggests that maintaining family ties is not just a social obligation but a spiritual imperative that enhances one's relationship with Allah. The promise of multiplied rewards for good deeds indicates Allah's generous nature in responding to human acts of kindness, establishing a cycle of divine appreciation that encourages continuous moral improvement.
orig: ذلك الذي يبشر الله عباده الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات قل لا أسألكم عليه أجرا إلا المودة في القربى ومن يقترف حسنة نزد له فيها حسنا إن الله غفور شكور

translation: Or do they say, "He has fabricated a lie about Allah"? But if Allah willed, He could seal your heart. And Allah eliminates falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He knows well what is within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's ultimate power over truth and falsehood, showing that if the Prophet were truly lying about divine revelation, Allah could have easily stopped him by sealing his heart. The fact that the Prophet continues to receive and spread revelation serves as proof of his authenticity, as Allah actively supports truth and eliminates falsehood through His divine wisdom and knowledge of what lies in people's hearts.
orig: أم يقولون افترى على الله كذبا فإن يشإ الله يختم على قلبك ويمح الله الباطل ويحق الحق بكلماته إنه عليم بذات الصدور

translation: And He is the One who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds, and He knows what you do
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's infinite mercy and His eagerness to forgive those who turn back to Him. The use of the present tense in "accepts" indicates that this is an ongoing, constant attribute of Allah, not limited by time or circumstance. The mention of "His servants" rather than "believers" specifically suggests that this opportunity for repentance is open to all humanity. The verse concludes by reminding us that Allah's knowledge of our actions is complete, which serves both as a warning against sin and as reassurance that He recognizes genuine repentance.
orig: وهو الذي يقبل التوبة عن عباده ويعفو عن السيئات ويعلم ما تفعلون

translation: And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds and increases them from His bounty. And the disbelievers will have a severe punishment
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine principle of reciprocity where Allah's response to sincere faith and good actions is not merely acceptance, but an amplification of blessings beyond what was earned. The mention of "increases them" suggests that divine rewards operate on a multiplier effect, where one good deed can yield manifold returns, reflecting Allah's infinite generosity toward those who align their lives with His guidance.
orig: ويستجيب الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات ويزيدهم من فضله والكافرون لهم عذاب شديد

translation: And if Allah had extended [abundant] provision for His servants, they would have committed tyranny throughout the earth. But He sends [it] down in an amount which He wills. Indeed He is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse reveals a profound divine wisdom in the distribution of wealth and resources. Allah's restraint in provision is actually a mercy, as unlimited abundance could lead humans to transgression and corruption due to their nature. The controlled distribution of resources serves as a test of human character and helps maintain balance in society. It also highlights that Allah's distribution of wealth is not random but based on His perfect knowledge of His servants' nature and what truly benefits them.
orig: ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض ولكن ينزل بقدر ما يشاء إنه بعباده خبير بصير

translation: And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's perfect timing and mercy in providing relief when His servants have lost all hope. Just as the physical rain revives dead land, Allah's spiritual and material blessings can transform situations that seem beyond repair, teaching us to never lose hope in His mercy. The mention of "Wali" (Protector) and "Hamid" (Praiseworthy) emphasizes that Allah's care for His creation is constant and deserving of gratitude, even during periods of apparent hardship.
orig: وهو الذي ينزل الغيث من بعد ما قنطوا وينشر رحمته وهو الولي الحميد

translation: And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the living creatures He has scattered through them, and He is able to gather them whenever He wills
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power over creation by highlighting how the vast expanse of the cosmos and all living beings within it serve as evidence of His creative ability. The mention of His power to gather all creatures points to the reality of resurrection, suggesting that the same divine power that initiated creation can easily reconstitute it on the Day of Judgment, regardless of how scattered or decomposed creatures may become
orig: ومن آياته خلق السماوات والأرض وما بث فيهما من دابة وهو على جمعهم إذا يشاء قدير

translation: Whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your hands have earned; and He pardons much.
interpretation: This verse teaches us about the divine law of cause and effect in our lives, emphasizing personal responsibility while simultaneously highlighting Allah's mercy. When hardships occur, they are often connected to our own actions and choices, serving as natural consequences or opportunities for growth and reflection. However, Allah's mercy is greater than His punishment, as He forgives and overlooks many of our mistakes that would otherwise deserve consequences.
orig: وما أصابكم من مصيبة فبما كسبت أيديكم ويعفو عن كثير

translation: And you cannot escape on earth, and you have no protector or helper besides Allah
interpretation: This verse emphasizes human vulnerability and complete dependence on Allah, reminding us that no matter how powerful or resourceful we might think we are, we cannot outrun or escape Allah's decree. It serves as a profound reminder that seeking protection or assistance from other sources besides Allah is futile, as He alone holds absolute power over all matters.
orig: وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير

translation: And among His signs are the ships that sail in the sea like mountains
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's power and grace through maritime technology, suggesting that humans' ability to construct and navigate massive vessels is a divine gift. The comparison to mountains emphasizes both the ships' grandeur and their relative insignificance compared to Allah's creation, reminding us that even our greatest achievements are manifestations of His wisdom and mercy.
orig: ومن آياته الجوار في البحر كالأعلام

translation: If He willed, He could still the wind, and they would remain motionless on its surface. Indeed, in this are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's absolute control over natural phenomena, specifically highlighting how even the mighty winds submit to His command. The imagery of ships becoming stranded without wind serves as a powerful reminder that human technological advancement and capabilities are ultimately dependent on Allah's mercy. The mention of "patient and grateful" people suggests that true understanding of divine power comes to those who maintain steadfastness during hardship and express gratitude during ease.
orig: إن يشأ يسكن الريح فيظللن رواكد على ظهره إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار شكور

translation: Or He could destroy them for what they have earned; but He pardons much
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's perfect balance between justice and mercy. While He has the power and right to punish people for their misdeeds immediately, He often chooses to forgive and overlook many sins, demonstrating His overwhelming mercy which takes precedence over His punishment. It serves as a reminder that despite our continuous transgressions, Allah's forgiveness is vast and encompasses much of what we do wrong.
orig: أو يوبقهن بما كسبوا ويعف عن كثير

translation: And those who dispute concerning Our signs will come to know that they have no place of escape
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine warning about the futility of arguing against Allah's truth. It emphasizes that those who choose to dispute or deny God's signs and revelations will ultimately face an inescapable reality, highlighting that no amount of argumentation or denial can change the absolute nature of divine truth or help them evade its consequences.
orig: ويعلم الذين يجادلون في آياتنا ما لهم من محيص

translation: Whatever you have been given is [only] enjoyment of worldly life, but what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who believe and rely upon their Lord
interpretation: This verse teaches that material possessions and worldly pleasures are temporary and fleeting, serving only as a brief enjoyment in this life. True and lasting fulfillment comes through the eternal rewards that Allah has prepared for those who maintain their faith and place their complete trust in Him rather than in worldly gains. It encourages believers to shift their focus from temporary worldly acquisitions to the permanent spiritual treasures that await them in the hereafter.
orig: فما أوتيتم من شيء فمتاع الحياة الدنيا وما عند الله خير وأبقى للذين آمنوا وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

translation: And those who avoid major sins and immoralities, and when they are angry, they forgive
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of righteous believers who exercise self-control in two significant ways. First, by consciously staying away from major transgressions and immoral acts, showing their commitment to moral excellence. Second, and perhaps more challenging, by mastering their emotions to the extent that they can overcome anger with forgiveness, demonstrating spiritual maturity and emotional intelligence that aligns with divine teachings.
orig: والذين يجتنبون كبائر الإثم والفواحش وإذا ما غضبوا هم يغفرون

translation: And those who respond to their Lord, establish prayer, conduct their affairs by mutual consultation, and spend out of what We have provided them
interpretation: This verse establishes the fundamental principles of Islamic governance and communal life, emphasizing that true believers combine their spiritual obligations with democratic consultation. The mention of "mutual consultation" (shura) alongside prayer and charitable giving suggests that collective decision-making is as essential to Islamic society as worship and generosity. It presents a model where leadership and community decisions should emerge from collaborative dialogue rather than autocratic rule.
orig: والذين استجابوا لربهم وأقاموا الصلاة وأمرهم شورى بينهم ومما رزقناهم ينفقون

translation: And those who, when tyranny strikes them, they defend themselves
interpretation: This verse highlights the Islamic principle that self-defense is not only permissible but commendable when faced with oppression. It establishes that Muslims shouldn't be passive victims but should actively resist injustice and defend their rights, though within moral and ethical boundaries. The verse validates the human dignity to stand against wrongdoing while maintaining balance between patience and resistance.
orig: والذين إذا أصابهم البغي هم ينتصرون

translation: The recompense for an evil is an evil like it, but whoever pardons and makes reconciliation - his reward is with Allah. Indeed, He does not like wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes a divine balance between justice and mercy in human relations. While it affirms the legitimate right to reciprocate harm with equivalent response, it elevates the moral choice of forgiveness and reconciliation as a superior path that earns divine reward. The mention that Allah dislikes wrongdoers serves as a reminder that even when exercising the right to retaliate, one must not transgress proper bounds, suggesting that forgiveness is the more spiritually elevated choice when possible.
orig: وجزاء سيئة سيئة مثلها فمن عفا وأصلح فأجره على الله إنه لا يحب الظالمين

translation: And whoever takes revenge after having been wronged - those are not to be blamed
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine recognition of the human right to seek justice when wronged. It acknowledges that defending oneself against oppression is not only permissible but is free from moral culpability. However, this should be understood within the broader Islamic framework that encourages forgiveness and restraint, suggesting that while self-defense and justified retaliation are allowed, they should be proportional and not exceed the boundaries of justice.
orig: ولمن انتصر بعد ظلمه فأولئك ما عليهم من سبيل

translation: The blame is only against those who oppress people and commit injustice on earth without right - for these there will be a painful punishment
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine accountability and condemnation are specifically directed at those who abuse power and authority to harm others, highlighting that oppression and tyranny are among the gravest sins in Allah's sight. The mention of "without right" suggests that any form of injustice that lacks legitimate justification is particularly egregious, and the promise of painful punishment serves as a stern warning to those in positions of power to exercise their authority with justice and mercy.
orig: إنما السبيل على الذين يظلمون الناس ويبغون في الأرض بغير الحق أولئك لهم عذاب أليم

translation: And whoever is patient and forgives - indeed, that is of the matters [requiring] determination
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that exercising patience and extending forgiveness in the face of wrongdoing requires tremendous inner strength and moral fortitude. It suggests that these virtues aren't merely passive responses but active choices that demand strong willpower and determination. The verse elevates patience and forgiveness as traits of high moral excellence that reflect spiritual maturity and self-control.
orig: ولمن صبر وغفر إن ذلك لمن عزم الأمور

translation: And whoever Allah sends astray - there is no protector for him beyond Him. And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying, "Is there any way to return?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute sovereignty of Allah over guidance and misguidance, emphasizing that once someone has firmly chosen the path of deviation and Allah has confirmed their misguidance, no force or power can guide them back. The image of wrongdoers begging for a second chance when facing divine punishment serves as a powerful warning about the finality of our choices in this life and the futility of regret in the afterlife.
orig: ومن يضلل الله فما له من ولي من بعده وترى الظالمين لما رأوا العذاب يقولون هل إلى مرد من سبيل

translation: And you will see them being exposed to it (Hell), humbled by disgrace, looking with a stealthy glance. And those who believe will say, "Indeed, the losers are they who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Behold! The wrongdoers are in an enduring punishment."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound psychological and spiritual state of those who rejected faith when confronted with their ultimate fate. Their posture of looking with furtive glances reveals their deep inner recognition of the truth they once denied, while their humiliation stems from the realization that their arrogance in worldly life led to their downfall. The believers' statement emphasizes how the greatest loss isn't of material wealth or worldly status, but rather the loss of one's own soul and the eternal separation from loved ones due to wrong choices in life.
orig: وتراهم يعرضون عليها خاشعين من الذل ينظرون من طرف خفي وقال الذين آمنوا إن الخاسرين الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة ألا إن الظالمين في عذاب مقيم

translation: And they had no protectors to help them besides Allah. And whoever Allah sends astray, for him there is no way (of guidance)
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah and humanity's complete dependence on divine guidance. It illustrates that when someone has truly strayed from Allah's path, no amount of worldly support or assistance can compensate for this spiritual loss. The mention of "protectors" points to the futility of seeking refuge in false deities or earthly powers when divine guidance is absent.
orig: وما كان لهم من أولياء ينصرونهم من دون الله ومن يضلل الله فما له من سبيل

translation: Respond to your Lord before there comes from Allah a Day that cannot be averted. You will have no refuge on that Day, nor will you have any denial.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency of spiritual awakening and the importance of heeding Allah's call while there is still time. It suggests that our current life represents a window of opportunity for redemption and righteous action, warning that once the Day of Judgment arrives, it will be too late to make amends or seek alternative paths. The mention of "no refuge" and "no denial" indicates the absolute nature of divine justice and the futility of seeking escape from accountability.
orig: استجيبوا لربكم من قبل أن يأتي يوم لا مرد له من الله ما لكم من ملجإ يومئذ وما لكم من نكير

translation: But if they turn away - We have not sent you over them as a guardian; upon you is only [the duty of] notification. And indeed, when We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices therein. But if evil afflicts them for what their hands have put forth, then indeed, man is ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse illuminates the dual nature of human behavior in response to divine experiences, while clarifying the Prophet's role. When humans receive blessings, they quickly rejoice without true gratitude, but when faced with hardship resulting from their own actions, they become ungrateful and forgetful of previous mercies. This pattern reflects humanity's inherent tendency toward short-sightedness and ingratitude, while also emphasizing that the Prophet's sole responsibility is to convey the message, not to force people to accept it.
orig: فإن أعرضوا فما أرسلناك عليهم حفيظا إن عليك إلا البلاغ وإنا إذا أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة فرح بها وإن تصبهم سيئة بما قدمت أيديهم فإن الإنسان كفور

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; He creates what He wills. He gives to whom He wills female [children], and He gives to whom He wills males
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and creative power, highlighting that the distribution of children's gender is a divine decision that transcends human control or preference. It serves as a reminder that what we receive in life, including our offspring, is based on divine wisdom rather than our personal desires or societal preferences. The verse implicitly challenges cultural biases about gender by presenting both male and female children as divine gifts.
orig: لله ملك السماوات والأرض يخلق ما يشاء يهب لمن يشاء إناثا ويهب لمن يشاء الذكور

translation: Or He makes them [both] males and females, and He renders whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's absolute control over human reproduction and fertility, highlighting that the ability to have children - whether male or female or none at all - is entirely within divine wisdom. It serves as a reminder that fertility and infertility are not mere biological coincidences but rather divine decrees that align with Allah's greater plan and knowledge of what is best for each individual.
orig: أو يزوجهم ذكرانا وإناثا ويجعل من يشاء عقيما إنه عليم قدير

translation: It is not for any human being that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil or that He sends a messenger to reveal, by His permission, what He wills. Indeed, He is Most High and Wise.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the profound nature of divine communication and establishes the three exclusive methods through which Allah communicates with humans. It emphasizes that direct communication with the Divine is not a casual or ordinary occurrence, but rather a carefully structured process that maintains the appropriate boundaries between Creator and creation. The mention of "behind a veil" particularly signifies the transcendent nature of Allah and the limitations of human capacity to directly perceive the Divine, while also protecting the human recipient from being overwhelmed by Allah's majesty.
orig: وما كان لبشر أن يكلمه الله إلا وحيا أو من وراء حجاب أو يرسل رسولا فيوحي بإذنه ما يشاء إنه علي حكيم

translation: And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was, but We have made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed, you guide to a straight path
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine nature of revelation and spiritual enlightenment, showing how Allah transforms individuals through divine guidance. Before receiving revelation, even the Prophet Muhammad was unaware of the deeper spiritual truths, but through Allah's mercy, he was granted spiritual insight that became a source of illumination. This divine light isn't merely knowledge, but a transformative force that Allah uses to guide chosen individuals, highlighting that true guidance is a gift from Allah rather than purely human effort.
orig: وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان ولكن جعلناه نورا نهدي به من نشاء من عبادنا وإنك لتهدي إلى صراط مستقيم

translation: The path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Indeed, to Allah all matters return.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine sovereignty and ultimate accountability. By highlighting Allah's ownership of everything in existence, it establishes that following His path is the natural consequence of recognizing His complete dominion. The phrase "all matters return" suggests that every decision, action, and outcome ultimately traces back to divine authority, reinforcing the futility of seeking guidance or solutions outside of Allah's prescribed way.
orig: صراط الله الذي له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض ألا إلى الله تصير الأمور

translation: Ha Mim
interpretation: These mystical letters at the beginning of this surah point to the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, highlighting that despite being composed of regular Arabic letters that people know, its divine composition remains inimitable and serves as a sign of its divine origin
orig: حم

translation: By the clear Book
interpretation: Allah is swearing by the Qur'an itself, emphasizing its nature as a clear and unambiguous source of divine guidance that leaves no room for doubt in its teachings and principles. The use of the word "clear" (mubeen) suggests that its message is accessible and comprehensible to those who approach it with sincerity.
orig: والكتاب المبين

translation: Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an so that you might understand
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah chose Arabic as the language of divine revelation to ensure clear comprehension for its immediate audience, highlighting the principle that divine guidance should be accessible and comprehensible to its recipients in their own language and cultural context
orig: إنا جعلناه قرآنا عربيا لعلكم تعقلون

translation: And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and full of wisdom
interpretation: This verse reveals that the Qur'an's origin exists in its perfect, complete form in Al-Lawh Al-Mahfudh (the Preserved Tablet), indicating that Allah's knowledge and wisdom are timeless and unchangeable. The divine message wasn't created at the time of revelation but has always existed in Allah's eternal knowledge, emphasizing the Qur'an's divine authenticity and protected status.
orig: وإنه في أم الكتاب لدينا لعلي حكيم

translation: Should We then turn away the Reminder from you completely because you are a transgressing people?
interpretation: This verse conveys Allah's mercy and patience despite human disobedience. It rhetorically questions whether divine guidance should be withheld from people just because they are excessive in their wrongdoing, implying that Allah continues to offer guidance and reminders even to those who transgress. This demonstrates Allah's infinite compassion, as He doesn't abandon people even when they stray far from righteousness.
orig: أفنضرب عنكم الذكر صفحا أن كنتم قوما مسرفين

translation: And how many prophets did We send among the earlier peoples
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's consistent pattern throughout history of sending divine guidance to humanity, highlighting that Muhammad wasn't the first messenger but part of a long chain of prophets who came to guide different communities. It suggests that the resistance and rejection that Prophet Muhammad faced was similar to what previous prophets encountered, offering him consolation and emphasizing the recurring nature of the struggle between truth and falsehood.
orig: وكم أرسلنا من نبي في الأولين

translation: And no messenger came to them except that they used to ridicule him
interpretation: This verse reflects a recurring pattern in human history where people often meet divine guidance with mockery and derision. It highlights the arrogance and spiritual blindness that prevents many from accepting truth when it comes to them, choosing instead to belittle those who bring God's message. This behavior stems from an attachment to existing beliefs and a resistance to change, even when presented with clear signs and wisdom.
orig: وما يأتيهم من نبي إلا كانوا به يستهزئون

translation: And We destroyed those who were greater than them in power, and the example of the former peoples has passed away
interpretation: This verse serves as a divine reminder that worldly strength and might are temporary, highlighting how civilizations that were far more powerful and technologically advanced were still subject to Allah's will. It emphasizes that no matter how mighty a nation becomes, they remain vulnerable if they defy divine guidance, suggesting that true security lies in moral and spiritual strength rather than material power.
orig: فأهلكنا أشد منهم بطشا ومضى مثل الأولين

translation: And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say: "The All-Mighty, All-Knowing created them"
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent recognition of Allah's existence even among those who deny Him. It demonstrates that deep within human nature, there is an innate acknowledgment of a supreme creator, as even the disbelievers, when confronted directly about the origin of the universe, would attribute its creation to the All-Mighty and All-Knowing God rather than claiming it came about by chance.
orig: ولئن سألتهم من خلق السماوات والأرض ليقولن خلقهن العزيز العليم

translation: Who has made for you the earth as a bed and made for you therein paths that you may be guided
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's divine providence in creating the Earth specifically suited for human habitation and survival. The metaphor of Earth as a "bed" suggests its perfect design for human comfort and stability, while the mention of "paths" refers not only to physical routes but also to the various means Allah has provided for humans to find their way, both literally and spiritually. The ultimate purpose is divine guidance, indicating that the physical features of Earth are signs pointing to Allah's existence and wisdom.
orig: الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهدا وجعل لكم فيها سبلا لعلكم تهتدون

translation: And who sent down water from the sky in a measured way, then We revived thereby a dead land; thus will you be brought forth
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's perfect system of balance and renewal, showing how He precisely controls rainfall to transform barren landscapes into thriving ecosystems. This natural phenomenon serves as a powerful metaphor for the resurrection, suggesting that just as Allah has the power to revive dead land through rain, He will similarly resurrect human beings from their graves on the Day of Judgment.
orig: والذي نزل من السماء ماء بقدر فأنشرنا به بلدة ميتا كذلك تخرجون

translation: And He Who created all the pairs and made for you ships and cattle on which you ride
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's comprehensive design in creation, highlighting how He has provided humanity with various means of transportation, both through maritime vessels and domesticated animals. This divine provision demonstrates Allah's mercy in facilitating human civilization and commerce, enabling us to traverse both land and sea. The mention of "pairs" also points to the fundamental duality in creation, suggesting that everything in existence has been created with a complementary counterpart, reinforcing the perfect balance in Allah's design.
orig: والذي خلق الأزواج كلها وجعل لكم من الفلك والأنعام ما تركبون

translation: That you may mount upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you have mounted thereupon and say: "Exalted is He who has subjected this to us, and we could not have [otherwise] subdued it"
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and humility in recognizing Allah's blessings. When humans utilize animals for transportation or labor, they should acknowledge that this ability is not from their own power but rather a divine gift. The prescribed supplication teaches us to maintain perspective about our limitations and dependence on Allah's provisions, reminding us that even our mastery over animals is granted by divine permission rather than our inherent capability.
orig: لتستووا على ظهوره ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم إذا استويتم عليه وتقولوا سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين

translation: And indeed, to our Lord we will return
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the temporary nature of our worldly existence and reinforces the Islamic concept that all souls will ultimately return to their Creator for accountability. It serves as both a comfort in times of hardship and a reminder of our ultimate purpose, encouraging believers to live with conscious awareness that their actions and choices will be accounted for when they return to Allah.
orig: وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون

translation: And they have attributed to Him from His servants a portion. Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse criticizes the practice of associating God's creation with His divinity, particularly highlighting how some people consider angels to be God's daughters. It points to humanity's inherent tendency to show ingratitude towards divine blessings by attributing divine qualities to created beings, despite clear evidence of God's absolute uniqueness and sovereignty.
orig: وجعلوا له من عباده جزءا إن الإنسان لكفور مبين

translation: Or has He taken, out of what He creates, daughters and chosen you for [having] sons?
interpretation: This verse criticizes the pre-Islamic Arabian belief that angels were Allah's daughters while they themselves preferred sons over daughters. It exposes the inherent contradiction in their thinking - how could they attribute to Allah what they themselves looked down upon? The verse challenges their illogical attribution of gender to the Divine while highlighting their own gender-based prejudices.
